A detector trained only on real photographs and their autoencoder copies matches one trained on 162k generated images on GenImage (+2.3 points, 95% CI [0.9, 3.7]) and complements it in fusion, but one resize with JPEG re-save, or a mild blur, costs it 19-27 points. Two lessons concern benchmarks. The in-the-wild benchmark Chameleon can be solved from image width alone. And on Synthbuster, how the real photographs are matched to the generated images' size decides whether our detector leads or trails (+4.4 or -9.7 points): the matching protocol alone can reverse a detector comparison. Code and per-image scores: https://github.com/iamsaugatpandey/deja-vae

title: SurgeCount: A Protocol-Guided Composition Harness for Bimanual Surgical Sponge Counting
abstract: We present SurgeCount, a system for auditable robotic surgical sponge counting that composes learned skills under a written procedural protocol. Retained sponges cause preventable harm, and surgical teams count every sponge before closure to reduce that risk. The robot repeatedly isolates one deformable sponge from a tangled pile and places it in the next numbered counting-tray slot, requiring handling of occluded grasp threads while preserving step order. We train one subtask-conditioned policy on eleven short skills and learn when each skill ends. At each learned boundary, a stateful vision-language model selects the next skill from an operator-authored specification of step order, visual verification, and recovery. This creates temporal commitment to each subtask and enables failures to be recovered by recomposing existing skills rather than using a dedicated recovery policy. We evaluate five methods across 100 real-robot trials using 20 matched layouts. SurgeCount fills 47 of 60 ordered slots and completes 12 of 20 procedures, compared with 27 of 60 and 3 of 20 for the strongest of four end-to-end policies trained on the same data. Replacing the detailed protocol prompt with a minimal prompt reduces performance to 29 of 60 slots and 5 of 20 completed procedures. These results show that long-horizon performance depends not only on visuomotor capacity, but also on how learned skills are committed, verified, and composed. This tabletop proof of concept motivates further evaluation of protocol-guided robotic sponge counting in clinically representative settings.

title: Boltz-Flow: Generating High-Quality Robot Action from Boltzmann Machine
abstract: Flow-matching policies integrate a velocity field from a fixed, observation-independent Gaussian source. However, since the source is unimodal and identical across all tasks, the limited representational capacity of Gaussian distributions constrains how far a policy can scale with growing task diversity. Moreover, the source factorizes over time steps and control dimensions, discarding the coordination that manipulation requires. We introduce Boltz-Flow, which replaces Gaussian initialization with a more powerful, observation- and instruction-conditioned Boltzmann source while leaving the base VLA unchanged. Boltz-Flow parameterizes this source with a conditional Boltzmann machine that assigns an energy value to each binary source state. A listwise objective, supervised entirely by offline demonstrations, aligns this energy with the quality of actions produced after frozen flow integration. At inference, the energy defines an Ising instance whose solution is decoded into continuous noise before a single standard integration. We use a physical coherent Ising machine during training. Experiments show that Boltz-Flow improves $π_{0.5}$ across three benchmarks, outperforming the compared strong policy baselines and competing noise optimization methods on LIBERO and RoboTwin 2.0 and ranking second only to LEAP on LIBERO-Plus. Additional experiments show gains under noise-adapted fine-tuning, with action-to-action warm starts, and on the SmolVLA backbone.

title: Boundedness and $L_p$-estimates for non-local operators with square-Dini continuous coefficients
abstract: We prove the boundedness of the non-local operator $\mathcal{L}^a$ of order $σ\in(0,2)$ with kernel $a(x,y)|y|^{-d-σ}$ from $H^σ_{p,w}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $L_{p,w}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for the whole range of $p\in(1,\infty)$, where $w$ is a Muckenhoupt weight. The coefficient $a(x,y)$ is bounded, merely measurable in $y$, and its modulus of continuity $ω$ in $x$ satisfies the square-Dini condition $\int_0^1ω(t)^2t^{-1}dt<\infty$. This condition allows, for instance, $ω(t)=(\log(1/t))^{-1}$, which is not a Dini modulus, and it improves the Hölder continuity assumption in previous work. Using the boundedness result, we obtain global estimates and the unique solvability in weighted $L_p$ spaces, as well as interior $L_p$-estimates, for the corresponding elliptic and parabolic equations. We also show that the square-Dini condition is sharp. By adapting a recent construction of C. Liu, we show that for every regular modulus $ω$ with $\int_0^1ω(t)^2t^{-1}dt=\infty$, there is a coefficient with modulus of continuity $ω$ for which the boundedness, the global estimates, and the interior estimates all fail. In particular, on the scale $ω(t)=(\log(1/t))^{-θ}$, the threshold is $θ=1/2$.

title: Finite Temperature Isoscalar Instabilities and Moat Regimes in Relativistic Nuclear Matter
abstract: We study the finite-temperature isoscalar collective response of symmetric nuclear matter in three relativistic mean-field descriptions: the linear Walecka model, its nonlinear extension, and the quark-meson coupling (QMC) model. The Walecka models are formulated in terms of nucle- onic degrees of freedom, whereas QMC incorporates quark degrees of freedom confined inside the nucleon. These models differ in their treatment of scalar interactions at finite density, affecting instability boundaries. Focusing on the coupled scalar-vector channel, we track how the boundaries of homogeneous instabilities evolve with temperature. In all three models, we find a nonmonotonic momentum dependence of the static response, characterized by a minimum at finite momentum, a moat regime that selects a preferred length scale for density fluctuations. Our results show that this moat structure is robust against thermal effects across these relativistic nuclear matter models, providing motivation for future studies of inhomogeneous phases in hot and dense astrophysical matter.

title: Closure of averaged Einstein equations by DESI data
abstract: We benchmark the hypothesis that the redshift dependence of postulated dark energy in the standard model, measured by the DESI collaboration, is a natural outcome of dark energy-free models of structure formation in general relativity. We recall fundamental results and the properties of averaged dust cosmologies that suggest to replace the dark energy equation of state through the nonperturbative impact of the inhomogeneous geometry. The relevant mechanism can be phrased in terms of an effective mean field description of inhomogeneities using the fluid analogy of a scalar field (the `morphon'). Without violating energy conditions this effective field exhibits a cross-over to phantom behaviour, compatible with observations. The exact dark energy-free framework needs a single closure condition that we implement in terms of parametrizations of the 3-years data of the DESI team. The resulting redshift dependence of effective cosmological characteristics is then illustrated and subject to physical interpretation. The aim of this paper is to set a benchmark that has to be met by any structure formation model or simulation investigated within general relativity in a flow-orthogonal foliation of spacetime, given the hypothesis.

title: Degree three unramified cohomology of homogeneous spaces with finite stabilisers
abstract: We provide an explicit formula for the third unramified cohomology group of homogeneous spaces of $\mathrm{SL}_n$ with finite stabilisers and a rational point, valid over an arbitrary field of characteristic prime to the order of the stabilisers. As a concrete application, we compute this group explicitly for every generalised quaternion group over an arbitrary field of characteristic 0, and settle Noether's problem over the rational numbers in the negative for those of order at least 16, thereby generalising a classical result of Serre. Over an algebraically closed field, our formula recovers and sharpens a theorem of Peyre; we further show that universal triviality of unramified cohomology in degree at most three is equivalent to its vanishing in the same degrees. Over the function field of a $p$-adic curve, we extend a result of Harari-Scheiderer-Szamuely. Over a finite field, the formula is effective and yields an algorithm for computing the group explicitly.

title: What Do Sound Event Embeddings Reveal? Auditing Speaker Leakage in Audio Representations
abstract: Pretrained audio embeddings are increasingly used as intermediate representations for sound event detection (SED) and other always-on acoustic sensing tasks. While these representations are selected for their utility on downstream tasks, they may also retain sensitive information unrelated to their intended purpose, creating privacy risks even when raw audio is not exposed. In this work, we present an empirical framework for auditing privacy leakage from pretrained audio embeddings using two complementary approaches. First, we quantify representation-level leakage by measuring statistical dependence between an audio embedding and a representation specialized for encoding sensitive information. Second, we measure attack-level leakage by training lightweight adversarial probes to recover sensitive attributes directly from the embedding. We apply this framework to four widely used audio representations (CLAP, PANNs, AST, and YAMNet) and evaluate leakage of speaker identity and gender. We found that speaker identification balanced accuracy ranges from $0.43$ to $0.72$, while gender information is also strongly recoverable. Moreover, representation-level and attack-based measurements exhibit consistent trends, with CLAP leaking the most and YAMNet leaking the lest speaker identity. These results demonstrate that intermediate audio representations are not inherently privacy-preserving interfaces and motivate privacy leakage as an explicit criterion, alongside downstream utility, when selecting representations for acoustic sensing systems.

title: Grower-in-the-loop AI for Deployable Precision Fertilisation in Sustainable Agriculture
abstract: In agriculture, typically over half of the applied nitrogen fertiliser is lost to water and to air. Precision fertilisation aims to reduce these losses while maintaining yield and quality, yet existing tools struggle to capture farm-specific challenges in determining optimal nitrogen rates. Static recommendations are common and overlook on-farm constraints, such as delays due to weather or machinery availability, or change in budgets. Each constraint governs when and how growers apply fertiliser in practice. Here we present a grower-in-the-loop framework for winter wheat in England, combining baseline fertilisation planning from a machine learning-derived nitrogen-response curve with in-season adaptation via a large language model. We evaluated the framework using data from long-term experiments (LTEs), replicated field trials, and farm deployments. Retrospective model validation using LTEs confirmed low economic decision-loss across multiple seasons. Using field and farm trials, baseline schedules were shown to match standard-practice yields with less nitrogen, whereas in-season adjusted schedules additionally retained grain quality standards. Given this enhanced performance, in-season adaptation absorbed weather, machinery and budget constraints to keep recommendations executable. The framework therefore shows promise for translating static recommendations into adaptable, grower-informed decisions for sustainable fertiliser management.

title: When Positivity Matters: Maximal Distance Integrals on Curves and Surfaces
abstract: How far apart, on average, can $n$ points in a set $A$ be? As $n\to\infty$ the answer is the $\textit{maximal energy}$ $M^{+}(A)$, the largest possible value of $\mathbb{E}|X-Y|$ when $X$ and $Y$ are independent random points of $A$ with a common distribution. If the distribution is allowed to carry negative mass, we obtain a second constant $M(A)\ge M^{+}(A)$. It is often far easier to compute: when a signed equilibrium measure exists, it is characterized by a $\textit{linear}$ potential equation, whereas the positive problem must also locate the support of the mass. This paper asks when positivity matters, that is, when $M^{+}(A)<M(A)$. For polygons and polyhedra the extremal mass sits on the vertices and closed forms abound. Even so, every hollow convex polygon has $M^{+}<M$, and a simple kite shows how a vertex can be forced out of the support. For smooth curves and surfaces the answer depends on the shape. Circles and spheres have $M^{+}=M$. The ellipse $x^2+4y^2=4$ has $M^{+}=M$ numerically, and we give its value to 50 digits. The ellipses $x^2+9y^2=9$ and $x^2+25y^2=25$ have $M^{+}<M$ numerically, with gaps in the support. For the ellipsoid $10x^2+15y^2+12z^2=15$, studied by Larcher, Schmid and Wolf, we compute 50 digits of $M$ and give strong numerical evidence that $M^{+}<M$. The extremal measure vanishes on two caps around the ends of the shortest axis. Proofs and numerical methods are collected in appendices.

title: Total curvature and area growth of entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space
abstract: We prove that entire minimal graphs in Heisenberg space $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ have infinite total curvature. Since their Gauss curvature is negative, this means that their intrinsic area growth is not quadratic, as conjectured by Pérez, Rodríguez and the author. It follows that vertical planes are the only orientable complete stable surfaces with constant mean curvature and quadratic area growth in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$, and this classification is extended to surfaces with critical and supercritical constant mean curvature in the homogeneous spaces $\mathbb{E}(κ,τ)$. We also prove that the height of an entire minimal graph in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ grows at most quadratically, as conjectured by Nelli and the author, whence the extrinsic and cylindrical area growths of such a graph are exactly cubic. Our arguments rely on the conformal Calabi-Lee duality between minimal graphs in $\mathrm{Nil}_3(τ)$ and spacelike graphs with constant mean curvature $τ$ in the Lorentz-Minkowski space $\mathbb{L}^3$, for which we also get sharp gradient estimates.

title: Revealing Geometry under Strong Noise: Spectral Embeddings and Clustering via Random Geometric Graphs
abstract: Modern massive datasets often contain useful low-dimensional nonlinear structures that are hidden by noise. Spectral embedding algorithms rely on meaningful local relationships between observations, but noise accumulated across many coordinates can make the observed distances unreliable. This also complicates clustering when groups have curved or concentric shapes and cannot be distinguished by their centers. In this paper, we develop a new method that denoises pairwise distances before using them to construct spectral embeddings and identify communities. Our approach uses cross-fitted projections to estimate distances between the underlying signals, selects a neighborhood radius from the observed sample, and builds a random geometric graph whose spectral coordinates represent the latent geometric structure. By connecting nearby points, such a geometric graph can distinguish different groups even when their centers coincide. A novel recursive procedure is then proposed to extract clusters from the graph using its spectral embeddings when such clusters exist. On the theoretical side, under a manifold model, we provide guarantees for our spectral embedding algorithm, which can be understood through the eigendecomposition of an integral operator associated with the underlying geometry. We show that the algorithm is robust to noise when the total noise energy is comparable to the total signal energy or, under additional conditions, exceeds it. To our knowledge, this is among the first spectral embedding algorithms that can handle such strong noise in datasets with nonlinear structures. In addition, our proposed clustering algorithm can recover the underlying clusters even when their centers coincide. Numerical studies demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed method in mitigating noise and revealing geometric structures for both spectral embedding and clustering.

title: Distill the Correction, Not the Rewrite: Hindsight Twins for Self-Improving Text-to-Image Models
abstract: Text-to-image models can learn from their own mistakes by distilling a self-teacher conditioned on a vision-language critic's revised prompt. However, such self-teachers barely improve alignment, and both they and their hindsight-contrast variants absorb the critic's unintended additions to the scene, such as lighting or scenery. We attribute this to two factors: (1) the prompt already specifies the desired fix, so a useful revision must go beyond the failed span, often rewriting the entire scene and adding details that overshadow the fix; (2) although the critic localizes the error to a single span, self-teachers condition on the rewrite, entangling the intended fix with unintended additions. Motivated by these insights, we propose Hindsight Twins (HinT), which fills the critic's revision template once with the intended fix and once with the observed error and distills only their velocity difference, anchored at the user's prompt. Because text encoders spread the edit of a single slot to all other tokens, HinT further aligns the twins' token states outside the slot. Across Qwen-Image-2512, SD3.5-M, and FLUX.2-klein, HinT keeps the rate of critic-induced bias at the base-model level while matching or exceeding the alignment gains of prior self-distillation, and it keeps improving over twelve rounds of self-training where contrastive baselines decay.

title: RoFE: Rotated Frozen Embeddings for Low-Data Multimodal Tabular Learning
abstract: Multimodal tabular learning combines tabular data with images and text, often in settings where labeled data are scarce. Tabular foundation models such as prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) offer a promising solution via in-context learning without task-specific training. However, modern image and text encoders produce embeddings with hundreds or thousands of dimensions, far exceeding the number of features encountered during PFN pretraining. Existing approaches bridge this gap using principal component analysis (PCA) to compress frozen embeddings. Surprisingly, we find that this PCA interface can underperform simple linear classifiers when labeled examples are scarce, even though PFNs are designed for small datasets. We identify the underlying failure mechanism: the PFN's per-column standardization removes the variances of the PCA scores. When the PCA keeps every direction of the labeled examples, the examples collapse into a regular simplex in which all pairwise distances are equal. To address this problem, we propose Rotated Frozen Embeddings (RoFE), a training-free method that rotates PCA scores before PFN inference. We theoretically show that rotation makes the column variances nearly equal, so that standardization approximately preserves the embedding geometry. Across image and text classification tasks, encoders, and tabular foundation models, RoFE improves low-data performance over the PCA interface and outperforms baselines that require task-specific training. The improvements also extend to regression.

title: Gradient formula from the sphere for perturbative RG flows near critical dimensions
abstract: We study the gradient property of perturbative renormalisation group flows in $d=d_c-\varepsilon$, with a potential and a metric regular at $\varepsilon=0$ up to logarithms of gauge couplings. We state properties of the renormalised functional with local couplings on the sphere $S^d$: finiteness, a local Weyl anomaly, the Ward identity of a conformal Killing vector, rotation properties and statements on the free theory. From them we derive a Ward identity without anomaly for a combination of the functional and its anomaly. Its first variation is a gradient formula whose symmetric metric contains the two-point function on the sphere and whose potential at fixed points is, in an extended form of the properties, proportional to the sphere free energy $\tilde F$ up to a constant. Sources of relevant operators enter through their Weyl variation, and in a scheme which we construct the gradient formula persists, with a nondegenerate metric if a matrix of the free theory is invertible. For multiscalar $ϕ^4$ theory and for scalars and Dirac fermions with Yukawa and quartic couplings in $d=4-\varepsilon$, for sextic scalars in $d=3-\varepsilon$ and for cubic scalars in $d=6-\varepsilon$, we derive all these properties from a finiteness hypothesis. The gradient formula then holds to all orders for the beta function defined on the sphere. For interacting gauge theories the properties remain assumptions.

title: Automatic Occupational Coding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Annually 1.9 million deaths and 89.7 million disability-adjusted life years are caused by exposure to agents during work (e.g., welding fumes, silica dust, and noise pollution). To improve worker health, high-quality exposure assessments are crucial. Therefore, free-text job descriptions from large-scale occupational cohorts are manually standardized through occupational classifications and linked to hazardous exposures using Job Exposure Matrices (JEM). However, manual coding is slow, unreliable (i.e., 44-89% inter-coder reliability), and costly, due to i) short, ambiguous free-text job descriptions, ii) classifications containing hundreds to thousands of categories, and iii) the absence of gold standards. With 46%-79% accuracy, state-of-the-art automatic occupational coding tools achieve classification performance on human level. However, their performance drops to 17-26% on out-of-distribution datasets. Furthermore, their supervised architectures limit them to occupational classifications present in the training set. Consequently, JEM using other classifications are incompatible, leaving vital exposure-response associations unexplored. Our Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework, OPERAG, enables classification into any occupational classification without expert-labelled databases. It retrieves coding index information and combines this with Large Language Model-based classification. Validated on AsiaLymph's 36,062 real-world job descriptions, OPERAG achieved 42.6% occupational classification accuracy on the 4th coding level, substantially outperforming existing tools and approaching human coders' 51-56% inter-coder reliability. Using two JEM named ALOHA+ and SHOCK, 89.9-98.6% accuracy was achieved on exposure assessment. OPERAG approaches human-level, universal occupational classification, enabling efficient and effective large-scale exposure assessment to improve worker health.

title: From Head to Tail: LLM-Augmented Sequential Recommendation and Trade-off Optimization
abstract: Recommender systems exhibit popularity bias, often under-serving long-tail and cold-start items with sparse interaction data. We propose a group-specific data augmentation approach that leverages LLMs to generate synthetic interactions, formulated as a constrained optimization problem, maximizing group-specific NDCG@20 and coverage while bounding overall NDCG@20 degradation within an acceptable threshold. Items are partitioned by interaction frequency to find the optimal augmentation strategy for each group. We further study combining the augmentation across groups simultaneously and find that while individual optimal strategies navigate the multi-group augmentation design, they are not simply additive. We further ablate on the LLM-based augmentation itself, comparing LLM scales, augmentation configuration under token constraints, finding that augmentation quality scales with contextual richness, albeit at a proportionally higher cost. Experiments with SASRec demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, achieving over 100% and 60% improvement in group-specific NDCG@20 for extreme and regular long-tail items, respectively, on our industrial dataset, and 40%, 25% for MovieLens-32M, while increasing their coverage without significant overall degradation.

title: ReWeave: Emergent Physical Task Topologies for Embodied Harness Optimization and Cross-Task Meta-Distillation
abstract: Long-horizon embodied tasks involve physical dependencies that may only become clear through interaction. As task understanding deepens, past trials can reveal new information for adaptation and transfer. However, coarse progress feedback cannot identify which physical preconditions held, leaving search unguided, while task-specific optimization easily overfits to individual scenes, making cross-task transfer brittle. We introduce ReWeave, a framework that jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction without updating policy weights. Keeping execution policies and perception frozen, ReWeave co-optimizes coupled context, workflows, and control loops. As new evidence revises the topology, ReWeave reprojects past trials onto the updated task understanding, exposing retained progress, regressions, and bottlenecks that guide parent selection and search width. Across tasks, matching verified local mechanisms to unmet preconditions consolidates 72 specialist units into 44 reusable groups ($0.34\times$ full concatenation) within a compact shared harness capable of continual learning. ReWeave improves held-out success from 89.00% to 98.75% on LIBERO-PRO and from 25.50% to 58.25% on RoboDojo, while uncovering retained progress in 89% of 159 failed RoboDojo development trials and translating stronger offline reasoning into higher online performance. On eight unseen LIBERO-PRO tasks, the shared harness reaches 51.3% success versus 41.3% for direct distillation, rising to 75.0% after continual learning.

title: Completing analytical conversion scheme among DH, Hayati, CPC and POE models for manipulator calibration
abstract: Building on Mooring's decomposition of the calibration procedure into four stages - modeling, measurement, identification, and correction - this paper investigates the role of analytical kinematic model conversion algorithms within the calibration framework and their potential to improve calibration performance. Four prominent and widely cited kinematic models: Denavit-Hartenberg (DH), Hayati (HAY), Complete and Parametrically Continuous (CPC), and Product of Exponentials (POE), - are considered. A systematic analysis of the existing conversion relationships reveals that, although most conversions among these models have already been established in the literature, a direct analytical conversion between POE and HAY, and CPC and HAY remains unavailable. Relying instead on a sequential combination of the existing POE-DH and DH-HAY conversions, for example, introduces several limitations. To address this gap, we develop a constructive analytical conversion between POE-HAY and HAY-CPC models based on Lie group theory, formally established through a set of lemmas and propositions. The proposed algorithms are illustrated using an RRRP SCARA robot and an RRHHHH Puma 560 manipulator. The direct POE-HAY conversion is compared with the sequential POE-DH-HAY approach, as well as HAY-CPC in terms of several relevant criteria, demonstrating the advantages of the proposed solution. Finally, we demonstrate the practical significance of the completed analytical conversion framework in an open-loop kinematic calibration experiment on an ABB IRB 1600 manipulator, using an API Radian EMSD3 Laser Tracker for measurements. The experimental results demonstrate that proper model selection combined with completed analytical conversion scheme directly improves calibration accuracy.

title: CAST: A Deployed Speech-to-Text Cascade for Closed Captioning of Entertainment Television
abstract: Despite rapid progress in automatic speech recognition (ASR), caption generation for long-form entertainment video remains challenging for content dense in music and effects, rich in accents, crosstalk, and noise. The transcript quality depends on segmentation and surrounding modules as much as the acoustic model. A single pass voice activity detection (VAD) can miss faint, low-energy voice while forwarding near-silent segments that induce hallucination and repetition in an autoregressive decoder. These competing errors motivate a hierarchical VAD that revisits rejected segments under semantic and acoustic retention checks. We present Captioning ASR Stack for Television (CAST), an integrated speech-to-text pipeline for closed captioning (CC) combining frozen Whisper large-v3 with segmentation, language identification, lyrics routing, and targeted hallucination detection and repair on a single NVIDIA L4 GPU. On 100 in-house assets spanning 60.46 hours, CAST reduces normalized WER from 6.99% to 5.36% and subtitle edit rate from 254.2 to 221.9 min/hour against the WhisperX pipeline, and improves deletion rate by 11% on public datasets. We also present the behavior of each stage in the pipeline. CAST entered the production speech-to-text (STT) stage of our CC pipeline in late August 2026; we report the evaluation evidence and path to full-scale operation.

title: DKnown-Jev-2: Article-Level Answer-Evidence Classification and Efficient Inference with a Pre-trained Language Model
abstract: Evidence selection in normative knowledge question answering requires determining whether a candidate article contains content that directly supports an answer under the applicable conditions of the question. We present DKnown-Jev-2, an article-level answer evidence classifier designed for evidence integration across multiple paragraphs. The model jointly encodes question conditions, article metadata, and paragraph content, and uses a pointer-style classification head to predict Answer Evidence (AE) and Non-answer Evidence (NE) in a single forward pass. Ona manually annotated test set of 972 evaluation instances, DKnown-Jev-2 achieves 91.77% accuracy and 91.28% macro-F1, outperforming Jev by 2.16 and 2.37 percentage points, respectively, while reducing both evidence misses and non-evidence false positives. The test set contains 317 multi-paragraph instances, with a maximum body length of 9,322 characters. Shared article encoding and non-autoregressive classification support low-latency inference. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for article-level evidence selection in normative knowledge question answering.

title: Dawn of the Gaia Era: Revisiting Cold Jupiters Orbiting M Dwarfs with Astrometry+Doppler Data Joint Analysis
abstract: We perform a joint analysis of ground-based radial velocities (RVs), Hipparcos Intermediate Astrometric Data, and two-epoch Gaia astrometry for known M dwarfs hosting cold Jupiters discovered through long-term spectroscopic monitoring. Among a sample of 25 planets in 19 systems, we derive robust absolute masses and orbital solutions for 13 planets in 11 systems with companion inclination uncertainties lower than 30 degrees. These include first mass measurements for five planets: GJ 328b, GJ 649b, GJ 849b and c, and GJ 9066c. We also reclassify one object, HIP 79431B, as a brown dwarf. We further compare the mass ratios of these 13 cold Jupiter systems with those of giant planets orbiting M stars characterized via transit, microlensing, and direct imaging. Without correcting for detection bias, we find that (1) there is likely a deficiency of high-mass-ratio hot Jupiters around M dwarfs compared with cold Jupiters, and (2) the local cold Jupiters orbiting M stars found by RV observations exhibit a similar mass ratio distribution as the counterparts in the Galactic bulge found by microlensing. Cold Jupiters orbiting stars with masses above $0.65~M_\odot$ tend to be more massive than those around M dwarfs. Our study establishes a sample of local cold Jupiters with precise mass determinations around M dwarfs, and reveal a tip of the iceberg in the upcoming Gaia DR4 and DR5.

title: Kushel--Tyaglov's problem, sharp Schoenberg-type inequalities and majorization relations between zeros and critical points
abstract: In this paper, we give a purely complex-analytic proof of Schoenberg's conjecture. We also determine the sharp constants in Schoenberg-type inequalities for every real exponent $p>0$ and every degree $n\ge2$, and characterize all corresponding extremal configurations. In particular, we confirm two conjectures posed in \cite{TZ25} and provide a complete solution to a problem of Kushel and Tyaglov. Furthermore, we introduce the tool of weighted weak majorization and establish, under the zero-centroid condition, new weak-majorization relations between the moduli of the critical points and those of the zeros. As consequences of these relations, we obtain refinements of several known results.

title: On the stress-bienergy tensor of conformal immersions and hypersurfaces
abstract: We study the stress-bienergy tensor $\bar S_2$ of a conformal immersion $ϕ:(M^m,\bar g)\to(N^n,h)$ with conformal factor $λ$, and we compute it, together with its trace and its divergence, in terms of $λ$ and of the second fundamental form of the associated isometric immersion. This gives a characterization of biconservative conformal immersions and, for hypersurfaces, we prove that $\mathrm{div}\,\bar S_2=0$ if and only if the tangent part of the bitension field vanishes. We introduce conformally biconservative hypersurfaces and show that a totally umbilical hypersurface of a space form is conformally biconservative with a non-constant conformal factor if and only if this factor is an isoparametric function satisfying an explicit ordinary differential equation. We illustrate this result with several examples, in which dimension four plays a special role. Finally, we study the equation $\bar S_2=0$: on a compact manifold of dimension $m\neq 4$, it forces the associated isometric immersion to be harmonic.

title: Sharp High-Dimensional Self-Normalized Central Limit Theorems
abstract: We study Gaussian approximation over all coordinate rectangles for coordinatewise self-normalized sums of iid centered random vectors. The Gaussian reference has the population correlation matrix, which may be singular. Under a fixed bound $K>1$ on the standardized marginal third absolute moments, uniform approximation over the corresponding moment class holds exactly when $d=o(\sqrt n)$ under arbitrary coordinate dependence. If $R_{jk}\le1-a$ for $j\ne k$ and a fixed $a\in(0,1]$, the necessary and sufficient condition becomes $\log d=o(n^{1/3})$. For marginal moment order $q\ge3$, we also allow the correlation gap $a_n$ to depend on $n$. For every fixed $0<β<1/3$, uniform approximation over the corresponding class in dimension $d_n=\lfloor e^{n^β}\rfloor$ holds if and only if $a_n\log n\to\infty$. Under arbitrary dependence, we determine the sharp error order $1\wedge\{d/n^{(q-2)/2}\}^{1/q}$ for every $q\ge3$ and $d\ge2$. At a fixed positive gap, we identify, for every $q>2$, the supremum of the decay exponents in uniform error bounds that allow fixed logarithmic factors. The proofs replace observations one at a time, keeping their contributions to both numerator and denominator in the same expansion. The resulting weights depend only on the retained sample, allowing the remainders to be controlled by marginal moments.

title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far from the primary the friction tracks the local DM density, which increases with spin. Near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning BHs $(a\gtrsim 0.37)$, however, frame dragging forces bound DM particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the DM density peaks. We show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. We also show that commonly used Chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. Our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling DM effects on EMRIs.

title: X-BQSR: Holistic Acceleration of Base Quality Recalibration for Scalable Genomic Analysis
abstract: With the continued decline in sequencing costs, genomics-based precision medicine is gaining increasing importance. The Genome Analysis Toolkit (GATK) is the standard framework for converting raw genomic data into actionable variants, but one of its most expensive steps is base quality score recalibration (BQSR), which corrects systematic sequencing errors. Despite significant work on accelerating other parts of the variant calling pipeline, BQSR has not been systematically explored on GPUs. In this work, we analyze BQSR to identify computational and I/O bottlenecks and show that simply offloading key stages to an accelerator is insufficient to achieve overall gains. We then present X-BQSR, a holistic redesign of the entire BQSR pipeline, including I/O, compression, and kernel execution, to better leverage GPU parallelism. We implement X-BQSR using portable SYCL kernels for NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel GPUs, along with native CUDA and HIP backends for comparison, and we evaluate its performance against previous FPGA work. Our evaluation shows up to 141.7x acceleration compared to standard GATK and 8.7x acceleration compared to a proprietary GPU-accelerated solution.

title: From Local Errors to System Failures: Modeling and Benchmarking Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
abstract: In multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs), errors can propagate through intermediate messages and compromise final answers. However, outcome-based evaluation obscures how agents amplify, attenuate, or correct these errors. We propose Response-Aware Error Propagation among Agents (REPA), a structural model that connects measured local responses to system-level error propagation. REPA separately estimates input assembly and agent processing across multiple error channels, while theoretical analysis relates local modeling errors to endpoint prediction error. Experiments span three Qwen base models, six MAS workflows, and ten knowledge and reasoning settings in ErrPropBench-10. REPA achieves a mean condition-level Spearman correlation of 0.84 across base models, compared with 0.47 for direct regression. Controlled experiments also demonstrate its utility for targeted recovery. REPA-guided retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves accuracy over no retrieval by an average of 19 percentage points with 16% additional tokens. By linking local agent behavior to system susceptibility, REPA provides an interpretable foundation for studying error propagation and developing targeted optimization in MAS.

title: A Comparison of Uncertainty in AI and Dynamical Climate Ensembles
abstract: Climate model ensembles and their uncertainty estimates are essential for evaluating risk and designing climate policy. Yet, in the assessment of newly developed AI climate models, evaluating uncertainty is often secondary to diagnosing mean-state climate biases and trends. In this work, we conduct the first systematic comparison of uncertainty representation in ensembles of state-of-the-art AI and dynamical atmospheric climate models. Examining 2-meter temperature, 500 hPa geopotential height, and precipitable water, we find that the AI ensemble exhibits reduced internal variability and model uncertainty across variables relative to the dynamical ensemble. We show that this dampened variability causes the AI ensemble to produce more limited climate extremes and yields underdispersion relative to ERA5. Under a uniform warming scenario, the AI ensemble shows increased model uncertainty. Dynamical models grapple with their own challenges, exhibiting stronger miscalibration (overdispersion) relative to ERA5 and larger climate biases than the AI models. As AI and dynamical climate models are mutually integrated into operational climate prediction, careful consideration of their differences in uncertainty representations is crucial for grounded assessment of climate risk.

title: Decoupling Solving from Abstention: Single-Rollout Conformal Risk Control for Hard-Budget LLM Reasoning
abstract: Hard token budgets often interrupt LLM reasoning before an answer is produced. Forcing reasoning to terminate recovers correct solutions but also increases confident errors, creating a joint challenge of solving within budget and deciding when to abstain. Existing remedies are costly or lack guarantees: supervised fine-tuning offers no error control, penalizing wrong answers during reinforcement learning (RL) can suppress exploration, and multi-sample conformal methods multiply inference cost. We propose Tail-CRC, a single-rollout framework that separates candidate generation from submission control. We first adapt the solver to budget forcing with pure binary correctness rewards; after freezing it, we apply conformal risk control to upper-tail token surprise in the answer span. Each rollout yields both an answer and an uncertainty score from token log probabilities, enabling finite-sample control of expected wrong submissions under exchangeability and recalibration across risk targets or domains without retraining. We show that wrong-answer penalties create failure-only comparisons in group-relative RL, derive an exploration-starvation boundary, and identify length-induced ranking reversals and single-token spike sensitivity in answer scores. Across Qwen3.5-4B and Qwen3-8B, 50 RL updates on 400 problems improve correct-submission rates by 15.0--29.6 points on DAPO and 4.3--12.8 points on out-of-domain Omni-MATH over inference-only budget forcing, while reducing generation cost by 3.5--12.6\%. On 8B Omni-MATH, target-domain calibration cuts wrong submissions from 30.3\% to 5.8\% at 4K and from 41.8\% to 6.5\% at 8K. At 4K, generation is 2.05$\times$ faster for 4B and 2.23$\times$ faster for 8B than unforced 8K decoding in local amortized batch time. Tail-CRC thus enables reliable, efficient budgeted reasoning from a single rollout.

title: Griffiths-Dwork Reduction For Smooth Hypersurfaces in Grassmannians
abstract: We give an explicit Griffiths-Dwork pole-order reduction algorithm for a smooth hypersurface $Z$ in a Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(k,n)$. Under two arithmetic conditions on $k,n$, and the degree of $Z$, the residue construction describes the Hodge filtration on the middle cohomology of the complement in terms of the Jacobian ring. We explicitly characterize the required cohomological vanishings. As applications, we compute group representations on the vanishing cohomology of two symmetric hyperplane sections of $\mathrm{Gr}(3,10)$ and deduce maximal Picard rank for their associated Debarre-Voisin fourfolds. We also compute a Picard-Fuchs equation for a pencil of symmetric Gushel-Mukai fivefolds.

title: $k$-ary Legendre pairs
abstract: We study $k$-ary Legendre pairs and derive arithmetic restrictions on their existence and balance. For an odd prime $p$, we determine the component sums of a $p$-ary Legendre pair and show that, after normalization, each component has fixed symbol composition. As a consequence, every $p$-ary Legendre pair of length $\ell$ yields a Butson Hadamard matrix $H(2p,2\ell+2)$. For ternary Legendre pairs we combine fixed-content necklaces, integral-PAF symmetries, exact half-frequency restrictions, compression-decompression, and PSD tests. These reductions lead to ternary Legendre pairs for every admissible length $\ell\le32$. We conjecture that ternary Legendre pairs exist for every admissible length.

title: UMAMI: A Multimodal Benchmark Dataset for Evidence-Grounded Dietary Decisions
abstract: Dietary decisions require identifying a food's nutrient content and considering individual dietary needs, but recognizing food from an image alone does not provide this information. Visually similar foods can have different nutrient profiles, so selecting the wrong food record can lead to incorrect decisions even when nutrient rules are applied correctly. Furthermore, satisfying nutrient constraints does not necessarily establish a food's relevance to a person's intake. Evaluating these challenges together requires connecting food images, nutrient records, and individual intake histories. To support this evaluation, we introduce UMAMI (Unified Multimodal Assessment of Meals and Intake), a multimodal dataset and benchmark linking independently collected food images with nutrient profiles and respondent health and intake records. Using this dataset, we construct three diagnostic tasks covering visual nutrient question answering, personalized food recommendation, and condition-aware food substitution. Paired instances and input controls examine how visual identity and respondent context affect decisions. Our experiments identify errors in both food-record selection and nutrient-rule application, while showing that higher rule compliance does not necessarily improve alignment with subsequent recorded intake. These findings highlight the need to evaluate how multimodal systems select and use structured evidence for dietary decisions. The dataset, code, and dashboard are available at https://umami-benchmark.github.io.

title: A hybrid effective field theory description of diffuse baryons
abstract: Galaxy feedback mechanisms that displace baryonic gas on large scales are a dominant uncertainty in many cosmological analyses. Measurements that directly probe the baryonic component, such as Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure (FRB DM) and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect, can therefore be used to place constraints on feedback and inform other analyses, such as weak lensing. Thus far, analytic methods to model the effects of feedback are either limited to large scales, missing the regime of high signal-to-noise, or have many parameters, weakening constraining power. We propose a Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT) approach, relying on the full gravitational displacement field computed in an $N$-body simulation. We account for feedback via a Lorentzian suppression with a single effective parameter, $c_f^2$. To describe the diffuse baryon field, we extend the arguments by Andrew et al. (arXiv:2604.25828), leveraging most baryons being in a diffuse state to reduce a full bias expansion to just the linear bias, $b_{1,d}^L$. With just these two parameters, we fit the diffuse gas power spectrum in most variants of the FLAMINGO suite of cosmological simulations at percent-level accuracy out to $k=1\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$ at redshift $z=0.5$ and $k=1.5\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$ at $z=1$. Further, by fitting the diffuse gas power spectrum including terms argued to be negligible, we show that their contribution is minimal. Applying this prescription for diffuse electron gas enables constraints on both cosmology and astrophysics without the need to marginalize over many unknown parameters.

title: A quasi-tree expansion for the two variable Bollobás--Riordan polynomial using a single basepoint
abstract: We give a quasi-tree expansion formula for the two variable Bollobás--Riordan polynomial of ribbon graphs that uses a single basepoint (a point on the boundary of the ribbon graph) as auxiliary datum.

title: Quantitative thick-fiber property
abstract: We introduce the quantitative thick-fiber property, an analogue of the Entov--Polterovich non-displaceable fiber theorem for maps whose coordinate functions need not Poisson commute. We prove that this property holds for closed symplectic manifolds admitting a suitable, not necessarily linear, functional on the space of continuous functions. Conversely, we establish an obstruction and show that the property fails for certain irrational symplectic four-tori and Kodaira--Thurston manifolds. These results reveal a new rigidity--flexibility distinction: whereas the Entov--Polterovich theorem gives a universal fiber-rigidity phenomenon, its quantitative counterpart holds on some closed symplectic manifolds and fails on others, thereby defining a new symplectic rigidity invariant. We also introduce the non-displaceability width of a continuous map, defined as the infimum of the radii for which a non-displaceable thick fiber exists, and use it to obtain quantitative obstructions to uniform approximation by maps with small Poisson brackets.

title: Planar Graphs Embed into Graphs with Treewidth $O(\log n /ε)$
abstract: We construct a stochastic embedding of $n$-vertex planar graphs into graphs of treewidth $O(\log n/ε)$ and expected distortion $1+ε$ for any parameter $ε\in (0,1)$. This result yields randomized polynomial-time approximation schemes (PTASes) for a broad class of connectivity problems on planar graphs, including the $k$-MST problem. The treewidth bound is asymptotically optimal and settles a conjecture of Chang, Cohen-Addad, Conroy, Le, Ma. Pilipczuk, and Mi. Pilipczuk (2025). The key idea is a new construction of a stochastic balanced cut of size $O(\log n/ε)$ and expected distortion $1+ε/\log n$ for every edge. We construct these cuts using the minimax principle, an approach that differs significantly from existing cut constructions based on a random clustering hierarchy. Our embedding extends to minor-free graphs using the Robertson-Seymour decomposition, giving the same treewidth bound. Using this decomposition, we obtain the first randomized PTASes for many connectivity problems in minor-free graphs, including the Steiner tree problem and its prize-collecting variant.

title: A locally conservative LDG method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem
abstract: This paper proposes and investigates a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) method for the evolutionary Navier-Stokes-Darcy coupled problem representing the interaction between incompressible flows and porous media flows through the Beavers-Joseph-Saffman interface conditions. A fully discrete numerical scheme has been proposed and analyzed employing backward Euler temporal discretization and a locally conservative LDG scheme for the space discretization. The well-posedness of the numerical scheme has been obtained under a small data condition. Optimal a priori error estimates have been proven in the energy norm, as well as the L2-norm for t>0. Numerical experiments ensure the efficiency of the theoretical results

title: Fifth-order KdV solitary waves in a nonlinear electrical transmission line
abstract: We report the controlled experimental observation of solitary waves governed by the fifth-order dispersion Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation. To achieve vanishing cubic dispersion, we use a mutual inductive coupling between nearest-neighbor inductors within a nonlinear electrical transmission line. We then experimentally characterize the resulting solitary waves through direct spatiotemporal measurements of the dispersion relation, its oscillatory tail profiles, amplitude-width scaling, and amplitude-velocity relation, finding good agreement with semi-analytical predictions. Collision experiments between two (co- or counter-propagating) solitary waves also show that their self-similar profile persists after interaction, up to a time shift. Dissipation effects are also quantified.

title: Rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
abstract: We introduce and classify rational extensions of the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process that are solvable by polynomials. These diffusions are closely related to exceptional Hermite polynomials and rational extensions of the quantum harmonic oscillator. We obtain explicit formulas for their transition densities, fundamental solutions and Green functions. We also show that each such diffusion can be constructed from killed Brownian motion by a finite sequence of Darboux transformations followed by a Doob $h$-transform. Finally, we derive an explicit formula for the connection polynomials in the generalized Mehler formula and use it to prove several conjectures concerning these polynomials.

title: AlphaDefect: Expert-Level AI for Slay the Spire 2
abstract: Slay the Spire 2 (STS2) is a single-player deck-building game that requires long-term planning under heavy randomness. We present AlphaDefect, an expert-level AI system for STS2: for each character, one network trained with proximal policy optimization (PPO) makes every decision of a run, in combat and outside it. At the highest difficulty, Ascension 10, on two versions of the game current in November 2026 and on test seeds not played in training, AlphaDefect wins 62-77% of runs across six characters with greedy play and 68-80% with test-time search, after 1.3 to 6.7 billion decisions of training per character; runs uploaded by human players of all levels are won 11-20% of the time at the same difficulty. The networks read the game as entity records that identify each card, relic and enemy through a learned embedding and attributes from the game data, together with consequences of public information computed by the engine. Ablations show how much the agent depends on this encoding: without these identities, the network did not win a single run, and without the computed consequences it won 8.3 points fewer. To our knowledge, AlphaDefect is the strongest publicly reported STS2 agent as of November 2026.

title: Underlying-event properties in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV measured with the ALICE detector at the LHC
abstract: This contribution reports measurements characterizing the underlying event at midrapidity in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV, based on LHC Run 3 data collected by ALICE. The charged-particle number and summed transverse-momentum densities are measured as a function of the leading-particle transverse momentum ($p_{\rm T}^{\rm leading}$) in the toward, transverse, and away regions, defined relative to the azimuthal direction of the leading charged particle. The particle densities in the transverse region are observed to increase steeply at low $p_{\rm T}^{\rm leading}$, followed by a plateau for $p_{\rm T}^{\rm leading}>5$ GeV/$c$. The results are compared with measurements at lower center-of-mass energies to illustrate the energy dependence of the underlying-event activity, and with predictions from PYTHIA 8 and EPOS4.

title: Physics-Informed Fusion-MIONet with IFENN: A Generalized Framework for Coupled Poroelasticity Problems
abstract: Complex, high-dimensional, large-scale poroelasticity simulations using traditional numerical solvers can be prohibitively expensive in terms of computational resources. We introduce an innovative framework for poroelasticity problems that integrates physics-informed machine learning (PI-ML) models with high-performance FEM solvers. This integration is achieved through the Integrated Finite Element Neural Network (IFENN) setup, which uses a staggered scheme between an FEM solver for mechanical equilibrium and a PI-ML model for fluid-flow predictions. We introduce a novel Physics-Informed Fusion-MIONet (PIF-MIONet) architecture, in which a fusion network encodes the outputs of the MIONet branches. The MIONet encodes different input functions, and the fusion network enables early interaction between the inputs, supporting generalization across multiple scenarios while adhering to the underlying physics of the poroelasticity problem. We study different examples, covering 2D and 3D domains and considering variable material properties and time discretizations. We test the models on unseen loading histories, demonstrating accuracy and generalizability across scenarios. For complex geometries and boundary conditions, we show that with both physics and data considered in the loss function, a PI-ML model can be trained using only 0.1\% of the training increments used for pure data-driven training. In addition, we expand the PIF-MIONet to incorporate a domain decomposition approach, which was found to be particularly useful when modeling flow over more complex geometries with more localized phenomena. For the first time, IFENN is implemented using the open-source multiphysics simulator GEOS for the FEM part, providing a path for the framework's application to industrial-scale simulations and complex multiphysics problems.

title: Wrist-Camera Video Diffusion as Generalizable Robot Policies
abstract: A generalist manipulation policy should perform new tasks, operate in unfamiliar scenes, and transfer skills across robot embodiments. We present Wrist Video Policy (WVP), a closed-loop manipulation framework that learns how manipulation unfolds through video prediction and recovers executable motion through geometric estimation. Our key idea is to represent robot motion through wrist-camera trajectories, which determine the corresponding end-effector poses through a fixed hand-eye transformation. We pair a video generator that predicts future wrist views with a pose estimator adapted from a pretrained 3D model to recover the corresponding camera trajectories. Model stitching maps the generator's predicted latents directly into the estimator's intermediate feature space, bypassing RGB decoding. This decomposition allows task knowledge to expand through broad human and robot video data while reusing geometric motion estimation across tasks and embodiments. The resulting pose estimator transfers across Franka Panda, PiPER-X, and Galaxea R1 Pro without further fine-tuning. Across tabletop and laundry-room settings, WVP generalizes to tasks ranging from precise grasping and inserting to handling deformable objects, achieving a success rate of over 50% in zero-shot out-of-distribution evaluations. Our project page is at https://wrist-video-policy.github.io.

title: Kaon-pair production with NNLO effects
abstract: The Monte Carlo framework McMule has been extended to support the processes $e^+\,e^-\to K^+\,K^-$ and $e^+\,e^-\to K^0\,\bar{K}^0$. Our results include NNLO initial-state QED corrections together with NLO mixed corrections. The latter are evaluated in the FsQED approach, using disperon QED. The implementation is fully differential and can be used with any kaon form factor. We present the total cross section for energies relevant to the CMD-3 experiment and observe very large corrections. For $e^+\,e^-\to K^+\,K^-$ we also present selected differential observables for energies around the $ϕ(1020)$ resonance.

title: Uniqueness of the Bryant Soliton via the Positive Mass Theorem
abstract: For all $n\ge 4$, we prove that every $n$-dimensional complete noncompact steady gradient Ricci soliton asymptotic to the cylinder $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ is, up to scaling, isometric to the Bryant soliton. Our proof combines the exponential Bryant asymptotics of Bamler-Lai with the positive mass theorem in all dimensions through a scalar curvature comparison.

title: ChiProgramBench: Can LLM Agents Rebuild Efficient Circuits from Pin-Level Experiments?
abstract: Understanding a system that can be run but not inspected is a core engineering skill: one designs experiments, forms hypotheses about hidden state and timing, discards those that observations refute, and finally builds a replacement that works and is efficient. To evaluate this capability of LLM agents in the hardware domain, we present ChiProgramBench, 18 tasks derived from open-source processors, accelerators, codecs, transforms, interconnects, and control circuits. Agents can only drive and read the pins of a hidden, stateful simulated reference, then submit a gate-level netlist made of public library cells. Agents work in two settings: black-box discovery gives only anonymized functional pins and the interfaces of fixed memories, while function-guided reconstruction adds the circuit's purpose and each pin's role. Hidden test cases compare outputs with the reference cycle by cycle; power, delay, and area earn credit relative to the reference only when every case passes. Across 432 trials of 6 LLM agent configurations, successful agents recover algorithms and numerical conventions, yet only 12.0% of black-box and 14.8% of function-guided trials pass every case. Function-guided reconstruction raises the mean functional score, the cycle-weighted share of passed cases, from 24.6% to 30.9%. Of the 58 fully passing designs, only three improve on the reference's combined power, area, and delay, so behavioral recovery and efficient implementation remain distinct challenges.

title: AI-Assisted Programming and Labor Demand
abstract: Generative AI has demonstrated human-level performance on technical work tasks, yet evidence on how these task-level capabilities are changing labor demand remains scarce. We study the firm-level adoption of GitHub Copilot, an AI coding assistant, across 5,414 multinational firms accounting for 38% of the U.S. programming workforce. To identify causal effects, we exploit a natural experiment generated by firms' predetermined software procurement cycles. Early AI-adopting firms hired more workers before the launch of GitHub Copilot and had larger, more technical, and older workforces. After one year, GitHub Copilot adoption reduces quarterly technical hiring by 29% among review-induced adopters, with no effect on separations, overall technical headcount, or vacancy duration. The hiring slowdown is concentrated in the subset of junior technical roles that involve the highest share of coding work. Overall, AI coding assistance causes firms to shift demand towards more experienced workers and roles that pair some coding with broader design responsibilities.

title: A Unified View of Operator Splitting and Interior-Point Methods
abstract: First-order splitting and interior-point methods offer contrasting computational trade-offs for convex conic quadratic programs, yet their linear systems look remarkably similar. We make this connection precise through the Moreau slack, an unconstrained variable from which multipliers and (ordinary) slacks satisfying exact or barrier-perturbed complementarity are recovered. The remaining feasibility equations define a unified residual whose roots are KKT points at zero barrier parameter and central-path points at positive barrier parameter. Applying splitting to this residual yields projection methods at zero barrier parameter and barrier splitting at positive parameter; Newton's method in the latter setting gives an implicit interior-point method. At fixed positive barrier parameter, matching the splitting metric to current barrier curvature equalises the primal variable corrections under the same regularisation and leaves a factor of two between the Moreau-slack corrections. With metrics frozen at a barrier solution, local analysis identifies when doubling improves (local) convergence and when the primal solve remains the bottleneck. Metric choices that simplify linear solves (eg make them diagonal) become Newton regularisations, exposing a shared convergence cost associated with computational convenience. Finally, a computable defect in the regularised Newton equations gives an accuracy-based criterion for reusing a splitting factorisation.

title: Marginal-Cost Clustering for Courier Dispatch: A Parallel Decomposition for Pickup and Delivery with Time Windows and Fleet Sizing
abstract: Courier dispatch poses a pickup and delivery problem with time windows in which requests are batched, windows are soft, couriers start where they are and take open routes, and a fixed dispatch charge makes fleet size a decision. We contribute to the cluster-first, route-second family a grouping criterion that scores a request by its marginal cost, the travel and lateness it adds to the route a courier already plans, rather than by its distance to a centroid, one point standing for a whole workload in space and time. The marginal cost instead knows where a courier is, when it becomes free and what it already carries. Each pass, we hold the marginal costs fixed while we solve one integer program that assigns every request to a courier and chooses which to open, then improve its solution by a descent that relocates and swaps requests between couriers. We then route each dispatched courier exactly. That subproblem is naturally a mixed-integer program, and we solve it by label setting over visited sets, which we prove optimal and cheap enough to run every pass. On instances we generate and on adapted Li & Lim benchmark batches, we beat the best of six published clustering rules by 29% as published and by 12% once those rules carry the same descent. Against an adaptive large neighbourhood search at matched wall-clock we are ahead on the generated instances and level on the benchmark, and we handle 1000 requests and 300 couriers in about a minute.

title: Optimization of Piezo Operation for Superconducting TESLA Cavities at EuXFEL
abstract: Superconducting cavities with high-Q factor require precise tuning to match the RF frequency, ensuring stable electromagnetic fields and minimizing RF power consumption. At the European XFEL (EuXFEL) accelerator, TESLA cavities are tuned using slow tuners (step motors) for coarse adjustments and fast tuners (piezoelectric actuators) for fine-tuning and compensating disturbances such as Lorentz Force Detuning (LFD). Piezo actuators, critical to this system, require high-voltage (up to 100V) and high-current (up to 1A) driving signals for effective LFD compensation. However, they are vulnerable to overvoltage, overcurrent, and overheating, and their protection is crucial since replacing damaged piezos in fully assembled modules is infeasible. Additionally, piezo-induced vibrations can affect the machine's stability. Optimizing piezo excitation, by reducing voltage, current, and current slope while ensuring effective LFD compensation, improves equally efficiency, reliability and machine stability. This paper explores the optimization of piezo excitation at EuXFEL, detailing methods and results applicable to other facilities with superconducting cavities as well.

title: Leading-order dynamical QED corrections to the thermodynamics of isospin-asymmetric QCD
abstract: We present a first lattice calculation of the leading-order effect of dynamical photons on the thermodynamics of QCD at nonzero isospin chemical potential $μ_I$, across the onset of charged-pion condensation. In QCD this onset is a second-order transition, which dynamical photons are expected, on general grounds, to drive first order. However, a direct simulation is not possible since unequal quark charges render the QCD+QED action complex at nonzero $μ_I$. We therefore expand the free energy density $f$ in the electromagnetic coupling $e$ around $e=0$, where the sign problem is absent. The leading-order expansion coefficient, $\partial^2 f/\partial e^2|_{e=0}$, is the convolution of the photon propagator with the electromagnetic current-current correlator, which we measure with a newly proposed planar source on existing (2+1)-flavor pure-QCD ensembles at nonzero $μ_I$ and pionic source $λ$. At physical quark masses and a single lattice spacing, after extrapolating to vanishing $λ$, we find that $\partial^2 f/\partial e^2|_{e=0}$ is, within errors, independent of $μ_I$ below the onset and rises sharply across it.

title: MAASAI: A Tool-Augmented Multi-Agent System for Astronomical Data Analysis
abstract: Modern astronomical workflows require the coordinated use of specialised software, scientific archives, heterogeneous data, and domain-specific knowledge. Advances in large language models and multimodal foundation models enable natural-language interaction with scientific data and tools. Realising this potential requires integrating these models with established scientific capabilities. We present MAASAI (Multi-agent Astronomy Assistant for Scientific Analysis and Inference), a modular multi-agent system combining foundation-model reasoning, retrieval-augmented knowledge, and specialised astronomical tools within a graph-based execution framework. MAASAI coordinates request preparation, planning, execution, and response synthesis via specialised workers. Its architecture supports native and external applications, artefact and provenance management, optional human approval, and configurable inference backends, including fully local deployment with open-weight models. Motivated by SKA-era data-analysis challenges, MAASAI is also designed to support other astronomical domains. We evaluate MAASAI through radio-image benchmarks, single- and multi-step workflow demonstrations, and literature-grounded reasoning. Compared with a commercial-model baseline, MAASAI improves macro-averaged F1 scores from 0.53 to 0.72 for extended/diffuse emission classification and from 0.37 to 0.88 for source morphology classification. Workflow demonstrations show the coordination of measurements, source extraction, archive queries, and catalogue processing. A 94-question literature benchmark yielded generally favourable automated assessments, with comparable ratings from a pilot expert evaluation of 59 answers. These results highlight how tool-augmented multi-agent systems extend foundation-model reasoning to specialised astronomical analyses through established scientific software.

title: Orthogonally Mixed Sign Coding with Progressive Residual Refinement for Transformer Weight Compression
abstract: LLM quantization reduces storage but often degrades predictive fidelity at low bit rates. We propose a training-free, CDF-free, Gaussian-CLT-motivated progressive residual-sign quantization framework that uses randomized orthogonal mixing to promote Gaussian-like residual distributions and improve sign based reconstruction of Transformer weights. Each stage independently normalizes residuals and analytically calibrates reconstruction, progressively recovering quantization errors. The framework enables flexible storage-fidelity trade-offs without learned codebooks, empirical CDFs, or trellis optimization. We evaluate GPT-2 Large and Llama-3-8B across attention and MLP projections. At five residual stages, joint quantization preserves near-baseline predictive fidelity, achieving perplexities of 32.16 and 12.73, compared with full-precision values of 29.89 and 11.07, respectively. Ablations further demonstrate that orthogonal mixing substantially improves reconstruction over identity-based sign coding, while activation-aware scaling improves output fidelity and reduced-precision statistics lower storage overhead with negligible perplexity degradation. Comparisons with conventional quantizers establish the method's progressive fidelity recovery and characterize its storage-quality and runtime trade-offs. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of orthogonally mixed residual-sign coding for flexible, training-free Transformer weight compression.

title: Revisiting Learning to Delegate: LLM Discovered Heuristics for Large-Scale Vehicle Routing
abstract: Efficient vehicle routing is critical to logistics and transportation, yet solving large-scale capacitated vehicle routing problems (CVRP) remains computationally challenging due to their combinatorial complexity. One approach to solve large-scale vehicle routing optimization is to identify promising subproblems and then optimize them using solvers. In this paper, we propose a framework of automatic heuristic design (AHD) in which a large language model (LLM) autonomously refines heuristics for selecting subproblems, enabling effective optimization of large-scale CVRP instances. Compared to prior approaches that train task-specific neural networks to select among heuristically constructed subproblems, our method discovers generalizable, interpretable LLM-generated heuristics to directly construct subproblems. Experiments show that our approach achieves comparable in-distribution performance while outperforming neural network-based policies on out-of-distribution instances with large-scale problems.

title: Harmonic functions near isolated subanalytic singularities: generalized horns and regular blow-up
abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a subanalytic set of dimension $d\ge 2$, closed near $0$, with an isolated singularity at $0$ and connected link, whose regular part carries the induced Riemannian metric. We study harmonic functions on $X\setminus\{0\}$ near $0$. (i) If $X$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, for the intrinsic metric, to a generalized horn $\{(z^γy,z):\ y\in L,\ z\ge 0\}$, with $γ\ge 1$ rational and $L$ compact, connected, subanalytic and analytic, then: - every bounded harmonic function extends continuously to $0$; - every positive harmonic function near $0$ can be written as $qG_X+u_b$, with $q\ge 0$, $u_b$ bounded and $G_X$ a fixed singular profile; - a Bôcher-type theorem holds: a positive harmonic function is either bounded or tends to $+\infty$, and two divergent ones have a nontrivial linear combination that extends continuously. The proof relies on a volume doubling and weak Poincaré condition on intrinsic balls away from $0$, invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms, which together with an annular connectedness condition implies a Harnack inequality on annuli; the decomposition then follows from a Picard-principle argument whose geometric input is the Harnack inequality on the links. (ii) If $d\ge 3$ and the spherical blow-up of $X$ at $0$ is a regular manifold with boundary parametrizing $X$ near $0$ (condition (R) of the paper), the singular profile has a polyhomogeneous expansion, which is described and may contain a $\logρ$ term, $ρ=|x|$. (iii) For the rotational cusps $|x|^2=z^m$, $m>2$, $d\ge 3$, whose spherical blow-up is not regular, the profile is radial of order $ρ^{1-m(d-1)/2}$, so that its exponent depends on the rate at which the sections shrink.

title: A Systematic Method of GPU Verification on Subsystem Modelling
abstract: ARM Fast Model is a software modelling system for simulating multiple systems IPs integrated in a subsystem. Fast Model allows customer to run whole software stack as early as system IPs' specification is just ready. In this paper, we talk about a systematic method to enable GPU modelling and make whole system software stacks executable for both CPU and GPU in the integrated modelling environment, and eventually the major GPU IP can be verified. With our solution, we can directly run commercial benchmarks like Antutu and GFX Bench in Android target system with underlying ARM Fast Model mobile subsystem support. This was unbelievable in the past due to 3D rendering simulation for GPU verification is very slow. We also introduce some special techniques to improve performance. Eventually the whole software stack can directly work on real hardware without any changes as soon as the first tape-out is ready.

title: Quantum and classical transport in the underscreened Kondo lattice
abstract: We investigate quantum effects in high-spin Kondo-lattice transport as resistivity approaches the classical spin-disorder limit. Using dynamical mean-field theory and the numerical renormalization group, we calculate resistivity, the Seebeck coefficient, and optical conductivity for the paramagnetic single-channel Kondo lattice away from half filling. At intermediate temperatures, the resistivity for large local spin $S$ approaches the double-exchange plateau. Thermopower retains a positive quantum excess even where resistivity is nearly classical. The excess arises from the transport kernel's particle-hole asymmetry. Even the full Kelvin approximation, often accurate for incoherent correlated metals, captures only part of it. Incomplete Kondo screening leaves residual moments and leads to singular Fermi-liquid behavior at low temperatures. For $S=1$, the apparent power-law resistivity is consistent with a $1/\ln^2(T_ρ/T)$ asymptote. Above the Kondo scale $T_K$, weak-coupling resistivity follows $1/\ln^2(T/T_K)$. Above the band and exchange scales, the charge susceptibility decreases as $1/T$, while the effective diffusion constant becomes nearly temperature independent, resulting in linear resistivity. A many-body coherent-potential approximation accounts for the spin dependence of the linear coefficient without adjustable parameters.

title: Unlocking the Power of Loops in Pretrained LLMs with Loop Residuals
abstract: Looped Transformers iterate a shared block of layers to increase computation without adding parameters, offering stronger performance and test-time scaling. However, this power has so far required training from scratch and yielded only modest gains for LLMs. Finetuning existing models into loops is far cheaper, yet also brings only marginal gains over SFT. We propose LoopRes, an effective, scalable, and simple approach that turns loops into significant and consistent gains for pretrained LLMs. Building on Attention Residuals, LoopRes lets each looped layer attend directly to the outputs of earlier loops. Since these outputs are iterates of the same layers and become harder to tell apart, we give each a trainable loop-aware key that encodes its structural identity. Attending to all earlier loops also lets layers skip intermediate ones, so we restrict each layer to a residual window of the latest W loops, forcing every loop to build incrementally on recent ones. Across 6 pretrained LLMs from 3 model families and 9 benchmarks, LoopRes delivers significant and consistent gains: at 2x compute, it improves Qwen3-1.7B-Base by 29.1% over SFT, more than doubling the gain of the state-of-the-art baseline. The gains hold on larger models up to 30B and across all three families. More importantly, from 1.7B to 8B, LoopRes scales more steeply than SFT as compute grows, reaching a higher ceiling while needing less compute on long outputs. These results establish LoopRes as an effective looping approach, delivering both better performance and better test-time scaling.

title: Tradeoffs between objective outcomes and human enjoyment of work in human-AI task allocation
abstract: For people, tasks at work are defined by more than their outcome: they are colored by the experience of engaging in that task. As AI systems become increasingly capable of performing human-level work they may be deployed to tasks that people find enjoyable while simultaneously creating comparatively more aversive tasks such as monitoring AI outputs.
