Combined with a frozen, separately pre-trained generator, a temperature curriculum for hard negatives and a 512-to-8192 length curriculum, we train two compact encoders: EdgeCoder-31M, an 8-layer English model, and EdgeCoder-Multilingual-61M, a 16-layer model covering 46 languages, each on about 1T tokens. They reach 86.0 and 85.1 on GLUE. The English model outperforms Ettin-Enc-32m (83.5) and MiniLM-L12 (84.6) on GLUE while matching them on MTEB English v2 (51.1), and the multilingual model outperforms the 2.3x larger mmBERT-small on GLUE and Multilingual MiniLM and mDistilBERT on XTREME over the languages it covers. We also describe FlashDeBERTa, our open-source fused implementation of DeBERTa's disentangled attention that stores no $n \times n$ score matrix: at 4096 tokens it is 10x faster and uses 93% less memory than the reference implementation, and it loads existing DeBERTa checkpoints unchanged.

title: Reading Between the Layers: Where Representation Quality Lives, and What Geometry Reveals
abstract: Representation quality in pretrained text foundation models is not concentrated at the final layer, yet practitioners routinely probe it there because layer selection without labels has remained an open problem. We present a large-scale empirical study of where layer quality lives across 25 models spanning four architectural families and four pretraining strategies, evaluated on 13 datasets across classification, pair classification, semantic textual similarity, and multiple-choice question answering. Peak probing layers depend systematically on pretraining strategy and architecture: masked encoders peak in late-middle layers, sequence-to-sequence models shift their peak with task type, contrastive sentence encoders concentrate signal at the final layer under CLS and last-token readouts but peak early under mean pooling, and decoder-only models exhibit distinct phase structure tied to depth. We distill these findings into the Stable Geometry Index (SGI), a closed-form, fully label-free selector with no fitted coefficients combining power-law fit quality, effective-rank capacity, spectral stability, and a weak depth prior. Across 383 evaluation groups SGI improves over the last-layer baseline and lifts Hit@3 from 0.39 to 0.52, recovering 40% of the gap to the oracle without using any labels, and exceeds a supervised ELMo-style layer mix on the matched subset despite using strictly less information. Our ablations also reverse a common assumption in the spectral-decay literature: power-law fit quality is a stronger predictor of layer quality than the exponent's proximity to one.

title: Dispersive estimates for limit-periodic Schrödinger operators
abstract: We prove dispersive estimates for limit-periodic operators that are super-exponentially well-approximated by periodic operators. The key ingredient is a sharp enhanced convexity statement for the density of states of periodic Jacobi matrices. This statement implies log-convexity of the density of states and hence is a strengthening of existing results on the convexity of equilibrium measures. We expect that it will be of interest and use outside of this work. We also construct almost-periodic discrete Schrödinger operators with purely singular continuous spectrum whose unitary groups enjoy recurrent dispersive motion: on one subsequence of time scales, the unitary group has a dispersive estimate at a rate as close to the free rate as one desires, while on another set of time scales, the unitary group is as far from dispersive as possible. In fact, this behavior is generic within the class of limit-periodic operators.

title: XRL4T1D: A Post-hoc Explainability Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Type 1 Diabetes Management
abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) requires lifelong insulin therapy, and reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for automated dosing in the UVA/Padova simulator. However, the decisions of RL controllers remain difficult to interpret. We present XRL4T1D, a post-hoc explainability framework for evaluating pretrained insulin-dosing policies without retraining. Each policy uses 60 minutes of continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and administered-insulin history, sampled every 5 minutes, to recommend insulin. We use SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to compare the importance of CGM and insulin-history inputs and summarize insulin-history attributions over three 20-minute windows motivated by insulin-on-board. We assess whether these attributions correspond to policy-output sensitivity through targeted input replacement and compare temporal rankings with TimeSHAP. In all 80 patient-policy-mask-size cases, replacing the highest-attribution inputs changes the normalized insulin recommendation more than replacing the lowest-attribution or random inputs. The highest-attribution insulin-history window is also the most output-sensitive in 115 of 120 patient-policy-scenario configurations, and KernelSHAP and TimeSHAP select the same top window in 111 of 120. Applying XRL4T1D to PPO and G2P2C across 20 virtual patients, we find that both controllers rely predominantly on CGM history, especially G2P2C. However, the distribution of insulin-history importance across recent, middle, and older windows varies by cohort, explainer, and analysis settings, without a consistent separation between controllers. Global feature-attribution rankings remain stable under the tested observation corruptions. These results show why attribution fidelity, temporal reproducibility, and controller-comparison robustness should be assessed separately.

title: Measuring Counterfactual Credit in a Replayable Wildfire-Suppression Benchmark
abstract: In cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, learned critics are usually evaluated by how well they predict the team's return. Yet predicting a team's return and assigning credit to individual actions are distinct tasks. To test credit directly, we introduce FLARE (Fireline Learning Agents in a Replayable Environment), a stochastic wildfire suppression benchmark in which any moment of a fire can be replayed with different actions under the same random events. Replaying one step measures the immediate effect of each agent's suppression, which we call simulator credit and use for training. Replaying to the end of the episode measures the effect of each action, which we use for grading critics. In a comparison over eight seeds with multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO), simulator credit reduces the interquartile mean burn score (each cell's burning time, capped and averaged over the map; lower is better) from 26.6% with shared reward to 20.9%. Learned credit from a centralized COMA-style critic does no better than the shared reward. Four trained critics predict the team's return well, yet the credit they assign is 9 to 42 times larger than the credit measured by replay. The critics also give heterogeneous agents nearly identical action rankings. These results show that a good fit to the team's return is a weak test of a critic's credit.

title: Airy Path Integral Representation for the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation
abstract: We give a representation for solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation as path integrals over the Airy line ensemble. The initial condition enters directly as a potential, bypassing the usual direct and inverse scattering constructions. We establish the representation for broad classes of signed initial data, prove uniqueness in specified solution classes, and derive a restart identity expressing solutions as Airy path integrals of their own earlier states. For arbitrary real $L^2$ initial data, a centered version of the Airy occupation represents the standard global KP-II flow. We show how the representation recovers the classical Marchenko determinant for Korteweg-de Vries (KdV), and identify a Brownian-path amplitude with the classical KP-II heat-scattering coefficient. We obtain explicit formulas for soliton solutions and derive KP from a Toda equation for nonintersecting Brownian bridges. Finally, we use the restart identity to characterize one-point distributions of the KPZ fixed point through their singular initial conditions, and derive sharp lower-tail asymptotics directly from KP.

title: Dijet photoproduction in ep and eA collision in POWHEG
abstract: We present the implementation of dijet photoproduction in electron-proton and electron-nucleus collisions in the POWHEG BOX V2 Monte Carlo event generator. The process is computed at next-to-leading order in QCD including both direct and resolved photon contributions and is consistently matched to parton showers using the POWHEG method. The implementation is validated by using POWHEG BOX V2 internal consistency checks as well as by comparing fixed-order results with SHERPA. We compare our predictions to dijet photoproduction data from DESY HERA I and II, finding good agreement within theoretical uncertainties, and provide predictions for both electron-proton and electron-gold collisions at the upcoming BNL EIC, illustrating its potential to further constrain both photon and nuclear parton distribution functions.

title: Imaging Compressible and Incompressible Kinetic Energy of a 2d Bose-Einstein Condensate
abstract: We introduce a method based on velocity-sensitive two-photon transitions to reconstruct the two-dimensional velocity field as well as the local atomic density of a Bose-Einstein condensate in a single realization. We quantitatively benchmark the method on a quantized vortex. Applied to a condensate far from equilibrium, the method reveals the contrasting behaviors of the system's flow kinetic energy components, where the compressible component quickly decays while the incompressible one remains, dominating the long-time dynamics.

title: Translation Method Bounds for 3D Isotropic Conductivity--Shear Modulus and the Search for Attaining Microstructures
abstract: We compute conductivity--shear-modulus cross-property bounds in three-dimensional isotropic two-phase composites using the translation method, and obtain the tightest bounds reported to date. To assess attainability, we perform unit-cell topology optimization on thousands of distinct initial structures and compare optimized designs to the isotropic bounds using an effective-medium approximation that models the macroscopic material as an isotropic assembly of randomly oriented grains. The best jointly performing designs are consistently bicontinuous, triply periodic minimal surface-like microstructures; however, a small but notable gap to the translation bound remains.

title: Strong Co-O exchange interaction in $P4/nmm$ KCoO$_2$ and its effect on spin wave and Néel temperature
abstract: The exchange interactions of a classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian in KCoO$_2$ in the $P4/nnm$ structure are calculated using a linear response approach, derived from the transverse spin susceptibility, integrated over atomic spheres using a projector proportional the local magnetization and including all atoms as magnetic atoms. The exchange interaction between Co and its apical O is found to be by far the largest interaction and ferromagnetic. Its effect on the Néel temperature and the spin wave spectrum are evaluated. The Co-O exchange is found to strongly enhance the critical temperature in the mean field approximation but not in the random phase approximation.

title: Topological Inference for degree-Cech complexes
abstract: We study topological inference for the degree-Cech bifiltration from noisy samples of a manifold. Under a model combining uniform sampling on the manifold with uniform noise, we show that suitable choices of the radius and degree parameters recover the homotopy type of the underlying manifold with high probability. The analysis explains how the degree parameter suppresses sufficiently distant outliers while the radius scale captures topological signals. Our results provide theoretical support for the common intuition that degree bifiltrations carry meaningful topological information in the presence of noise.

title: HyMTS: A Multiscale Tensor Factorization-Based Network for Hyperspectral Image Restoration
abstract: Hyperspectral image (HSI) restoration has been explored using deep learning techniques recently. Because hyperspectral images have strong spectral and spatial redundancy, the underlying clean signal is usually represented in a low-dimensional spectral subspace and locally low-rank spatial structures. Existing methods primarily explore dense attention or feature mixing across spectral bands. In this work, we propose HyMTS, a hyperspectral restoration network with a backbone built on the Multi-scale Tensorial Summation (MTS) factorization operator. HyMTS provides a natural architectural mechanism for exploiting a low-rank prior, embedded directly in the network operator rather than imposed via an auxiliary loss or a constraint on the reconstructed output. Specifically, HyMTS stacks a unified block that couples factorized layers with input-adaptive layers, capturing both local and global dependencies across the spectral and spatial dimensions. Extensive experiments without auxiliary data on standard benchmarks for Gaussian and real-noise denoising and single-image super-resolution show that HyMTS efficiently achieves superior or comparable performance to various state-of-the-art approaches.

title: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
abstract: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, χ_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, André, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

title: An easy proof of transience of one-dimensional Rademacher walk with power weights
abstract: Using a version of a local limit theorem, we provide an easy proof that the Rademacher random walk with step sizes $n^α$, $α>1/2$, is transient.

title: TokenJoule: Energy Modeling for Distributed Training and Inference of LLMs
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) scale, energy dictates operating cost, cooling, and cluster capacity across training and inference. Early hardware design-space exploration (DSE) requires predicting energy before silicon exists, yet performance models miss hidden component work while prior energy predictors calibrate to deployed GPUs. We present TokenJoule, an open-source analytical tool that derives device kernel sequences, tiled compute, shared-memory staging, cache residency, and collective traffic, pricing activity directly with component energies. With zero workload fitting, TokenJoule achieves 3.3-6.6% activity error (151 A100/H100 runs) and 3.0-6.8% A100 energy error, guiding parallelism, memory packaging, and 3D-DRAM chip co-design.

title: Partition growth homomorphisms on Specht modules
abstract: There is a unique (up to scalar) representation homomorphism between the Specht modules $\mathcal{S}^λ$ and $\mathcal{S}^μ$ when $μ$ is obtained from $λ$ by adding one to a part of $λ$. We find explicit formulas for these homomorphisms in the Specht polynomial bases of $\mathcal{S}^λ$ and $\mathcal{S}^μ$. Furthermore, given two representation homomorphisms corresponding to adding one to two different parts of $λ$, we find the commutator for the composition of these two homomorphisms. We also extend the Specht polynomial basis of $\mathcal{S}^λ$ into a basis of the permutation module $\mathcal{H}^λ$ and explicitly find a formula for the skew isomorphism from $\mathcal{S}^λ$ to $\mathcal{S}^{λ'}$.

title: Near-Zero Forgetting Is Not Enough: Out-of-Distribution Robustness in Continual Learning of Pretrained VLAs
abstract: Recent work shows that pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit near-zero forgetting in specific continual learning settings with experience replay. However, robustness to domain shift of learned tasks remains unexplored. In this work, we study the robustness of Pi0 fine-tuned with experience replay under out-of-distribution (OOD) data using the LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks. While the in-domain (ID) setup achieves near-zero catastrophic forgetting, OOD performance on previous tasks quickly collapses. Specifically, we show that during the continual learning process, the OOD capabilities of the model degrade, following a shared representational pattern across domain shifts, which is also visible behaviorally in the two simpler suites. Representational analysis shows that drift concentrates in the multimodal and action features. Linear probes indicate that OOD features still retain task-relevant information, but appear unreadable, consistent with representation misalignment. These findings suggest that even when ID stability remains intact, severe OOD forgetting can still occur, accompanied by representational drift during continual learning.

title: Electrical Degradation of Vertical $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky Barrier Diodes Under Au-Ion Irradiation to a Fluence of $1.3 \times 10^7$ cm$^{-2}$
abstract: The electrical degradation and time-dependent current behavior of vertical $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) subjected to energetic Au-ion irradiation were systematically investigated. Two successive irradiation exposures were conducted under a constant reverse bias of $-100$ V to evaluate the effects of heavy-ion irradiation on device performance and transient current response. Following irradiation, the devices exhibited degraded forward conduction, increased specific on-resistance, enhanced reverse leakage current, and reduced apparent carrier concentration. During irradiation, pronounced increases in leakage current and transient current spikes were observed. Following each beam termination, the leakage current exhibited an initial rapid decay followed by a slower relaxation process. Single-exponential fitting identified distinct fast and slow relaxation components, while a double-exponential model provided a more comprehensive description of the overall current decay. After the second irradiation exposure, the characteristic time constants of the fast and slow relaxation processes increased from 33.50 to 40.64 s and from 190.35 to 282.29 s, respectively, indicating prolonged recovery dynamics under repeated irradiation. A charge-trapping-based model is proposed to explain the irradiation-induced current enhancement and subsequent fast and slow relaxation processes through modulation and gradual recovery of the effective Schottky tunneling barrier. These findings provide insights into the relationship between heavy-ion-induced electrical degradation and time-dependent current relaxation in $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ SBDs.

title: How to build and train your recurrent-depth model: A fixed-point perspective
abstract: Recurrent-depth models are trained with truncated backpropagation, yet it remains unclear why this works. We show that input injection, commonly used in recurrent-depth models, is exactly Halpern iteration, and that a slowly vanishing stepsize provably converges with a backpropagation window polylogarithmic in the depth. The guarantees require a Lipschitz operator, which for SwiGLU leads to a weight constraint in both row and spectral norm, while only a row norm constraint for gates. Based on these constraints, we develop an optimizer tailored to each parameter group, Sparrow, which provides a drop-in replacement of Muon/MuonH with no overhead, that speeds up training even beyond recurrent models.

title: Blueprint for DOE Quantum Supercomputing
abstract: Quantum computing stands at the threshold of a transformative decade, where the field will evolve from small-scale demonstrations toward practical scientific computing at scale. This Blueprint identifies fault-tolerant quantum computers (FTQCs) as a viable, scalable, and broadly applicable path to achieving "quantum scientific utility." It outlines a strategy to prepare the US Department of Energy (DOE) for FTQCs and their integration into the US national scientific computing infrastructure. Its purpose is to identify the steps, milestones, and research directions necessary for DOE to enable initial deployment of FTQCs in 2028 as a scientific tool for the nation and mature this capability into the 2030s. Given recent demonstrations of logical operations on error-corrected logical qubits and the advancement of commercial hardware roadmaps, DOE should begin preparations for large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computing deployment for DOE science missions. This Blueprint proposes that DOE focus on (1) deploying first-generation scientifically relevant quantum computers with at least 100 logical qubits and performing at least 10,000 to 100,000 hard logical operations in scientifically relevant calculations; (2) developing essential FTQC programming competencies, system software, and facility readiness; and (3) investing in cutting-edge focused R&D that fosters breakthroughs in scientific applications, algorithms, and logical architectures needed to accelerate the advent of scientific utility. This effort will position DOE to transition to larger systems: production-scale quantum computers that comprise 1,000 to 10,000 logical qubits, perform 1 to 10 billion hard logical operations, and execute scientifically useful computations at scale. The Blueprint calls for transformative R&D and collective action to accelerate the advent of scientific quantum utility and bring it within reach by 2028.

title: Synthetic Augmentation for Data-Scarce Object Detection: Allocation, Dose, and Filtering Across Six Datasets
abstract: Robotic perception for capturing uncooperative orbital objects and inspecting variable industrial products must often operate with limited labelled imagery. We examine a modular synthetic-augmentation pipeline, evaluating generation planning and post-generation filtering as separate interventions, with computational cost as a design constraint. Across six object-detection datasets, FLUX.1-Fill with class-specific LoRA adaptation produced dataset-dependent dose effects; the validation-selected augmentation improved mAP@50:95 on four datasets and reduced it on two. Filtering did not yield consistent gains, and FID, KID, precision, recall, and LPIPS did not consistently track detector changes. The results do not establish that image quality alone identifies useful samples. They motivate standardised evaluation and inexpensive candidate-utility measures that could identify useful samples before detector retraining, reducing repeated training cost.

title: InitFree-SfM: When Initialization-Free Bundle Adjustment meets Learned Structure-from-Motion
abstract: Initialization-free bundle adjustment (InitFree BA) aims to jointly recover camera poses and scene structure without requiring an initial global estimate. It is a very challenging problem, especially compared to traditional BA where a good estimation is assumed. While recent methods optimize surrogate Object Space Error (OSE) objectives from random initialization, a low objective value does not necessarily yield an accurate reconstruction, revealing a gap between optimization and reconstruction. We show that existing InitFree BA pipelines struggle to produce accurate 3D reconstructions on modern SfM benchmarks, and demonstrate that incorporating learned metric depth substantially improves their practical feasibility. We introduce InitFree-SfM, a complete initialization-free SfM pipeline combining learned correspondences, metric depth, depth-consistent track construction, and joint metric refinement. Within this framework, we propose a simple depth-augmented OSE (dOSE), which complements the directional constraints of OSE by constraining landmark positions along their viewing rays. Our approach substantially outperforms existing InitFree BA methods and achieves competitive accuracy with established SfM pipelines, including on challenging low-overlap image collections. Importantly, our analysis challenges the prevailing emphasis on surrogate objectives in previous InitFree BA research, revealing that geometric constraints play a central role in accurate reconstruction, while OSE-based optimization provides further improvements.

title: Optimal Signaling Mechanisms for One-round Matching Markets
abstract: Signaling mechanisms are used in various types of matching markets so that applicants may credibly signal interest in firms. They have been observed to improve outcomes in job markets and dating markets, and proven to improve outcomes in several stylized theoretical models. In this paper we develop optimal signaling mechanisms for a simple one-round matching market consisting of $n$ applicants and $n$ firms. We consider a much richer space of signals than have been used previously, in theory or practice, and also consider randomized signaling mechanisms, which have not been systematically studied. For each $k \geq 1$, we determine the optimal deterministic and randomized signaling mechanisms in which applicants signal $k$ firms. In the limit as $k\to \infty$, our deterministic mechanism guarantees that in expectation, $\approx 75.4504\%$ of the applicants receive job offers, and this is optimal. Likewise, for $k \to \infty$, our randomized mechanism guarantees that $\approx 78.197\%$ of the applicants receive offers, which is also optimal. The optimal $k$-signal randomized mechanism is non-constructive, and has a rather complex description. We describe some simple randomized signaling mechanisms whose efficiency surpasses that of the limiting optimal deterministic mechanism. Finally, we also discuss incentive-compatibility for the firms to follow the mechanism.

title: Burning the Bridge: Agentification and Domestic Value Added
abstract: Firms that replace local work with foreign AI agents can produce more per paid hour while generating less income at home. We study this trade-off in a small open economy where exporters and local services both use agents. Once wages reach a reservation floor, extending agent use in local services lowers domestic income at unchanged foreign costs. Value added at constant prices and consumption also fall if suppliers capture enough of the saving. Exporters have an offset: adopting agents can expand production and earn the foreign exchange needed to pay for them. The difference is substantial. Using Brazilian accounts as a reference, a supplier bargaining share above about 0.15 is sufficient to make further local-service adoption reduce value added even at negligible foreign costs. The corresponding threshold in tradables is about 0.66. We derive separate export-growth requirements for preserving income and consumption and illustrate them using historical accounts for Brazil and Mexico. Cheaper agents ease the consumption requirement; lower export prices raise it. Over time, declining domestic capabilities can also make returning to local production more expensive, allowing suppliers to charge more at renewal.

title: Excess noise and electron-phonon energy transfer in Au wires: Length and temperature effects
abstract: As a mesoscopic diffusive wire at low temperatures is driven out of equilibrium by a current, excess noise is observed compared to the equilibrium Johnson-Nyquist fluctuations. The expected form of the excess noise varies depending on the relative rates of wire traversal, electron-electron inelastic energy transfer, and electron-phonon inelastic energy transfer. We measure noise as a function of bias current in diffusive Au nanowires on SiO2/Si with lengths ranging from sub-μm to 30 μm and temperatures from 3 K to 50 K, to map out the interplay between charge shot noise and the crossover to electron self-heating and phonon-dominated noise suppression. As expected qualitatively, shot noise is suppressed with increasing wire length and substrate temperature, as electron-phonon scattering is of increasing importance. In long wires, the simple model of electron-phonon energy loss known to be quantitatively effective below a few Kelvin underpredicts the excess noise in the high bias, high temperature limit. This issue is more severe in wires on SiO2/Si than on bare Si, implying that interfacial thermal conduction must be considered in the thermal path even at comparatively high temperatures.

title: Your Codec, Your Generator: Idempotent Generative Compression without Retraining
abstract: We introduce an image compression framework with three properties: (i) adaptation of pretrained codecs without retraining or fine-tuning, (ii) cycle-consistent recompression, even of already-encoded images, and (iii) decoding with independently chosen generative priors. We wrap the frozen encoder with non-learned operations so that every continuous latent has a preimage, yielding a surjective pseudo-invertible neural network. A nonlinear right inverse built from the pretrained decoder satisfies $E'(D'(E'(x)))=E'(x)$. To extend consistency to quantized bitstreams, the receiver searches for a continuous latent that reproduces both the transmitted main symbols and entropy side information. A successful search and an exact correction preserve both streams under deterministic coding; the final reconstruction is checked through the actual coding path. The encoder's pseudo-inverse enables a nonlinear counterpart of back-projection. In the linear case, back-projection has the closed-form solution $x'=x+A^\dagger(y-Ax)$, giving the closest reconstruction to $x$ satisfying $Ax'=y$. Our nonlinear formulation enforces the transmitted code on proposals from an independently chosen generative model. Adjusting the starting noise controls the prior's influence without changing that code. Experiments show small first-pass quality changes, higher retained quality than trained consistency codecs over 50 recompressions, also under 8-bit storage, and decoder-side control of the perception-distortion trade-off. Decoupling the codec from its prior lets the receiver adopt future generators without retraining or re-encoding.

title: PatientFlowSynth: Evaluating FHIR Agents with Matched Patient Charts
abstract: Agents that search patient charts must classify claims from retrieved records, including cases with missing or conflicting evidence. In Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR), status fields can change how those records should be interpreted. PatientFlowSynth provides 18,000 tasks from 225 synthetic patients and 18 templates that hold the patient, question, and retrieval program fixed across chart variants representing four evidence states. Re-executing the program verifies each variant's reference answer, evidence sets, and search requirements. Strict success requires a completed response with correct labels and citations exactly matching an accepted evidence set retrieved during the episode. Where required, a tool response must also show a complete search at the specified scope. In a study using GPT-5.6 Luna and 225 synthetic patients (3,600 matched pairs), explicit Encounter-status guidance increased strict success from 40.7% to 51.3% (+10.6 percentage points; 95% patient-bootstrap confidence interval, 8.4 to 12.8). Among cases whose primary reference label was insufficient evidence, label agreement fell from 49.2% to 29.3%. A prespecified two-model replication reproduced both changes. Failed retrieval can mask interpretation errors by producing a correct insufficient-evidence label without examining the relevant records. Additional model comparisons showed that the benefit of guidance was model-dependent. Retrieval, citation, and classification should be evaluated separately.

title: One Step, Four Clocks: How GUI Agents Fall Out of Step
abstract: GUI agents can choose correct actions yet fail as interfaces change during deliberation. Latency alone cannot explain these failures because actions may become invalid at different interaction stages. We model four events: environment change, observation availability, decision commitment, and action receipt (EODA). We introduce ChronotopeGym to study these failures under Paused, Replay, and Live execution. Across five tasks, agents can fail in Live despite succeeding when responses remain valid, even when actions meet deadlines. On Moving Balloon, updating a pending click raises success from 0% to 100% without changing response time. Our accelerator-resident GUI controller, Chronotope, maintains compact interaction history and selectively keeps, updates, or redecides pending actions. Compared with Agent S3, Chronotope reduces median end-to-end latency by 85.5% for a 27B model, expanding its performance envelope to 100% Live success at an 8-second deadline versus 0%. Chronotope enables real-time GUI control through compact interaction history, knowing when to preserve, revise, or replace actions, and an overall efficient architectural design that obviates verbose reflection, reasoning, and grounding calls.

title: The Work of Mathematical Production in the Age of AI
abstract: The emergence of powerful artificial intelligence has unsettled the relationship between mathematical production and the human intellectual activity that mathematical artifacts have traditionally documented. We argue that mathematical practice cannot be adequately understood through the production of mathematical knowledge alone, and distinguish four interrelated dimensions of inquiry: knowledge, understanding, making sense, and figuring out. Building on Kitcher, Dewey, and subsequent philosophy of mathematical practice, we develop an expanded framework incorporating the cognitive and computational capacities of mathematical communities, their conceptual organizations, provisional investigative models, and the role of unsuccessful inquiry. We propose reconceptualizing artificial intelligence as a manifestation of physically organized computation whose mathematical behavior itself can become an object of experimental investigation. This perspective motivates a program of \emph{natural mathematics}, by which we mean the construction and comparison of artificial intellectual communities developing mathematical practices under different cognitive, conceptual, and normative conditions. Our aim is not simply to automate mathematical research or increase the production of theorems, but to investigate the robustness and contingency of mathematical concepts, the possibilities of alternative mathematical practices, and what such investigations might reveal about human mathematical cognition. Finally, we consider the future of human intellectual agency in a world where mathematical production need no longer depend upon humans. We argue for intergenerational epistemic stewardship as a justification for sustaining human mathematical traditions and opportunities for intellectual participation, independently of humanity's continued indispensability to mathematical progress.

title: Fast Anatomy-Aware Diffeomorphic Augmentation for Brain MRI
abstract: Data augmentation is essential for training deep learning models that are generalizable, particularly when training data are limited. In brain MRI, augmentation methods that synthesize anatomically diverse images without relying on large cohorts are particularly attractive, especially when training supervised models for scans with a specific resolution or MRI contrast. While conventional random nonlinear fields offer a simple means of achieving such diversity, they fail to capture the underlying spatial dependencies among morphological changes across brain regions. To address this limitation, we introduce BrainAug, an anatomy-aware augmentation framework that generates diverse, anatomically coordinated deformations without relying on population imaging data. BrainAug constructs an anatomical graph encoding spatial proximity and bilateral correspondence between brain regions, then incorporates these relationships into a probabilistic model designed to sample correlated regional volume changes. These sampled variations are translated into diffeomorphic transformations, enabling substantial structural changes while preserving anatomical topology. Combined with contrast-agnostic image synthesis, BrainAug generates training images with independently varying anatomy and appearance. Evaluations across eight brain MRI datasets demonstrate stronger segmentation generalization across diverse populations, while registration experiments show improved alignment under substantial morphological differences.

title: SOTS: Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection
abstract: Training data selection for machine learning models is a critical bottleneck in industrial applications where expert annotation is costly and time-consuming. Existing coreset selection methods for time series either ignore temporal structure entirely or cannot handle variable-length, irregularly sampled, multi-channel signals, the setting most common in industrial monitoring and testing. We introduce SOTS (Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection), an unsupervised coreset selection framework for irregular multivariate time series (IMTS) classification. Each sample is mapped to a truncated path signature, capturing the joint geometric structure of its channels, and the coreset is selected by greedily minimizing the Sliced Wasserstein distance between the empirical signature distributions of the candidate subset and the full dataset, a criterion for which we establish a convergence guarantee for random coresets. We validate SOTS on a real-world, highly imbalanced industrial I&C testing dataset, where SOTS-Greedy exceeds 95% of full-dataset accuracy using only 30% of the training data, outperforming standard coreset baselines at most budgets. This advantage generalizes to public UEA regular multivariate time series benchmarks specifically when class-discriminative information is purely geometric.

title: Diagnosing Epistemic Uncertainty in Neural Operators: Effects of Initialization, Discretization, and Function Sampling
abstract: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for mappings between function spaces, but their reliability cannot be characterized by the performance of a single trained model. Existing neural operator uncertainty quantification approaches often characterize predictive uncertainty without separately identifying the contributions of individual sources of epistemic uncertainty. Finite sampling of the training function space, output discretization, and model initialization can produce substantial variation among learned operators even when the underlying physical problem is deterministic. We systematically investigate these sources of epistemic uncertainty across a diverse set of operator learning architectures. Across our experiments, we train approximately 46,000 neural operator models and construct ensembles over training datasets, model initializations, and output discretizations to characterize distributions of relative $L_2$ error rather than individual trained realizations. We find substantial architecture-dependent differences in epistemic uncertainty, with model initialization often accounting for the largest proportion of variance in relative $L_2$ error. The ranked performance of neural operator architectures can invert as the number and spatial distribution of output samples change, with the best architectures under sparse or randomly sampled observations differing from those at higher-resolution or structured discretizations. Furthermore, ensembles that reliably characterize aggregate operator error can provide unreliable estimates of error quantiles for individual test functions. These results highlight the importance of distinguishing the sources of epistemic uncertainty when evaluating neural operator reliability and establishing robust benchmarking practices.

title: ECLIPSE: Embedding-Centered Foundation-Model Federated Knowledge Transfer for Data-Free Edge Intelligence
abstract: Foundation Models (FMs) are envisioned to become an integral component of intelligent federated edge networks because of their strong representation and generalization capabilities. However, their integration into resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive edge environments remains challenging. This challenge is particularly pronounced in data-free settings, where no shared, public, or server-accessible reference dataset is available to establish a common reference space for aligning distributed knowledge. To address this challenge, we propose ECLIPSE, which is an embedding-centered FM-based federated knowledge transfer framework developed for data-free edge intelligence. ECLIPSE enables edge intelligence capitalizing on a server-hosted FM without sharing raw data, local models, or a public reference dataset. It establishes a shared embedding reference space through which edge devices encode their local task knowledge. Only the resulting embeddings are transmitted to the server for alignment and aggregation. Using the aggregated embeddings, the server constructs a task-aware surrogate dataset through an embedding-guided generative process. This surrogate dataset is then used to adapt the server-hosted FM to the downstream task. The adapted FM is subsequently distilled into a lightweight global model and distributed to the edge devices. This process allows edge devices to benefit from both distributed task knowledge and the generalization capabilities of the FM. Experimental results across diverse classification datasets show that ECLIPSE outperforms conventional Federated Learning (FL) and data-free Federated Knowledge-Transfer (FKT) baselines. It also achieves competitive performance compared with databased approaches. Furthermore, the framework remains robust under statistical and model heterogeneity across different data distributions and local architectures.

title: Exact Scalar and Fermionic Propagators in a Uniform Electric Background
abstract: By implementing an analytical hybrid framework that combines the Ritus eigenfunction technique with Schwinger's proper-time formalism, we construct exact propagators for charged scalar and fermionic fields in a constant, homogeneous, external electric field in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A central advantage of this approach is that the resulting propagators retain a four-dimensional momentum representation after the spectral summation, connecting the structure of the Ritus basis with the operator formulation of the proper-time method, without requiring the full traditional derivation of Schwinger's approach and the coordinate restrictions originally associated with the Ritus method for fermions. The translationally non-invariant component emerging after the Laguerre-polynomial summation is isolated through a suitable change of variables, yielding translationally invariant kernels and maintaining the background field strength unchanged. As a consistency check, we successfully rederive Schwinger's seminal expression for the fermionic pair production rate.

title: A steady-state genetic algorithm with multi-ratio seeding and pair exchange for the quadratic knapsack problem
abstract: The quadratic knapsack problem (QKP) seeks a subset of items of maximum total linear and pairwise profit whose total weight does not exceed a given capacity. Most QKP heuristics rank items by a profit-to-weight ratio. We show on benchmark instances that this ranking can steer the search away from the best known solutions, and that on an almost full knapsack a local optimum can be separated from a better solution by an exchange where every single swap loses profit. We propose SSGA-P, a steady-state genetic algorithm with pair exchange that addresses both effects. Its initial population contains greedy solutions built with a grid of exponents between 0.5 and 3 applied to the item weights, and its pair exchange move combines an improving swap violating the capacity with a second swap or removal that restores feasibility. Incremental contribution vectors keep the method practical up to 10{,}000 items. SSGA-P finds optimal solutions in every run on the 100 classical instances and reaches all best known values in 99.8\% of the runs on the 80 instances with 1000 and 2000 items and in 99.75\% on the 40 instances with 5000 and 6000 items, significantly above the 87.7\% of the iterated hyperplane exploration algorithm, improving one best known value. On the 144 Large-QKP instances of Hochbaum et al. (2025), with the same 120-second limit, it improves 20 best known values and matches the other 124. An ablation study shows that the multi-ratio seeding and the pair exchange account for most of this performance.

title: Ultra-Wideband Stacked Patch Antenna for D-Band Applications
abstract: This article proposes a wideband stacked dual-patch antenna designed for D-band applications. The antenna is demonstrated with both wireless and dielectric waveguide (DWG) channels. The patch dimensions and spacings are chosen to ensure that the $10~dB$ return loss (RL) bandwidth covers the entire D-band ($110$--$170~GHz$). The antenna is fabricated on a seven-layer organic packaging technology. The patches are fabricated on layers 1 and 3 within a shielding cavity formed by closely spaced vias of $< λ/20$ pitch. The fabrication technology supports direct chip-level excitation of the antenna using a flip-chip packaging interface, and the design methodology for this feeding approach is outlined in the paper. In the fabricated design, however, a transition to the WR6 metallic waveguide with ($<~1~dB$) insertion loss (IL) is incorporated for feeding. This facilitates alignment and measurement of the structure using external test equipment. The full antenna and transition are integrated in a back-to-back configuration, achieving a measured $10~dB$ return loss bandwidth of more than $60~GHz$ ($110$--$170~GHz$) for the wireless link, thereby covering the entire D-band. To the best of our knowledge, this is the widest antenna bandwidth reported in the same frequency range. The measured peak gain is $8.5~dBi$ (35$^\circ$ H-plane $3~dB$ beamwidth) with a gain variation of $3.5~dBi$ within the operating bandwidth. For the dielectric waveguide configuration, the measured $10~dB$ RL bandwidth also exceeds $60~GHz$, fully encompassing the D-band. The simulated insertion loss coupling into the dielectric waveguide is $3.5~dB$. A 1-meter dielectric waveguide channel fed with the proposed antenna is measured. The overall channel exhibits a total insertion loss of $14.7~dB$, of which a simulated $3.5~dB$ at $140~GHz$ is attributed to the loss of each side that feeds the DWG.

title: Eigenvalue-based computation of Richardson pairing spectra and finite-size thermodynamics
abstract: We present a numerical workflow for the reduced BCS Richardson model, combining the eigenvalue-based Bethe equations, Baxter-polynomial reconstruction, and complex root finding. Newton-Raphson iteration solves the nonlinear equations for the eigenvalue-based variables; a linear system yields the polynomial coefficients, and Laguerre iteration with polynomial deflation extracts the rapidities. We apply the procedure to equally spaced, quadratic, and hydrogen-like non-degenerate single-particle spectra as the pairing strength varies. For finite systems, we calculate canonical observables from the complete seniority-zero spectrum and check benchmark spectra against exact diagonalization. In an eight-level, four-pair system with a hydrogen-like spectrum, the heat capacity has two maxima at weak coupling. With increasing coupling, the low-temperature maximum shifts upward and the high-temperature maximum downward; the latter ceases to be a distinct local maximum near $g\simeq0.03515$ in the units used. The equally spaced benchmark instead has a single dominant maximum over the coupling interval displayed for that spectrum. This comparison illustrates how single-particle level spacings can shape finite-size thermal response. The C++ code is publicly available; numerical instabilities remain possible near ill-conditioned configurations and at larger sizes.

title: Can LLM-Simulated Respondents Pre-Test Survey Questions? Evidence From Preregistered Prospective Validation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can be conditioned to simulate behavioral responses, including survey responses, but it remains unclear whether and how these simulations can support downstream research tasks. Here, we evaluate whether simulated respondents can support pre-testing new candidate survey questions before fielding them, operationalized as prioritizing candidate survey items. Specifically, we rank candidate questions by their mean responses, which can reveal ceiling or floor effects; their variance, which indicates whether responses contain meaningful variation; and differences between subpopulations, which indicate whether questions capture distinctions between relevant groups within a population. We introduce a preregistered, prospective evaluation that commits model predictions before target human responses exist, ruling out memorization of those responses by design. Using two waves of a local survey (2025: N = 1,271; 2026: N = 1,161), we built simulated respondents from 2025 participants and preregistered GPT-4.1 predictions for 22 questions introduced in 2026. Simulations accurately ranked questions by mean responses (Spearman \r{ho} = 0.71) and anticipated which questions distinguished city from county residents (\r{ho} = 0.88), Black from White residents (\r{ho} = 0.68), and employed from unemployed residents (\r{ho} = 0.57), suggesting simulations can help prioritize questions before fielding. More broadly, our prospective, preregistered design provides a general framework for evaluating AI simulations without contamination from memorized target outcomes.

title: JevBench: Metamorphic Coherence Testing for Typed Probabilistic Decision Models
abstract: Typed probabilistic decision models return distributions over specified answers, such as yes or no, a set of options or levels on an ordered scale. We ask whether their probabilities remain coherent when questions about the same input are reworded, negated, combined, given different options or placed in different batches. JevBench tests this coherence without gold labels. Its 50 metamorphic relations each test one law of probability or choice across five dimensions: representation, batch independence, probability measure, logical order and choice-set conditioning. Each test changes the question or batch while keeping the input fixed. Every model receives the same requests, fixed in advance. JevBench-240 contains 12,000 tests across 240 synthetic cases in 12 decision domains. A fixed subset of 1,200 tests, JevBench-mini, closely reproduces the full-suite ranking (Spearman 0.983). Across 21 openly released models, coherence scores range from 56.5 to 83.9. Batch independence holds for most models. Additivity fails broadly, particularly for complements, where the probabilities of a proposition and its negation should sum to one. A uniform reference model ignores the input and scores 89.4 at chance accuracy, exceeding every evaluated model's coherence score. Among decoders, accuracy ranges from 82.4% to 89.2%, while coherence ranges from 64.2 to 83.9. These results show why both measures are needed to assess decision models. JevBench is available as an open-source Python package.

title: All-electronic geometric phase gate on Doppler-cooled trapped ions using an axial mode
abstract: We report the experimental demonstration of a high-fidelity oscillating magnetic gradient entangling gate on the axial stretch mode of a two-ion crystal in a micro-fabricated surface Paul trap, therefore allowing for mixed-species sympathetic cooling. With only Doppler-cooled $^{171}$Yb$^+$ ions at $\bar{n}$ = 50(5), we achieve Bell-state fidelities far above the relevant fault-tolerant threshold, simplifying transport protocols within a shuttling-based-architecture. The control fields consist only of an oscillating current applied to submerged integrated wires emitting a B-field gradient near-resonant with the axial mode, and resonant microwave pulses at the qubit frequency constituting very low gate calibration overheads. We also demonstrate an adiabatic elimination of spin-motion entanglement (AESE) version of the gate, showcasing significant robustness.

title: Hi3R-VLA: Grounding Semantics and Actions in 3D
abstract: While recent vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly incorporate 3D geometry, how to effectively exploit it for precise and generalizable action prediction remains a central challenge. We introduce Hi3R-VLA, a 3D policy that grounds heterogeneous modalities - vision, language, and action - in explicit 3D geometry for robotic manipulation. Our model integrates spatially-aligned visual features and language conditioning into point cloud representations, enriching scene geometry with fine-grained, task-relevant semantics. It then anchors low-level control commands in the same 3D coordinate frame and uses 3D-RoPE enhanced action-to-point attention over coarse-to-fine point features to model geometric relationships between action targets and observed points. Our analysis demonstrates the importance of semantic fusion within 3D and spatial alignment between observations and actions. With fewer than 250M trainable parameters, Hi3R-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance on RoboCasa, RLBench, RoboTwin2, DexJoCo and DexSuite across diverse manipulation tasks and embodiments, from single-arm and dual-arm grippers to dexterous hands. Real-robot evaluations further demonstrate its effectiveness in the physical world. The model, code and dataset are publicly released at https://cshizhe.github.io/projects/hi3r_vla.html.

title: Tempering and few-shot calibration of pathology foundation models improve digital biomarker reproducibility across slide scanners
abstract: Pathology foundation models underpin a growing number of histology-based cancer biomarkers, but sensitivity to slide scanner-specific image signatures degrades cross-center reliability and reproducibility. We developed a foundation model fine-tuning method that improved consistency in head-and-neck cancer human papillomavirus (HPV) prediction, colorectal cancer microsatellite instability (MSI) identification, prostate cancer grading and breast cancer phenotyping. This tempering method decreased cross-scanner prediction differences by 67.5% for HPV (95% CI 59.0-73.9%), 69.3% for MSI (95% CI 51.9-76.5%) and 63.4%-81.2% for breast signatures. Cross-scanner prostate grade agreement rose from 42.5% to 92.7%. Under full scanner-HPV confounding during training, AUROC fell from 0.80 to 0.68 with original model features but only from 0.86 to 0.84 with tempering. Unlike post hoc feature calibration, tempering used only public data yet matched or exceeded on-site calibration. These findings support tempering to reduce scanner dependence of pathology foundation models.

title: Density-dependent photocarrier recombination in $γ$-InSe
abstract: We studied the photocarrier dynamics in $γ$-InSe using femtosecond transient reflectance spectroscopy. By measuring the dependence of the differential reflectance on the injected carrier density, we established an empirical relation between the optical response and carrier density, allowing quantitative analysis of the recombination dynamics. The carrier decay exhibits a strong density dependence, indicating a substantial contribution from nonlinear recombination. At high carrier densities, the dynamics are dominated by a second-order recombination process, with a rate constant of $3.8\times10^{-6}~\mathrm{cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At low densities, the decay becomes approximately exponential, with a carrier lifetime of about 7 ps. We also resolved an initial rise of the band-edge response with a time constant of less than 1 ps, which is attributed to hot-carrier cooling. These results reveal the competition between first-order and second-order recombination in $γ$-InSe and provide quantitative insights into its ultrafast photocarrier dynamics.

title: An equivariant index theorem for the Heisenberg calculus
abstract: We derive a local fixed-point formula for the equivariant index of Heisenberg elliptic operators on closed contact manifolds equipped with an action of a compact Lie group preserving the contact form. The formula expresses the character of the equivariant index in terms of a cyclic-cohomological character of the noncommutative Heisenberg principal symbol. The main new ingredient is the construction of traces, one on each fixed-point set, defined by integration over twisted conjugacy classes in the Heisenberg group. The proof proceeds by a K-theoretic reduction to the equivariant index theorem of our paper "Toeplitz operators on contact manifolds and equivariant K-homology".

title: Agent Evaluation Without Ground Truth: A Null Proportion Perspective
abstract: The correctness of actions taken by agents is typically evaluated against known, externally verified ground truth labels, such as whether a proof is correct or whether code compiles and passes unit tests. However, as coding and science agents are entrusted with more end-to-end autonomy -- proposing interventions, running experiments, and deciding what to deploy and investigate next -- whether an agent's actions genuinely improve an outcome must be inferred from noisy, often inconclusive experiments. To evaluate agents in this setting, we define agent quality as a weighted sum of correct decisions along its trajectory, using sequences of $e$-values as statistical evidence regarding correctness in place of ground-truth labels. Our framework accommodates arbitrarily dependent decisions, data-dependent trajectory termination, dynamically generated hypotheses, and quality measures defined after the trajectory concludes. We construct upper and lower bound estimators and confidence sets for agent quality with statistical guarantees that hold uniformly over agent trajectory distributions and establish instance-wise sharpness of our estimator class. We demonstrate our methods with a case study comparing the success of Claude Opus and Claude Haiku in improving the runtime of an open-source Python package.

title: ExitLUT: Boolean Early Exits for Efficient FPGA-Based Neural Network Inference
abstract: Early exit neural networks reduce average inference cost by terminating once sufficient confidence is reached. On FPGAs, conventional confidence-based exits add arithmetic control paths poorly matched to LUT fabrics, consuming resources that could otherwise support the main datapath. We present ExitLUT, which replaces softmax-style exit decisions with learned Boolean functions mapped directly into FPGA LUTs. In our CNN evaluation, fpgaConvNet is the static spatial-dataflow baseline, while ATHEENA is its softmax-based early exit extension. ExitLUT reduces ATHEENA's exit-decision LUT usage by 2.58$\times$ over the softmax path and eliminates decision-path DSP usage, while preserving accuracy and exit behavior. Rerunning design-space exploration reinvests these savings into the datapath, improving throughput by up to 4.08$\times$ over fpgaConvNet and 1.82$\times$ over ATHEENA. For LUT-based NNs, embedded ExitLUT exits achieve 1.41-1.89$\times$ average time-to-decision speedup over static NeuraLUT-Assemble designs with under 1% LUT overhead.

title: Where Agent Defenses Fail: A Case Study of Policy Compositions and Measurement Limits
abstract: A coding agent may need to upload a report while its sandbox blocks network access. A host mediator can restore delivery, but an injected instruction may add a secret to the approved request. We study this interaction using files and HTTP receipts to measure effects independently of control logs. Two prospective frozen-input cohorts comprise 110 and 300 runs on previously explored authored tasks. Restrictive sandboxing produces no observed attack harm but reduces benign utility to 6/8 and 12/24. Mediation restores uploads and admits disclosure; complete-line matching retains full benign utility but misses two value-only disclosures in the expanded cohort. A separate 72-run boundary study identifies encoded disclosure, observer misses, and formatting checks that obscure benign refusals. An 80-run SafeAgents/OpenShell follow-up shows that containment stops the tested guard misses among valid observations, while mediation restores benign uploads and delivers both encoded-attestation attacks. Twelve judge-error rows remain unscored. A separate response-capture diagnostic reproduces their failures at the native token budget. A 12-run exact-publication-contract experiment blocks both attacks but also rejects both benign formatting variants; a 4-run normalized follow-up restores both benign uploads while still rejecting both attacks. These small, single-model studies identify delivery-path and measurement limits; they do not establish general attack resistance.

title: Neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional phonon Boltzmann-Fourier coupling for multiscale heat transport in silicon fin arrays
abstract: Localized heating in semiconductor devices can produce non-diffusive phonon transport near heat-generating regions, while heat spreading through the surrounding substrate remains well described by Fourier conduction. We present a hybrid framework that couples a pretrained neural operator for the phonon Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) within individual fins to a Fourier model of a shared substrate. To reduce the cost of repeated BTE solves across fin positions and coupling iterations, a DeepONet maps each fin's substrate-interface temperature and heating state to its temperature and heat-flux fields. The operator is trained on interface temperatures generated by a linearized proxy of the coupled problem, which avoids explicit training data collection from full coupled runs. An energy-balance penalty regularizes the learned operator, and a mixed finite-element formulation represents substrate heat flux in an H(div)-conforming space. The two models exchange temperature and normal heat flux through a non-overlapping Schwarz iteration with adaptive Aitken relaxation. We evaluate the framework on an idealized three-dimensional array of 100 silicon fins. For a held-out switching configuration, the neural-operator-Fourier solution differs from the direct BTE-Fourier reference by a maximum of 0.3 K in temperature and 0.6% in relative flux across all fins. Excluding the one-time substrate factorization, the coupled surrogate run takes about 50 s, compared with 2 h 28 min for direct coupling, a speedup of approximately 180x. Additional held-out switching patterns converge with the same trained operator. These results demonstrate neural-operator acceleration of bidirectional kinetic-continuum coupling for the tested geometry and material. This bidirectional strategy may extend to other multiscale materials problems coupling learned local neural models with continuum solvers.

title: Reproducible Social Structure Emerges From Free-Form Interaction Among LLM Agents
abstract: Multi-agent LLM simulations are increasingly used as models of social systems, but most published findings are anecdotal, i.e., drawn from a single run. It is therefore unclear which observed phenomena are robust findings of the simulated system itself, and which were random events in one particular run. Here, we introduce a repeatable, goal-free, proactive multi-agent framework in which fifty persona-conditioned agents with persistent memory choose whether, with whom, and how to communicate across three social platforms. The framework supports non-perturbative measurements across temporal snapshots and repetitions. Running the same world ten times from identical initial conditions for a total of 700 hours, we find that most measured network- and agent-level parameters are stable across repetitions. Throughout a run, initially broad communication contracts into sparse sustained dyads in all ten worlds. Importantly, we find that many identical dyads re-form across worlds significantly more often than expected by chance or from agent-specific sociability alone. Static personality similarity largely fails to predict these dyads. Instead, alignment and extremity in the emotions and traits expressed during first contact predict whether a pair later forms a sustained dyad. Additionally, individual agents' emotion and trait expression in their chain-of-thought predicts their future behavior. Finally, swapping either persona prompts or accumulated memories between agents causes recipients to exhibit behavior more similar to donors. Both kinds of transplant move the recipients about 60% of the way toward its donor personality, and state-transplanted agents start behaving similar to their donor agent from their next turn on. Overall, we show that repeated worlds enable robust, statistically-grounded conclusions about emergent within-configuration behavior in agent societies.

title: Airport-level runway-incursion rates normalized by movements: hierarchical shrinkage estimates, ranking uncertainty and severity for FAA-towered airports, FY2008-FY2024
abstract: Runway incursions are one of ICAO's five high-risk occurrence categories, yet airport-level comparisons of incursion risk in the United States still rest on raw counts or on fixed-count thresholds that select on sampling noise. We assemble an airport-fiscal-year panel of 565 FAA-towered airports holding 27,079 runway-incursion records from the FAA Runway Safety database as held in the FlightFinder corpus (himaxym.com), normalized by tower operations from the FAA Terminal Area Forecast (ATADS/OPSNET actuals). A hierarchical negative-binomial model with log operations as an exposure offset, airport random effects, fiscal-year effects and traffic-mix covariates yields, for every airport, a shrinkage-adjusted rate per million operations, an exceedance probability relative to the national median, and a posterior rank with a 90% interval in the manner of Goldstein and Spiegelhalter. Severity (Category A-D) is modeled separately as an ordinal outcome, and empirical-Bayes and fully Bayesian shrinkage are compared. The crude national rate is 29.4 incursions per million operations (95% interval 29.1-29.8), with an index of dispersion of 8.61. Between-airport dispersion after exposure adjustment is sigma_u = 1.05: an airport one standard deviation above the mean carries 2.84 times the national rate. 199 of 565 airports exceed the national median with probability above 0.9, and the 90% rank interval at the median airport spans 134 positions, so much of the league table is statistically indistinguishable from its middle. Severity and frequency respond to different determinants: the airport-level rank correlation between them is -0.08 (90% interval -0.14 to -0.02), so a frequency ranking carries little information about where a severe outcome is likely. The results offer a reproducible, uncertainty-aware alternative to count thresholds for prioritizing runway-safety interventions.

title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Parameter-Varying Systems With Noisy Data
abstract: This paper proposes a tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme for unknown discrete-time linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems using offline noisy input-scheduling-state data. We establish a multi-trajectory simplified LPV fundamental lemma yielding a collective Hankel representation of finite-horizon trajectories. Constraining the Hankel coefficients to a scaled simplex uniformly bounds the noise-induced predictor mismatch but may exclude relevant constrained lifted trajectories. A convex-hull coverage condition for admissible receding-horizon continuations restores the required representability. LPV data-consistency and robust positively invariant sets provide tube-tightening ingredients computed directly from noisy data. The online problem is a quadratic program, for which recursive feasibility, closed-loop constraint satisfaction, and practical input-to-state stability are established. Numerical results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

title: Smale's Mean Values And Geometric Mean Values
abstract: We prove that, for every integer $d>2$ and every $L>0$, there exists a polynomial of degree $d$ whose geometric mean value exceeds $L$. This result demonstrates that the geometric mean value alone is insufficient to establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale's mean values. Under certain additional assumptions, we derive upper bounds for the geometric mean value, thereby verifying Smale's mean value conjecture for several subclasses of polynomials. Furthermore, we connect Smale's mean values to Fekete points. Motivated by this connection, we formulate a new problem concerning Fekete points in the spirit of Smale's mean values.

title: Aftershock: Yesterday's Linux Kernel Bugs, Tomorrow's Android Exploits
abstract: Android kernels have long suffered from slow patch propagation from Linux upstream, with fixes often reaching devices far later than conventional Linux distributions. Until recently, this lag was largely a patch-management problem. With rapidly improving LLM agents, it is becoming an exploitation problem: public upstream patches can now serve as blueprints for building working n-day exploits before downstream devices are fixed. We test this threat end to end by building an automated pipeline that screens upstream Linux patches, reproduces memory-safety vulnerabilities on Android targets, and drives an LLM agent to construct local privilege escalation exploits from an untrusted application. Across 152 candidate CVEs reported over 33 months, we reproduce 38 vulnerabilities and generate 17 independently verified exploits under production defenses. Exploitation takes a median of 14.3 agent-hours and $321 in API cost, with 90% median reliability; 12 of 14 trials succeed on Pixel 9 and Pixel 10 devices. Notably, the pipeline relies only on publicly available, off-the-shelf models. Surprisingly, only 3 of the 17 exploited CVEs appear in Android Security Bulletins, suggesting limited visibility into which upstream fixes address vulnerabilities that affect Android kernels. For these 17 CVEs, the corresponding upstream patches reach Pixel devices with a median delay of 181 days. Together, these results reveal a stark asymmetry: attackers can increasingly automate exploitation in hours, while defenders still identify and deploy fixes on the timescale of months.

title: Spin Hamiltonian, magnetic anisotropy and excitation spectrum in altermagnetic $α$-MnTe from first principles
abstract: The hexagonal altermagnet $α$-MnTe combines a near-room-temperature collinear order with a strongly spin-split electronic structure, yet the microscopic origin of its easy-plane anisotropy, its zone-center magnon gap and its anomalously large magnetostriction have remained unexplained. We derive the complete low-energy magnetic Hamiltonian of $α$-MnTe from first principles, combining density functional theory and dynamical mean-field theory with a force-theorem evaluation of the full anisotropic intersite exchange, single-ion terms and classical dipolar couplings. The isotropic exchange, including the altermagnetic splitting of the tenth-neighbor coupling, agrees with inelastic neutron scattering data. Contrary to the common single-ion picture, we find that the easy-plane anisotropy and the magnon gap at $Γ$ are governed by classical dipole-dipole interactions, which enhance the zone-center magnon splitting threefold leading to quantitative agreement with experiment, while the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term is irrelevant despite its size. The same Hamiltonian reproduces the chiral magnon splitting along antinodal directions, mirroring the electronic spin splitting, and quantitatively accounts for the giant magnetovolume coupling of $α$-MnTe through the volume dependence of superexchange.

title: A Hereditarily Atomic Domain without ACCP
abstract: An integral domain for which every subring is atomic is said to be hereditarily atomic. Every hereditarily atomic cancellative commutative monoid satisfies the ascending chain condition on principal ideals (ACCP), but it remained an open question whether every hereditarily atomic domain satisfies ACCP. We construct a hereditarily atomic domain which does not satisfy ACCP, answering this question in the negative. This domain is an overring of the ring of integer-valued polynomials $Int(\mathbb{Z})$, and its subrings that fail ACCP are precisely those of finite additive index.

title: An Introduction to Semialgebraic Geometry
abstract: The first chapter of these lecture notes explains algorithms for counting real roots and the Tarski-Seidenberg theorem. In the next two chapters we study semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ , which are defined by boolean combinations of polynomial equations and inequalities. The main tool for this study is the cylindrical algebraic decomposition, which is introduced in Chapter 2. The principal result of Chapter 3 is the triangulation theorem. This theorem shows that semialgebraic sets have a simple topology, which can be effectively computed from their definitions. Chapter 4 contains examples of finiteness results and uniform bounds for semialgebraic families. In particular, we give an explicit bound for the number of connected components of a real algebraic set as a function of the degree of the equations and the dimension of the ambient space.

title: Flexible algebraic curves and fake vanishing cycles
abstract: We prove that complex curves in sufficiently ample linear systems on simply connected projective surfaces are topologically (spin) flexible: any (spin) mapping class of the underlying real surface extends to a topological mapping class of the ambient 4-manifold. As a corollary, we prove that smooth curves in the complex projective plane are topologically (spin) flexible. A consequence of topological flexibility is the existence of fake vanishing cycles, that is, simple closed curves on the underlying real surface that are not vanishing cycles, yet still bound a topologically embedded $(\pm1)$-framed disk in the surface exterior. We also give examples of pushed in Seifert surfaces in $D^4$ that are not topologically spin-flexible, but become spin-flexible after a single internal stabilization. Our methods utilize the equivariant intersection form on the surface exterior.

title: On the unirationality of anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces: the infinite families
abstract: Anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces fall into finitely many sporadic families and four infinite families. We prove that the anticanonical surfaces lying in the infinite families are unirational over their field of definition. Over a Hilbertian field, we further prove that a Hilbert subset of members consists of nonrational surfaces.

title: Multiplicities and $k$-numerical Range
abstract: We study the wedge and projection multiplicities of a point in the $k$-numerical range $W_k(A)$ of a complex matrix $A$. The representatives are decomposable wedges of orthonormal $k$-frames and rank-$k$ orthogonal projections, respectively. For $1\le k<n$, put $r=\text{dim}_\mathbb{R}\text{span}_\mathbb{R}\{I_n,H,K\}$, where $H=(A+A^*)/2$ and $K=(A-A^*)/(2i)$. We prove that every $ξ\in\text{relint} W_k(A)$ satisfies $p_{A,k}(ξ)=n^2-r+1$ and $w_{A,k}(ξ)=\binom nk$. We determine both multiplicities at every boundary point of $W_k(A)$, including non-exposed points. For complex symmetric matrices we establish lower bounds for both real multiplicities, including singular interior fibers, and obtain exact formulas for boundary points, line ranges, and commuting symmetric parts. We also relate the two multiplicities by quadratic inequalities.

title: Agent Recovery Gone Wrong: Measuring Harm Beyond Duplicate Calls
abstract: Code-executing LLM agents submit blocks of code that issue several API writes. If a block fails after some of its writes have taken effect, the agent rewrites the block and continues. It is unknown how often such a recovery harms the external state when the failure occurs naturally in the code written by the agent. In this paper, we measure it on recorded trajectories of AppWorld agents. In a stratified random sample of 200 candidate episodes across ten models, 145 are partial executions confirmed by the database state. In the sample, 30 of 143 confirmed partial executions with a determinable outcome are followed by a harmful recovery, and its violation remains at the end of the run, which gives a stratification-weighted estimate of 24.6%. Two thirds of the harmful recoveries duplicate an effect, and the rest delete user data or make a wrong first-time write, e.g., an order of a wrong product. A rule that searches for repeated calls finds 75% of duplications but only 41% of all harm. We also examine two sources of operation identity for an idempotency contract. In a small pilot (17 episodes, one local model), identifiers supplied by the model do not detectably reduce harm, because the model issues a new identifier for the same operation. Identity derived from the call content, evaluated counterfactually on the sample, would have matched every harmful write in 14 to 18 of the 30 harmful recoveries, but in none of those with a wrong first-time write, and it would also have matched writes required by the task in 30 episodes. Based on these results, we outline design requirements for safer agent recovery.

title: Radiation from periods: Bremsstrahlung functions, wound loops, latitudes and integral constraints in ABJM
abstract: The Bremsstrahlung functions of the 1/2BPS and 1/6BPS Wilson lines of ABJM theory measure their response to small deformations. We show that a single geometric object, the spectral curve of the localisation matrix model, captures both of them in closed form, together with the planar wound and latitude Wilson loops at any complex winding and framing. The fermionic function turns out to be a period of the second kind: a single hypergeometric function, which solves a second-order differential equation and is quasimodular. The bosonic one is not a period but a ratio of periods. At every coupling it is the smaller of the two, so radiation grows along the defect flow from the bosonic to the fermionic line. The key role is played by a new observable, the winding velocity, which turns out to be the 't Hooft coupling shifted by four times the fermionic function. It is at the same time the winding derivative of the wound loop and the curvature of the latitude, and the curve captures it in both incarnations through its logarithmic periods and through its periods with two charges. It is also a datum of the defect conformal field theory on the 1/2BPS line, since it fixes a new integrated four-point function of the tilt operators. All results extend to ABJ theory when the ranks of the gauge groups are not equal.

title: Real-Time AI Acceleration on a 2D Spatial Dataflow Architecture
abstract: Machine Learning (ML) is increasingly being integrated into real-time systems, which makes the timing analysis of ML accelerators necessary. However, the most popular commercial accelerator, the Graphics Processing Unit (GPU), remains difficult to analyze as several aspects of its behavior, including scheduling of threads involved in single-instruction multiple-thread computations and memory access latency, are not fully documented.
