These results establish an experimental route to distinguishing mechanisms that produce similar vortex structures by resolving the nonlinear interactions within them.

title: TableRouter: Query-Aware Evidence Construction for Long-Table Question Answering
abstract: LLMs can reason over tables, but when tables outgrow the context budget, retrieving relevant rows is only part of the solution. A retrieved subset may omit information required for an exact aggregate; even complete evidence may remain difficult for an LLM to use. We introduce TableRouter, a training-free framework that analyzes each query, then chooses between two routes: a computation route, which derives question-conditioned statistics from the full table, and a coverage route, which retrieves relevant rows and column summaries. The chosen context is passed to a frozen LLM in one call. Across three LLMs and three large-table benchmarks, TableRouter outperforms the strongest of six single-call baselines in all nine settings by 1.2-18.3 accuracy points, using 77-95% fewer estimated FLOPs than truncated-table prompting, with indexing amortized across questions. The gains extend to long tables from databases not used in earlier experiments, where TableRouter achieves 35.8% with Qwen2.5-7B, versus 16.4% for the strongest external baseline. A controlled experiment shows that explicitly providing computed statistics improves accuracy by up to 40.0 points, even when all answer-determining rows are available. These results distinguish evidence access from evidence use: long-table reasoning depends on how information is represented, not only on which rows are retrieved.

title: Finite rank and compactness of finite sums of Toeplitz products on the harmonic Bergman space
abstract: We completely characterize finite rank and compactness for finite sums of products of Toeplitz operators on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk, assuming boundedness only of the full harmonic symbols. Reflecting the appropriate symbols reduces sums of Toeplitz products and small Hankel products to Toeplitz product sums. For sums of mixed Toeplitz and small Hankel products in either order, right multiplication by a fixed unitary reflection gives the corresponding reduction. These reductions preserve rank and compactness. Finite rank is characterized by symbol identities and a cubic divisibility condition on the coefficient polynomials obtained after choosing bases over one-variable rational function fields. We also obtain an exact rank formula. Compactness is characterized by boundary vanishing of the diagonal symbol sum and uniform decay of the centered symbol tensor on hyperbolic disks of fixed radius as their centers approach the boundary. For a sum of $N\ge1$ products, an equivalent compactness criterion uses weighted derivatives of the symbol components up to order $N$. When $N$ is even, the conditions of order $N$ cannot be omitted. Mixed commutators of finite rank vanish. We characterize small Hankel commutators of nonzero finite rank in terms of a bounded analytic function and its bounded reciprocal, both with rational primitives.

title: LIBRA: Runtime Co-Tuning of Batch Size and Parallelism for Time-Efficient LLM Training
abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) requires choosing both a batch size and a parallel configuration. Existing systems make these decisions in isolation, tuning parallelism for throughput and batch size for convergence, but neither objective alone determines training efficiency. We present LIBRA, a lightweight runtime framework that co-tunes batch size and parallel configuration to minimize end-to-end time. LIBRA treats throughput and convergence as two noisy objectives and searches their joint space using parallel noisy expected hypervolume improvement (qNEHVI). To make this runtime search efficient, we propose hierarchical pruning, which removes infeasible and low-throughput parallel configurations through system-level performance estimation and then narrows batch-size candidates through critical-batch-size-aware convergence monitoring. We further design acquisition-guided parallel evaluation (AGPE), which evaluates surviving candidates concurrently across GPU groups in order of their acquisition values. On clusters of up to 256 GPUs, LIBRA reduces time-to-convergence by 31.1% on average over state-of-the-art methods, while runtime tuning accounts for only 0.3-3.5% of overall time.

title: Calm Agent: Reframing Agent Interaction around Intermittent Human Attention
abstract: AI agents can carry out auxiliary tasks while users focus on other work. Yet users still need to understand task state, make changes, and respond when help is required. We argue that agents for ongoing auxiliary tasks should be designed around intermittent human attention: tasks should continue between interactions, and users should be able to return with little effort to understand and control them. We develop this position as Calm Agent. It connects three on-demand interaction modes: Delegate, Adjust, and Check, through a persistent task representation. Generative interaction provides controls and feedback suited to open-ended goals, while existing controls support routine actions. We illustrate these principles with Orvlet, a desktop prototype for background execution and compact task interfaces. We identify challenges in adapting interfaces while preserving continuity, coordinating attention across tasks, providing responsive interaction, and learning user habits over time. The aim is to support continuing task control while protecting attention for primary work.

title: Elastic rebound in viscous fluid: an efficient rigid--elastic splitting with an asymptotic gap model
abstract: We formulate and test a model for an elastic body that falls under gravity onto the bottom of a container filled with a viscous incompressible fluid and rebounds without topological contact. The body is a rigid body plus a small, quasi-static elastic deformation, represented by a fixed compliance operator. In the near-contact patch, the thin fluid film is described by a Reynolds equation with cavitation. This allows the use of coarse meshes that need not resolve the gap, enabling efficient simulation. The film is coupled implicitly to the elastic surface displacement and to the rigid normal motion. The bulk fluid is coupled monolithically to the rigid body. For the axisymmetric case with vertical translation, the coupled step reduces exactly to a small dense nonlinear problem for the film pressure, with the bulk eliminated through a $2x2$ affine map. The model is implemented in NGSolve and compared with the experiments of Hagemeier et al. (2021) and the Eulerian FSI simulations of Wahl et al. (2021a). For a PTFE ball the approach agrees with the Eulerian FSI to 1\%. For a soft rubber ball (St $\approx 120$) the purely elastic model gives about three times the measured rebound. Material damping is the most important missing effect: a Kelvin--Voigt compliance with loss factor $\tanδ=0.6$ gives 4.0\,mm, against 4.4\,mm measured. A planar version of the model is compared with the recently published 2D benchmark of Corti et al. (2026). The radius of the film patch is the only numerical parameter of the splitting. It is fixed by one a-priori rule for all configurations, derived from a dry Hertz estimate of the approach, and the results depend only weakly on it.

title: Distractors are the Real Enemy: Visual Distraction Adversarial Perturbations on SAM2-Based Video Tracking and Segmentation
abstract: Promptable video trackers such as SAM2 achieve accurate and robust performance through strong temporal consistency, making them important foundations for downstream video understanding and tracking applications. As their use continues to expand, understanding their robustness to adversarial perturbations becomes increasingly important. Existing attacks on SAM2 largely focus on local mask degradation and short-term temporal feature disruption, leaving its longer-term dynamics and competing object interferences (Distractors) insufficiently explored. We observe that SAM2 itself exposes useful distractor cues when tracking becomes uncertain. Based on these observations, we propose DistractAttack, a white-box attack that uses background distractors to disrupt target tracking persistently. Its core procedure, Counterfactual Distractor Search (CDS), propagates clean and attacked trajectories in parallel to discover plausible competing regions and identify those that become increasingly effective under perturbation. The discovered evidence is accumulated over time to weaken target support and promote recurrent alternatives or disappearance predictions. Extensive experiments under video-level and one-shot perturbations across Visual Object Tracking and Video Object Segmentation demonstrate strong attack effectiveness, raising DRE to $4.4\times$ and NRE to $7.3\times$ their nearest baselines under video perturbation, while transferring effectively across model scales and tracker variants in black-box settings. Project page: https://adonaydem.github.io/sam2-da-page/

title: Marketing-Bench: Evaluating Frontier Models and Agents on Real-World Marketing Capabilities
abstract: As frontier AI models and agents are deployed more broadly in the real world, marketing is emerging as one of their largest applications. Marketing teams use AI models to produce brand assets like website copy and social media posts, while consumers' agents autonomously discover products, research purchases, and navigate websites. However, evaluating marketing capability is difficult because unlike areas like software development, customer support, or legal review where ground truth is more objectively defined, marketing is subjective, and output quality is judged based on taste and brand. We introduce Marketing-Bench, the first open-source marketing benchmark, which pairs discriminative tasks (detecting brand anomalies) with generative tasks (remediation), while keeping answers verifiable. Marketing-Bench tests five key pillars: factuality, consistency, coherence, structure, and brand voice, all crucial elements for good brand content on the web. We find that frontier models are far from solving the benchmark: the average model corrects only about half of the introduced issues (53.1%), whereas a marketing expert corrects nearly all of them. Even the strongest, GPT-6 Astra, reaches only 74.8%, with Claude Opus and Fable, Gemini Argon, and GPT-6 Sol falling well short. These findings suggest that marketing capabilities are less mature than adoption implies, and that principled evaluation should precede further scaling of usage. Marketing-Bench is a first step toward "frontier marketing models" with superhuman marketing performance.

title: To Critic Or Not To Critic
abstract: As large language models tackle longer and more complex tasks, understanding when a critic improves the efficiency of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes increasingly important. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) trains a critic to reduce variance and provide fine-grained credit assignment, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) drops the critic and avoids the bias of bootstrapping from the critic's value estimates. Although recent critic-based methods have reported strong performance relative to GRPO, it remains unclear when each approach is preferable. We argue that there is no universal answer; instead, the choice depends on several interacting factors, including batch size, critic reliance, and task complexity. We study the bias-variance tradeoff in terms of gradient direction, measuring how closely each method's gradient estimates align with the true policy gradient as batch size grows. Under a shared actor objective, we compare GRPO with PPO in control tasks, short-horizon math, and long-horizon terminal agents. Across more than 1,200 training runs, including 96 with LLMs, we find that PPO generally leads at small batch sizes, while GRPO often overtakes heavily bootstrapped PPO and reaches parity with lightly bootstrapped PPO at larger batches. At longer horizons and in more complex domains, GRPO needs larger batches to catch up to PPO's performance. Accounting for training compute, critics pay off at small budgets, but their returns diminish at larger budgets.

title: DynaCue: Comparing Motion and Timing Between Groups of Videos
abstract: A score that distinguishes videos with different temporal-consistency ratings can miss differences associated with motion preference. VideoScore's temporal consistency score distinguished higher- from lower-rated Pika videos in 95% of comparisons with 15 videos per group, yet could not detect the difference between preferred videos and their same-prompt alternatives in any of the 200 comparisons of 41 VideoGen-RewardBench pairs. We introduce DynaCue, a two-sample permutation test that combines complementary measurements of motion, frame continuity, and appearance to compare groups of videos without choosing a single cue in advance. DynaCue measures local changes in optical flow both before and after accounting for each clip's usual activity, captures interruptions through frame differences and freeze counts, and incorporates scores for motion and appearance. In controlled experiments, DynaCue detected group differences across five interventions affecting playback continuity, displacement, or rhythm. In real-world evaluations of generated videos where viewers rated temporal consistency or chose which of two videos they preferred for its motion, DynaCue detected group differences in at least 80% of resampled comparisons on each of the three datasets at the smaller sample sizes studied. Every other method evaluated on all three had a detection rate of 60% or less on at least one dataset.

title: When Online Adaptation of Resilience Policies Hurts: Safe Exploration and Measurement Pitfalls in Resilience4j
abstract: Circuit breaker, retry, and bulkhead settings in Java microservices are tuned once and frozen, although the best setting depends on the fault a dependency is currently showing. We study whether an online learner can pick these settings at runtime. AdaptR4j swaps Resilience4j policies atomically in Spring Boot 3 and lets a contextual bandit choose among complete CircuitBreaker/Retry/Bulkhead configurations from Prometheus signals. Our first, naive design scored worse than keeping the default policy in three of four winnable fault scenarios under the reward it optimised: exploring a menu that contained aggressive circuit breakers rejected most traffic while the learner was still learning. Two safeguards fix this: a safe policy menu (no breaker stricter than the latency SLO) and safe exploration with a bounded reward. With them, AdaptR4j beats the production default in every winnable scenario (p < 0.001, three runs each, run-to-run SD <= 0.03), beats the best fixed policy when the fault changes over time, and cuts user-visible failures up to 3.7x compared with the naive design. A context-free bandit on the same safe menu performs statistically indistinguishably, so the safeguards - not the learner - carry most of the benefit. We also report how an earlier version of our harness produced convincing but wrong results: a unit mismatch made every circuit breaker 100x too strict and rejected calls were invisible to the metrics, so 94% of user requests failed while latency and error metrics looked excellent.

title: RoboHarness-RL: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for VLM-Based Robot Manipulation
abstract: Agentic harnesses enable frontier vision-language models (VLMs) to manipulate robots through perception, planning, and control tools, yet achieving comparable performance with compact open-weight VLMs remains challenging. We present RoboHarness-RL, an agentic reinforcement learning framework for improving VLM-based robot manipulation through tool calls. Starting from supervised fine-tuning on successful teacher demonstrations, the VLM further improves through multi-turn reinforcement learning with task-outcome rewards, without relying on vision-language-action models or world action models. To support efficient multi-turn training, we develop LiteHarness, which uses hierarchical memory to keep interaction contexts compact while preserving task performance. With Qwen3.5-9B, RL raises success from 31.2% to 44.0% on RoboTwin 2.0 and from 57.8% to 73.3% on LIBERO-Pro; these gains extend to randomized RoboTwin scenes unseen during training (26.4% to 38.0%). Behavioral analysis further shows that RL reduces repetitive-call rates by up to $4\times$, shortens successful executions, and improves recovery from negative feedback. Project page: https://aim-uofa.github.io/RoboHarness-RL/

title: Learning Agent States for Latent Action Modeling
abstract: Latent action models (LAMs) learn action-like latents from unlabeled video by coupling frame-pair inference with latent-conditioned prediction, enabling policy and world-model pretraining. However, what the latent must explain depends on the representation space used for action inference and transition prediction. When this space entangles the agent's evolving physical state with visual context, such as background and persistent agent appearance, inferred latents can encode information unrelated to the agent's actions. To address this challenge, we propose Agent-State LAM, which jointly learns a compact agent-state representation and latent actions modeling its transitions. The compact state aggregates dense visual features into a shared space for both action inference and forward prediction. To guide what this state retains, we introduce spatially matched temporal discrimination (SMTD), which trains the state to distinguish its source frame from nearby frames through spatially flexible matching with frozen local visual features. Rather than comparing global frame representations, SMTD scores each frame by emphasizing its strongest local feature matches across spatial locations. This scoring allows background and persistent agent appearance to remain matched across frames despite displacement, making these shared cues less informative for identifying the source frame and encouraging the representation to capture the agent's evolving physical state. Extensive experiments on distracting control tasks and six real robot video datasets demonstrate improved action recovery, downstream control, and world-model prediction. Code and checkpoints are available at https://github.com/Mid-Push/Agent-State-LAM.

title: Structure-Aware Transformers for Hierarchical Authorization in Personal AI Agents
abstract: Personal AI agents can carry out complex, multi-step tasks on users' behalf, but doing so often involves numerous permission requests. Manually reviewing each request is time-consuming, while indiscriminate approval poses privacy and security risks. Predicting users' authorization preferences offers a way to reduce this burden while preserving user control. However, authorization prediction is challenging because permission requests are often hierarchical and observed user decisions are sparse and potentially correlated. To address these challenges, We propose the Parent-gated Authorization Transformer for Hierarchies (PATH) to predict users' authorization preferences for personal AI agents. PATH is a novel neural network architecture that combines hierarchy-aware attention masks with a parent-gated probability formulation to ensure hierarchy-consistent predictions. Hierarchy-level embeddings further support learning from sparse observations and patterns shared within each authorization level. We establish finite-sample risk bounds and provide sufficient conditions for consistent authorization probability estimation and algorithmic convergence. Experiments on simulated data, AI-generated user profiles, and real user authorization data demonstrate strong predictive performance with zero hierarchy violations.

title: PFedHASNet: A Personalized Federated Hybrid Analog-Spike Network for Multi-Subject Motor Imagery EEG Decoding
abstract: Motor imagery electroencephalography (MI-EEG) data are often collected and stored separately across subjects or institutions, and EEG acquisition and annotation remain costly. Training models solely on individual subject data limits the use of information from other subjects, whereas centralizing raw EEG recordings raises privacy and data governance concerns. Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without sharing raw EEG data, providing a practical approach to leveraging information from multiple subjects. Accordingly, we propose PFedHASNet, a personalized federated hybrid analog-spike network for MI-EEG decoding. The shared encoder integrates continuous-valued temporal features, leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) spike responses, and channel-wise log-variance statistics through learnable fusion weights. Client-private residual adapters and classifiers perform subject-specific feature refinement and personalized prediction, respectively. Experiments on held-out trials from participating subjects across four public MI-EEG datasets show that PFedHASNet achieves the highest mean client macro-F1 among 18 model configurations in cross-model comparisons, while maintaining competitive decoding performance with a compact client-side model in comparisons using the same backbone. Ablation studies further examine the contributions of hybrid representations and personalization components to decoding performance.

title: DesignEvo: Recovering and Tracking Repository-Level Implemented Design Systems Across Commits
abstract: Modern frontend applications rely on design systems to maintain consistency across pages and releases. However, documentation and component libraries do not fully capture how interface patterns are implemented, reused, and adapted in practice. Existing UI analysis techniques focus on visual defects, interface structure, or element correspondences, providing limited support for automatically recovering and tracking implemented design systems at the repository level. To bridge this gap, we present DesignEvo, which combines screenshots, DOM structure, element geometry, and style values to recover functional UI groups. DesignEvo constrains vision-language model judgments to program-generated candidate regions, aggregates recovered groups and styles into repository-level records, and infers lifecycle states across adjacent commits. We evaluate DesignEvo on 10 open-source repositories comprising 317 page-version instances, 3,478 annotated functional UI groups, and 2,435 lifecycle-state labels. DesignEvo achieves an F1 score of 0.85 for group recovery and an overall lifecycle-state accuracy of 0.84, compared with 0.71 for the strongest lifecycle baseline. Ablations demonstrate the contributions of candidate constraints, functional categories, and style evidence. The resulting records provide structured, traceable evidence of recurring UI patterns and their evolution to support frontend maintenance and change auditing.

title: HuluOPD: Unifying Heterogeneous Medical Specialists into One Lightweight Model with Unlabeled Prompts
abstract: Specialist medical vision-language models (VLMs) are strong within their specialties but hard to unify: their training data are often private, and independently developed specialists cannot be assumed to share an architecture. Deploying these large models separately is costly. We present HuluOPD, an on-policy distillation recipe that unifies heterogeneous specialists into one lightweight VLM using only unlabeled prompts, without requiring reference answers or the specialists' training data. The lightweight model answers each prompt, and the specialist of the prompt's modality supervises its response; a continuation-aligned cross-tokenizer loss makes this possible even when they differ in architecture and tokenizer. We apply HuluOPD to five specialists, for ultrasound, pathology, optical coherence tomography, fundus photography, and dental imaging. To distill and evaluate them, we build HuluOPDCorpus, 914k unlabeled prompts, and HuluOPDBench, 47k held-out test items, from over 90 public datasets, and score all models under one protocol on 132k test items, including third-party benchmarks. A single model with 10% of the five specialists' combined parameters retains 94% of their question-answering performance, and one with 2% retains 89%. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of unifying heterogeneous medical specialist VLMs without requiring their training data or a shared architecture.

title: Beyond Before-and-After Images: Evaluating Temporal Grounding in a Lightweight VLM for Disaster Assessment
abstract: Bi-temporal satellite imagery is central to disaster assessment: deciding what was damaged requires comparing a pre-event scene with its post-event counterpart. A vision-language model (VLM) can nonetheless appear to answer change questions while relying mainly on the post-event image or on the prompt's temporal framing. We present a controlled diagnostic of temporal grounding and apply it to one lightweight VLM, InternVL3-2B, on DisasterM3: 1,659 optical and SAR image pairs from 41 events and nine disaster types, in event-disjoint partitions, with 9,031 reasoning questions. We compare post-only input, the true pre/post pair, the post image repeated twice, reversed image order, and an unrelated pre-event image. The true pair scores $+0.5$ accuracy points above the repeated-post control (95\% paired bootstrap CI $[-0.2, +1.2]$), and reversing the order changes accuracy by $-0.2$ points ($[-0.8, +0.5]$). Under this protocol we therefore find no measurable benefit from the content of the true pre-event image and little sensitivity to temporal order. The model is not blind to the first image, however: the true pair scores $2.5$ points above a pair whose pre-event image comes from another event ($[+1.6, +3.4]$). State-transition and multi-hop questions remain hard, and optical and SAR inputs show different profiles. We outline temporal scene graphs as a testable next step, not a validated solution, and argue that temporal benchmarks for Earth observation should report whether answers depend on the intended evidence, not only how often they are right.

title: IncrementDET: Continual AI-Generated Music Detection via Enrollment
abstract: AI-generated music has become common on music streaming platforms, and listeners often cannot distinguish it from music made by humans. AI-music detection is therefore needed, but detectors trained on a fixed set of generators often fail on unseen generators. As new generators emerge frequently, updating a universal detector, a single model for all generators, typically requires substantial training data and computation, while risking performance degradation on previously learned generators. We therefore introduce IncrementDET, a detector that learns each new generator by a process called enrollment. For each generator, IncrementDET trains one linear classifier, which we call a needle, to separate samples of that generator from a fixed set of human reference tracks. Enrolling a new generator adds one needle while the previously constructed needles remain unchanged. A Sidak correction keeps the overall false-positive rate at its target as needles are added. To compare detectors under these conditions, we define the task of continual AI-generated music detection and introduce a benchmark in which generators arrive one at a time. The benchmark measures the accuracy of a detector before and after each update and the cost of each update. For this benchmark, we also construct EvoMusicFake-17K, a dataset of instrumental music from six recent generators and four human music platforms. Compared with SpecTTTra, a state-of-the-art universal detector, IncrementDET learns a new generator more accurately from only a few samples, generalizes better to unseen generators and better preserves detection performance on previously learned generators, at a substantially lower update cost. The structure of IncrementDET can also be applied to the detection of generated images and video, where new generators are released just as frequently.

title: APQKE-DR: Entropy-Failure Analysis of a Post-Quantum-Initialized Ratcheted Channel
abstract: Long-lived secure channels for embedded and cyber-physical systems (CPSs) must resist quantum attacks and failures in endpoint randomness. While several post-quantum key exchange protocols exist, their security assumes reliable randomness at the endpoint, but this assumption is not always true in embedded devices. In this paper, we introduce the Entropy Attack Suite (EAS) to evaluate secure channels facing endpoint randomness failures, such as low-entropy boot and Random Number Generation (RNG) path subversion. As a case study, we design and implement APQKE-DR, a post-quantum secure channel. Its handshake uses ML-KEM [1] and ML-DSA [2], producing a root key for an X25519 Double Ratchet. We assess the performance of APQKE-DR and security for smart grid communication, and integrate it beneath ANSI C12.22 and DNP3 without altering payload formats. On a Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5, the APQKE handshake exchanges 9,610 bytes with median latencies of 1.99 ms (node) and 0.82 ms (server). The ratcheted channel adds 31 bytes per message. With fresh randomness and ideal cryptographic primitives, ProVerif verifies the modeled secrecy and authentication properties. If randomness fails, EAS can recover the RNG stream and root key from public transcripts. Under RNG-path subversion, a weak generator exposes the root key across sessions. If subversion also affects X25519 keys, attackers may access ratchet keys and plaintexts. TPM seeding prevents early-boot attacks but not later subversion, while measured boot can block modified firmware. Secure deployment thus requires integrity along the entire entropy path, not just strong cryptographic primitives.

title: View Management with Gaussian Placement and Opacity Regularization for Online 3DGS
abstract: The realistic rendering of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has drawn interest from real-time applications that require maps to be built online. This led to coupling 3DGS with SLAM, providing camera poses and initial Gaussians for the map. However, the map is still optimized with designs inherited from conventional SLAM, which train only on keyframes selected for localization and regularize geometry with uncertain frontend depth. These designs overlook the model complexity of a 3DGS map: with millions of parameters but few views of each region, the map overfits to sparse inputs. Resolving this is challenging, as every view and Gaussian added to the map competes for the same real-time budget. We close this gap from both sides. To add views while keyframes preserve the structure of the map, we progressively admit non-keyframe images as mapping updates complete and allocate the limited updates across different groups of frames according to the supervision each group provides. To control the model complexity of the map, edge-guided initialization places new Gaussians where image detail requires them. To complement the uncertain frontend depth, Self-Referenced Opacity Regularization (SOR) uses accumulated rendering evidence, at no extra rendering cost, to suppress the opacity of Gaussians that persistently contribute in front of a map-derived surface reference. Together, these designs improve both the appearance and the geometry of online maps within the real-time budget.

title: Aalen-Johansen as an augmented IPCW estimator
abstract: We show that, in every sample, the widely used Aalen-Johansen estimator of a state occupation probability is an inverse probability of censoring weighted estimator augmented by a working Markov prediction from each subject's current state. This identity explains the robustness of the Aalen-Johansen against departures from the Markov assumption. It also reveals that its influence function differs from the semiparametric efficient one by two orthogonal components: the information in earlier history beyond the current state, and the error of the Markov prediction. Based on this decomposition, we propose a practical, model-free least-squares augmentation of the Aalen-Johansen that regresses the outcome on a history score, narrowing the gap under non-Markov processes without increasing the asymptotic variance. Its advantages are validated both theoretically and in simulations.

title: Environmentally assisted transport in a diamond chain
abstract: We study quantum transport in a diamond chain coupled to Markovian reservoirs at its boundaries. The system is subject to uniform dephasing and an external magnetic field threading a flux $Φ$ per plaquette. We derive exact analytical solutions for $Φ=0$ and $Φ=π$. We show that in the all-bands-flat regime at $Φ=π$, dephasing destroys Aharonov-Bohm caging, leading to environment-assisted quantum transport. Our results demonstrate that coupling a flat-band system to a dissipative environment provides a viable route for controlling transport in regimes where coherent dynamics alone would result in complete localization.

title: The polygonal Weinstock inequality and quantitative stability
abstract: For every integer $N \ge 3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes the perimeter-normalized first positive Steklov eigenvalue $J(P) = |\partial P|σ_1(P)$ among all simple planar polygons $P$ with at most $N$ sides, up to similarity. More generally, if $P$ has $p$ strictly convex vertices and $q$ reflex vertices after merging consecutive collinear sides, then $J(P) \le J(R_{p+\min(q,2)})$, with equality if and only if $q = 0$ and $P$ is similar to $R_p$. Among polygons with at most $N$ sides, restricting to those that are nonconvex or have fewer than $N$ genuine sides lowers the supremum of $J$ by $12πζ(3)N^{-4} + O(N^{-5})$ as $N \to \infty$, with a positive gap for every $N \ge 4$. For convex $p$-gons, the spectral deficit $J(R_p) - J(P)$ controls the normalized squared deviations of support heights, midpoint offsets, and side lengths with weights $1$, $p^{-2}$, and $p^{-3}$, as well as $p^{-3}$ times the sum of squared exterior-angle deviations from $2π/p$; the length weight $p^{-3}$ is sharp. For triangles, the deficit is instead comparable to the square root of the relative area deficit at fixed perimeter, or equivalently to $1 - r$, where $r$ is the singular-value ratio of an affine map from an equilateral triangle. Independently of the number of reflex vertices, a boundary phase identity in arc-length balanced disk coordinates yields the sharp fourth-order bound $2π/J(P) - 1 \ge 2ζ(3)p^{-3} + 8ζ(4)p^{-4} + O(p^{-5})$. For fixed $p$, a degree-$p$ Blaschke transport links this identity to $H^{1/p}$ coercivity for the regularized square root of the conformal derivative, perimeter-concentration rigidity at equally spaced convex prevertices, and quadratic Hausdorff stability for $p \ge 4$.

title: Do Occupancy World Models Really Follow Actions?
abstract: Occupancy world models predict future 3D scenes conditioned on ego actions, yet their predictions may not faithfully follow the specified trajectory under counterfactual actions. Because driving datasets provide sparse coverage of alternative trajectories for each scene, existing models learn the spatial effect of ego motion implicitly from observed scene--trajectory combinations, which may entangle action effects with scene--trajectory correlations. We propose ReCast, an ego-trajectory-guided transformer that grounds future prediction in action-induced geometric correspondence across ego-centric frames. ReCast decouples historical encoding from future decoding and aligns deformable interactions using relative ego transformations, while retaining flexibility for non-rigid scene evolution. We also introduce a counterfactual action-faithfulness benchmark covering in-distribution, tail, and out-of-distribution trajectories. On Occ3D-nuScenes, ReCast achieves competitive standard forecasting performance while improving counterfactual forecasting, with particularly clear gains under out-of-distribution trajectories.

title: An Inverse-Square Gain over Threshold Rounding at Bounded Degree: Reasonable Boolean 2-CSPs and Beyond
abstract: Bounding the number of constraints in which a variable occurs can improve the approximation ratio of semidefinite rounding. For weighted Max-Cut and Max-2-Lin(2) of degree $d$, the known gain over the worst-case ratio is $Ω(1/(d\log d))$ (Buhai, Ghoshal, Huang, Kothari, Lee, Makarychev, and Makarychev, 2027). For binary Boolean CSPs satisfying a geometric condition, the algorithm of Ghoshal, Huang, Lee, Makarychev, and Makarychev (2026) achieves $a+Ω(1/(d^4(\log d)^{7/2}))$, where $a$ is the expected fraction of the total weight satisfied by Gaussian rounding at fixed, bounded thresholds. For weighted Max 2-SAT, the same analysis gives a gain of $Ω(1/(d^2\log d))$ over the worst-case ratio $α_{\rm LLZ}\simeq0.94016567$. We give a randomized polynomial-time algorithm with guarantee $a+Ω(1/d^2)$ under a weaker geometric condition that holds for a strictly larger class of binary instances. For weighted Max 2-SAT we obtain the ratio $α_{\rm LLZ}+Ω(1/d^2)$. To improve a worst-case ratio, only the binary constraints close to equality in the baseline guarantee need to meet the new condition jointly. This gives an inverse-square gain for Max $\{1,2\}$-Horn-SAT and for positive binary disjunctions with unit clauses of either sign, each over its own sharp worst-case ratio (Brakensiek, Huang, and Zwick, 2024).

title: Unifying Partner and Environment Diversity to Improve Human-AI Coordination
abstract: Real-world applications of modern AI systems require generalization to both unseen environments and novel human users. The field of zero-shot coordination (ZSC) has focused primarily on deploying AI to cooperate with novel partners in otherwise familiar environments. Popular population-based methods achieve this by partnering the agent with a diversity of simulated human users during training in a fixed environment, but does not consider the more realistic scenario where both the users and the environment are unseen during training. Recently, training across environments has been explored in training a single self-play agent, which shows better generalization on both novel human users and unseen environments. In this work, we ask whether jointly modeling partner diversity and environment diversity yields stronger coordination with novel partners in novel environments. We introduce Cross Environment Co-Play (CECP), a two-stage framework that first trains a population of self-play agents across a distribution of procedurally generated environments, and then trains a cooperator policy against this partner population. To further couple social and environmental reasoning, we add a next-state prediction module that encourages representations to encode both partner behavior and task structure. We evaluate CECP on both a neuroscience-inspired cooperative foraging task, and the popular ZSC benchmark Overcooked, under held-out partner and held-out environment conditions. CECP achieves the strongest performance among the compared baselines and attains state-of-the-art results under our evaluation protocol for human-AI collaboration. We analyze the model's latent representation encoded by the next-state prediction module, showing it can not only improve the performance of the cooperative AI, but also provide more interpretable latents, demonstrated by the inference of partner skill levels.

title: Provenance-Isolated Epistemic Quorums: Execution-Bound Evidence Certification and Plausible-World Safety Gating in Agentic Control Planes
abstract: Agreement among large language models is not physical evidence for mutating production infrastructure. Because generative models share pretraining priors and conform to peer rationales during deliberation, voting ensembles correlate errors instead of providing independent fault tolerance; yet attaching rigid deterministic checks to unconstrained agent outputs paralyzes incident remediation. We present Provenance-Isolated Epistemic Quorums (PIEQ), an execution-bound certification layer that keeps every language model strictly outside the trusted computing base. PIEQ unifies assumption-based truth maintenance, physical provenance isolation, control-theoretic plausible-world safety shielding, and linearizable concurrency governance around three distinct obligations: certifying diagnostic preconditions from disjoint physical failure domains, gating candidate mutations across all unrefuted fault worlds while falling back to read-only diagnostic probes under ambiguity, and binding admission certificates to target execution through snapshot barriers, revision checks, authorization freshness, trusted temporal-precondition policies, and capability-tiered enforcement. Across formal guarantees, automated etcd fault suites, frozen software benchmarks, and live language-model runs, PIEQ achieves zero within-assumption unsafe admissions and zero false-precondition commits, converting occasional agent proof omissions into recoverable false blocks rather than unsafe actions. On a physical PostgreSQL/Patroni cluster, PIEQ gates supervised failovers alongside Patroni and etcd's native split-brain protection and enforces a full Tier E2 contract inside a single serializable PostgreSQL transaction for bounded capacity reservations. All benchmarks are author-labeled, live model snapshots are unpinned, and Tier E2 physical failover promotion as well as multi-host hardware fault isolation remain open work.

title: Scale-Robust and Global-Aware Representation Learning for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: Multivariate time series anomaly detection (MTSAD) is an essential task for identifying abnormal system behaviors and supporting reliable operations across diverse real-world applications. Despite substantial advances in MTSAD, two key challenges in representation learning remain underexplored: (C1) how to learn scale-robust temporal representations that capture anomalies across different temporal scales and (C2) how to learn global-aware relational representations that capture inter-series dependencies by incorporating series-level global characteristics beyond local windows. To address these challenges, we propose STAGER, a novel method that jointly learns two complementary representations: scale-robust temporal and global-aware relational representations. Specifically, STAGER employs (1) a scale-robust temporal encoder that constructs a multi-scale temporal directed acyclic graph (DAG) to learn scale-robust temporal representations and (2) a global-aware relational encoder that incorporates learnable series-level global embeddings into the temporal representations and models inter-series relationships through graph neural networks. Two complementary auxiliary objectives further enhance the distinctiveness of the global embeddings. Extensive experiments on three real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that STAGER achieves the best average rank among ten evaluated MTSAD methods across three evaluation metrics. Ablation and sensitivity analyses validate the effectiveness of the proposed components and auxiliary objectives, while efficiency evaluations demonstrate that STAGER achieves a favorable trade-off between detection performance and inference time compared with existing methods.

title: BodyWeave: Native Body-Conditioned 3D Garment Generation
abstract: Generating 3D garments for digital characters requires preserving a reference design while adapting the garment to the target body's shape and pose. Sewing-pattern methods can struggle to reproduce unfamiliar designs and fine details, while image-to-3D generators offer rich shape priors but typically lack explicit 3D body context. We present \textbf{BodyWeave}, a framework that unifies garment generation and fitting through native 3D body conditioning. Building on 3D generative priors, BodyWeave uses the body as a spatial reference throughout geometry generation: a \textbf{Global Body Adapter} guides garment placement and extent in the shared coordinate frame, while \textbf{Local Body Attention} guides surface refinement using nearby body geometry. A \textbf{Surface Penetration Loss} supervises decoded surfaces to reduce body intersections, and the resulting geometry conditions material synthesis to produce garments with physically based rendering attributes. To support learning across designs and wearers, we construct \textbf{GarmentWeave3D} with 293K aligned garment--body observations, including 114K same-design cross-body pairs. Evaluations on out-of-domain \textbf{Artist-Created Garments} demonstrate high geometric fidelity and low body penetration. Cross-body evaluations demonstrate accurate adaptation to new wearers with consistent garment--body spacing, while appearance comparisons show faithful fabric reproduction. Additional results and resources are available at https://gavin-jy.github.io/bodyweave-page/

title: DeCo-Attention: Decompose to Compensate for Low-Precision Attention
abstract: Self-attention over tens of thousands of tokens dominates the generation time of video diffusion transformers, because its cost grows quadratically with sequence length. The FP4 matrix products of modern GPUs can speed up attention, but the 4-bit rounding of the queries Q and the keys K introduces large errors. We show that the exponential in softmax amplifies the error of their product QK, which therefore dominates the attention error. We propose DeCo-Attention, a co-design of algorithm and system for low-precision attention. DeCo-Attention is training-free and compensates the rounding error of Q and K along a few principal directions found by a per-head eigendecomposition. The lightweight compensation terms are appended to Q and K as extra channels, so the FP4 matrix product corrects its own rounding error while it computes the attention scores. Once the products run in FP4, the softmax bounds the kernel, and we optimize the softmax so that the gain of FP4 computation translates into realized speedup. With QK in FP4, we implement DeCo-Attention with the rest of attention in FP8 on GB300 and VR200 and in FP4 on RTX PRO 6000. On Wan2.2, these kernels run 2.13x, 2.49x, and 2.82x faster than BF16 attention, and the whole generation runs 1.55x, 1.68x, and 1.80x faster. On four video generation models, the FP8 configuration achieves LPIPS comparable to prior 8-bit QK methods, and the fully FP4 configuration lower LPIPS than prior fully 4-bit kernels.

title: Eliminating Incompatibility in Quantum Multiparameter Estimation with Antiparallel Probes
abstract: The simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters is fundamentally constrained by complementarity and measurement incompatibility, which limits the sensitivity of quantum measurement devices by preventing the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) from being saturated. We show that antiparallel probe configurations can overcome this limitation when the dynamics of the parameter encoding preserve the said configurations. We characterise the quantum channels that satisfy this requirement and establish conditions under which such configurations exist and can saturate the SLD-CRB without compromising the quantum Fisher information, leading to a metrological advantage. For qubit probes, we prove that this advantage is present if and only if the encoding channel is unital. We extend this analysis to the two probe, finite dimensional qudit case by considering derivative reversal and transpose map based probe states, as well as more general multiprobe configurations. For each of these cases, we identify conditions under which an advantage exists. Our results establish connections between channel symmetries, probe configurations and the attainability of multiparameter precision limits.

title: Online Environment Repair for Coding Agents
abstract: Programmatic verifiers provide scalable reward signals for training coding agents with reinforcement learning, yet subtle harness defects and incomplete unit tests allow policies to earn full credit without solving the intended task. Existing training-time defenses intervene either by penalizing suspicious outputs or by filtering flagged tasks and rollouts. However, output penalties leave the underlying verifier exploitable, driving policies to disguise shortcuts under reasoning monitors or zeroing out valid solutions under detector false positives, whereas task and rollout filtering discards or mutes the hardest problems where shortcuts emerge earliest. Pre-training verifier hardening repairs the environment directly, but misses vulnerability classes that surface only as the policy improves during reinforcement learning. In this paper, we propose online environment repair, which leaves triggering rollout rewards unchanged to remove hiding incentives and asynchronously patches exploited environments during training. Candidate repairs triggered by execution invariants or differential fuzzing are deployed only after passing three automated validation gates that block the exploit while preserving valid solutions, canceling detector false positives and enabling structural propagation across repositories without scaffold labels or reference solutions. Across 20 controlled GRPO experiments on heterogeneous software-engineering repositories, online environment repair reduces cumulative reward hacking from 36.9% to 0.06% and improves held-out Pass@8 from 21.7% to 46.7%, consistently outperforming reward-penalty, rollout-filtering, and static-hardening baselines while eliminating zero-shot exploitation on unseen loophole classes.

title: Exact Response Theory based on Karhunen-Loève Expansions for Brownian Oscillators
abstract: We extend Exact Response Theory (ERT) to an overdamped Brownian oscillator driven by thermal white noise. The stochastic forcing is represented by a Karhunen--Loève series and embedded into an autonomous, augmented phase space using a harmonic auxiliary phase. This representation allows us to construct the ERT dissipation function for fixed mode amplitudes and recover stochastic averages by averaging over the amplitudes and the initial phase. For the variance, we derive the response at finite spectral truncation and show analytically that, with uniform phase sampling, the full-spectrum white-noise limit reproduces the generator-based result for a sudden temperature change. Furthermore, a comparison with first-order linear response theory highlights how this may fail in general. In particular, if the noise-induced variance is quadratic in the noise amplitude, it is completely omitted by linear response. The analysis provides a framework for this model and for studying more general forcing; extensions to non-Markovian dynamics require separate convergence and regularity analyses.

title: FlashQLA: Efficient Context Parallelism for Gated DeltaNet
abstract: Gated DeltaNet (GDN) achieves linear computational complexity through recurrent state updates, but sequential dependencies between chunks limit parallelism, particularly for long-context workloads with small batch sizes or limited head-level parallelism per GPU. We present FlashQLA, a context-parallel execution framework for GDN that exposes additional sequence-level parallelism while reducing boundary-state preprocessing overhead. FlashQLA reduces boundary-state preprocessing overhead through decay-aware preparation and extends sequence parallelism across GPUs with Dual CP, which shares summary computation across parallelism levels. Workload-adaptive Auto CP and CP-aware kernel co-design further improve execution efficiency. FlashQLA achieves $1.7\times$-$3.1\times$ forward speedup and up to $4.4\times$ backward speedup over Flash Linear Attention (FLA) on a single GPU. On eight GPUs with context lengths up to 1M tokens, Dual CP achieves up to $4.8\times$ forward speedup and $4.4\times$ speedup for combined forward and backward execution over FLA KCP.

title: Active road noise control using networked mean-square learning and lightweight conditional compensation experts
abstract: Multichannel active road noise control (ARNC) requires effective noise reduction (NR) under causality and computational constraints. A computationally efficient method is proposed that separates linear control from condition-dependent nonlinear residual compensation. A finite impulse response (FIR) baseline filter is obtained through networked mean-square learning that can be made adaptive, while a multi-resolution FIR mixture-of-experts (MRF-MoE) module provides possibly nonlinear corrections. Training comprises baseline initialization, sample-graph-regularized expert and router optimization, and joint refinement. Target channels are treated as nodes in a connected network for mean-square error minimization, whereas training windows define a graph for regularizing routing probabilities. Each expert combines short-time dense and long-tail low-rank FIR filtering, and causal single-expert routing reduces inference computation. Compared with WaveNet-VNN under the same configuration, the proposed method reduces estimated inference cost by 96.3% while achieving higher NR on the test set.

title: Spec-CoFrGeNet: Reparametrizing Continued Fraction Networks for Stable and Accurate Training
abstract: Continued fractions have been shown to be a function class capable of constructing expressive yet parameter-efficient neural networks. These neural networks are not only effective for supervised learning, but also for training LLMs. However, the rational form of this function class introduces poles when the denominator approaches zero, which prior work has avoided by enforcing a small positive (non-smooth) lower bound. We show that performance and training stability can be highly sensitive to the choice of this lower bound. In this work, we introduce a novel transformation of the partial denominators, inspired by its connection to the Green's function in physics, that mitigates the above issue elegantly by constraining the spectra of the constructed tridiagonal Hamiltonian. Our approach further eliminates the need for incremental training used by previous works for stability, thus avoiding involved modifications to standard pre-training procedures. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our reparameterization by replacing FFNs with a previously proposed continued fraction architecture for both language and image generative modeling. Across diverse models, such as GPT-2 XL, (nano) Llama-MoE, and Granite, we show that our proposed method achieves performance comparable to the original (FFN-based) architectures while maintaining ~30%-50% parameter savings as before, and in most cases even outperforms the more complicated incremental training baseline. We further demonstrate, for the first time for continued fraction networks, that their effectiveness also carries over to image generative modeling, that utilize diffusion objectives. On a state-of-the-art Diffusion Transformer, we show that our approach again achieves performance comparable to the original FFN-based models with ~30% parameter savings and significantly outperforms the previous incremental training approach.

title: Instant LiDAR: Feed-Forward Gaussian Reconstruction for LiDAR Simulation
abstract: LiDAR reconstruction supports closed-loop autonomous driving simulation, but hours of per-scene optimization make large asset libraries costly to build and maintain. We present Instant LiDAR, a feed-forward pipeline that reconstructs multiple LiDAR scans as reusable Gaussian assets in minutes without per-scene optimization. LiDAR measurements provide strong geometric priors, but directly initializing Gaussians from them yields poor reconstruction due to nonuniform sampling and a limited field of view. Sparse returns leave surface gaps, while combining scans expands coverage but introduces redundant primitives. To address these challenges, Instant LiDAR combines measurement-anchored Gaussian prediction, sampling-aware Gaussian scales, and multi-frame consolidation. The predictor refines attributes anchored to recorded returns, while the scales adapt spatial support to LiDAR sampling. Multi-frame consolidation merges overlapping predictions into a compact asset spanning the driving log. Compared with NuRec, Instant LiDAR reconstructs scenes approximately 46 times faster on Physical AI (PAI) and 70 times faster on Waymo. It also achieves comparable downstream 3D detection accuracy on Waymo.

title: A Unit-Gradient Neural Variational Method for Anisotropic Eikonal Equations
abstract: We develop a variational neural method for computing viscosity solutions of the anisotropic eikonal equation. Building on the vanishing-viscosity principle, we minimize an energy functional whose Euler--Lagrange equation is the viscous anisotropic eikonal equation and introduce an auxiliary variable for the gradient, enforcing the constraint through a penalty. A key challenge in this formulation is to handle nonlinearity of the functional while controlling the interaction between the viscosity and penalty parameters. To address this challenge, we impose a unit-norm constraint on the auxiliary variable exactly, as prescribed by the eikonal equation. This removes the gradient from the exponentially weighted part of the functional and allows the viscosity and penalty limits to be studied separately. We establish two convergence results. First, for each fixed viscosity parameter $ε>0$, we prove convergence to the viscosity solution as the penalty parameter $λ\rightarrow\infty$. Second, for the distance function to the boundary of a convex or smooth domain, we prove convergence as $ε\rightarrow0$ for any fixed $λ>0$. The latter result motivates our stable numerical strategy, which keeps $λ$ fixed while decreasing $ε$ whenever the training loss stagnates. The formulation is implemented using a neural network that satisfies the unit-norm constraint by construction and a mesh-free approach that evaluates the singularly scaled functional at randomly sampled points without requiring mesh refinement as $ε\to0$. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the method on diverse isotropic and anisotropic problems, including three-dimensional open-surface reconstruction from point clouds.

title: CHORAL: A Multi-Agent Scaffold for Longitudinal Prognostic Reasoning from Patient-Generated Health Data
abstract: Longitudinal patient-generated health data can inform prognostic reasoning about how patients' conditions may evolve between follow-up visits. Existing approaches summarize trajectories or predict symptom states, but provide limited support for examining how heterogeneous evidence informs prognosis. We present CHORAL, a multi-agent scaffold that forms domain-specific appraisals before cross-domain synthesis and review, preserving evidence and revisions. Informed by a formative study with 12 psychiatrists, we evaluated CHORAL quantitatively and with 22 clinicians. CHORAL achieved balanced accuracy comparable to persistence (0.673 vs. 0.672), while detecting 40% of LOW-to-HIGH deterioration cases missed by persistence. Versus a single-agent baseline, it improved balanced accuracy from 0.639 to 0.673 and evidence coverage from 70.1% to 89.2%. Clinicians rated CHORAL significantly higher for evidence appraisal, alternative interpretations, grounds for challenge, and distinguishing what to rely on from what required verification. These findings show how multi-agent deliberation can support review by exposing alternative interpretations and grounds for verification.

title: SegPFN: Training-Free In-Context Segmentation with Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Networks
abstract: In-context segmentation (ICS) uses one or a few annotated reference images to specify what to segment in a target image. Existing training-free ICS approaches typically rely on manually designed inference procedures, which may limit how flexibly reference information is combined. Learned in-context inference offers an adaptive alternative, but acquiring this capability through segmentation-specific training can compromise generalization to unseen domains. We therefore ask: can a pretrained in-context learner infer what to segment from annotated references without segmentation-specific training? We introduce SegPFN, a training-free framework that reformulates ICS as tabular classification over frozen visual features. A frozen tabular prior-data fitted network (PFN) uses labeled reference patches as context to classify patches in the target image. We comprehensively benchmark SegPFN against major existing ICS methods across 11 datasets spanning semantic, part, and personalized segmentation. SegPFN improves overall mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) by 4.7 points over the strongest overall baseline and achieves the highest average mIoU in four of five task-shot settings. Further analyses show that hard-negative reference patches improve fine-grained target discrimination, while joint conditioning enables SegPFN to use multiple references effectively. These results show that SegPFN offers a simple and effective paradigm for training-free in-context segmentation.

title: From Rule-based to Agentic: LLM Agent based Real-time Control of Urban Drainage Systems for Flooding and Sewer Overflow Mitigation
abstract: Real-time control (RTC) for urban drainage systems (UDS) remains hampered by sparse in-network sensing. While heterogeneous multi-modal meteorological early warnings often contain decision-critical information for UDS RTC, none of the existing approaches can exploit such externally-sourced information within the control workflow. Here we introduce AgenticAI-Control, an agentic artificial intelligence framework able to assimilate multi-source meteorological early warnings in RTC. Two coupled large language model agents are integrated to generate control strategies by retrieving meteorological early-warnings and fusing them with domain engineering expertise. Validated via simulation studies of a combined sewer catchment in eastern China across 10 real-world rainfall events, the AgenticAI-Control achieved 69.1-90.6% reduction in aggregated flood and overflow volumes compared to the rule-based baseline control. Rigorously standardized prompt engineering and modular workflow constraints substantially compress performance disparities among four distinct LLMs. Our work establishes AgenticAI as a viable tool to unify multi-source meteorological monitoring and practitioner domain knowledge, surmounting longstanding monitoring limitations of UDS RTC and delivering cost-efficient, robust intelligent control solutions for sensor-sparse sewer infrastructures.

title: Machine-Learning-Assisted Hybrid Cooling of a Raspberry Pi 5
abstract: Thermal management is a critical challenge in compact computing platforms operating under sustained high computational loads. Elevated processor temperatures can lead to thermal throttling, degraded performance, and reduced reliability. This study develops and experimentally evaluates a smart hybrid heat sink that integrates passive thermal energy storage with active cooling for sustained device operation. The proposed design comprises an aluminum cavity containing paraffin wax as a phase change material (PCM) embedded within a copper foam and integrated with an adaptively controlled fan. Fan operation is guided by a Random Forest regression model trained on experimentally measured CPU temperature data to predict future CPU temperatures. The predicted temperature is then used to support the adaptive fan control strategy. The heat sink is mounted directly on the CPU of a Raspberry Pi 5 and experimentally evaluated under an extreme CPU workload of approximately 99 percent CPU utilization. The performance of the proposed hybrid system is compared against two benchmark scenarios: passive cooling using PCM embedded in copper foam and a commercial Raspberry Pi 5 active cooler. The proposed heat sink demonstrates superior thermal performance to both benchmarks, achieving peak CPU temperature reductions of approximately 9 C relative to the PCM-copper foam configuration and 6 C relative to the commercial active cooler.

title: Minimizing Total Busy Time with Bounded Parallelism: A $3/2$-Approximation for Parallelism Two and a Forest Characterization for General Parallelism
abstract: We study the minimum total busy time problem: jobs with fixed processing intervals must be assigned to identical machines, each of which can process at most g jobs at a time, so that the total time during which the machines are busy is minimized. The problem is NP-hard already for g=2, and, to the best of our knowledge, no approximation ratio below 2 was known for general instances with g=2, where the ratio 2 is attained by giving every job its own machine. We present a combinatorial 3/2-approximation algorithm for g=2. The algorithm applies the two-phase local-ratio technique to the known pair formulation of the problem, processing the overlapping job pairs in order of the right ends of their overlaps. The cost of its schedule is at most $L-λ/2$, where L is the total processing time and $λ$ is the optimal value of the linear relaxation of the pair formulation; hence the integrality gaps of this relaxation and of the configuration LP are at most 3/2. The result extends to temporal bin packing with items larger than one third of the bin capacity. For general g, we show that optimal schedules correspond exactly to maximum-weight forests of a special kind, which we call g-caterpillar forests; this yields an exact integer program and a linear relaxation of polynomial size for every fixed g. We also observe that securing a (1-1/g) fraction of the optimal savings suffices for a (2-1/g)-approximation. On random instances with g=2, evaluated with exact optima or tight lower bounds obtained from the pair formulation, the average ratio of the algorithm to the optimum is at most 1.075 for 100 jobs and at most 1.070 for 200 jobs.

title: The Anatomy of Piecewise-Linear Learned Indexes
abstract: Piecewise-linear approximation (PLA) learned indexes (PGM-index, FITing-Tree, RadixSpline, PLEX, PLIN) compress sorted keys into $\pm\varepsilon$ segments, yet prior theory stops at coarse $Θ(\varepsilon^2)$ single-segment bounds. At the bottom layer, optimal greedy PLA covers $κ_{\rm opt}\varepsilon^2/v_0 \approx 3.54\,\varepsilon^2/v_0$ keys per segment on independent gaps and $κ_{\rm opt}\varepsilon^2$ under any smooth density ($v_0=1$), while anchored and chord fitters retain $Θ(\varepsilon^2/v_0)$ coverage. Across recursive layers, a law-of-large-numbers heuristic--invoked to claim $O(\log\log n)$ height for the PGM-index--suggests summing $Θ(\varepsilon^2)$ gaps averages out fluctuations. We prove this fails under Endpoint Promotion (EP): stopping-time fluctuations reset relative gap variance at every depth, locking fanout at $C_\varepsilon \approx 19.861\,\varepsilon^2$, expected height at $\log n/\log C_\varepsilon + O(1)$, and lookup at $Θ(\log n)$. To break this barrier, Rank-Equispaced Promotion (RE) samples pivots at equal rank strides. Each stride sums a fixed number of base gaps, so relative variance decays across layers and cumulative coverage squares at each step. Expected height drops to $\log_2\log_\varepsilon n + O(1)$ on independent gaps and $\log_2\log_\varepsilon n + \log_2^+(\log n/\log(\varepsilon/δ)) + O(1)$ on smooth densities with curvature $δ$. A compact bucket directory routes across unaligned RE pivots with $<1$ extra comparison per layer on average, giving RE-PGM $O(\log\varepsilon \cdot \log\log_\varepsilon n)$ expected lookup in $Θ(n/\varepsilon^2)$ space and $O(n)$ build time without radix skew sensitivity. Our constants match empirical fanout within $0.3\%$ down to $\varepsilon=2$, and all core theorems are formalized in Lean 4.

title: Do Clinician-Scored Examples Help LLMs Code ADOS-2 from Hour-Long Transcripts?
abstract: Large language models can apply a written rubric to a transcript, making automated coding of the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS-2) look within reach. A common way to align such a rater with clinicians is to show it expert-scored examples, but whether correct labels improve agreement is rarely tested. We test this for eight speech-based items of hour-long ADOS-2 Module 3 sessions from 48 children, with one local model and a pre-registered, placebo-controlled design. We compare few-shot scoring, an anchored comparison in which the model only judges a child better, similar or worse than scored anchors and a fixed rule gives the score, post-hoc calibration, protocol-based evidence routing and direct scoring of the full transcript. On 40 held-out children, agreement with clinicians was modest, with quadratic weighted kappa between 0.22 and 0.30. Replacing every example's label with a wrong one changed about a third of the few-shot predictions, more often towards the corrupted labels than chance, but did not lower agreement, 0.25 with correct and 0.23 with wrong labels. A larger second model did the same. The anchored comparison did not improve on few-shot scoring, its cross-child judgements were no more accurate than those implied by absolute scores, and routing did not help. Among the registered, uncalibrated arms, direct scoring of the full transcript agreed best at 0.30. Exploratory follow-up analyses found that the model's graded judgements ranked children better than its final scores, that existing batch calibration raised agreement to 0.46 on the same children, and that in controlled synthetic sessions scoring episodes separately did not beat calibrated whole-transcript scoring. Expert-scored examples do not by themselves calibrate model-based clinical raters, and claims of calibration or added pipeline complexity need corrupted-label controls and strong baselines.

title: An extended Matsumoto--Yor property for free GIG distributions
abstract: We prove a two-parameter extension of the Matsumoto--Yor property for free generalized inverse Gaussian distributions. The transformation is the reciprocal form of a known matrix Yang--Baxter map. Our proof combines the independence-preserving property for matrix generalized inverse Gaussian distributions with asymptotic freeness. Since the relevant spectra stay in compact subsets of the positive half-line, continuous functional calculus and polynomial approximation suffice to handle all inverses. The same argument yields the free Matsumoto--Yor property itself for all positive rates of the free Poisson law, including those for which this law has an atom at zero. We also discuss the limit in which one of the two parameters tends to zero: the limiting laws are free Poisson only when the rate is at least one, so for smaller rates this limit does not recover the free Matsumoto--Yor property.

title: Full Support For the Degree-Zero Hitchin Morphism
abstract: We present a draft argument for the full-support conjecture for the canonical GLn Hitchin morphism in degree zero over a smooth complex projective curve of genus at least two. The whole-base Ngô support equality yields a finite necessary classification in terms of weighted products of maximal equigeneric spectral-factor families. We study their generic nodality, develop moving-cycle arguments for arbitrary multiplicities, and give an intersection calculation using generalized parabolic presentations and intrinsic Nash transforms. We relate the full-base Ngô string to the BPS formula for intersection Hodge numbers in every rank and give the genus-two rank-three Hodge table. The arguments developed here are presented for mathematical checking and revision by the authors. And the article is generated by ChatGPT, the author is trying his best to comprehense the article and the human's version is coming soon.

title: EffectWAM: Learning Action-Grounded Effects for Robot Manipulation
abstract: World-action models connect visual prediction with executable robot control. We present EffectWAM, which develops this connection through three complementary components: Effect, camera positional encoding (CaPE), and Action Grounding. Effect represents visual change as the difference between independently encoded future observations and a shared current-observation anchor. CaPE conditions endpoint pooling on relative camera pose when reliable extrinsics are available, while sharing the same learned parameters with pose-free pooling for uncalibrated trajectories. Action Grounding trains the visual representation to retain measured changes in end-effector pose and gripper state. An exponential moving average of the observation encoder supplies Effect targets. A shared generation expert learns to jointly predict Effect and an executable action chunk through flow matching, and reuses the sampled pair to generate future video on demand. This allows the controller to execute actions without waiting for video synthesis. We train on more than 20,000 hours of heterogeneous embodied data, excluding unused chain-of-thought data, and accommodate dataset-specific joint, end-effector, and hand-pose representations. Our evaluation uses the Small (8B) configuration on all five benchmarks and additionally evaluates the Large (26B) configuration on RoboDojo. Experiments examine closed-loop manipulation across complementary benchmarks, and comparisons across multiple baseline policies show consistent improvements from Action Grounding.

title: SurgGenesis: A Generative Surgical World Model for Future-Aware Surgical Understanding
abstract: Surgical scene understanding is constrained by data scarcity and long-tail class imbalance, as annotating surgical videos demands scarce clinical expertise while rare procedural events remain underrepresented. We tackle this through data generation and propose SurgGenesis, a generative surgical world model that learns future surgical state transitions in a latent space from visual observations and textual procedural descriptions, serving as a scalable surgical data engine. To adapt a large-scale video diffusion model to the data-scarce surgical domain without catastrophic forgetting, we introduce a three-stage progressive LoRA strategy that incrementally injects endoscopic visual priors, procedural semantics, and spatial motion cues. Rather than judging generation by visual fidelity alone, we validate SurgGenesis along two axes that separate a world model from a generic generator: (i) future-awareness, by comparing predicted futures against the real future through a GT-latent prediction gap and temporal-horizon analysis, and (ii) action-faithful usefulness, by checking that generated clips contain the commanded surgical triplet and that using them to rebalance long-tail events and drive downstream understanding (segmentation, triplet recognition, 3D reconstruction) yields action-specific gains. Conditioned futures therefore complement conventional long-tail sampling. Code: https://zh-qr.github.io/SurgGenesis

title: More Powerful, Less Verifiable? Mitigating Hard-to-Verify Hallucinations in MLLM's Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) strengthens model capabilities through feedback from humans and environments. However, emerging evidence suggests that reward optimization can produce outputs whose errors are harder for humans to detect. To address this issue, we construct ITHV (the Image-Text Hallucination Verifiability Dataset), comprising 2,728 visually grounded instances that distinguish between obvious hallucinations, which humans readily detect, and elusive hallucinations, which humans struggle to identify. We then propose DAPO-V, an extension of DAPO that maximizes correctness subject to a budget on verifiability-aware risk. Specifically, DAPO-V combines a verifiability-aware reward with adaptive dual control, where larger penalties are assigned to incorrect responses on questions with lower human verification accuracy. An adaptive multiplier further adjusts the penalty strength according to risk-budget violations. Across three MLLM base models, DAPO-V improves overall accuracy while substantially improving accuracy on elusive hallucination questions by 5.78--9.72 percentage points over accuracy-only DAPO. We further test DAPO-V with a blinded human study, which shows that hallucinations are more readily detected in DAPO-V than those of the base model.

title: Model Order Detection with Parameter Estimation Guarantees for the Matrix Pencil Method
abstract: Detecting the model order and estimating the parameters of sums of damped complex exponentials in noise is challenging when poles are closely spaced, the sample size is small, or the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is low. We propose REECAP, a matrix pencil (MP) algorithm for joint model order detection and pole estimation. The algorithm computes candidate poles using an overestimated working rank and classifies them using a score derived from their associated eigenvectors. The model order is then estimated by counting the retained candidates. The score measures the eigenvector energy concentration in coordinates corresponding to the dominant right singular subspace of the data Hankel matrix. Under a suitable rank condition, we derive a deterministic sufficient condition guaranteeing that a candidate whose score exceeds a certain threshold lies within a prescribed tolerance of at least one signal pole. This establishes a theoretical connection between eigenvector energy concentration and pole-estimation accuracy. Extensive simulations demonstrate improved model order detection and frequency estimation performance relative to conventional MP order detection methods, recent structure-aware MP methods, and information-theoretic criteria (ITC), across a broad range of scenarios, including clustered frequencies, low SNR in the threshold region, and small sample sizes. Runtime comparisons further demonstrate substantial computational savings, and moderate sensitivity to noise model mismatch, compared to the evaluated structure-aware and information-theoretic methods.

title: Generalized Tensor Parallelism: Powering Trillion-Parameter LLM Training at 10+ EFLOP/s
abstract: Pretraining state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) with up to trillions of parameters is memory- and compute-intensive. Existing parallelization schemes compromise on either per-GPU memory or throughput: data parallelism replicates parameters; tensor parallelism and fully sharded data parallelism (FSDP) add communication of activations and parameters, respectively, to every microbatch; and pipeline parallelism leaves GPUs idle while the pipeline fills and drains. We show that, for linear layers, five commonly used parallelisms (data, tensor, sequence, context parallelism and FSDP) are special cases of one framework, generalized tensor parallelism (GTP), in which each layer's parameters and activations are partitioned and either can be re-materialized with an all-gather before use. In GTP, a parameter all-gather is an optional preprocessing step on one input of a matrix multiplication (GEMM), whereas FSDP implementations typically treat it as a step before an entire Transformer block, which can increase memory footprint and delay GEMMs. The GTP view lets us schedule all-gathers per GEMM rather than per block, issuing each early enough to hide its communication but late enough to limit memory.
