abstract: In this paper, we formulate conjectural formulas for the arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori level structure. We first introduce a framework for formulating Kudla-Rapoport conjectures: we develop the theory of weighted representation densities and special cycles for general parahoric level structures, prove dimension-reduction formulas on both the analytic and geometric sides and duality relations for special cycles. We then formulate the Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for Iwahori level structures based on these properties. Finally, we prove the conjecture when $n=2$.

title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
abstract: We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$. These elements form a basis. In every reachable seed chart, every Gauss valuation takes a nonzero basis expansion to the minimum of its values on the nonzero summands. Suppose the algebra has Laurent coefficients and smooth spectrum over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After setting the curve parameters to one, we compute theta products on the intrinsic mirror from the exchange polynomials and give a finite presentation of the mirror algebra. A seed has a polynomial corner if each exchange polynomial can be multiplied by a unit of the coefficient ring to give a polynomial with constant term one. At such a corner, order the exponents by a weight with strictly positive, rationally independent coordinates. For every lattice exponent $a$ and integral weight $p$, the theta function indexed by $p$ has least $a$-weight $\min_{b\in Q_a}\langle b,p\rangle$ in the corresponding mirror chart. This reciprocity holds for cyclic exchanges and arbitrary pole orders. For fixed exchange supports and constant terms one, we determine when the mirror is smooth and the second mirror recovers the original algebra in the chosen torus coordinates. The coefficient tuples for which both conditions hold form a computable finite set. All their entries are positive integers.

title: Breaking Routing And Inter-device Dependencies in Mixture-of-Experts
abstract: As Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models scale, Expert Parallelism (EP) becomes increasingly important for distributing experts across devices. However, the resulting token dispatch and combine operations can become a major bottleneck during inference. Overlapping these communication phases with computation is constrained by the sequential dependencies of standard MoE architectures. We introduce BRAID-MoE, an architecture that pairs laddered residual connections with early routing to relax these dependencies. Laddered residuals enable each expert combine to be deferred to the following block, while early routing computes the next routing decision from the pre-combine residual, with experts still receiving the updated post-combine hidden state. This creates an extended communication window in which the preceding combine and next dispatch can execute back-to-back on a dedicated communication stream, overlapping attention computation. On Qwen3-shaped MoEs with 0.4B-A0.1B and 2.5B-A0.5B parameters, BRAID closely matches sequential training at matched compute, with validation-loss increases of only 1% and 0.5%, respectively. We further demonstrate that existing MoE checkpoints can be adapted to BRAID with limited additional training, largely recovering their original accuracy. On a converted Qwen3-30B-A3B model, BRAID achieves speedups of up to 1.29$\times$ in prefill and 1.37$\times$ in decode, and at least 1.12$\times$ across diverse workloads and EP configurations on one or two four-H100 nodes. It outperforms competing overlap strategies in all tested settings, with the strongest gains when communication is a major latency bottleneck and its duration approaches the available computation window. These results demonstrate that early routing enables more effective communication-computation overlap in MoE inference at a modest cost in model quality.

title: Boiling Down Uncertainty: Deep Generative Scenario Search with Decision-Guided Evolution Strategies for Two-Stage Stochastic Optimization
abstract: One of the most common models for handling uncertainty is two-stage stochastic programming. Choosing the right number of scenarios is a trade-off between the uncertainty that can be represented and computational cost. A recent method, Deep Generative Scenario Search, generates synthetic scenarios and improves them by learning from the decisions they induce. The original approach used a black-box gradient estimate, since decisions are piecewise constant across scenarios. This paper provides the missing analytical foundation by deriving the gradient in closed form from recourse duality and an adjoint solve of the regularized reduced problem. The decision-focused direction, with a heuristic direction as a backup when duals are unavailable, defines the sampling subspace of a guided evolution strategy rather than being used as a direct update. For any guiding subspace, the expected update is a descent direction of the smoothed objective, so an inaccurate guide adds variance while the expected step still descends. For six problem families, both guided estimators outperform the baseline. The decision-focused version reduces the mean gap by three-quarters, and on the two families with the most integer variables the reduced sets beat the exact solver's two-hour incumbent in most runs, using a fifth of the time.

title: Propagation-tunable fractional Stokes skyrmions in conical refraction
abstract: Conical refraction in a biaxial crystal generates Stokes textures whose finite-domain skyrmion number takes fractional values tunable through free-space propagation, while the underlying azimuthal winding remains unchanged. For a circularly polarised Gaussian input, the skyrmion number is governed by the boundary Stokes parameter, $N_\mathrm{sk}=[1-s_3(R_\mathrm{cut},Z)]/2$. Six-state polarimetry reveals fractional values of 0.523, 0.565 and 0.266 in the Lloyd, Poggendorff and Raman regions, respectively, in close agreement with Belsky-Khapalyuk-Berry predictions of 0.530, 0.550 and 0.250, and reproduces the predicted longitudinal evolution. Conical refraction thus provides a passive route to propagation-tunable fractional Stokes skyrmions, in which continuously evolving polarisation geometry coexists with a fixed topological winding.

title: Convolution Algebras of Generalized Preprojective Algebras and Kac-Moody Positive Parts
abstract: We realize the enveloping algebras of positive parts of symmetrizable Kac-Moody Lie algebras as convolution algebras of constructible functions on module varieties of Geiss-Leclerc-Schröer generalized preprojective algebras $Π(C,D)$. We characterize all pairs $(C,D)$ for which such a realization exists. These realizations generalize Lusztig's classical preprojective construction. The construction uses a folding embedding and torus actions on flag varieties.

title: Accelerating Dynamic Route Re-solving via Robust Solver Evolution in Automatic Heuristic Design
abstract: Multi-goal route planning uses spatial data on service locations and pairwise travel costs to determine a visiting order that minimizes total travel cost. This task can be formulated as the traveling salesman problem (TSP) and has benefited from large language model-based automatic heuristic design (AHD) for constructing effective solvers. Despite their effectiveness in static settings, existing methods exhibit substantial re-solving inefficiency when location changes, new requests, or request cancellations alter the underlying request data during execution. Our empirical analysis suggests that ``static-overfitting'' contributes to this inefficiency, as evolved solvers may repeatedly direct search toward overlapping local neighborhoods after dynamic changes. We further find that this ``overfitting'' is associated with limitations in existing evolutionary processes, where lower objective values on some instances coincide with longer solving times. In this paper, we therefore propose ERDR, a plug-and-play framework that integrates two strategies into existing AHD pipelines to guide evolution toward solvers that re-solve dynamically changed instances faster. Specifically, 1) ERDR uses validation-guided reselection to reevaluate candidates on instances excluded from routine evolution, reducing specialization to fixed training instances. 2) ERDR applies runtime robustness-augmented evaluation, supplementing the original evaluation objective of AHD methods with inter-group variability and tail risk in solving time to discourage costly and uneven search. Experiments across multiple TSP scales and dynamic scenarios show that ERDR achieves average re-solving speedups of $2.2\times$ under guided local search and $4.4\times$ under iterated local search.

title: Optimal polynomial meshes on quasicircles via conformal scale comparison
abstract: We prove that every quasicircle $Γ\subset\mathbb{C}$ admits an optimal admissible polynomial mesh for univariate complex polynomials. More precisely, if $E$ denotes the closed Jordan domain bounded by $Γ$, then for every $Λ>1$ there are finite sets $A_n\subsetΓ$ with $\mathrm{card}(A_n)=O(n)$ and $\|p\|_E=\|p\|_Γ\leqΛ\|p\|_{A_n}$ for every $p\in\mathcal{P}_n(\mathbb{C})$. The nodes may be chosen as images of equally spaced points of the unit circle under the inverse exterior conformal map, equivalently as equal-mass points for harmonic measure at infinity. The proof combines the classical conformal level-curve scale with a discrete norming principle. If $ρ_n(z)$ denotes the distance from a boundary point to the exterior level curve $|Φ|=1+1/n$, Bernstein--Walsh and Cauchy's formula show that any sufficiently fine $ρ_n$-net is norming. A scale-comparison property then turns $O(n)$ equally spaced angular samples into such a net. Quasicircles satisfy this property by quasisymmetry. The argument requires no smoothness or rectifiability and applies in particular to the classical von Koch snowflake.

title: Phase information and measurement in the Stochastic--Quantum correspondence
abstract: The recently proposed stochastic-quantum correspondence establishes a connection between general stochastic processes and quantum dynamics, in which stochastic transition probabilities admit compatible representations on a Hilbert space, known as quantum lifts. We ask how the predictive information represented by off-diagonal degrees of freedom in the quantum lift is encoded within the stochastic description. We introduce the notion of a family of context-dependent stochastic processes and show that their continuation probabilities encode this predictive information. In particular, suitable continuations allow the intermediate lifted quantum state to be reconstructed entirely from system configuration probabilities. This perspective also clarifies the nature of quantum measurement: active continuations make basis-dependent quantum probabilities accessible as configuration probabilities, while a separate physical interaction records the realized configuration and introduces measurement disturbance. Although the rooted quantum probabilities alone do not guarantee that every stochastic realizer of the idealized recording interaction faithfully records the system's pre-measurement configuration, we show that at least one faithful stochastic realizer always exists.

title: Follow-Bench 2.0: An End-to-End 3D Benchmark for Socially-Aware Robot Person Following
abstract: Socially-aware robot person following (RPF) requires a mobile robot to follow a designated person in dynamic human environments while maintaining target identity, avoiding obstacles and pedestrians, and preserving socially comfortable formations. Existing benchmarks only partially evaluate this coupled problem: embodied visual tracking benchmarks emphasize target visibility with limited social interaction, person re-identification benchmarks study perception without closed-loop control, and motion-planning benchmarks often assume ground-truth target and pedestrian states. We introduce Follow-Bench 2.0, an end-to-end 3D benchmark for evaluating socially-aware RPF under coupled perception--planning challenges. Built in Unreal Engine, Follow-Bench 2.0 provides difficulty-leveled scenarios with diverse pedestrian flows, lighting and weather conditions, cluttered layouts, bottlenecks, queueing behaviors, distractors, and temporary target occlusions. The benchmark supports modular perception--planning pipelines, end-to-end visual policies, and foundation-model-based active trackers under a unified closed-loop protocol. It further evaluates both back- and side-following configurations and reports safety--comfort metrics covering task success, target visibility, target recovery, social-space intrusion, following formation, and motion smoothness. Experiments show that RPF-oriented modular pipelines substantially outperform current end-to-end visual policies on close and socially comfortable following, but also reveal that socially-aware RPF remains far from solved in interaction-heavy environments and especially in side-following. Follow-Bench 2.0 therefore provides a diagnostic platform for studying how perception errors, occlusions, crowd interactions, and following configurations jointly affect robot person following.

title: Identifying the critical mass in a quasilinear chemotaxis model with indirect signal production
abstract: The mass threshold separating boundedness and unboundedness of global solutions to a critical quasilinear parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model with indirect signal production is identified in the radially symmetric setting in a ball. Specifically, solutions emanating from initial values with mass below a critical mass M\textsubscr{c} > 0, which is characterized in terms of a variant of the Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality, are global and bounded. In contrast, for any M > M\textsubscr{c}, there are initial values with mass M such that the corresponding global solutions are unbounded. The proof relies on the variational structure of the system and a detailed study of the stationary states.

title: Witnessing Gaussian Coexistence and Correlation-Ellipse Tomography
abstract: Gaussian light is specified by second-order field moments, yet their hidden correlation geometry can demand higher-order intensity measurements. We establish a measurement hierarchy for "Gaussian coexistence", i.e., the simultaneous presence of cross covariance and cross pseudocovariance. For two zero-mean Gaussian modes with circular marginals, all unperturbed intensity moments of second or third order are blind to coexistence. In contrast, a balanced fourth-order residual provides a necessary and sufficient witness. Their identities, however, remain fundamentally ambiguous: recovering the two correlation strengths does not reveal which belongs to the covariance and which to the pseudocovariance. Unexpectedly, adding thermal fluctuations resolves this ambiguity: an independent, correlated thermal probe selectively modifies the covariance while leaving the pseudocovariance unchanged, allowing the two correlation strengths to be individually identified. Moreover, a coherent reference in only one arm then makes their relative phase accessible through third-order intensity correlation. Together, these measurements reconstruct a correlation ellipse and its Poincaré-sphere coordinates, determining the relative channel strengths and the ellipse orientation. The framework separates what intensity detection can witness, what thermal probing can identify, and what a single phase reference can orient, turning inaccessible Gaussian correlation structure into a quantitatively reconstructible geometry.

title: Design, Control, and Teleoperation of a Dexterous Robotic Hand with Soft-Rigid Hybrid Fingers
abstract: Adding compliance to robot hands results in higher grasp quality and robust contact with the environment. Soft hands are inherently compliant, but are typically more complex to control and model than rigid equivalents. We extend prior work on soft-rigid hybrid robot fingers into a five-fingered dexterous gripper --- an integrated tendon-driven hand that is highly compliant and controllable. Structural compliance combined with a rigid skeleton, when realized in a five-fingered hand, allow us to use linear control to achieve soft-grasping generality. We evaluate the use of this hand in a variety of teleoperated manipulation tasks, demonstrating the effectiveness of the overall mechanical design and control strategy. Our contributions include: (1) Mechanical design of the a five-fingered Soft-Rigid Hybrid Hand, composed of 12 active degrees of freedom, demonstrating a high degree on generalization enabled by the soft-rigid architecture, with our gripper, able to complete 28 of the 33 (84.8\%) grasp postures in the human range. (2) Precise, high bandwidth (up to 1432deg/s extension speed, compared with 700deg/s for the equivalent human joint). (3) Position and task space controllers for the soft-rigid hybrid finger and whole hand. (4) A teleoperation framework for control of this hand, as well as demonstrations of its efficacy in a variety of grasping and manipulation tasks Further tests illustrate the hand's advantages in completing non-rigid manipulation tasks, such as picking up thin deformable objects (such as a dollar bill or folding cloth) as well as in interfacing with soft or delicate targets.

title: A convective $1$-homogeneous $p$-Laplacian problem
abstract:
Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{N}$ be a bounded, smooth domain, and let $a:\overlineΩightarrow\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function that may change sign. We study the $1$-homogeneous problem \[ \left\{  egin{array} [c]{lll} -\operatorname{div}\left( \left\vert

title: An XR-Based System for Enhanced Spatial Awareness in Mobile Robot Teleoperation
abstract: Teleoperation of mobile robots represents a critical capability for operations in hazardous environments, yet maintaining adequate situational awareness remains challenging without effective visualization and control interfaces. This work presents a multi-modal extended reality (XR) system for robot teleoperation and scene exploration that integrates immersive visual and haptic feedback modalities. To address motion sickness commonly induced by 360-degree camera feeds in head-mounted displays (HMDs), the system employs a fixed dual-camera configuration: a forward-facing camera for primary navigation and a rear-facing camera for enhanced situational awareness without operator discomfort. For navigation in confined or low-visibility conditions, a 16-channel Velodyne LiDAR generates real-time 2D occupancy grid maps, which are converted into vibrational haptic feedback on handheld controllers to provide intuitive, non-visual obstacle detection. User evaluation with 20 participants demonstrates that this haptic modality significantly reduces the cognitive load associated with obstacle avoidance during teleoperation.

title: Understanding the Importance of Massive Activations through Adversarial Robustness
abstract: A common occurrence in Large Language Models (LLMs) is the emergence of so-called massive activations. This phenomenon is well known in the literature and has been connected to attention sinks, representational compression, as well as signal propagation. However, the reasons and consequences for their appearance are not yet well understood. In this paper, we explain the role of massive activations in deep learning by showing that they are connected to the region migration phenomenon in delayed robustness. Under the spline theoretic interpretation of deep networks, we show that massive activations push the representations away from the nonlinearity boundaries of the network, decreasing the complexity of its input-output map around data points. Furthermore, we uncover for the first time that this phenomenon is not unique to transformers and actually appears in a number of common architectures performing simple supervised learning tasks. We validate this connection through extensive experiments on a diverse set of architectures including residual MLP, ResNet18, Vision Transformers and GPT and datasets including MNIST, CIFAR10, Imagenette and Shakespeare Text. We consistently observe that massive activations and region migration co-occur with adversarial robustness. Furthermore, we illustrate that this connection holds in the large-scale pretraining of LLMs by showing that the rise of massive activations in LLMs closely tracks the adversarial accuracy of the model under perturbations of the token embeddings.

title: Topological terahertz fields from tunable vectorial currents
abstract: Future information processing calls for photonic architectures with greater capacity, intrinsic resilience to noise, and direct integration with quantum materials and devices. Topological light pulses have recently emerged as promising candidates to meet these demands, yet the complexity underlying their unique properties also makes them challenging to generate, tune, and fully resolve in space and time. Here, we generate and actively tune topological light fields through transient vectorial currents in an optoelectronic metasurface. Incident linear polarization steers the local direction of photocurrents in graphene via nanoplasmonic resonators with triangular symmetry, while a global winding pattern enables continuous tuning between compressional and circulating charge flows. Under ultrafast excitation, these currents radiate single-cycle terahertz toroidal pulses spanning electric- and magnetic-dominant modes with dynamically evolving skyrmion textures. Full spatiotemporal mapping and reconstruction provide a complete visualization of the toroidal structure of light, directly tracing the closed field surfaces while continuously tracking skyrmion number and helicity throughout a single cycle. These results connect two-dimensional vectorial currents to rich three-dimensional electromagnetic field structures, while establishing a versatile integrated platform for higher-dimensional photonic information processing and emerging material spectroscopies.

title: New families of vertex-transitive quaternionic lattices in products of trees
abstract: We describe infinite families of quaternionic arithmetic lattices in $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_1)\times \cdots \times \operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{T}_n)$ acting transitively on the vertices of the Cartesian product $\mathcal{T}_1\times \cdots \times \mathcal{T}_n$, where $\mathcal{T}_1,\dots, \mathcal{T}_n$ are regular trees. We present an algorithm to determine a presentation for each of these lattices. We also introduce a method for constructing such lattices that act regularly on the set of vertices. We illustrate our results with numerous explicit examples, including several families of known cases, as well as many new instances in arbitrary characteristic.

title: CoReQ: Condition-Aware Cross-Modal Repair and Quality-Guided Robust Collaborative Perception
abstract: Multi-vehicle collaborative perception can use observations from different perspectives to alleviate the problems of occlusion and limited sensing range. However, missing echoes and false echoes caused by bad weather will reduce the quality of single-vehicle features and affect collaborative detection. LiDAR provides richer geometric information, and 4D Radar has strong weather adaptability. The complementarity of the two provides the possibility to improve perception under degraded observations. However, how to adjust cross-modal repair according to the current observation conditions and how to reasonably integrate multi-vehicle features whose reliability still differs after repair are still problems that need to be solved. To this end, we propose CoReQ, a condition-aware repair and quality-guided collaborative perception framework. For the former, the condition-guided bidirectional cross-modal repair module (CBCR) extracts vehicle-level observation conditions from point cloud occupancy, density and feature statistics, and adjusts the bidirectional correction of LiDAR and Radar features accordingly. For the latter, we combine local reliability assessment with collaborative weighting: first, the task-aware quality estimation module (TaQE) uses the classification and positioning information of the EMA teacher to construct a supervision target and predict the spatial quality of the repaired features; then, the condition and quality guided fusion module (CoQF) matches the quality information with the content, and the observation conditions of both parties are jointly used for multi-vehicle feature weighted fusion. Experiments on V2X-R and V2X-Radar-C show that the framework is competitive under a variety of observation conditions, achieving significant gains in AP@0.7 on V2X-R under snowy conditions, and achieving the highest AP among the compared V2X-Radar-C methods.

title: A consistent generalised kinetic equation for damped ocean waves
abstract: Contemporary spectral wave models, including those used in operational wave forecasts and in coupled earth system models, assume damping and non-linear wave energy exchange to be independent. Here, we critically examine this assumption. Starting from the equations of weakly non-linear waves, we rigorously derive a governing equation that consistently couples damping and non-linear interactions. This consistent generalised kinetic equation does not lead to an appreciable change in total wave--energy dissipation, but compared to the standard additive damping approach there is a noticeable difference in the distribution of energy among the wave frequencies. This effect is particularly important for weak damping, and is a consequence of a memory effect retained in model. Even stronger differences are observed when damping is allowed to depend on wave frequency, as is characteristic of many wave processes of growing interest such as the interaction with other components of the earth system, e.g. the cryosphere. Compared to the purely additive formulation, our new damped generalised kinetic equation has improved numerical stability characteristics. The formulation presented therefore provides a possible basis for future operational wave modelling. While our results are for ocean waves, the derived generalised kinetic equation can be applied to other weakly nonlinear dispersive systems where external damping (or forcing) applies.

title: LazUnirec: Unifying Retrieval and Ranking in Multi-scenario Industrial Recommendation
abstract: Modern industrial recommendation systems typically divide retrieval and ranking into two separate cascaded stages, leading to inconsistent optimization objectives, redundant encoding of user sequences, and a waste of computational resources. Previous efforts have investigated using Transformers to model both retrieval and ranking simultaneously. However, these studies still face two major limitations: (1) Since retrieval and ranking share a single Transformer backbone, the gradient conflict arises when the gradient directions of the two tasks are inconsistent. (2) When gradient conflict occurs, the model cannot determine a reliable direction for gradient updates. To this end, we propose a Unified Retrieval and Ranking approach for Multi-scenario Industrial Recommendation, termed as LazUnirec. Specifically, we construct task-shared and task-private parameters on the Transformer backbone to mitigate the gradient conflict. Wherein, for the attention components, we propose LoRA-modulated attention, enabling retrieval and ranking to share attention parameters while preserving task-private parameters. For the feed-forward networks (FFN), we present task-adaptive sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) to mitigate gradient conflict by constructing task-shared and task-private experts. Moreover, we propose an uncertainty estimation that evaluates the gradient reliability of the retrieval and ranking, thereby guiding the model toward a more reliable gradient update direction when gradient conflict occurs. In addition, knowledge distillation from ranking to retrieval further enables cross-task knowledge transfer. Extensive offline experiments and online A/B testing demonstrate the effectiveness and superiority of LazUnirec. LazUnirec has been deployed in online multi-scenario industrial recommendation system and currently delivers significant gains for the platform.

title: FewRef-5: Fixed-Reference Test-Time Adaptation for Virtual Staining
abstract: Virtual staining synthesizes special-stain images from routine hematoxylin and eosin (H&E), extending the information available from an existing digital slide. However, a fixed inference rule can leave available real target-stain references unused, limiting query-specific correction of stain appearance at deployment. Test-time adaptation (TTA) provides a mechanism for this reference-guided, query-specific refinement without retraining the generator. We therefore propose FewRef-5, a reference-assisted TTA method for virtual staining built on StainPromptInversion. We extract tissue-masked optical-density means and standard deviations from five real Masson's trichrome (MAS) training patches and average them into a fixed stain target. A scheduled statistic-matching loss introduces this target into per-query visual-prompt optimization alongside our edge/Gram consistency penalties and the inherited reconstruction objectives. The target remains unchanged across queries, avoiding recursive dependence on earlier generated outputs while the pretrained generator stays fixed. On recorded H&E-to-MAS outputs for 1,989 queries, FewRef-5 reduces target-set FID from 183.201 to 166.904 and increases source-referenced SSIM from 0.92787 to 0.94996 relative to our Edge+Gram variant. Source PSNR and MS-SSIM decrease, showing an endpoint trade-off rather than uniformly better reconstruction.

title: The dust attenuation scaling relation in the TNG50 simulation
abstract: The infrared excess (IRX = L_IR / L_UV) of star-forming galaxies (SFGs) follows a tight scaling relation with star formation rate, gas-phase metallicity, and size up to z ~ 3, providing a key benchmark for galaxy formation models. We test whether TNG50 SFGs, post-processed with the radiative transfer code SKIRT, reproduce the universal IRX relation - linking IRX to metallicity, infrared luminosity, size, and inclination - and identify the origin of any offsets. We analyse 7280 TNG50-SFGs across 0 <= z <= 4, comparing their predicted IRX relations with observations and the EAGLE simulation. We test different dust-to-metal (DTM) ratios and dust compositions, recalibrate galaxy properties to observed scaling relations, and decompose the offsets into individual parameter contributions. TNG50-SFGs match the universal IRX relation closely at 0.5 <= z <= 1, but lie above it at z = 0 (+0.5 dex) and below it at z >= 2 (-0.25 dex). They follow a relation of the same functional form, with a shallower, metallicity-independent L_IR slope. At z ~ 0, TNG50-SFGs are ~1 dex fainter in L_IR than the local calibration sample, requiring extrapolation; at fixed stellar mass and L_IR, simulated and observed IRX agree within 0.04 dex. At z >= 2, TNG50-SFGs are less obscured than predicted, an offset largely removed by lowering their metallicities by ~0.2 dex. Varying the DTM ratio and dust type shifts the offset normalisation without resolving its redshift evolution: a redshift-dependent DTM ratio helps at high z, but not at z = 0. Resolving the low-z discrepancy requires both improved dust models and observational constraints on IR-faint galaxies.

title: Perfect Scores, Misplaced Explanations: A Controlled Study of Explainability in Audio Deepfake Detection
abstract: What if an explanation achieves perfect scores but it is uninterpretable? We show that this happens when explaining audio deepfake detectors. Using an optimization-based method, we explain a state-of-the-art wav2vec2-based detector. The explanations achieve optimal scores on standard explainability metrics, i.e. fidelity and faithfulness. Visual inspection, however, reveals unintuitive and uninterpretable patterns. To understand this discrepancy, we run a controlled perturbation study in which we modify known frequency regions of the speech signal. Although we propose a model that is able to obtain close-to-optimal results with respect to the metrics, the explanations locate the manipulated region only when it is fixed across samples, and mostly fall to chance level when it varies. We further show that the signal used to fill the removed regions largely determines the explanation and its localization, without being reflected in the metrics.

title: On some off-diagonal hypergraph Ramsey problems
abstract: We give a new short proof of a theorem of Fox and He that the $3$-uniform Ramsey number $r_3(K_4^-, K_n)$ is at least $2^{Ω(n \log n)}$. The construction exploits a new connection with a directed graph recently introduced by Bradač in his work on off-diagonal graph Ramsey numbers. Moreover, it generalizes naturally to give sharp bounds for several extensions of this problem in higher uniformity, answering questions raised by Mubayi and Suk.

title: Degree-bounded Satisfiability of Local MPNNs with Sum Aggregation is NEXPTIME-hard
abstract: We prove that the following problem is NEXPTIME-hard: given a message passing neural network (MPNN) $M$ with local sum aggregation and truncated ReLU activations, and a degree bound $d$ encoded in unary, decide whether there is a pointed graph $(G,v)$ with rational node labels and degree at most $d$ that is accepted by $M$. Hardness already holds for the fixed degree bound $d=3$.

title: Emergent cloud patterns from stochastic jump models of parcel microphysics
abstract: Warm clouds organize into bands, cells, and intricate wave networks, yet the dynamical mechanisms connecting these forms remain difficult to isolate. To bridge unresolved parcel microphysics and cloud organization, we formulate a spatial jump-process model of cloud-water and rain-water anomalies in an activated regime and analyze its mean-field closure. Eliminating fast supersaturation adjustment from droplet growth and vapor transport supplies a screened environmental kernel, which we couple to a cubic Stuart-Landau oscillatory law. Averaging over Poisson parcel episodes and closing third-order moments yields a pseudoparabolic Ginzburg--Landau equation (PGLE), whose mixed space--time derivative encodes dynamic inertia, slowing fine-scale relaxation. Unlike diffusive amplitude equations, the PGLE splits into a regularized nonlinear Schrödinger Hamiltonian sector and a pseudoparabolic Allen--Cahn gradient sector governed by a conserved Noether charge, alongside an open-system liquid-water budget separating conversion from vapor exchange, fallout, and triad-driven domain-mean oscillations. Exact stability criteria show how dynamic inertia and amplitude-dependent frequency shifts (twist) control modulational loss of synchrony and resonant cross-carrier sideband gain above a critical twist threshold. Numerical integrations show that increasing twist transforms undulatus-like bands into defect-rich asperitas-like waves via defect proliferation, while subcritical competition consolidates cellular patterns into rolls. Even without twist, random anomalies evolve into a persistent cellular exclusion scale and actinoform-like spiral arms, while 1D wave breakup reorganizes into a two-frequency combination-tone spectrum. The jump model identifies omitted fluctuation moments for calibration against large-eddy simulations.

title: Uniform Algebraic Degeneracy of Entire Curves into Complex Projective Varieties
abstract: This paper is devoted to the algebraic degeneracy of entire curves intersecting a simple-normal-crossing divisor on smooth projective varieties over C, within the logarithmic Green-Griffiths-Lang program. For negativelytwisted global logarithmic jet differentials, we introduce an intrinsic weighted conormal filtration along each positive-dimensional closed boundary stratum, with weights prescribed by the contact orders along boundary components. Applying the maximal Harder-Narasimhan slopes of logarithmic cotangent bundles and the normal degrees of the strata, we define an integer vanishing threshold which can improve the pole bound obtained from the slope-based ceiling. Under the stable-base-locus hypothesis for the logarithmic Semple tower, we then establish an improved second main theorem whose counting coefficients depend on the boundary stratum, actual contact orders and the ratio of source weight to twisting exponent. These coefficients are independent of the powers used to realize the stable base locus. We further derive a uniform algebraicdegeneracy criterion allowing positive corrected pole coefficients, formulated via a finite system of stratumwise inequalities together with the ampleness of a residual divisor class. This yields conditional orbifold Green-Griffiths-Lang type statements. Refinements arising from conormalbundle decompositions and sharp local pole estimates at surface boundary crossings are established. Our examples exhibit strict improvement over naive slope-based bounds and illustrate that full-weight poles can persist at boundary crossings, and furnish concrete instances satisfying the stablebaselocus hypothesis.

title: On the Effectiveness of Resampling for Supervised Graph Anomaly Detection
abstract: Class imbalance and scarce anomaly labels motivate oversampling in supervised graph anomaly detection (GAD), but its benefits across detectors and benchmarks remain unclear. In the low-label setting of GADBench, with 20 labelled anomalies and 80 labelled normal nodes, we compare class weighting and up to six oversampling strategies in ten detector configurations from three families: graph neural networks (GNNs), tree ensembles on neighbourhood-aggregated features, and tabular foundation models, on 17 datasets. On the eight datasets with organic anomalies, no strategy has a statistically resolved average gain in any configuration, and which nodes are labelled matters as much as the strategy. On the nine datasets with injected anomalies, Gaussian-noise oversampling (ROSE) gains up to 5.2 AUPRC points in four of the six tree and tabular foundation model configurations, and in all six only on attribute-swap anomalies; in four GNNs its gain is not distinguishable from zero. This gain depends on the injection recipe, which gives swapped nodes an atypical feature norm: it is no longer distinguishable from zero when the swap uses a single random donor or preserves the norm, although most detectors then also stop detecting the swaps. Over the 17 datasets, tuning the tree detectors adds about three points, as much as ROSE, and cuts ROSE's gain by about half or more. With the same source nodes and class weight, sampled graph views are not distinguishable from plain copies of those nodes. We recommend tuning baselines, repeating labelled splits, reporting organic and injected anomalies separately, and checking label-free degree and feature-norm baselines.

title: Total kinetic energy of fission fragments within time-dependent density functional theory: role of particle-number projection and collective deformations
abstract: Time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations of fission fragment total kinetic energy (TKE), restricted to axially symmetric trajectories and a single symmetry-violating mean-field state, underestimate TKE by 10-20 MeV away from the most probable mass split. We reexamine this for $^{240}$Pu and $^{252}$Cf within relativistic TDDFT+BCS, combining particle-number projection (PNP) with an extended collective space including hexadecapole and non-axial deformations. Varying the pairing strength leaves the TKE essentially unchanged, but PNP converts each trajectory into a resolved TKE distribution over fragment mass, and the enlarged collective space is needed to reach the correct scission configurations. Together, these reproduce the empirical TKE mass dependence substantially better than standard calculations, indicating the discrepancy reflects missing symmetry restoration and configuration space rather than a deficient energy functional.

title: Gated Concept Adapters: Layer-Wise Concept Bottlenecks for Auditable Text Understanding
abstract: Human-facing text understanding systems are used to infer affect, moderate harmful content, and support socially sensitive decisions. However, Transformer predictions are difficult to audit because they are produced from high-dimensional hidden states that do not provide a compact, inspectable interface for human analysis or intervention. We introduce Gated Concept Adapters (GCA), a layer-wise concept bottleneck framework that attaches gated, low-dimensional concept-producing readout adapters to selected outputs of pretrained Transformers. Token representations are mapped into concept activations, filtered by learned gates, pooled into layer-level summaries, and exposed to the prediction head as a concept-mediated interface. The dimensions can be inspected through usage statistics, signature n-grams, post-hoc concept names, and targeted concept interventions. We evaluate GCA on fine-grained emotion classification, toxicity detection, topic classification, and a controlled verb-cloze stress test. In the affective and safety-relevant classification settings, GCA learns comparatively low-redundancy and intervention-sensitive concept representations while retaining useful predictive performance. On toxicity detection, it remains close to an unconstrained ModernBERT baseline while enabling concept-level inspection, targeted intervention, and lightweight post-hoc control. On GoEmotions, the end-to-end concept model incurs a macro-F1 cost relative to unconstrained RoBERTa, while a task-initialized frozen variant substantially reduces this gap. On AG News, GCA remains competitive with recent concept-based baselines, and the Qwen verb-cloze experiment clarifies the limits of concept-mediated full-vocabulary prediction. Overall, GCA provides a neural concept interface for auditable text understanding, prioritizing transparency, diagnosis, and intervention over unconstrained accuracy maximization.

title: The one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system as a weak limit of solutions to a compressible two-fluid system
abstract: We study how a macroscopic mixture arises from two compressible fluids that share a velocity but occupy disjoint regions. We fix the initial density profiles and the common initial velocity, and let the partition between the fluids oscillate on increasingly fine scales. The fluids remain segregated as they evolve, but in the weak limit the phase indicator becomes a volume fraction that may lie strictly between zero and one. For independent adiabatic exponents $γ^\pm\geq9/5$, we prove that the sequence of segregated solutions converges to a global weak solution of the viscous one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system in three space dimensions. The mixture pressure is the volume-weighted average of the two phase pressures, while their difference drives the evolution of the volume fraction along the flow and contributes to dissipation in the macroscopic energy inequality.

title: ST-GNN-AAAS: Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for Anytime Automatic Algorithm Selection in the Traveling Salesman Problem
abstract: Anytime Automatic Algorithm Selection (AAAS) aims to make solver choices under varying time budgets. The existing AAAS approaches largely rely on static instance characteristics and make limited use of temporal information revealed during solver execution. We propose ST-GNN-AAAS, a Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network framework for AAAS in the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP). The framework represents evolving incumbent tours using time-varying node features, including distances from each node to its neighbors in the current tour, and combines these features with solver performance observations over a short history window. Given this short history, ST-GNN-AAAS predicts solver selections over a longer future horizon. We evaluate the method on a subset of diverse TSP benchmarks from NATIONAL, TNM, TSPLIB, and VLSI, releasing the corresponding solver execution data to support reproducibility. Our model achieves a selection accuracy of 76.59% and closes 46.05% of the average rank gap between the single best solver (SBS) and the virtual best solver (VBS).

title: Equivariant harmonic maps from $\mathbb{S}^3$ to $\mathbb{S}^2$: on a counterexample to a conjecture of J. Eells
abstract: The present paper builds on a remarkable AI-generated counterexample to a long-standing conjecture of James Eells. We present the rigorous construction of a smooth harmonic map $f:\mathbb{S}^3\to \mathbb{S}^2$ between the round spheres which does not factor through a Hopf fibration, and improve some arguments to get that the Hopf invariant of $f$ is either $0$ or $\pm 6$. The construction is based on a min-max scheme in a $5$-equivariant class of maps $f$ with an additional dihedral symmetry. By passing to a suitable associated sphere bundle over $\mathbb{S}^2$, the problem is reduced to a variational problem for sections, where the imposed symmetries guarantee the mountain pass structure and the non-constancy of the desired limit harmonic map.

title: Recursive estimation of the Oja median and related simplex medians
abstract: We study the recursive estimation of multivariate location functionals defined by minimizing the expected volume of a random simplex. This framework encompasses both the spatial median and the affine-equivariant Oja median. We introduce a sliding-window stochastic gradient algorithm and its averaged version, and establish their strong consistency and asymptotic normality. We further show that the sliding-window approach offers a favorable trade-off between statistical accuracy and computational cost compared with a naive disjoint-block stochastic gradient algorithm and offline methods, with the statistical comparison based on asymptotic covariances. Numerical experiments illustrate the computational advantages of the proposed procedures and their finite-sample accuracy.

title: How to Round Spiky Balls into Submission -- And Faster Algorithms For The Closest Vector Problem
abstract: We give the first single-exponential time algorithm for the exact Closest Vector Problem (CVP) in the $\ell_p$ norm for $1 < p < 2$. Prior to this, such an algorithm was only known for the Euclidean norm, i.e., $\ell_2$, or needed an additional promise that the target is close to the lattice. Using similar techniques, we also find a shortest non-zero vector in the $\ell_p$ norm in time $2^{O(n)}$ for every $p \in [1,2)$ with a constant in the exponent that doesn't depend on $p$, and that improves state of the art algorithms for the shortest vector problem in the $\ell_p$ norm. The problem of finding a single exponential time algorithm for CVP in the $\ell_p$ norm for $p \neq 2$ has been open since 2010, when Micciancio and Voulgaris resolved it for the Euclidean norm. One of our key ideas is that for $0<p\le2$, the function $z \mapsto e^{-|z|^p}$ is a mixture of Gaussians, so the $\ell_p$ discrete Gaussian distribution on a lattice shift is a mixture of Euclidean discrete Gaussians with random diagonal widths. Our algorithms use this to reduce the $\ell_p$ problem to the Euclidean CVP on a randomly scaled lattice.

title: Recursive Collective Intelligence: Emergence on an Equal-Budget Ladder in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
abstract: Large language models increasingly work as teams of agents, and a team is expected to solve problems beyond the reach of any single member. Most evaluations credit a team for outperforming a single agent, without accounting for the additional computation: a team may consume many times the tokens of one agent, and a plain vote over independent answers already explains most of the reported gain. Two questions therefore remain open: When does interaction itself make a group smarter, and can a group improve its next generation by learning from its own work? We answer both with the equal-budget ladder, which grades a group against independent agents at three levels: outperforming a single agent, a compute-matched majority vote, and compute-matched pass@n. On this ladder we define Recursive Collective Intelligence (RCI) as a group whose own output, without a teacher or external labels, makes its next generation smarter at equal cost. Three findings follow. First, interaction improves collective intelligence when it moves information across agents: forwarding split facts lifts groups above pass@n at three model scales, by about a third at 27B. Second, organization emerges spontaneously: identical 27B agents form hubs and improve accuracy by 18 percentage points; encoding their organization in a prompt enables them to reach level 3 at less than half the token budget in a descriptive comparison. Third, groups recursively improve themselves: Two label-free generations progressively climb the ladder, the second 9B generation surpassing both pass@$n$ and a control trained on base-model turns; on PlanBench, HiddenBench and Hanabi, each generation outperforms its predecessor on unseen problems for four to six generations. A group therefore outperforms its members when it forwards useful information more efficiently than it spends tokens on coordination, and learns to do so from its own work.

title: Sparse Additive Spanners and the Cost Spectra of Group Actions
abstract: How sparse can a Cayley graph become if we retain all its vertices and allow distances to increase by at most a fixed additive constant? We study invariant random spanning subgraphs, measuring sparsity by the expected degree at a vertex. On the square grid, a random translate of a sparse mesh brings the mean degree arbitrarily close to two. If the choice must be made equivariantly from independent vertex labels, every edge is forced. In this expository note we follow these two answers through other groups. Geometry alone forces a positive gap on each non-elementary hyperbolic Cayley graph, while on one four-regular nilpotent Cayley graph the choice of action realizes every additive cost in $[1,2]$. The minimum of the action spectrum recovers the geometric cost. Open problems are presented in the end.

title: Accuracy and Efficiency of Lowest-order and Higher-Order Single-Source Integral Equations
abstract: The single-source integral equation allows the modeling of the electromagnetic field by only tracking a single surface-supported current density. It features products of integral operators, which pose unique challenges for the modeler in both the discretization and solution of the equation. Due to the unique structure of the single-source equation, its conforming and stable discretization requires expanding one of the two physical traces in primal basis functions and the other in dual basis functions. Primal functions are expected to have better approximation properties than dual ones. In this work, we study the impact of this asymmetric representation on the accuracy of the solution and propose an approach from which both traces can be recovered using only primal functions with modest additional computational cost. Moreover, we propose an alternative discretization scheme based on approximating the inverse of the duality mapping induced by the surface normal cross-product operator through the quasi-Helmholtz decomposition. This discretization provides greater flexibility in the choice of function spaces, enabling both a higher-order extension of the single-source equation and a more efficient lowest-order discretization using only Rao-Wilton-Glisson basis functions. Numerical results show the impact of the representation in terms of primal and dual functions in both lowest- and higher-order discretization.

title: Thermodynamics of complex crystals from a generalized mean-field bond model
abstract: We extend our previously introduced mean-field bond model from unary fcc lattices to crystals with multiple chemical species and sublattices, accurately predicting finite-temperature thermodynamics without statistical sampling. Our generalization reformulates the model in terms of the Wyckoff positions of the crystal, representing each by one atom, and solving for the bond density of the reference bond of each of its neighbor shells. Bond-bond correlation functions are built from the zero-temperature force constants, allowing the deviation of every bond in the crystal to be expressed through linear functions of the reference bond of a shell. Thermodynamic self-consistency is enforced by requiring a single virial temperature for the whole crystal, and compatibility of average bond lengths with crystal volume. Model predictions are validated against molecular dynamics simulations of unary, binary, and ternary crystals using Morse-type bonding potentials, parametrized for each shell from the force constants of empirical interatomic potentials at several isotropic strains. In each case, the predicted bond densities and thermodynamics agree with the simulations to within their statistical uncertainty. We discuss strategies for combining the model with bonding potentials parametrized from first principles and foundation models to predict the finite-temperature thermodynamics of complex crystals at ab initio accuracy without statistical sampling.

title: Privacy Disclosure Control Benchmark (PDC-Bench): How Faithfully Do LLMs Keep Privacy Constraints on In-Context Disclosure Granularity?
abstract: In LLM task execution, a constraint on the permitted disclosure granularity of personal attributes is sometimes imposed on the output. For example, if a person's private attribute is their location (San Francisco) and disclosure is permitted only at the country level, an output at the state level (California) violates the constraint. Detecting such violations requires capturing not only direct privacy leakage (San Francisco) but also semantic leakage (California). However, existing benchmarks cannot measure the degree of leakage with respect to a given semantic constraint such as the country-level limit. We therefore formalize disclosure control as a constraint on the permitted ceiling over the hierarchy of a knowledge graph. Building on this formulation, we construct PDC-Bench, a benchmark of 16,105 samples covering geography, age, race and ethnicity, and occupation. In our experiments applying PDC-Bench to eleven LLMs, 62% of the constraint violations were semantic leakage. We further found that semantic leakage depends less on the model than on the permitted disclosure granularity and the task's need for the private attribute; reliable auditing must therefore target semantic leakage together with these two factors. Data, prompts, and code are available at https://github.com/fuji1655/PDC-Bench.

title: Modulations of the photoswitching performances of azobenzene-based molecular devices by the π-conjugated spacers
abstract: The nature of the π-conjugated spacer is a key element to tune the electrical conductance and optical switching properties of metal-spacer-azobenzene-metal molecular devices. We report that the azobenzene-based molecular junctions with a thiophene or a phenylthiophene spacer exhibit a high cis/trans conductance ratio (ca. 1,000), while those with a bithiophene spacer have a lower conductance switching ratio (ca. 500) at the stated conditions (light wavelength and intensity) and for one batch of samples (out of two). Similarly, the two former molecular junctions have quite similar trans-to-cis isomerization kinetics, while the latter has a lower switching rate. The energy level of the highest occupied molecular orbital, which controls the electron transfer in the molecular junction, is weakly influenced by the nature of the spacer, nor by the conformation of the azobenzene moieties. The large increase in the conductance of the molecular junction with azobenzene in the cis-state is explained by an increase in the electronic coupling energy between the molecule and the top electrode. Theoretical studies by Density Functional Theory and Non Equilibrium Green's Functions are qualitatively consistent with the experiments. We find a consistent structure-property trend, showing that the higher molecule/electrode coupling energy for the cis-state is explained by the top benzene ring of the azobenzene lying flat with respect to the top electrode for the thiophene, phenylthiophene and bithiophene spacers. On the contrary, we observe that a spacer with a carbon-carbon triple bond (acetylene thiophene) induces a large irreproducibility and unpredictability of the results.

title: Inflation at strong mixing as a connection problem: effective field theory, Stokes phenomenon and the cosmological collider
abstract: We study a massive field strongly mixed with the curvature perturbation during inflation, in the regime where the latter is described at low energies by a single-field effective field theory (EFT) with a quadratic dispersion relation. What this EFT captures, and what lies beyond it, are encoded in a connection problem, which relates the solutions that define the vacuum at early times to those that describe observables at late times. We solve it with a general method that does not rely on an exact solution. An expansion in the inverse mixing, keeping both fields, yields the EFT as its leading order, with corrections under systematic control. It selects the vacuum of the EFT, fixes a phase that the EFT cannot determine on its own, and describes the heavy mode at all times. Particle production lies beyond all orders of this asymptotic expansion. We show that it arises from a Stokes phenomenon at the complex branch points of the dispersion relation and that, in a rotating basis of the two fields, it reduces to the familiar production of particles with half the heavy mass. A reflection symmetry of the equations of motion, combined with the canonical commutation relations, then determines all exponentially small effects exactly, and with them the solution of the connection problem, which combines particle production with a conversion between light and heavy quanta. Together with the expansion, these exact results give a compact analytical formula for the cosmological collider signal, whose exponential suppression, half of the usual Boltzmann one, directly reflects the halved mass of the produced particles. The expansion only requires a separation of scales and the adiabaticity of the heavy mode, while the reflection symmetry holds for many systems in de Sitter space. We therefore expect this approach to bring physical understanding and simple formulas well beyond the present case.

title: The Zero Enrichment Rare Objects (ZERO) Survey I: Photometric Calibration of NB395 and Metallicity Estimation
abstract: We present the first results of the Zero Enrichment Rare Objects (ZERO) survey, a narrow-band photometric survey targeting metallicity-sensitive narrow bands using the Hyper Suprime-Cam on the Subaru Telescope. This paper outlines the scientific goals, survey strategy, current observational status, photometric calibration, and metallicity estimation. The current ZERO footprint comprises 21 pointings, covering approximately 35 deg$^2$ along the celestial equator in the NB395 band, reaching NB395 $\sim$ 24.5 mag (10$σ$) in one hour, significantly deeper than typical comparable narrow-band Ca H\&K surveys. The NB395 photometry is calibrated using corrected Gaia BP/RP spectra and the recalibrated SDSS Stripe 82 catalog, achieving a typical zero-point precision of $\sim$0.3 per cent and flat-field precision better than 1 per cent on spatial scales larger than 8$^\prime$. Under typical conditions (three repeats; total exposure time $\sim$1 hour), the photometric precision reaches $\sim$1.1 per cent at NB395 $\approx$ 12, $\sim$1.5 per cent at 20, and $\sim$10 per cent at 24. We estimate [Ca/H] using a Physics-constrained Stellar Locus Fitting Method. The resulting [Ca/H] precision is better than 0.18 dex for sources brighter than NB395 $\sim$ 20, spanning a wide metallicity range from metal-rich to the very metal-poor regime ($-3 \le$ [Ca/H]$\le +0.5$). We further show that NB395 traces [Ca/H] more directly than [Fe/H]. The final catalog contains one million sources with NB395 photometry, including 379,216 repeatedly observed and 61,845 with [Ca/H] estimates. These results provide a solid foundation for future ZERO survey, including photometric calibration, stellar parameter determination, and investigations of Galactic structure and chemical evolution.

title: When "Neutral" Means Irrelevant: A Construct-Validity Audit of NormAd-ETI
abstract: NormAd-ETI scores a model's judgment of everyday actions as acceptable, unacceptable, or neither as the cultural context shrinks from a specific rule to a country name. We audit what that three-way score measures. It combines two decisions: whether a supplied norm applies, and whether the action conforms to it. Separating them shows that when only a country is shown, applicability falls to near chance while conformity stays well above it, because the prompt withholds the rule a Neutral label depends on. Because one answer carries both decisions, the score follows the steadier conformity and hides the weaker applicability, and no single prompt recovers the two separately. Dedicated forced-choice probes separate them for frontier models but not for small open models, where the applicability judgment still tracks the hidden acceptability label. Adding a written rationale reduces that conflation without removing it. We recommend reporting the two results separately and measuring the conflation gap.

title: Partial Identification under Imperfect Compliance via Cross-World Correlation Restriction
abstract: This article develops a unified partial identification approach for the average treatment effect (ATE) and the local average treatment effect (LATE) in randomized experiments with imperfect compliance, incorporating the cross-world correlation between potential treatment statuses. Even under random assignment and exclusion restriction, the correlation is unidentified. However, given the two identified marginals, it uniquely determines the relative proportions of the four principal strata, with monotonicity corresponding to a special case. We derive explicit sharp bounds for both the ATE and LATE at a fixed correlation and extend the results to prespecified correlation ranges, providing a sensitivity analysis that incorporates substantive information about compliance behavior. For the ATE, the lower bound decreases and the upper bound increases with the correlation. Although imposing monotonicity does not tighten the conventional Balke--Pearl bounds, we show that restricting the correlation can yield tighter bounds, even when defiers remain possible. For the LATE, the sharp bounds may not vary monotonically with the correlation, and we establish necessary and sufficient conditions for point identification of the LATE at any feasible correlation value, with the conventional Wald ratio identification result under monotonicity as a special case. In addition, we derive a breakdown point for the correlation that determines when the Wald ratio falls outside the sharp identified set for the LATE. Applications to four empirical studies illustrate how cross-world correlation restrictions tighten the sharp bounds for the ATE and LATE and assess the breakdown of the Wald ratio.

title: A catalog of Gaia DR3 luminous blue variables and candidate luminous blue variables
abstract: Galactic LBVs are rare, evolved massive stars whose defining evidence is long-term spectroscopic and photometric instability, including S Doradus-type cycles, and, in exceptional cases, giant eruptions. Candidate LBVs (cLBVs) share LBV-like spectra and/or circumstellar nebulae; however, they lack long-term observational datasets that would detect their long-term variability and confirm their classification as bona fide LBVs. Modern time-domain surveys provide homogeneous light curves for many Galactic massive stars, but each survey has its own limitations in terms of depth, temporal coverage, and observing cadence. Using confirmed Galactic LBVs as a control sample, we aim to test what Gaia DR3 and complementary photometric surveys can and cannot establish about LBV-type variability. We assembled a vetted sample of 75 Galactic LBVs and cLBVs with near- and mid-infrared photometry from 2MASS, MSX, WISE, GLIMPSE, and MIPSGAL. The infrared material was used to validate identifications, evaluate source confusion, and place objects in a circumstellar-dust context. We then constructed light curves from Gaia DR3, the Bochum survey, the ASAS SN, and the ZTF, and analyzed large-amplitude and periodic cases with Lomb-Scargle (LS) and phase dispersion minimization (PDM) methods. Gaia DR3 matches are available for 67% of the sample and 76% are reported as variable. We identify high-amplitude variables and periodic systems that may be binaries rather than classical LBVs. Six confirmed LBVs and five candidates show variations larger than 0.6 mag in the Gaia RP filter. Their light curves are examined and three periodic variables are identified. The light curves of OMN2000 LS1 and DWC2011 140 show primary and secondary minima, strongly suggesting eclipsing binary systems. OMN2000 LS1 has a well-constrained period of 80.29 d, and DWC2011 140 of 95.07 d.

title: VenusOCR2.0: Towards Efficient and Effective Document Parsing
abstract: We present VenusOCR2.0, a compact 1B-parameter vision-language recognizer designed for both high-accuracy and high-throughput document parsing across text, tables, and formulas. To continuously improve recognition quality without self-training collapse, we build a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) data engine where the model acts strictly as a weakness probe, while external multi-expert medoid consensus, VLM visual verification, and factorized synthesis supply reliable supervision across pretraining, curated SFT, and RLVR. VenusOCR2.0 couples a dynamic-resolution SigLIP2 encoder and 2x2 spatial token merging with a Qwen3-0.6B decoder, adopting compact atomic OTSL tokens to shorten table sequences and reduce structural errors. To further eliminate the autoregressive decoding bottleneck, we introduce PTPv2, a lightweight ($\sim$67M) decoupled parallel draft module that combines frozen multi-layer verifier conditioning, a standalone learned mask, and block-causal all-position next-token prediction. On OmniDocBenchv1.6, VenusOCR2.0 achieves an overall score of 96.45 and a state-of-the-art 98.57 formula CDM, substantially outperforming massive general-purpose VLMs such as Gemini-3-Pro (92.91) and Qwen3-VL-235B (89.78). Deployed in vLLM on a single H20 GPU, PTPv2 delivers a 2.96x single-request speedup and up to 2.36x higher batched throughput while guaranteeing lossless, token-for-token equivalence with standard autoregressive decoding.

title: Spin-Group versus Magnetic-Group Selection Rules for Nonlinear Photocurrents in Compensated Ferrimagnets
abstract: Optical excitation offers a contact-free, ultrafast route to charge and spin currents, with symmetry determining which nonlinear photocurrents are allowed and whether they carry charge, spin, or both. Spin-group symmetry describes the limit without spin-orbit coupling (SOC), whereas magnetic-group symmetry accounts for SOC. We show that the two descriptions yield different selection rules for both charge and spin photocurrents in the multiferroic compensated ferrimagnet GaFeO$_3$. Without SOC, only linear shift and circular injection currents are allowed, with identical components for charge and spin, so every charge current is spin polarized along the moments. SOC leaves these charge currents nearly unchanged, activates magnetic linear injection and circular shift charge currents, and enables pure spin currents polarized perpendicular to the moments. Ferroelectric switching reverses the linear shift and circular injection charge currents and their spin polarization. These findings establish the importance of magnetic-group symmetry for a complete description of nonlinear charge and spin photocurrents in compensated ferrimagnets.

title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
abstract: We study the scalar Schrödinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate. We write the Hamiltonian as a Hermitian coupled-subband matrix and give an exact gauge-adapted variational representation. For a finite radius, the leading twist correction is quadratic, and changes sign at a critical aspect ratio; for an unbounded radial domain, it is linear in $|Ω_g|$. Retuning the aspect ratio through an isolated radial--axial resonance within one $m$ sector opens an avoided crossing with gap $Δ_{\mathrm{gap}}/E_R=1.648775\ldots|Ω_gR^2/L|^3$ to leading order. A transverse dipole transition forbidden without twist acquires an oscillator strength quadratic in the twist, with leading coefficient $0.0559408010$ for $R/L=2$ from perturbation theory. Dipole sum rules and the convergence of the currents serve as checks on the numerics. We also give the inverse-mass tensor required for a scalar realization and re-examine each statement and figure of the earlier article [Opt. Quantum Electron. \textbf{58}, 113 (2026)] within the corrected model.

title: Constrained Allen-Cahn phase-field topology optimization of flexoelectric devices
abstract: Topology optimization provides an effective approach to exploring performance-oriented designs for miniature devices. In this work, a phase-field framework for constrained topology optimization of microscale flexoelectric devices is developed using a continuum model under the assumption of infinitesimal deformations. The material distribution is optimized at the device level with the output voltage as the objective. The framework also accommodates objectives based on capacitance or stored electrostatic energy. Manufacturing variations are incorporated through a worst-case objective over the prescribed geometric realizations, with spectral constraints imposed to maintain the structural connectivity. The framework is applied to two-dimensional pressure and bending sensors and a three-dimensional thin-film device. The optimized nominal output voltages reach approximately 4.8 times the initial value for the pressure sensor and 2.5-3.4 times the initial values for the bending sensors. The voltage gains arise primarily from increased mechanically induced source charge, with capacitance reduction providing an additional contribution that varies with the device configuration. Erosion analyses of representative designs further show that structural connectivity is well preserved when structural members become locally narrower, with the output voltage remaining close to that of the nominal configuration. Combined with specific microfabrication processes, this optimization framework is expected to provide a numerical basis for configuration screening and prototype development of flexoelectric devices.

title: ShapeQuest: Towards Granularity-Controlled Edit-Conditioned 3D Asset Retrieval
abstract: Given a reference asset and an instruction such as "remove one armrest," a retriever must find variants that make the edit and preserve the other parts. This search is well established for images but remains underexplored for individual 3D assets. To study this problem, we introduce ShapeQuest and ShapeQuester, a new benchmark and model for edit-conditioned 3D asset retrieval. ShapeQuest's open-source pipeline edits textured meshes through part additions, removals, and material and colour changes. It controls edit granularity across five levels, defined by the fraction of the object's surface area each edit affects. It constructs multiple valid targets when an instruction leaves the choice of part open. A vision-language model judges each edit from views chosen to expose the edited parts, and human raters audit its judgments. ShapeQuest has 87,824 queries in 50 categories and a 50,919-shape gallery with competing edits. To distinguish these variants, ShapeQuester learns retrieval alongside reconstruction of the edited point cloud, with part masks supervising changed and preserved regions. With a frozen pretrained point encoder, ShapeQuester reaches 50.4 operation-macro mAP@10 on the test split, against 47.2 for the fusion baseline with the same inputs and 48.6 for the strongest baseline. Reconstruction adds 6.5 points on the validation split when the point encoder is trained from scratch, including 3.3 from part masks.

title: RoboRecast: Intent-Preserving Demonstration Augmentation via Diagnosis-Driven Optimization
abstract: Collecting diverse real-world manipulation demonstrations is costly, motivating the use of simulation to augment existing demonstrations for robot policy learning. When objects, layouts, or robots change, transferring motions from a source demonstration can produce behavior that is semantically implausible or physically infeasible in the new setting. We introduce RoboRecast, an agentic optimization framework that preserves the interactions required by the source task while jointly optimizing the simulated scene and robot motion to make those interactions executable in the target setting. When an interaction fails, the agent uses simulation feedback to diagnose the cause, revise the relevant scene or motion parameters, and test whether the revision resolves the failure. This flexibility allows RoboRecast to generate synthetic data from both human and robot demonstrations and to adapt them to new layouts, objects, and robot embodiments. When target demonstrations are available, adding RoboRecast data improves policy success on both real-world single-arm and simulated bimanual tasks. Even without demonstrations in the target configuration, RoboRecast adapts source demonstrations to support policy learning with new objects or robot embodiments.

title: REBEAL: Human References Are No Longer the Best Translation, and Metrics Do Not Notice
abstract: Reference-based MT evaluation assumes the human reference is correct and better than the systems it scores. Both assumptions now fail, since the human reference ranks first in none of the 2024 WMT MQM campaigns and carries annotated errors in 19% to 87% of its segments. What a metric does with a flawed reference is a question about the metric, and it would have been worth asking before reference quality came into doubt. We introduce REBEAL (Reference Bias EvALuation), a benchmark that probes how MT metrics respond to seven types of controlled reference contamination, drawn from the error categories those campaigns record. Across eight widely used metrics and three language pairs, recent learned metrics (xCOMET, MetricX) prove more robust than their predecessors, but each family fails in its own way. Surface metrics show no length sensitivity, so contamination hides in longer segments, while learned metrics accept references in unrelated languages as nearly correct. The failure they share is named-entity contamination, which no metric detects and which flips up to 8 of 36 system pairs when ranking nine MT systems.

title: HiCal: Offline Calibration for Hierarchical Scale Encoding in Accurate HiF4 Quantization
abstract: Block floating-point (BFP) quantization is widely adopted for efficient low-bit large language model (LLM) inference, where the choice of block scales plays a critical role in quantization accuracy. HiFloat4 (HiF4) employs a hierarchical scale encoding scheme consisting of a global E6M2 scale and two levels of binary scale extensions. However, its conventional rounding rule and fixed scale extension thresholds may not fully capture the statistical characteristics of the quantized tensors in practice, leading to suboptimal scale representations. In this work, we propose HiCal, an offline calibration approach that improves HiF4 quantization accuracy by refining the encoding decisions across all three scale levels. Specifically, we introduce a calibrated rounding bias for the Level-1 E6M2 scale and optimize the scale-extension thresholds at Levels 2 and 3 based on the empirical distributions of local group magnitudes. The resulting calibration parameters are determined offline and remain fixed during inference, while the hierarchical encoding continues to adapt to individual blocks through their local values. This design eliminates the need for per-block multi-candidate scale search while preserving the original deterministic HiF4 encoding procedure. Experiments across five synthetic and real activation distributions show that the proposed method reduces quantization MSE by 9.91%-23.50% relative to the original HiF4 scheme, including a 13.00% reduction on real Qwen3-8B activations. End-to-end evaluations across six benchmarks further show average-score improvements of 0.91 and 1.25 percentage points on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, respectively, without per-block multi-candidate search during inference.

title: On the Capabilities and Limitations of Zero-Shot Open-Vocabulary Cloud Segmentation
abstract: Recent advances in vision-language foundation models have enabled open-vocabulary semantic segmentation (OVSS) without task-specific training, offering new opportunities for Earth Observation (EO) applications. However, their capabilities for cloud detection remain insufficiently explored. In this work, we evaluate twelve OVSS approaches across six publicly available EO datasets in a zero-shot setting, i.e., without fine-tuning or adaptation to the target data. We investigate both binary cloud detection and multiclass segmentation, distinguishing between thick clouds, thin clouds, cloud shadows, and background. Our results show differences in performance across models and datasets, with SegEarth-OV3 achieving the highest binary cloud detection performance on four of the six datasets. While several approaches demonstrate promising performance in binary cloud detection, multiclass segmentation remains more challenging, particularly when distinguishing between fine-grained cloud categories. Furthermore, our controlled prompt sensitivity analysis reveals model-dependent responses to alternative textual descriptions, with appearance-oriented prompts benefiting certain approaches while degrading the performance of others. Overall, our findings demonstrate both the potential and current limitations of zero-shot OVSS for cloud detection, establishing a comparative benchmark for future research on generalisable cloud segmentation. Code will be available at: https://github.com/josesosajs/zero-shot-cloudovss.

title: On optimal packing of Minkowski spheres
abstract: A method has been developed for the optimal packing of a continuum family of one-dimensional Minkowski spheres in the real plane.
