This reduces the initial ghosting carried into progressive refinement. Surface-guided replacement then continues to repair the Gaussian distribution while preserving existing appearance. To provide more reliable supervision for this process, observation calibration mitigates interference from multi-temporal observations. Joint refinement further reduces conflicts among generated views. Experiments on DFC2019 and IARPA demonstrate reduced artifacts in low-elevation renderings while maintaining satellite-view fidelity. Compared with Skyfall-GS, CityRecast reduces FID-CLIP by 25.3% on DFC2019 and 51.8% on IARPA. MUSIQ increases by 14.54 and 24.95 points, respectively.

title: Fresh Keys, Stale Secrets: Numeric Leakage across Linked LLM Prompts
abstract: Small businesses repeatedly ask cloud language models about the same confidential prices, unit costs and margins. Numeric prompt disguises for such numbers are evaluated one prompt at a time, but a provider sees a firm's history, in which each fresh secret gives a new, independent view of the same numbers. Since real costs are not public, we measure on synthetic firms with known values how much an honest-but-curious provider recovers when it knows the disguise algorithm, holds sector-level price and margin statistics, and links a firm's queries. In one prompt, per-field scaling, a fixed-axis instantiation of Zhang et al.'s order-preserving substitution and Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt's released sanitizer keep the attacker's margin-hit advantage over a prior-only guess between -0.6 and +4.4 percentage points. After 16 linked queries with fresh secrets, every disguise we test (Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt at $\varepsilon\geq 0.5$) has a target recovered significantly more often: under the order-preserving substitution, margin recovery rises from 25.0% to 59.4%. The same attacker recovers 29.4 percentage points more margins with fresh maps than with one reused map. Theory explains the contrast: one reused secret bounds all queries by a single full-precision view of the fields shown, whereas fresh scaling keys are identifiable. Except for Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt at $\varepsilon=0.5$, the gains persist when the attacker's prior comes from another population model and when values drift by up to 5% between queries; on our firms, whose prose cues are weak, reading the prose with a language model adds at most 2.5 points. Code and data: https://github.com/Jamli58/fresh-keys-stale-secrets

title: Super-Eddington Neutron Star Accretion Columns: Comparing GRRMHD Simulations with Spectral Models
abstract: The geometry and structure of neutron star accretion columns affect the X-ray emission in super-Eddington accreting systems. We perform four axisymmetric general relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations of super-Eddington accretion onto magnetized neutron stars with the maximum surface magnetic fields ranging from $3\times10^{10}$ to $1\times10^{11}\,\mathrm{G}$. We measure the column width and estimate the characteristic radiation shock heights from the flow velocity and velocity gradient. Across the four models, the angular width decreases from approximately $0.14$ to $0.07\,\mathrm{rad}$, while the estimated shock height increases from $1.95$ to $3.89\,\mathrm{km}$. We then compare our solutions to the best-fit values derived from spectral modeling of super-Eddington Be/X-ray binary outbursts. We calculate area-equivalent column radii that vary between 5.2 and 3.2 km, three of which fall within the upper part of the range inferred from spectral results using the \texttt{bwcycl} model.

title: Weight Scale Rebalancing: Transferable Training Recipes for Transformers
abstract: Training Transformers requires careful hyperparameter tuning, which becomes increasingly costly for large models. We introduce UDV-Rebalance (UDVR), a reparameterization that inserts an auxiliary diagonal matrix $D$ between naturally paired weight matrices $(U,V)$ appearing throughout Transformer architectures. UDVR periodically rebalances the factors to maintain unit-norm columns in $U$ and unit-norm rows in $V$, with $D$ absorbing the corresponding scales. With rebalancing, a single hyperparameter setting of UDVR remains effective across model scales, architectures, and data distributions. This yields a tuning-free rule that adapts to each weight matrix using only its dimensions. We fit this rule once on ViT models trained on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100, and it remains valid when the activation function or the optimizer is changed. The same rule transfers to new image domains in DomainNet, to ViT, Swin, and MaxViT on ImageNet, and to language-model pretraining with up to 1.3B parameters. UDVR consistently outperforms Weight Normalization and $σ$Reparam and matches a vanilla baseline whose hyperparameters are swept on each target model.

title: Long-Range Hydrodynamic Communication in Active Matter
abstract: Directed transport in active matter is typically achieved by introducing geometric asymmetry, such as ratchets or gears, that rectify the stochastic motion of active particles. Here we demonstrate a fundamentally different route in which persistent mechanical motion emerges without any geometric bias. A symmetric passive rotor placed at the center of a circular domain undergoes spontaneous unidirectional rotation driven solely by the hydrodynamic flow generated by a boundary-confined flocks of Marangoni swimmers, despite the absence of direct physical contact. While individual swimmers produce intermittent torque reversals arising from transient hydrodynamic backflow, increasing the size of the flock establishes coherent circulation that stabilizes the rotor dynamics. Particle image velocimetry (PIV) reveals that the collectively generated flow transmits momentum over macroscopic distances, converting local active forcing into robust mechanical transport. Together with a minimal flow superposition model, our results identify the suppression of reverse-torque events as a collective signature of hydrodynamic coupling between active swimmers and a passive body, providing a contact-free mechanism for remote mechanical actuation in active matter.

title: Sound Distributed Runtime Verification under Incomplete Evidence
abstract: Distributed runtime verification often requires combining evidence from several nodes to check properties that cannot be evaluated locally. However, when messages are delayed, lost, or deliberately suppressed, the verifier may not know whether a violation occurred or whether the relevant evidence is missing. This creates a risk of incorrectly reporting compliance. We study the requirements for sound monitoring under these conditions. We first show that a deadline-bounded monitor cannot be simultaneously sound, decisive, and available when an adversary can suppress evidence. The monitor must therefore be able to abstain. We then distinguish two sources of incomplete evidence. Sequence numbers and periodic reports can identify missing events, whereas detecting silent streams requires timing assumptions. We also examine how membership changes and coordinator failures affect verdict soundness and recovery. We implement these mechanisms in a three-tier monitoring architecture using MQTT and NATS JetStream. Experiments with an LLM-planned robot swarm demonstrate the failure modes, show how the proposed mechanisms prevent unsupported compliance verdicts, and measure their runtime and communication costs.

title: AI, Bias, and Inclusion: A Two-Phase Mixed-Methods Study of Gender Bias, Awareness, and Trust in Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are widespread across fields such as healthcare, finance, employment, and criminal justice, with a substantial impact on the lives of individuals and society. However, it has been established that AI systems perpetuate existing social inequalities, particularly through biases that are not easily discernible. Such biases are embedded in the technical and social structures of artificial intelligence systems, making them difficult to detect. These biases challenge the concept of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI), which recognizes diversity as the acknowledgment of individual differences, equity as fairness and equal access, and inclusion as the value placed on all participants. This study argues that fairness in artificial intelligence systems cannot be achieved by focusing solely on their technical aspects, necessitating a holistic approach. This study employs a two-phase mixed-methods design. Phase 1 applies computational content analysis to 360 occupational narratives generated by ChatGPT across four countries (Canada, Germany, India, and Bangladesh) using gender-neutral prompts to examine whether professions are predominantly associated with one gender and whether these patterns remain consistent across regions. Phase 2 examines the extent to which students recognize potential bias in AI, their trust in AI for consequential decision-making, and how these perceptions relate to themes in EDI and AI ethics scholarship. By combining output-level bias analysis with user perception data, this study identifies the empirical foundations necessary for future EDI-AI co-design frameworks, outlining the sociotechnical dimensions that such frameworks must address to be effective.

title: Finite-time blowup in the inviscid GOY and Sabra models
abstract: For the inviscid GOY and Sabra shell models with zero boundary conditions at the lowest shells, we construct strong solutions with finitely supported initial data whose vorticity amplitudes blow up in the supremum norm in finite time, at the self-similar rate $(T-t)^{-1}$. The blowup is stable under small perturbations of the initial data in the same norm, including complex-valued ones. Guided by the work of Mailybaev, we use a travelling wave of the renormalized equations to obtain blowup in the original variables. We construct such a wave for the equations extended to all integer shells, decaying in both directions. We then show that the dynamics near this wave contract once the directions generated by time-translation and phase symmetries are removed by adjusting the symmetry parameters at each step (a modulation argument). This yields blowup solutions on the positive shells satisfying the original boundary conditions. Computer-assisted interval arithmetic is used to establish the existence of the travelling wave and the contraction estimate needed for the modulation argument.

title: Gorenstein symmetry can fail for noetherian rings
abstract: We construct a two-sided noetherian ring $A$ which has injective dimension $1$ as a left module over itself and infinite injective dimension as a right module over itself. This shows that Gorenstein symmetry can fail for two-sided noetherian rings. It is further shown that there is such an example over any field of characteristic different than $2$, that it has a dualizing complex, and that its derived category of right modules does not satisfy injective-generation in the sense of Rickard-Keller.

title: A short proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture
abstract: We give a short alternative proof of Seymour's Second Neighborhood Conjecture, recently proved by OpenAI. Our proof combines their reduction with a different argument showing that every nontrivial oriented graph $G$ contains a nonempty set $X$ such that $X^+\ne V(G)$ and $|(X^+)^+\setminus X^+|\geq|X^+\setminus X|$, where $X^+=N_G^+[X]$.

title: MXFP4 for LLM Inference: Complementary Post-Training Quantization Techniques and Their Interactions
abstract: Recent advances in low-precision representation have introduced several microscaling numerical formats for LLM quantization. By sharing a scale factor across groups of 16 or 32 elements, these formats enable aggressive low-precision quantization with minimal accuracy degradation, particularly when combined with modern PTQ algorithms. Their accuracy depends on how the numerical format interacts with rotation, PTQ, and scale selection. We study the composability of PTQ configurations across six LLMs and three microscaling formats: MXFP6, MXFP4, and NVFP4, systematically varying Hadamard rotation granularity, PTQ algorithm, and scale-selection strategy. Our central finding is that effective quantization recipes are format dependent: both MXFP4 and NVFP4 support accurate 4-bit inference, but techniques that benefit one do not necessarily transfer to the other. MXFP4 benefits substantially from rotation and error-correcting PTQ, whereas NVFP4 gains less from rotation, consistent with its finer-grained scales capturing more within-block variation. Building on these findings, we introduce Midmax, a calibration-free scale-selection strategy that mitigates clipping error in power-of-two block scales and improves accuracy across a majority of the evaluated MXFP4 configurations. We show that pairing MXFP6 activations with MXFP4 weights recovers most of the accuracy lost at 4-bit and, on Llama-3.1-8B, matches or exceeds our in-house BF16 baseline. An additional study finds that augmenting MXFP4 with a per-tensor macroscale, a mechanism intrinsic to NVFP4, does not improve average accuracy, suggesting that global rescaling alone does not address the limitations of E8M0 block scales for MXFP4 quantization. Together, these results provide practical guidance for combining numerical formats, rotation, PTQ, and scale selection for accurate low-precision LLM inference.

title: An intrinsic kinematic wave model with conservative fluxes for overland flow on curved terrain
abstract: Kinematic wave models, the simplest surface flow models, route overland flow by gravity alone and there is no pressure or inertial term to redistribute flow when the resulting velocities misroute it. Computed from piecewise-linear elevation data, this velocity jumps across the edges of the mesh: two neighboring cells can push water into each other, and the scheme can hold water in ponds that the terrain does not contain, or concentrate it where the data do not. We formulate the model intrinsically on the bed surface, with the depth normal to the bed as unknown, and obtain a single-valued edge velocity, in the unique edge frame of the intrinsic geometry, by correcting the raw cell field with the star-based conservative flux of Larson and Niklasson. Because the field is derived from data rather than from a Galerkin solution, the local problems are solvable only with a compatible load, the weak discrete divergence of the field being corrected, which for the slope is a discrete mean curvature of the terrain. With a Neumann boundary, every element is conservative, and the corrected field reproduces the cell average of the nodal divergence of the raw field, plus the divergence resolved inside the curved cells. Since any single-valued flux conserves mass, the correction is about consistency and robustness: the steady state of the upwind scheme solves an M-matrix system exactly when every cell drains to an outlet, and spurious ponds are closed classes of a transfer directed graph, computable before any simulation. Four rainfall tests, from a plane to a real catchment, are designed to verify the difference in storage and timing between the intrinsic and the classical form, the effect of the mesh on the consistency of the edge velocity, the robustness at a degenerate stationary point, and the application to terrain data.

title: Counting periodic points of rational self-maps of projective varieties
abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the number of isolated periodic points of a dominant rational self-map of a smooth projective variety. We first give an upper bound for this number in terms of the degrees of the iterates of the map, thereby extending a theorem of Dinh--Nguyen--Truong to arbitrary characteristic. Our approach is purely algebraic and bypasses the theory of densities of positive closed currents. We then establish the exact asymptotic growth of isolated periodic points of birational self-maps of surfaces over a field of characteristic 0. To do so, we extend Jonsson--Reschke's argument to any finitely generated field over $ \mathbb Q $ using Moriwaki's theory of heights.

title: MemHand: Memory-Enhanced World-Space Hand Motion Reconstruction from Egocentric Videos
abstract: Recovering the continuous world-space motion of both hands from egocentric video is essential for applications such as human-to-robot policy transfer and augmented reality. Achieving this goes beyond reconstructing the hands from each individual frame, as the context that a frame needs is often spread over time, especially around occlusions or when a hand moves out of sight. Recent works have explored how to exploit temporal context, yet they mostly draw it from fixed-length windows. Such windows cannot guarantee that every frame has the context required to reconstruct the hands in world space with accurate poses and metric scale. To address this limitation, we introduce MemHand, a memory-enhanced framework for world-space hand motion reconstruction. MemHand maintains two complementary forms of memory. The Short-Term Event Memory keeps the context of the well-observed hand around each occlusion or out-of-sight event and supplies it to frames with weak or missing visual evidence. In addition, since the metric scale holds over the whole recording, the Long-Term Scale Memory retains the most reliable observations across the video as scale anchors within a bounded state. Across benchmarks featuring severe occlusions and frequent out-of-sight intervals, MemHand achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and generalizes well to unseen domains. Benefiting from the synergy of both memories, it cuts W-MPJPE by 57\% on ARCTIC and 70\% on HOT3D relative to StableHand, delivering continuous and metrically accurate world-space hand poses and trajectories. We will release our code and models at the project page: https://irmvlab.github.io/memhand.github.io

title: Simultaneously Boosting Efficiency and Capability for Linear Attention via Adaptive Channel Compression and Activation Purification
abstract: Self-attention's quadratic complexity constitutes a core bottleneck for Vision Transformers (ViTs). Existing efficiency-oriented optimizations, including softmax-based and linear attention (LA) variants, generally compromise model representational capacity, leading to inevitable performance degradation. We propose a novel linear attention which alleviates this efficiency-capability dilemma. For the first time, we embed an Adaptive Channel Compression and Activation Purification (ACCAP) mechanism into the QKV projection of linear attention, which enables the model to retain high-dimensional feature information while performing computations with reduced channels. We further fuse a focused kernel function and a self-gating module into ACCAP to construct a lightweight linear attention module (ACCAP-LA). Our theoretical analysis shows that, compared to standard linear attention, ACCAP-LA reduces the attention module's parameter count by 79.17% and FLOPs by 77.5%. Extensive experiments demonstrate ACCAP-LA's effectiveness: when applied to ViT, it achieves 79.4% Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K with only 5.8M parameters, and more notably, it boasts strong cross-architecture compatibility, boosting EfficientViT-b1 and PVT-T by 3.3% and 3.4% respectively.

title: Regression calibration for logistic regression with correlated measurement error and multiple misclassification in covariates
abstract: Epidemiological analyses often suffer from covariate data quality issues: measurement error in continuous predictors and misclassification of categorical variables. Existing logistic regression correction methods mostly handle only one error type or a single misclassified variable, with limited tools for multiple misclassified categorical exposures together with correlated measurement error in continuous covariates. To address this gap, we extend regression calibration for logistic regression to jointly accommodate multiple continuous covariates with correlated additive measurement error and two or more misclassified categorical predictors. We build a unified framework integrating additive measurement error models and misclassification transition matrices, deriving the regression calibration estimator (RCE) using Kronecker product algebra. This computationally feasible approach extends naturally to more than two misclassified categorical variables. We evaluate RCE via simulations across varied misclassification rates, error magnitudes, sample sizes and effect sizes, comparing it with the naive estimator that ignores measurement error. We apply RCE to the EPIC-InterAct male case-cohort data to adjust for correlated error in protein and energy intake, plus misclassification in binary physical activity and three-category alcohol consumption. Results show that neglecting these error sources produces substantial bias and misleading inference for main and interaction effects in nutritional epidemiology. While the RCE is a practical correction tool, it treats validation nuisance parameters as known and does not account for their estimation uncertainty.

title: Convexification effects of $L_p$-sums
abstract: It is a classical result, quantified by Shapley, Folkman, and Starr, that the Minkowski averages of any compact set asymptotically approach its convex hull in the Hausdorff metric. In this paper, we investigate the analogous convexification phenomenon for the Firey $L_p$-sums of compact sets. First, we establish new structural properties of the $L_p$-sum. Notably, we show that the iterated $L_p$-sum of compact sets whose convex hull contains the origin is eventually starlike. We then study $L_p$-convexification for three classical measures of nonconvexity: Hausdorff metric, volume deficit, and effective standard deviation. For each of these measures, we prove that the $k$-fold $L_p$-sum averages of a compact set $A$ converge to $\text{conv}(0,A)$ when $1<p<\infty$, and to $\text{conv}(A)$ when $p=\infty$. In each case, we show that the convergence to the convex hull is eventually monotone. For the Hausdorff metric and effective standard deviation, we prove sharp upper bounds for the $L_p$-sum of two compact sets.

title: Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems
abstract: Zariski-van Kampen theorems are meant to constitute a complement to Lefschetz-Zariski theorems which, in turn, generalize the classical Lefschetz theorem on hyperplane sections to quasi-projective varieties or to the corresponding local case. Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems are developed here as a tool which is useful both in the local and in the global case.

title: Scalable Placement for Disaggregated LLM Serving on Heterogeneous Edge Fleets
abstract: Serving large language models (LLMs) at the edge is increasingly desirable for privacy-sensitive applications and scenarios that require data to remain on local devices. However, edge environments are constrained by limited computational resources and exhibit substantial device heterogeneity, making efficient LLM serving challenging. These limitations become particularly pronounced under bursty demand, where congestion and queue buildup can significantly increase response latency. Replicating the model into multiple pipeline instances can improve serving capacity and reduce congestion. Yet, deciding how devices should be grouped into replicas, assigning replicas to prefill or decode functions, and partitioning model layers across heterogeneous devices jointly creates a large combinatorial optimization problem. We present Spade, a scalable and runtime-efficient placement planner for disaggregated LLM serving with pipeline replication across heterogeneous edge clusters. Spade introduces a dominance-based pruning technique that discards inferior replica candidates and recursively eliminates larger candidates that contain them, dramatically shrinking the search space. It further combines a water-filling approach for layer partitioning with a bounded multidimensional knapsack formulation that optimizes placement under a congestion-aware objective. On a synthetic fleet of 30 devices spanning five hardware classes, Spade finds the optimal placement in 441ms. In contrast, a genetic-search baseline augmented with dynamic-programming partitioning requires approximately two hours and still produces solutions with a 19.7% worse congestion objective. When evaluated on fleets containing ten device types, Spade's pruning strategy eliminates 99.6% of candidate placements while yielding the same surviving candidate set as exhaustive enumeration.

title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has significantly increased data center (DC) power demand. Frequent operational and configurational changes, such as load surges caused by dynamic workload allocation, can induce electromagnetic transients (EMTs) whose accurate prediction is critical for reliable DC operation and maintenance. Although high-fidelity EMT solvers are widely adopted for transient analysis, their computational cost limits large-scale and multi-scenario studies. Digital twins address this computational bottleneck by emulating the behavior of a physical system and enabling fast prediction in place of expensive high-fidelity simulation. However,data-driven digital twins are non-adaptive and fail to generalize once the DC configuration changes. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an adaptive EMT-level digital twin for DCs based on in-context learning (ICL) with large language models (LLMs). We formulate the EMT prediction task as a system identification problem under parametric uncertainty and develop a GPT-2-based framework that adapts to unseen DC configurations at inference time from a small set of EMT trajectory samples, without model retraining. The proposed framework is validated on three representative EMT scenarios and benchmarked against three baseline non-adaptive twins. Results demonstrate superior prediction accuracy, improved adaptability to unseen operating conditions, and substantial computational speedups compared to high-fidelity EMT simulation.

title: 3D Tracking Any Point with Events and Frames
abstract: Tracking a fast-moving point in 3D is prohibitive when RGB frames are blurred or too far apart to reveal its motion. Event cameras record brightness changes between frames, providing measurements inside these temporal gaps. We introduce TrackAnyMotion, which combines monocular RGB frames and events to track arbitrary points in 2D and 3D, including at times when no RGB frame is available. The motion expected for a static point, given scene geometry and camera motion, provides a reference for identifying independently moving objects. An independent-motion decoder combines geometric motion cues with event guidance and 2D tracks, feeding its predictions back into iterative 2D and 3D refinement. We also introduce HyperEvent, a synthetic RGB--Event dataset with high-frequency 3D trajectories, geometry, and independent-motion labels. At RGB frame timestamps on this benchmark, TrackAnyMotion reduces 3D and 2D endpoint errors by 70\% and 32\%, respectively.

title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
abstract: AI agents working on long tasks often commit to an answer before they have enough evidence, a behavior called laziness. In our evaluations, they frequently commit even while their stated belief still names several possible answers. An outcome reward at the end of the episode scores only the final answer, so it cannot teach the agent when to commit, because a lucky guess receives the same reward as an answer backed by evidence. During training, however, the simulator can compute the exact posterior over the answer at every step and tell whether the evidence is already enough. We propose Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs (RLVB), which rewards the agent for taking further steps while this posterior still allows several answers and for committing once the evidence is sufficient. The reward needs no judge, critic or reward model, and it never reads the belief line the agent writes before each action. We also introduce Pro Worlds, a benchmark of visual puzzles where the agent views a large world through a small window. We evaluate three vision-language models on three benchmarks, two of which are never seen in training. RLVB improves the base model in all nine settings, by 17.1% on average. Under the outcome reward, GRPO and PPO fall below the base model on average. RLVB also outperforms PPO with a process reward from an LLM judge by 9.3% on average while using 1.6 times fewer GPU-hours. The trained agent answers with sufficient evidence in 51%, 12% and 74% of the episodes on the three benchmarks, against 8%, 0.4% and 36% for the base model. Its accuracy gain therefore comes from answering more often at high levels of evidence. The belief line shows how the agent reaches this evidence: it acts on its own belief. It commits at only 0.1 to 2.2% of the turns at which the evidence is insufficient and its line still names several answers, against 3 to 68% for the base model.

title: On the potential of widening the band of X-ray polarimetry
abstract: The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) has made X-ray polarimetry a routine astrophysical diagnostic, but its sensitivity is confined to the 2-8 keV band, where the photoelectric effect in a gas is most efficiently exploited. Several of the questions raised by its results, as well as some classical goals of high-energy astrophysics, require polarimetry below 2~keV, to reach the thermal emission of neutron stars, black-hole discs and blazars, and above 8~keV, where reflection, cyclotron lines and the non-thermal emission of supernova remnants, pulsar wind nebulae and magnetars can be isolated. Following a recent review of the subject, we discuss the scientific case for extending the band over roughly 0.1-80 keV and beyond, and the techniques that can deliver it: Bragg diffraction on graded multilayers, photoelectric gas imagers read out by pixel ASICs with time-of-arrival capability, time projection chambers and focal-plane Compton polarimeters, including their combination in stacked focal planes. We then summarise how these techniques are being implemented, or could be, in REDSoX and GOSoX, eXTP, XPP, WXPT and in EXPO and PHEMTO, proposed to the ESA M8 call, as well as in the wide-field transient polarimeter POLAR-2, and we discuss the trade-offs that will drive the design of a wide-band polarimetry mission.

title: The Capacity of Conference Key Agreement over GHZ Networks
abstract: $K$ users share independent GHZ states, each held by a subset of the users, and want a common secret key, using local operations and public classical communication (LOCC). We show that the conference key capacity, the largest number of secret key bits per copy of the resource, equals the key capacity of the classical source obtained by measuring every GHZ state. Measuring first is therefore optimal, even when the users keep quantum memory and communicate over any number of rounds. The capacity also equals the GHZ distillation capacity, the largest number of GHZ states shared by all users obtainable per copy.

title: Ancient solutions of mean curvature flow in a slab
abstract: In this paper, we study complete ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow in arbitrary codimension contained in slabs in Euclidean space. Under a natural principal-angle condition, we prove that a translating soliton contained in a slab of width less than $π$ cannot be bounded from below in the translating direction, and characterize the grim reaper cylinder in form of a rigidity result at the critical width $π$. We derive corresponding results for ancient solutions confined in slabs.

title: Generalizing Couple-Randomized Trials Under Limited Overlap and Missing Partner Linkage
abstract: We study how to generalize couple-randomized trials when some couple types are absent from the trial and the target survey reports partner characteristics without linking spouses. Under an additive effect model with unrestricted partner-profile terms, the target average effect is identified exactly when the wife and husband margins assign equal mass to each connected component of the trial support graph. A specified interaction is identified when its alternating contrast around at least one cycle is nonzero. Without linkage, we obtain sharp bounds by optimizing over pairings consistent with the survey margins. A spousal odds ratio can narrow the bounds for a binary interaction. We derive joint bounds for an index-patient design, quantify bias from common shortcuts, and estimate effects and bounds using Bayesian dyadic multilevel regression and poststratification. In a worked example based on 3,826 Health and Retirement Study couples and simulated trial outcomes, an index-patient trial and an unlinked survey yielded a 2.93 mmHg wide identified set for the couple-average effect. Linking the survey narrowed it to 2.38 mmHg. Adding 300 couples without diabetes narrowed the unlinked set to 0.28 mmHg and yielded point identification with linkage under the fitted model.

title: Joint Detection of Constructive Speech, Hate Speech and Agreement in Online Conversations
abstract: Online hate speech is an ever-growing issue with negative impacts on both groups and individuals, potentially causing users to withdraw from online conversations and debate. With some prominent social media platforms reducing their moderation efforts, constructive speech has emerged as an alternative strategy for countering hate. Automated detection of constructive and hateful speech can aid monitoring and improve understanding of their prevalence and online dynamics. In this work, we collect and annotate a large dataset of English and Danish social media comments for hateful tone, constructive tone, and agreement with parent comments. We fine-tune several multilingual LLMs to classify along these three dimensions and compare context-enriched and non-context-enriched model architectures. The E5-large LLM performs best on both the context-enriched (82% average F1) and non-context-enriched (81.6% average F1) classification tasks, demonstrating the potential of multilingual LLMs for scalable detection of hateful and constructive speech across languages.

title: Biomechanically Grounded Prediction of Selective Motor Control and Clinical Outcomes from Infant Video
abstract: Early identification of cerebral palsy (CP) relies on observational assessments of spontaneous infant movement, such as the General Movement Assessment (GMA) and the Baby Observational Selective Control AppRaisal (BabyOSCAR), which require trained raters and substantial scoring time. Existing automated approaches derive hand-engineered features from two-dimensional keypoints, which describe image-plane motion rather than the three-dimensional behavior of individual joints. We present Baby Biomechanical 3D Body (BB3D), an infant-adapted, biomechanical pipeline that estimates joint-angle trajectories from single-camera video. Against a multi-view markerless motion capture reference in 17 infants, BB3D's median Procrustes-aligned error was 17.5~mm for joint centers and 20.4~mm for marker sites. A spatio-temporal transformer, pretrained on BB3D joint-angle trajectories from 1k+ single-camera recordings, and fine-tuned on 550 videos from 350 infants, predicted each individual BabyOSCAR item with a mean within-site AUC of 0.79 and the BabyOSCAR total with a Spearman correlation of 0.86 on held-out recordings. Without being trained on diagnosis, the predicted total separated infants with CP from those without CP with an AUC of 0.86, exceeding a replicated two-dimensional feature classifier (0.67) but below the expert clinician rater's total (0.97). Predicted scores also carried information about functional ability and body distribution, though less than expert clinician scores. These results show that biomechanically grounded representations of monocular video can support scalable, joint-level assessment of selective motor control in infancy

title: Global regularities for the Dirichlet problem of Monge-Ampère type equations
abstract: We establish global a priori $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,α}$ estimates for elliptic solutions of the Dirichlet problem for cost-generated Monge-Ampère type equations under the weak Ma-Trudinger-Wang condition A3w, assuming continuous and Hölder continuous right-hand sides, respectively.

title: Shared information governs multi-view planted matching
abstract: We study when the rows of $K$ shuffled views of the same $n$ objects can be matched, where each object is observed once in every view through a Gaussian feature vector with known covariance. For every fixed $K$, all views can be matched up to $o(n)$ errors if the shared information $J$ of one object's $K$ observations exceeds $(1+ε)\log n$, and not if it is below $(1-ε)\log n$; this can hold although no two views can be matched on their own. Below the threshold, two views can still be matched if some set of views containing both has shared information above $\log n$; otherwise every estimator, even one that reads all views, has vanishing overlap between them. Matching every row is governed by the weakest bipartition of the views: with weak correlations the threshold is $2\log n$ for the mutual information across it. For a weak common signal observed through independent noise, the two thresholds are $4/K$ and $4/(K-1)$ in units of $\sum_\ellρ_\ell^2/\log n$, which answers a question of Wee, Yang, Fan and Mao. Beyond weak correlations the bipartition condition is not sufficient: rare subpopulations impose a Rényi condition for every partition into at least three blocks. We conjecture that the two conditions together characterize exact recovery for Gaussian laws, and prove this for three views with equal correlations and in several further cases, in part with computer assistance. With equal correlations, layered screening attains $4/K$ for $K=3,4$ in $O(Kn^2d)$ operations, and for general laws a recursive decoder attains $J$. The almost-exact thresholds extend to known product laws and to objects observed in random subsets of the views.

title: An intrinsic criterion for Pansu differentials to be homomorphisms of nilpotent Lie groups
abstract: By Pansu's theorem, Lipschitz maps between Carnot groups are differentiable almost everywhere, and their differentials are group homomorphisms. When the domain is instead a nilpotent Lie group with a bracket-generating left-invariant distribution, the Pansu differential is a homomorphism of an osculating Carnot group, which depends on an auxiliary choice of grading, and it need not be a homomorphism of the original group. We give an intrinsic criterion for when it is one, for a suitable choice of grading: the differential must vanish on an ideal that depends only on the group and its distribution, and comes from a universal quotient onto a Carnot group. The criterion holds automatically when the step of the target is small enough, and an explicit example shows that this threshold is sharp. Along the way, we determine exactly how the obstruction depends on the choice of grading.

title: Alert-Preserving Lossy Compression of Monitoring Time Series
abstract: Monitoring systems store large volumes of floating-point time series, and most of these data are read only by alerting rules: threshold tests on window aggregates with a hold duration. A lossy compressor with one error bound for all samples either wastes space far from the thresholds or changes alerts near them. We use the alert decisions as the correctness criterion. For every rule, the reconstructed series must produce the same sequence of alert states (Inactive, Pending, Firing) as the original, at any evaluation interval and phase. For PromQL threshold rules over last, avg/sum/min/max_over_time and rate we derive a sound error budget for each sample, computable in linear time. It is the smallest value, over all windows that contain the sample, of the window's distance to the threshold divided by a Lipschitz constant. Because the aggregates are monotone, the budget splits into separate bounds for downward and upward errors. For Prometheus' extrapolated rate, an order-preserving quantizer leaves only the first and last sample of each window constrained. Our codec combines predictive coding, a range coder and a lazy step choice that keeps the prediction whenever the budget allows, which suits the asymmetric budget. After encoding, it decodes the output, re-evaluates every rule and repairs any changed decision, so the guarantee holds for the floating-point output. Parts of the floating-point argument are machine-checked with Kani. On 13 real series from the public Prometheus demo servers (7 and 30 days), the codec keeps every alert decision (9,055 firings) at 1.0-1.5 bits per value. This is 4-6.5 times less than a uniform bound tuned on the same data and less than Compression Safeguards over SZ3 on 19 of 26 rule variants. In an ablation, the one-sided budget and the lazy step choice together reduce the size by a factor of 2.4-2.5

title: Trotterized hybrid qubit-boson simulation of the Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard model
abstract: The Jaynes-Cummings-Hubbard (JCH) model describes the interaction of light and matter in coupled optical cavities and provides a framework for studying their quantum dynamics. In this work, we design a Trotterized quantum circuit to investigate the real-time dynamics of the JCH model using Bosonic Qiskit and a Matrix Product State (MPS) backend. We simulate single-polariton transport and benchmark site occupations against exact diagonalization results. We then extend the simulations to the two-excitation sector under a hard-core photon constraint, examining excitation transport and symmetry properties. Finally, we study the dependence of bipartite entanglement entropy on the inter-cavity photon-hopping strength. The results illustrate how hybrid qubit-boson circuits, simulated with matrix product states, can be used to study light-matter lattice dynamics. This work provides a numerical benchmark for extending hybrid simulation approaches to more complex interacting and open light-matter systems.

title: DualSpec: Spectral Reconstruction with Optimized Stereo Cameras
abstract: Spectral imaging captures information that ordinary RGB sensors cannot, but dedicated spectral cameras can be expensive and bulky. Recovering dense spectra from RGB images offers an accessible alternative, but distinct spectra can produce the same camera response, generating an ambiguity that even more advanced recovery algorithms cannot always resolve. Therefore, increasing the spectral information captured at acquisition is essential. We propose DualSpec, a stereo acquisition framework that jointly optimizes two external optical filters and a reconstruction network. Each filter is placed in front of a standard RGB camera, and the two are designed to produce six responses that provide complementary information for the network. Experiments across reconstruction architectures and spectral ranges show that DualSpec reduces mean spectral angle error by 36-72% relative to a single RGB camera and by 11-29% relative to stereo pairs selected from commercial filters. Cross-dataset evaluations, including a new benchmark of spectral images captured from displaced viewpoints, show that the method generalizes and remains robust to viewpoint misalignment, while analyses of thin-film approximations support optical feasibility.

title: Discretely self-similar solutions to coupled fluid systems with locally $L^2$ data
abstract: In this paper we present a systematic way to construct discretely self-similar solutions of fluid systems, including the viscous resistive magnetohydrodynamics equations, the viscoelastic Navier-Stokes equations with damping, and the Oberbeck-Boussinesq system, for locally $L^2$ initial data which are not necessarily in the uniformly local $L^2$ space. The solutions satisfy local energy inequalities, local a priori bounds depending only on the $L^2$ norm of the initial data in a fixed ball (and, for the Oberbeck--Boussinesq system, on the force), and a limiting formula for the pressure.

title: A Dimension-Free Bound on the FDR of the Benjamini-Hochberg Procedure under Slowly Decaying Gaussian Correlations
abstract: The Benjamini-Hochberg (BH) procedure is proven to control the false discovery rate under independence and under positive dependence. Under arbitrary dependence, however, its guarantee deteriorates by a factor that grows logarithmically with the number of hypotheses. For Gaussian test statistics, it is unknown whether dependence can make the false discovery rate grow with the number of tests. We study this question when the correlation between two test statistics decays with the distance between their indices. We seek guarantees that hold uniformly over a wide class of correlation structures and over all configurations of the signals. We show that if the correlations decay at least as fast as a power of the inverse logarithm of the distance with exponent larger than one, then the false discovery rate of the original BH procedure is bounded by the nominal level times a factor that does not depend on the number of hypotheses. This factor grows only polylogarithmically as the level decreases. The result holds for both one- and two-sided tests, and the procedure uses no knowledge of the correlations. The class allows correlations of both signs. The required decay can be arbitrarily close to the inverse logarithm. The key technical tool is a truncated Hermite expansion of the exceedance indicators. It shows that their main fluctuations are common to all thresholds that BH may use. These fluctuations can be well controlled, while the remainder is too small to accumulate, which leads to a bound that does not inflate with the dimension.

title: Label leakage through file headers: geometry and batch confounds in public mammography datasets, and a pre-training acceptance gate
abstract: A dataset whose diagnostic label can be recovered from non-diagnostic information yields high, reproducible and uninformative model performance. We applied pre-training controls that see only image geometry, global texture, a sub-collection identifier or one covariate to six public mammography datasets, against a stop threshold of AUC 0.60. In KAU-BCMD, geometry alone predicted the BI-RADS class at AUC 1.0000 in a local copy and at a mean of 0.979 in a public Kaggle archive; after resizing, texture alone gave 0.847. In CMMD, the sub-collection prefix predicted malignancy at 0.7753; the restricted sub-collection passed geometry (0.5000) and texture (0.5810) but failed an identifier-order control added post hoc (test AUC 0.9926). CBIS-DDSM exceeded the stop on geometry (pooled mean 0.654 over 20 splits), a verdict statistic chosen post hoc; its official mass and calcification splits did not. M-SYNTH, INbreast and a partial VinDr-Mammo copy passed the few controls run. We release the code and derived tables. There is no quantum component in the inference path.

title: Motion Conditioned World Modeling for Embodied Visual Tracking
abstract: World models support embodied decision-making by predicting future environment states. In embodied visual tracking, uncertain target motion and robot-induced viewpoint changes jointly affect visual observations, making future-state prediction challenging. We propose Motion-Conditioned World Modeling, which incorporates predicted target-motion distributions and robot ego-motion into latent state transitions. A Geometry--Progress module jointly models geometric paths and single-step travel distances through shared motion modes and path-conditioned progress distributions. This formulation captures uncertainty in route selection and motion progress while preserving their dependence. Action-induced coordinate transformations express predicted paths in the next robot frame, providing geometrically grounded conditions for future visual-state prediction. Future visual feature reconstruction supervises the motion predictor through the conditioned transition branch, linking explicit motion representations to subsequent observations. The model is jointly optimized with motion likelihood, feature reconstruction, and expert-action supervision, enabling the tracking policy to combine visual context with predictive motion cues.Experiments on three embodied tracking benchmarks demonstrate improved tracking performance and cross-environment generalization with a lightweight $0.5$B backbone.

title: Fisher information in the flux landscape
abstract: We quantify the fine-tuning of the flux superpotential in Type IIB Calabi-Yau orientifold compactifications using the Fisher Information Metric. Treating the background fluxes as model parameters and the magnitude of the superpotential as the physical observable, we show that the Fisher matrix admits a unique non-zero eigenvalue that bounds the superpotential from above and factorises into axio-dilaton, complex structure components and a bounded factor depending on both moduli and the phase of the superpotential. In the canonical duality frame and over the full flux lattice, this eigenvalue grows linearly with the inverse string coupling and cubically with the complex structure saxions. Specialising to a two modulus orientifold of the degree 18 hypersurface in $\mathbb{P}^4(1,1,1,6,9)$ at large complex structure, we combine the flux integrality with the D3-brane tadpole condition to show that several flux components, including the one driving this growth, are forced to vanish across deep moduli space patches, truncating the twelve-dimensional flux lattice to an eight-dimensional sublattice. The Fisher eigenvalue restricted to these admissible flux directions either approaches a constant or grows at most linearly, much more slowly than over the full lattice.

title: Dirac Propagation for Simulating Fermionic Observables under Particle-Number-Conserving Unitaries
abstract: Simulating the dynamics of interacting fermions remains a central computational challenge across physics and chemistry. We introduce Dirac propagation, a classical method that simulates local observables in fermionic systems subject to particle-number-conserving unitaries. We show that, in the operator expansion, strings with weights above the total particle number can be discarded without incurring any error in the final expectation value. This exact cutoff bounds the number of retained strings polynomially in the number of modes at fixed particle number, including for interacting dynamics. The formalism combines a compact representation with explicit expressions for interacting gates and exact treatment of number-conserving fermionic Gaussian and Clifford unitaries. This framework offers an approach to simulating fermionic many-body dynamics and classically benchmarking fermionic quantum circuits.

title: IMPACT-Seg: Consistent Anatomical Segmentation and Representation Learning Across CT, CBCT, and MRI
abstract: Computed tomography (CT), cone-beam CT (CBCT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provide complementary representations of the same underlying anatomy, yet substantial differences in image appearance challenge consistent segmentation and deformable registration in adaptive radiotherapy. We investigate whether dense anatomical segmentation supervision can promote cross-modality correspondence without explicit feature alignment. We introduce IMPACT-Seg, which segments 126 structures across CT, CBCT, and MRI using shared network parameters. A collection of 8,290 volumes was assembled from public cohorts through label harmonization, model-assisted pseudo-label completion, iterative refinement, and 2,864 physics-based CBCT simulations with voxel-aligned CT labels. Unpaired images were used to jointly train 2.5D and 3D residual-encoder networks. On 139 real CBCTs, IMPACT-Seg 3D achieved a mean Dice of 0.842 versus 0.671 for the strongest comparator. On 497 voxel-aligned CT-simulated-CBCT pairs, the CT-to-CBCT Dice decrease was 0.022 versus 0.153-0.178 for competing methods. On independent pancreatic radiotherapy CBCTs, gastrointestinal Dice was 0.735 versus 0.634 for TotalSegmentator. Prediction agreement reached 0.881 on registered CT-CBCT and 0.790 on CT-MRI pairs. Adding MRI training data reduced CT-MRI encoder feature retrieval error from 36.8 to 3.2 mm. Registration pipelines incorporating IMPACT-Seg features ranked first on two multimodal Learn2Reg benchmarks. The 3D model segmented a whole-body CT in 15 s. These findings show that dense anatomical segmentation supervision can support consistent anatomical representations across modalities, with applications to both segmentation and registration. Code, datasets, and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/HEMONCedric/IMPACTSeg.

title: On Waring's problem for fourth powers
abstract: We prove that every sufficiently large integer $n$, satisfying $n\equiv 1,2,3,\dots,11\pmod*{16}$, can be written as a sum of $11$ biquadrates. In particular, $G^{\#}(4)\leq 11$. This improves upon $G^{\#}(4)\leq 12$ due to Vaughan in 1989.

title: TeV Gamma-Ray Transparency Bounds on Neutrinos and Axions
abstract: Multi-TeV gamma rays propagating over cosmological distances measure the extragalactic background light (EBL) through attenuation by electron--positron pair production. This is particularly valuable in the infrared, where the EBL is difficult to measure directly. Since the growing sample of observed multi-TeV photons provides tight constraints on the EBL photon intensity, this, in turn, constrains new particles that radiatively decay into meV--eV photons. We set the first TeV-transparency bounds on active-neutrino electromagnetic transition moments, obtain new constraints on radiatively decaying sterile neutrinos, and derive competitive limits on the axion--photon coupling.

title: Dark Matter Assisted Axion-Magnetic Resonance
abstract: An oscillating axion dark matter (DM) background can enhance the conversion of another relativistic axion into photons when traversing a magnetic field. The DM background rotates photon polarization relative the magnetic orientation, which compensates the photon's and the propagating axion's dispersion relation mismatch. We relate this mechanism to Axion Magnetic Resonance (AMR) and apply it to stellar axions in the starburst galaxy M82. We analyze its enhancement to the resulting X-ray signals while accounting for the finite magnetic domain size, dark matter coherence length, DM density morphology, plasma profiles, and the detector response. We derive strong constraints using existing X-ray data from NuSTAR. We show that this resonant conversion can lead to $\mathcal O(10^2)$ enhancement in the photon-axion conversion probability, improving the upper limits on axion's photon coupling over part of the mass range where ordinary conversion is suppressed. We also show that this type of resonance predicts distinctive features in the hard X-ray spectrum, which is moderately favored by the data over the background only model, yet it is currently still consistent with statistical fluctuations.

title: Geometrothermodynamics characterization of ABG-AdS black hole immersed by string clouds
abstract: Regular black holes, whose singular cores are replaced by smooth geometries sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, provide a natural setting to study how thermodynamic stability is encoded in spacetime geometry. Conventional stability criteria, however, depend on the choice of thermodynamic potential. Here we develop the quasi-homogeneous geometrothermodynamics of the regular Ayón-Beato--García anti-de Sitter (ABG-AdS) black hole surrounded by a cloud of strings, a Legendre-invariant framework in which no potential needs to be preferred. We show that the entropy, electric monopole charge and AdS radius act as extensive variables obeying a generalized quasi-homogeneity condition, and that the equilibrium manifold then carries three families of thermodynamic metrics. We establish an exact correspondence between response-function anomalies and curvature singularities: the first metric's curvature diverges on the zero-temperature extremal boundary, where the heat capacity vanishes, signaling Davies first-order transitions, whereas the second's diverges precisely where the heat capacity does, pinpointing Davies second-order transitions. The Gibbs free energy displays a swallow-tail structure that reveals a first-order small/large black hole transition, whose metastable region is bounded by these divergences of the heat capacity, together with a Hawking--Page-type transition to thermal AdS. The string-cloud density and the electric charge jointly control the horizon structure, the admissible thermal domain and the stability intervals.

title: KuroANN: Avoiding Unnecessary SSD Reads in High-Recall Filtered Vector Search
abstract: We present KuroANN, a new on-SSD filtered vector search system for partition indexes. Existing solutions assign the same number of SSD reads to all queries within a given selectivity range, wasting I/O for many queries. KuroANN instead assigns each query's SSD reads based on the number of vectors that pass its filter, called its match count. This is based on our observation that the match count is known before the search and that the number of SSD reads a query requires depends on this match count. KuroANN measures offline how many partitions to probe and candidates to read for the target recall at each count. At runtime, a query looks up these numbers, filters only the probed partitions, and stops reading from the SSD when further reads are unlikely to help. This significantly avoids unnecessary SSD reads and filtering work, improving throughput and latency at high recall. Experimental results show that KuroANN outperforms PipeANN-Filter and Faiss by up to 34.5x and 9.10x, respectively.

title: TESS discovers an eclipse of the Be star V1294 Aql (= HD 184279) by its not-so-small, low-mass companion
abstract: In a single sector of observations with the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), an eclipse-like event occurred in the Be star V1294 Aql. The reality of the eclipse is corroborated by $UBV$ photometry from the Hvar observatory. The event occurred at phase 17.97 of the linear ephemeris by Harmanec et al. (2022) for the upper conjunction of this SB1 binary (P$_{\rm orb}$ = 192.9 d). Therefore, we conclude that the Be star was eclipsed by its companion. With this elimination of the uncertainty of the orbital inclination, the mass of the secondary is 0.99 to 1.17 M$_\odot$ for masses of the primary from 14 to 18 M$_{\odot}$. The depth of the eclipse of $\sim$6.0% (0.06 mag) is incompatible with a white-dwarf (WD) nature of the companion. At the implied radius of $\sim$25% of that of the B0.5 primary, the secondary is not a bona-fide sdO/sdB star, either, but it could be still in its contraction phase. The increasing number of such stars may lend support to model calculations according to which the timescale of the contraction can be not thermal but instead is governed by the much slower removal of a residual H-rich envelope. It is also possible the companion is on the pre-main sequence in which case the two stars have not yet interacted. Two new interferometric observations were obtained near orbital quadrature but the secondary star was not detected, nor was it detected in high-resolution high-S/N echelle spectra.

title: Mask-Based Speech Enhancement for Spatial Audio: Effects of Signal Representation and Channel-Specific Masking
abstract: Speech enhancement for spatial audio needs to improve speech quality and intelligibility while preserving the spatial characteristics of the acoustic scene. Time-frequency masking provides an effective approach for speech enhancement, but its performance and spatial fidelity may depend strongly on the signal representation in which the mask is applied. This work systematically compares time-frequency masking in the microphone, beamformer, and first-order Ambisonics domains in simulated reverberant acoustic scenes. Both an ideal ratio mask (IRM) and a lightweight deep-learning-based mask estimator are considered, with performance evaluated in terms of speech reconstruction, perceptual quality, intelligibility, reverberation preservation, and binaural spatial-cue preservation. The results show that channel-specific masking in the beamformer domain provides the highest speech quality and intelligibility, while channel-specific masking in the Ambisonics domain better preserves the spatial characteristics of the residual interference. Reducing the spatial representation from third- to first-order Ambisonics substantially reduces the performance gap between the beamformer and Ambisonics domains due to the lower spatial resolution of the resulting beamformers. Furthermore, a shared mask across first-order Ambisonics channels achieves speech enhancement performance close to that of channel-specific masking while requiring only a single mask-estimation network. These results demonstrate that the choice of signal representation and masking strategy should be considered jointly, and indicate that first-order Ambisonics with shared masking provides a practical compromise between speech enhancement performance, spatial fidelity, and computational complexity.

title: Centerpoints with Few Radon Points
abstract: A point $z\in\mathbf{R}^d$ is a $β$-centerpoint of an $n$-point set $P\subset\mathbf{R}^d$ if every closed halfspace containing $z$ contains at least $βn$ points of~$P$. Iterated Radon points yield an $Ω(1/d^2)$-centerpoint in $\tilde{O}(d^9)$ time: each round replaces a population by Radon points of random $(d+2)$-tuples. Har-Peled and Jones improved the running time to $\tilde{O}(d^7)$. The known analyses certify that \emph{every} point of the population is central. We show that $O(\log^2 d)$ rounds of Radon computations suffice if a \emph{single} Radon point of the last round is output. The analysis tracks, for every $k$, the probability that $k$ random points of a round lie in a common ``bad'' halfspace, so the union bound over halfspaces is taken only once, for the input sample. For points in general position and constant $\varepsilon>0$, a $\frac{1-\varepsilon}{4(d+1)(d+2)}$-centerpoint is computed with constant probability using $O(d^3\log^3 d)$ Radon computations, in $O(d^{3+ω}\log^3 d)\subseteq O(d^{5.372})$ time ($ω$: matrix multiplication exponent), or $O(d^6\log^3 d)$ time with Gaussian elimination. The algorithm uses only linear algebra; among strongly polynomial algorithms for centerpoints of quality $1/\mathrm{poly}(d)$ it is the fastest known. For integer input, grid rounding keeps all points polynomially long and still yields an exact centerpoint. Dutta and Pisula obtained quality $Ω(1/(d\log d\log\log d))$ in weakly polynomial time by solving $\tilde{O}(d^3)$ linear programs, using Tverberg points with $Θ(\log d)$ parts instead of Radon points. Our analysis extends to rounds of such Tverberg points: for inputs of more than $\tilde{O}(d)$ points, it gives the same quality from $O(d^2\log^4 d\log\log d)$ linear programs in expectation.

title: Elimination Methods for Computing Invariant Algebraic Surfaces and Hopf Bifurcations
abstract: This paper presents efficient algorithmic methods for computing invariant algebraic surfaces and Hopf bifurcations in parametric polynomial differential systems. For invariant algebraic surfaces of bounded degree, we establish two complementary elimination frameworks: combining Gröbner bases with saturation and prime decomposition yields the Zariski closure of the parameter existence locus (necessary conditions), whereas triangular decomposition into strong regular systems recovers the exact pointwise constructible locus (necessary and sufficient conditions) via the projection property. We further present a hybrid approach for identifying such surfaces by integrating prime decomposition with branch-wise triangular solving, thereby efficiently deriving necessary and sufficient conditions with enhanced computational flexibility and rectifying subtle classification errors in a class of Liénard systems. For Hopf bifurcations, extending prior work on necessary conditions [SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 34 (1997)] and sufficient conditions [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 182 (1994); J. Symbolic Comput. 30 (2000)], we establish a complete algebraic characterization via two equivalent formulations: one using Hurwitz determinants and subresultant sequences, and another derived from the greatest common divisor (GCD) of the real and imaginary parts of the characteristic polynomial. From the GCD formulation, we obtain a novel and, for the first time, complete semi-algebraic description of the transversality condition, yielding a decision procedure via triangular decomposition of semi-algebraic systems and heuristic real quantifier elimination. Our approach resolves cases beyond the reach of state-of-the-art polynomial-based methods, and experimental results confirm the feasibility and efficiency of our frameworks.

title: Compositional Reachset-Conformant Modeling for Managing Uncertainty in the Development of Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: The development of cyber-physical systems (CPS) proceeds through iterative design revisions, and compliance with safety requirements must be re-established after every revision, typically based on a system model. Conventional models, however, predict only the most likely behavior, leading to model-plant mismatch that often surfaces only during late-stage testing, when redesign is most expensive. This article presents reachset-conformant modeling as a framework for managing uncertainty throughout the development process: instead of a single trajectory, a reachset-conformant model predicts a set of behaviors, calibrated from data to conservatively enclose the true system behavior with a statistical guarantee. Safety properties established on the model therefore transfer to the realized system. Beyond a practical introduction to reachset-conformant identification and its benefits for CPS development, our main theoretical contribution is a closure result: reachset conformance is preserved under serial composition, parallel composition, and feedback interconnection, and hence under any architecture assembled from these primitives. Subsystem models identified independently from local measurements can thus be substituted into the system architecture, and the interconnected model inherits a coverage guarantee from the subsystem guarantees. We complement this result with update strategies that adapt the uncertainty sets after design changes without restarting the identification workflow. Experiments on an automotive brake-system test bench demonstrate that a) a single model covers all operating conditions and hardware variants, b) late-stage modifications are absorbed by uncertainty set updates, c) a black-box hydraulic unit is conservatively abstracted from input-output data alone, and d) independently identified subsystem models form a conformant model by construction.

title: Sharp Casorati Inequalities for Pointwise Bi-Slant Riemannian Maps into Sasakian Space Forms
abstract: We establish Casorati inequalities for pointwise bi-slant Riemannian maps into Sasakian space forms with the characteristic vector field tangent to the range. The Sasakian structure imposes specific conditions on the second fundamental form, leading to refined inequalities for the normalized horizontal scalar curvature that also account for O'Neill's tensor. For proper pointwise bi-slant maps, equality in the two principal inequalities is characterized by the vanishing of the second fundamental form on the orthogonal complement of the characteristic direction in the range. We also derive corresponding inequalities for pointwise semi-slant, hemi-slant, and slant Riemannian maps and construct examples attaining equality.

title: Three mixed-precision preconditioners for CholeskyQR
abstract: CholeskyQR is an orthogonalization algorithm particularly well suited to modern computing architectures, but it may fail to produce numerically orthonormal columns when applied to ill-conditioned matrices. A customary solution is to first reduce the condition number of the input matrix by means of a preconditioner, and then apply CholeskyQR to the preconditioned matrix. We propose three mixed-precision techniques for constructing such preconditioners: mpSCQR, based on a shifted Cholesky factorization; mpEVDQR, based on the eigendecomposition; and mpLUCQR, based on a pivoted LU factorization. We prove bounds on the condition number of the matrix after mpSCQR, mpLUCQR, or a shifted variant of mpEVDQR has been applied. Our experiments compare the proposed preconditioners with existing deterministic and randomized alternatives. The results suggest that mpEVDQR and mpLUCQR can be substantially faster than traditional shiftedCholeskyQR, with mpLUCQR attaining performance comparable to that of the most efficient randomized preconditioners.

title: From Fermions to Vortices: Microscopic Simulations of Phase Ordering in a d-Wave Superconductor
abstract: Describing bath-induced superconducting phase ordering directly from a microscopic fermionic Hamiltonian remains a formidable challenge. Here we develop a microscopic framework for this problem using the recently introduced adiabatic variational principle (AVP) and demonstrate its application to a two-dimensional $d$-wave superconductor. The central construction maps evolving, spatially inhomogeneous bond-pairing fields onto constrained Bogoliubov-de Gennes states, with the associated Lagrange multipliers determining the thermodynamic driving forces. This enables dissipative evolution of the superconducting order while retaining its microscopic electronic structure, without assuming a phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau free-energy functional. Starting from disordered pairing configurations, we resolve the emergence of phase coherence through vortex-antivortex annihilation and the accompanying evolution of local electronic spectra. Vortex decay and dynamical scaling recover the characteristic kinetics of two-dimensional phase ordering, providing a nontrivial benchmark of the framework. The solver-independent AVP formulation opens a route to microscopic studies of dissipative ordering and metastability in superconductors with intertwined stripe and pair-density-wave orders.

title: SOARS: System One Assisted Reranking for Agentic Search
abstract: Deep search agents address complex information needs through iterative retrieval and reasoning, where the relevance of retrieved evidence influences downstream performance. Existing rerankers improve retrieval effectiveness but introduce substantial latency and cost when invoked throughout the search trajectory. We introduce SOARS, a training-free framework leveraging a System One model for fast, calibrated relevance estimation. At each search step, SOARS selects query-relevant passages from long documents and reranks candidates in a single call, jointly considering the original question and agent-generated sub-query. Across six LLM backbones on BrowseComp-Plus and WebShaper, SOARS consistently improves answer accuracy and evidence recall while reducing search calls, end-to-end latency, and inference cost. On BrowseComp-Plus, it improves GPT-5.4 Mini's accuracy from 73.9% to 84.7% while reducing search calls from 23 to 14, demonstrating the potential of System One reranking for more effective and efficient deep search.

title: InstructReplay: Replaying Assistant Turns to Preserve General Behavior During Factual Fine-Tuning
abstract: Fine-tuning an instruction-tuned language model on new facts often erodes its general abilities. We find that standard fine-tuning lowers instruction-following, reasoning and coding benchmarks by 35 points on average, and that these losses track a collapse in answer length: fine-tuned models at least halve their responses, and the further a response drifts from the initial model's length, the more often it fails. We propose InstructReplay: the initial model answers a set of general instructions once, and during fine-tuning the model is kept close to the initial model on these answers. Across three model families and two domains, InstructReplay reduces the average decline on five general benchmarks from 28.1 to 2.4 points and keeps answer length close to the initial model's, while learning the new facts as well as standard fine-tuning. It balances learning and retention better than seven adaptation methods in all six settings. Controlled comparisons attribute the gain to replaying the model's own answers to general instructions rather than to the form of the loss.

title: The Kelvin--Hicks Formula from the Energy--Casimir Principle
abstract: The classical Kelvin--Hicks formula expresses the propagation speed of a thin vortex ring in an incompressible ideal fluid in terms of its circulation, distance from the symmetry axis, and core radius. In this paper, we rigorously derive this formula from a variational principle based on Arnold's energy--Casimir method, without prescribing any of these geometric or physical quantities a priori. We introduce a scale-invariant variational principle involving the energy, impulse, and $L^p$ Casimir invariants. For $1 < p < \infty$, we construct orbitally stable energy-maximizing vortex rings and investigate how their geometry depends on the Casimir exponent $p$. For sufficiently large $p$, the vortex rings have cores homeomorphic to a ball and converge to Hill's spherical vortex as $p \to \infty$. In contrast, as $p\to1^+$, the energy-maximizing vortex rings concentrate onto a circular filament of radius $e^{1/3}$, uniquely selected by the variational principle. After suitable translations and rescalings, their vortex-core profiles converge to an optimizer of the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. Introducing an effective core radius $ε_p$ determined by the entropy of the vorticity distribution, we establish the Kelvin--Hicks formula \begin{align*} W_p = \frac{Γ_p}{4πR_p} \left(\log\frac{8R_p}{ε_p}-1+o(1)\right) \quad \textrm{as}\ p\to1^+, \end{align*} where $W_p$, $Γ_p$, and $R_p$ denote the propagation speed, circulation, and effective ring radius, respectively. In particular, the constant correction $-1$ is obtained for nonuniform vortex-core profiles without imposing any prescribed core structure.

title: Increasing the Precision of IR Mapping for Incremental Data Flow Analysis
abstract: Static analysis tools operate on an Intermediate Representation (IR) --- an internal model of the program on which dataflow analysis computes and stores facts against IR object identifiers. Incremental dataflow analysis reuses these cached facts across consecutive program versions, but requires an accurate mapping between IR objects in the old and new versions. When this mapping is imprecise, the consequence is not merely a missed optimization: unmapped IR objects inflate the change set, increasing the number of program points that the analyzer must recompute and forcing it to redo work that a more precise mapping would have avoided. This cost is not specific to any one kind of IR object; it arises wherever IR-level identity is unstable across versions. Any IR that decomposes nested source expressions generates temporary variables which are assigned names by a method-local counter that shifts whenever a statement is inserted or deleted earlier in the method, breaking any name- or attribute-based mapping. We present a systematic algorithm that establishes a sound, oneto-one mapping of these temporary variables across consecutive versions, and formalize and prove the soundness of the mapping, guaranteeing that every produced mapping is semantically correct. The resulting precise mapping shrinks the change set, reducing the number of program points the incremental analysis must recompute. Implemented within the Soot framework for Jimple IR and evaluated on 8 real-world Java projects with genuine edits from the BUGSWARM dataset, our approach reduces the IR change set by over 82% on average compared to Reviser's graph-differencing algorithm, while completing the full pipeline within 250 ms per project---directly countering the common assumption that a more precise change set necessarily costs more time to compute.

title: Analytic properties of Boolean-Narayana numbers
abstract: Very recently, Bóna introduced the Boolean-Narayana numbers BoNa(n,k) as the number of 0-1-trees on n+1 vertices with k right edges. We prove the total positivity of the Boolean-Narayana triangle by providing an explicit matrix factorization, and construct a planar digraph for this triangle. We give two combinatorial interpretations of the gamma-coefficients of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials. We also show the strong q-log-convexity of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials and the asymptotic normality of the Boolean-Narayana numbers. A bijection between 0-1-trees and colored Motzkin paths is constructed, presenting an alternative interpretation of the Boolean-Narayana numbers.

title: Whistler instability driven by electron trapping in magnetic dips
abstract: Using fully kinetic particle-in-cell simulations, we show how free energy released by an ion-scale instability reaches electron scales through its effect on the electron distribution. An initial ion temperature anisotropy drives partly compressional ion cyclotron waves, which form magnetic dips. Electrons trapped in these dips develop an enhanced temperature anisotropy and butterfly-shaped distributions, similar to those observed by spacecraft in the Earth's magnetosheath. By tracking the energy transfer in velocity space, we show that the gradients created by trapping drive whistler waves through cyclotron resonance. The whistlers in turn scatter the electrons in pitch angle, flattening velocity-space gradients and heating the electrons along the magnetic field. As a result, the electron anisotropy drops to about half of the double-adiabatic prediction once the whistler power peaks. Our results show that it is the shape of the electron distribution in magnetic dips, rather than its temperature anisotropy alone, that drives the whistlers.

title: Theory-Informed Quantum Error Mitigation for Shor Order Finding with Fourier Neural Operators
abstract: Quantum noise distorts the distribution of circuit measurement outcomes, often leaving enough information to infer the algorithm's correct result. To recover this latent information from the noisy distribution in Shor order finding, we introduce a theory-informed quantum error mitigation method. We model how circuit errors shift, broaden, or weaken peaks in the output distribution. These models guide both the generation of synthetic training data and the design of a Fourier neural operator with a learned gain that attenuates or amplifies higher retained Fourier modes. We score each candidate order by averaging the correlations between its ideal distribution and the distributions measured in three circuit executions. The network adjusts these scores to guide the order estimate and determine the weights of a normalized mixture of the ideal distributions.
