This yields an agnostic-PAC bound on the estimation error, with sample complexity scaling additively in the two terms; this bound becomes closed-form on additive input transformations and is matched by a lower bound on an explicit binary classification construction. For (2), the same structure decomposes the approximation error exactly into the source-label information loss and output-mapping restriction with a source-conditional upper bound on this gap. We extend the approximation analysis to logit-exposing source models, where the upper bound is empirically estimable. The wrapper-side analysis localizes both errors to specific components, giving a structural view of reprogramming practice.

title: Privacy-Aware Adaptive Client Selection for Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Federated retrieval-augmented generation retrieves evidence from distributed corpora. However, broadcasting queries to all clients increases the retrieval burden and query exposure. We present Privacy-Aware Adaptive Client Selection for Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation (PACS-FedRAG), an online selector that takes into account perturbed semantic profiles along with evidence feedback, latency, payload cost, and exploration. In a ten-client setting where three clients are chosen, the archived end-to-end benchmark reports an evidence overlap of 0.372 and an answer accuracy of 0.287. The retrieval-only evaluation, on the other hand, reuses a full-broadcast baseline with a different fusion tie-breaking policy. Rank fusion across disjoint client corpora imposes an overlap ceiling of 0.375, limiting its interpretation as a relevance measure. Answer accuracy is below the fixed-label diagnostic of 0.645, and raw generator responses are unavailable for parser verification. Corrected baselines and a new answer-level evaluation are needed to assess whether quality is preserved. Selecting three clients reduces the number of query recipients by 70%. Profile perturbation does not provide confidentiality of queries or passages.

title: Cascading LO-phonon-mediated resonant energy transfer from excitons to Eu3+ for ultrahigh color purity red luminescence in europium-doped GaN
abstract: High-efficiency, wavelength-stable red micro-LEDs with ultrahigh color purity remain a critical bottleneck for monolithic III-nitride full-color displays. Europium-doped GaN (GaN:Eu) offers a compelling solution, yet the microscopic energy transfer mechanism from the GaN host to Eu3+ ions has remained unresolved for three decades, impeding rational performance optimization. Here we report polaron-mediated resonant energy transfer in high-crystalline-quality GaN:Eu epilayers grown by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. Eu3+ doping stabilizes a distinct bound exciton (BX3) state at 3.478 eV, which couples strongly with longitudinal optical (LO) phonons via the Frohlich interaction to form cascading polarons with up to seven phonon replicas at a uniform energy spacing of 92.0+/-0.7 meV. The BX3 polaron coupled with 5LO phonons matches precisely the 7F0-->5D3 intra-4f transition energy of Eu3+ at 3.019 eV. Temperature-dependent photoluminescence reveals non-equilibrium phonon emission, evidencing directional resonant energy transfer. After rapid nonradiative relaxation from the 5D3 excited state to the 5D0 metastable state, the hypersensitive 5D0-->7F2 transition yields sharp 622 nm red emission. Time-resolved spectroscopy confirms a single dominant Eu3+ luminescent site with reduced local symmetry, attributed to off-axis EuGa-VN complexes. This work identifies a key energy transfer channel and provides a clear framework for designing high-efficiency GaN:Eu red emitter.

title: Certifying a Sufficient Gaussian Dependence Regime for Learned Weighted FDR Control
abstract: Learning hypothesis weights from informative auxiliary data can improve the power of multiple testing. Even when the weights are learned independently of the tests, the validity of weighted Benjamini-Hochberg depends on their joint distribution. We use reference observations to certify a sufficient dependence condition for one-sided Gaussian tests. An intersection-union test of uncertain correlation signs determines whether to apply weighted Benjamini-Hochberg or a prespecified fallback at an adjusted level. Under conditional separation of certification and testing, the procedure controls the false discovery rate (FDR) for every Gaussian correlation matrix satisfying the stated sampling assumptions and weight constraints. We establish a boundary obstruction to uniform certification and matching minimax sample-size bounds for worst-case pair sets and the all-pairs problem. In the parameter ranges of the matching bounds, the minimax sample size grows logarithmically with the number of checked pairs and quadratically with the inverse of their positive margin. For homogeneous Gaussian observations with known marginal variances, residual contrasts from the testing subjects provide an independent source of certification scores. Simulations with up to 4,950 checked pairs, comparisons under a common subject budget, and Gaussian designs based on correlations estimated from the Healthy Brain Network illustrate the trade-off between certification and detection power.

title: When Are Parallel Subagents Effective for Coding? An Empirical Study on Repository Construction
abstract: LLM-based coding agents are increasingly used for long-horizon tasks such as building an entire program from a specification. Products like Codex and Claude Code let an agent delegate work to parallel subagents, multiplying run cost, yet it remains unclear whether and when delegation produces a better program. We compare a single agent with a main agent delegating to subagents on repository-construction tasks from NL2Repo and ProgramBench (which also provides an executable reference program). We compare scores at equal time and equal cost, run intervention experiments, and analyze fine-grained behavior. On randomly drawn tasks, parallel subagents raise hidden-test pass rates by only about 1 to 5 percentage points at up to 3.8x the cost of a single agent. Their gain is larger on hard tasks, where we find evidence of three mechanisms. Self-checking: with GPT-5.6 Sol, one sentence telling a single agent to probe the reference program first recovers most of this gain at a fraction of the cost; from GPT-5.6 Sol to GPT-6.1 Sol, the gain shrinks as single agents check their own work more. Fresh context: in extended runs, a single agent that periodically starts a new session with an empty conversation makes faster early progress in every comparison than one that resumes its conversation. Modularity: multi-agent runs produce more modular code (more files and shorter functions), closer to the upstream source. We observe similar patterns in a smaller replication with Opus 5.5 on Claude Code. Overall, subagents help when (i) a single agent stops checking too early, (ii) a long session keeps editing with little improvement, or (iii) modular code helps on the task; otherwise, they mainly add cost.

title: SIA: Selective Image Analogy
abstract: Image analogy transfers a demonstrated transformation from a before/after pair (A, A') to a new query image B. Existing methods assume all changes in (A, A') should be fully transferred, limiting flexibility when users want only a subset of the demonstrated edits. We introduce Selective Image Analogy (SIA), a new setting where a single demonstration pair encodes multiple edits, and the user selects at inference time which edits to apply to B. To support this, we curate a multi-edit analogy dataset with full-edit and partial-edit targets. We then train a model that first learns to transfer the complete demonstrated transformation, and then gains selective control through a mask-aligned suppression mechanism: a token-gated LoRA that restricts adapter updates to suppressed edit tokens during denoising, paired with a concept suppression vector that weakens the selected tokens in the text embeddings before denoising. Together, these components allow SIA to suppress unwanted edits that remain visible in A', while preserving the user-selected ones, all without requiring a new demonstration pair for each edit combination. We perform extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations along with user studies to demonstrate the efficacy of our approach.

title: TWIST: Teacher-Weighted Initial-Noise Spherical Transform for Quality-Preserving Diversity in Distilled Diffusion Models
abstract: Timestep-distilled diffusion models generate high-quality images in one or a few steps, but often suffer from reduced mode coverage and limited diversity. Recent methods improve diversity by optimizing the initial noise at inference time, requiring costly backpropagation through the denoiser. Moreover, their diversity objectives typically repel generated samples without accounting for how the corresponding teacher model distributes its outputs. We introduce Teacher-Weighted Initial-noise Spherical Transform (TWIST), a lightweight network that transforms the low-frequency components of initial noise to improve diversity without inference-time optimization. TWIST uses a teacher-guided determinantal point process (DPP) objective to align the feature-space diversity of student samples with that of the teacher. By amortizing noise optimization into a single network, TWIST eliminates inference-time backpropagation while preserving the efficiency of few-step generation. On SDXL-Turbo, TWIST matches the diversity of MoNO at less than 25% of its inference cost, while achieving higher recall and better PickScore, ImageReward, and CLIPScore under matched compute budgets. On SDXL-Lightning, it achieves comparable recall at lower cost without the ImageReward degradation observed with MoNO.

title: Looped Models are Fast Multi-Token Predictors
abstract: Looped language models can adapt computation for predicting a token without a proportional rescaling in unique model parameters by adjusting the number of loops. This property has been used for self-speculative decoding, taking shallow loops as fast drafters and deep loops as verifiers, which is effective since drafting still uses full parameters. In this paper, we show that shallow loops can be also predictive of several future tokens and leverage this to drastically accelerate the inference of looped language models. To that end, we present Floodgates, a simple self-speculative decoding method that appends a block of mask tokens as a suffix and learns via low-rank adaptation to draft these tokens in parallel. Across seven models, five benchmarks, a range of batch sizes, and both greedy and sampled decoding, Floodgates is the fastest lossless decoding method in most cases, attaining up to 7.5x acceleration. Through analysis, we show that this speedup is enabled by all-depth training of looped models, with the shallow drafter's ability to leverage full-depth computation by conditioning on deep prefix cache evaluated during verification.

title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
abstract: Medical reasoning agents combine large language model (LLM) reasoning with clinical workflows and specialized neural tools. However, general-purpose LLMs receive limited training exposure to domain-specific medical tools, and the uncertainty and distributional shifts of neural tool outputs make selecting tools from simple descriptions significantly more challenging than in deterministic settings such as calculators or dictionary lookups. In this paper, we propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that leverages accumulated tool-use trajectories to improve tool selection in medical reasoning agents. EATS constructs a memory of past interactions, including queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback, and retrieves relevant experiences to guide tool selection for new queries. As memory construction does not require ground-truth supervision, EATS scales naturally with test-time experience. We evaluate EATS on tool-augmented medical reasoning tasks, including closed-ended visual question answering and free-form report generation. Experiments on four public datasets, ChestAgentBench, CheXbench, MIMIC-CXR, and SLAKE-VQA, across three multimodal LLMs, Qwen3-VL 2B, Qwen3-VL 32B, and GPT-5.5, show consistent gains in tool selection behavior and downstream medical reasoning performance. Code is available at https://github.com/Limingyuan001/EATS.

title: MoS: Mixture-of-Modality Streaming for Low-Latency Online Video LLM Analytics over Dynamic Networks
abstract: The serving model for next-generation video analytics systems is shifting from traditional task-specific vision models to general-purpose online video Large Language Models (LLMs). Online video LLMs enable flexible, contextual understanding of continuously arriving video content via natural language. However, their substantial resource requirements typically mandate cloud-based inference, making continuous video streaming from user devices necessary to keep the cloud model's context current for online interaction. This introduces significant challenges under existing dynamic and often harsh networks, degrading both accuracy and responsiveness in latency-sensitive applications. In this paper, we propose MoS, a new streaming system that adaptively streams a combination of visual and derived textual modalities over fluctuating networks to enable Pareto-optimal video LLM analytics. The key insight is to leverage the complementarity and interchangeability of different modalities, hidden in video LLM, to improve system performance. Concretely, MoS introduces adaptive anchor frame selection and incremental content tracking to enable low-latency text description generation at the device side. A joint profiler characterizes the accuracy and overhead of paired video and textual configurations, including caption input resolution and output-token budget. A stochastic optimization-based modality controller then selects modality combinations and configurations using this profile and the asynchronous latency of the two modalities to adapt to network conditions. Across 500 StreamingBench video-question pairs, 4G/5G uplink traces, and the VideoLLM-Online and DisPider backends, MoS reduces latency violations by up to 94.3% and improves accuracy by up to 60.4% relative to the evaluated streaming baselines.

title: Directional Statistics of Synchrotron Polarization in Mixed Emitting and Faraday-Rotating Turbulence
abstract: Polarization directions provide a sensitive probe of Faraday rotation without weighting the signal by polarized brightness. We develop their spatial statistics for a turbulent volume in which synchrotron emission and Faraday rotation coexist. For independent, zero-mean Gaussian polarized emissivity, we derive an exact relation for the directional correlation. We derive strong stochastic coherence-depth scalings, including an additional interval for steep Faraday-density spectra, and distinguish them from the conditions needed to infer directional spectral slopes. We also quantify the weak-rotation response of a coherent uniform emitter and demonstrate that the scalings of the normalized tangential polarization gradient follow directly from the direction spectrum. A combined use of the techniques, including those introduced earlier in Lazarian & Pogosyan (2016), provides a way for detailed study of astrophysical turbulence.

title: Correlation-Aware Evidential Fusion for Trusted Multi-View Classification
abstract: Trusted multi-view classification aims to make accurate and reliable predictions by integrating information from multiple views. Existing methods typically estimate class evidence and uncertainty for each view and combine the resulting opinions through aggregation rules. However, they generally treat different views as independent information sources, overlooking the correlations among them. Highly correlated views tend to produce similar evidence, and treating them as independent sources may repeatedly count consistent information and give it disproportionate influence, while weakening complementary evidence that provides additional information. Consequently, such correlation-unaware fusion may not only limit classification performance but also produce miscalibrated uncertainty estimates. To address this issue, we propose Correlation-Aware Fusion of Evidence (CAFE), a framework for trusted multi-view classification. CAFE applies complementarity-based trust discounting to the evidence produced by view-private experts and introduces a correlation-aware constraint to reduce the repeated contribution of similar evidence. It then learns sample-specific weights from the global multi-view context to adaptively combine the correlation-adjusted private evidence with cross-view collaborative evidence. Extensive experiments on six real-world datasets demonstrate that CAFE consistently improves classification and calibration performance in general settings, with particularly significant gains when strong correlations exist among views.

title: Free boundary MHD equilibria with surface tension
abstract: Free boundary equilibria of an ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) plasma, at rest, with surface tension and an exterior vacuum are studied. Within the frozen-in orbit of a reference magnetic field, every equilibrium is a critical point of the magnetic plus surface energy over the space of volume-preserving embeddings; the capillary boundary condition is the first-variation boundary term, and no assumption on the connectivity of the boundary is required. In the plane the frozen-in law fixes the distribution of the stream function and turns the energy into a rearrangement functional. For a single-axis reference field a sharp lower bound is proved that depends only on that distribution and is attained by an explicit area-preserving diffeomorphism, smooth across the axis, which yields a classical equilibrium. For Morse stream functions sharper bounds governed by the level-set topology are obtained, with a strict gap at an isolated simple saddle merge. In three dimensions no such reduction is available: the energy does not control the full gradient of the embedding, no scalar rearrangement principle applies, and the axisymmetric reduction yields only a conditional lower bound.

title: Ion and electron temperature recovery for Irkutsk incoherent scatter measurements
abstract: Recovering ion and electron plasma temperatures from Irkutsk Incoherent Scatter Radar (IISR) data is a challenge due to rapid Faraday rotation, which significantly distorts signal correlation profiles. This paper presents an adaptation of the full-profile analysis (FPA) method tailored to the specific conditions of the IISR using a two-step inverse problem framework. The core novelty of the approach lies in the integration of data from both narrowband and wideband channels: experimental power profiles from the wideband channel are incorporated directly into the forward model for temperature recovery. By mathematically establishing the link between the wideband signal amplitude and the temperature ratio, we introduce a non-linear constraint that significantly narrows the solution search space. This addresses the problem of "stretched" global minima in the objective functional, effectively filtering out physically inconsistent results. The inverse problem is solved using the Improved Stochastic Ranking Evolution Strategy (ISRES), which enables fully automated parameter estimation without the need for manual initial guesses.

title: RelPRM: Grounding Visual Process Reward Models in Relational Evidence
abstract: Visual process reward models (PRMs) can detect calculation errors yet assign high scores to steps that misread visual relations. Supervision based on subsequent answer success does not directly establish whether a step's relational claim holds. To strengthen visual-relation verification, we first build an automated pipeline that programmatically verifies each claim and identifies the required objects, relations, and image regions. It produces RelProcessTrain and RelProcessBench (RPB), which tests whether scores respond appropriately to relational evidence through controlled image edits and step rephrasings. Building on this pipeline, we further introduce RelPRM, a visual-relation-oriented method for process reward modeling with two training mechanisms. Relation-evidence self-distillation constructs views preserving necessary objects, relations, and dependencies, reducing the burden of finding decisive evidence in complex scenes and transferring reliable evidence-assisted judgments to full images. Relation-evidence-driven consistency training encourages appropriate score changes when relation edits reverse a step's truth, stability under irrelevant edits, and similar score changes across paraphrases. At inference, RelPRM directly scores the current step using only the original image and reasoning context. RelPRM achieves 66.2% on VisualProcessBench (VPB) and 68.4% on RPB, gains of 4.2 and 9.9 percentage points over VisualPRM-8B. These results show that training for visual relations improves both relational verification and step assessment across broader multimodal reasoning tasks.

title: Estimating subcritical multiplication from stochastic neutron noise: a branching Brownian motion model for leakage counts
abstract: A neutron detector placed outside a subcritical system records fission chains as correlated bursts of counts. The time dependence of these correlations gives access to the $α$ eigenvalues governing the decay of the system and, with additional physical information, to its effective multiplication factor $k_{\mathrm{eff}}$. The usual analysis relies on point kinetics, which ignores where chains are born and which neutrons escape. We examine this approximation in a model simple enough to be solved: branching Brownian motion, that is, one-group neutron diffusion with capture and fission, in a domain whose absorbing boundary plays the role of the detector. For a stationary Poisson source we derive the Feynman $Y$ function (the count variance-to-mean ratio minus one) by following pairs of neutrons from their common ancestor to their detection. In a homogeneous cube the result is an explicit sum over spatial modes whose weights are fixed by the geometry and the source. We compare it with direct branching simulations and with one-speed OpenMC transport calculations in which fission is sampled with analog reaction selection and FREYA multiplicities. At the longest simulated gate the model agrees with transport to about $1\%$ at $k=0.8$ and $0.9$, and to $10\%$ at $k=0.5$. The corresponding point-model discrepancies range from $25$ to $48\%$. When geometry, source and material parameters are known, retaining the spatial modes also reduces the bias on the inferred multiplication factor. Two extensions prepare the use of the model in inverse problems. Correlations between opposite faces distinguish systems that share the same fundamental decay rate but differ in leakage, and a hierarchy of three stationary problems links this spatial benchmark to multiplicity counting. Modal convergence, detector imbalance and spectral evolution remain limitations for quantitative inference.

title: Tortho-Gaussian++: Suppressing Geometric Drift and Floaters for Robust Gravity-Aligned TDOM Generation in Large-Scale Aerial Scenes
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has demonstrated remarkable performance in aerial scene reconstruction, motivating its recent extension to true digital orthophoto maps (TDOMs) generation. We propose Tortho-Gaussian++, a novel 3DGS training framework that suppresses geometric drift and floaters and automatically prunes unreliable peripheral regions, coupled with a robust gravity-aligned TDOM rendering solution. First, we explore geometric support via viewing-ray-based geometric observability analysis, quantitatively characterizing the reliability for each Gaussian and subsequently pruning peripheral regions with particularly weak geometric support. Second, the optimizer state initialization is refined for newly created Gaussians during densification, intrinsically suppressing drift and floaters without external priors. Lastly, a robust gravity direction estimation solution is designed, combining image-derived gravity cues, camera-distribution priors and nadir views, to achieve a gravity-aligned orthogonal projection reference for TDOM rendering. Extensive experiments on multiple large-scale UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) datasets demonstrate that our Tortho-Gaussian++ outperforms vanilla 3DGS by 0.5-3.5 dB in average PSNR and yields comparable or superior performance to prior-guided 3DGS methods. Notably, it reduces the training time, VRAM and Gaussian number by 45.5%, 47.2%, and 58.6%, respectively. Qualitative evaluations confirm that our method effectively suppresses drift and floaters, while robust gravity direction estimation reduces tilt-induced facade artifacts in TDOMs.

title: Fast radio bursts track cosmic star formation history with time delay: the effect of burst fluence
abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) are luminous millisecond-duration radio transients of extragalactic origin, yet their progenitor systems remain unidentified. The redshift evolution of the FRB event rate provides a powerful, model-independent discriminant between young progenitors and old progenitors, but recent studies have reached conflicting conclusions. In this work, we perform a forward-modeling analysis of the apparent non-repeating FRB sample from the CHIME/FRB catalogs to constrain the intrinsic FRB population. We find that the FRB rate follows the star formation rate (SFR) with little time delay when both dispersion measure (DM) and fluence are considered. In contrast, when only DM is taken into account, a significant time delay ($3 \sim 4$ Gyr) exists between the FRB rate and the SFR. The main reason for this discrepancy is that systematic biases exist in the mapping process from burst fluence to signal-to-noise ratio. These results support that at least a fraction of FRBs arise from a progenitor population whose event rate is delayed relative to star formation.

title: Random dyadic shift scattering: scale-uniform deformation stability and phase-aligned Hilbert multipliers
abstract:
Petermichl's theorem represents the Hilbert transform by averaging a single dyadic shift over dilations and random dyadic lattices. We study how the deformation stability of the lattice-averaged shift, and of a parameter-free feature map $Φ$ built from it in the spirit of Mallat's wavelet scattering, depends on the number $J+1$ of scales. For the Haar generator as well as compactly supported $C^1$ orthonormal wavelets, the covariance error under a deformation $f\mapsto f(\cdot-τ(\cdot))$ is $O((J+1)
orm{τ'}_\infty
orm f)$ without a $
ormτ_\infty$ term, because lattice averaging absorbs the translation part of $τ$ exactly. The deformation defect splits into a first-order Calderón commutator, bounded uniformly in $J$ by the $T(1)$ theorem, and a second-order remainder. On a single lattice, affine warps and $C^{1,δ}$ generators give a lower bound $c\,σ_\eps\sqrt{J+1}-C\eps$ for the defect, with an explicit constant $σ_\eps\ge0$ computed to be positive for sym4 and db4 at three values of $\eps$. Averaging over lattices turns the defect into a Fourier-multiplier quadratic form, yielding $J$-uniform bounds both for affine warps, with a logarithmic loss in the Haar case, and for $C^2$ warps with $C^{1,δ}$ generators, and hence a scale-uniform Mallat-type stability estimate for $Φ$. With the standard child pair, the Hilbert component of the averaged shift nearly cancels for smooth Daubechies-type generators; re-indexing the children by integers restores this component. For Haar and general warps, numerical computations agree with a conjectured $J$-uniform bound.

title: The Brauer--Manin obstruction to weak approximation on a constant K3 surface
abstract: We construct a constant supersingular K3 surface over every global field of characteristic two for which rational points are Zariski dense but are not dense in the Brauer--Manin set. This shows that the analogue of Skorobogatov's conjecture over global function fields does not hold for supersingular K3 surfaces.

title: EGSE: Evidence-Grounded Skill Evolution for Medical Reasoning Agents
abstract: Medical reasoning agents combine foundation models with specialized tools to interpret medical images, yet reusing their historical experience remains challenging. A correct final answer can conceal flawed reasoning or tool use, synthesized advice may lack source support, and superficially similar cases may require different diagnostic procedures. In this paper, we propose EGSE, an evidence-grounded skill evolution framework that distills historical dialogues from similar cases into reusable conditional workflows and progressively refines a multi-faceted skill library through supported and validated updates to improve medical agents. EGSE evaluates intermediate reasoning and tool use and contrasts repeated successful and failed rollouts to extract useful practices and evidence-supported avoidance guidance. These experiences are synthesized into workflows with applicability conditions and checks traceable to source dialogues. Library additions and merges require source-grounded review and execution validation. At inference time, EGSE routes queries to skill nodes organized by imaging modality, question task type, and disease category, then retrieves and selects applicable workflows based on their conditions, the current images, and the question to guide evidence acquisition and interpretation. Experiments across four chest X-ray benchmarks show that EGSE outperforms representative medical agents and skill evolution methods in reasoning accuracy while reducing tool calls. It also delivers consistent accuracy gains across seven foundation models and supports skill transfer across datasets.

title: A Sweedler dual seen as a terminal object in a category of bialgebras
abstract: We study the Sweedler dual of the polynomial algebra $\mathbb{K}[X]$ equipped with the multiplicative coproduct $δ(X) = X \otimes X$, and show that the resulting bialgebra $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$ is the terminal object in the category of pairs $(B, λ)$, where $B$ is a bialgebra and $λ$ is a character of $B$. This generalizes a result of Aguiar, Bergeron, and Sottile on combinatorial Hopf algebras in the graded and connected setting. We describe the subcoalgebras and subbialgebras of $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$, which lead to the introduction of the spectrum of a bialgebra. We also study the particular cases double bialgebras (bialgebras equipped with two compatible coproducts), firstly examining their connection to unital near-semirings or near-rings. Introducing a subbialgebra of $\mathbb{K}[X]^\star$ obtained from the intersection with another Sweedler dual, we prove it is the terminal object in the category of double bialgebras. As a consequence, we show that the spectrum of any double Hopf algebra is a subgroup of the group of roots of unity. This imply that not any bialgebra can become double. We finally apply this framework to a bialgebra of graphs with a coproduct given by contraction and deletion of edges, relating its invariants to Bergman colorations of edges arising from graphical matroids.

title: CoTAMP: Cooperative Task and Motion Planning for Quadruped Robots with Large Language Models
abstract: Some environments cannot be traversed by a single quadruped robot, for example a ledge that one robot can climb only from its partner's back or a gap that must be bridged with boxes. Solving them requires cooperative task and motion planning (TAMP). Previous works are limited to the motions of a single robot or only select actions from a predefined set of skills. We propose a framework with two parts: task planning that invents motions not defined in advance, and motion generation that realizes the invented motions. Both parts consist of large language model (LLM)-based modules and code-based modules. Task planning divides the trajectory of the whole task into steps and fixes the robot poses at the step boundaries. Motion generation produces keyframes that describe the motion of each step and turns them into a continuous trajectory through kinematic synthesis. The code-based modules check every plan and motion and return failures to the LLM-based modules for correction. The whole trajectory is then refined by trajectory optimization to satisfy the dynamics. On three simulated courses with two RAIBO2 robot models, our framework produced kinematically valid references in all 30 trials, all of which converged in trajectory optimization. Compared with several baselines, our framework showed advantages in success rate, dynamic feasibility, execution time, and generation time and cost. Project page: https://woojin8098.github.io/CoTAMP/

title: Phono3GPU: GPU-Accelerated Linear Tetrahedron Integration for Phonon Thermal Transport
abstract: Materials with high or low thermal conductivity are increasingly important for thermal management and energy technologies. Machine-learned interatomic potentials have accelerated anharmonic force-constant calculations, shifting the bottleneck toward phonon transport calculations for large materials datasets. Existing GPU solvers often rely on smearing, whose width can require material-dependent choices, while the linear tetrahedron method used in phono3py avoids this parameter but becomes costly for complex structures. Here we introduce Phono3GPU, which reformulates three-phonon scattering and linear tetrahedron integration for massively parallel GPU execution. Across benchmark crystals, Phono3GPU accelerates total calculations by up to 41 times relative to a CPU implementation, with larger gains for complex unit cells, and by 2 to 6 times relative to a recent GPU plug-in for phono3py. We further demonstrate atom-resolved scattering analysis in defective silicon supercells as an application enabled by the reduced computational cost. Phono3GPU thus lowers the cost of tetrahedron-based thermal-conductivity calculations and of detailed investigations of structure-dependent phonon transport.

title: PerovAgent: Autonomous Ligand Design for Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals
abstract: Designing surface-capping ligands for high-performance halide perovskite nanocrystals requires navigating a vast molecular space while discovering design rules that govern ligand-surface interactions. Here, we introduce PerovAgent, an autonomous multi-agent framework that combines large language model (LLM)-driven scientific reasoning with computational tools for atomistic model construction, machine-learned interatomic potential evaluation, and statistical validation. Across ten independent campaigns on CsPbBr3 surfaces, PerovAgent adaptively explored and refined diverse ligand chemistries while progressively improving the binding-energy objective. Beyond optimization, the framework converts recurring chemical observations into explicit design principles that can be statistically evaluated. Of 35 formulated principles, 19 were prospectively supported, of which seven also passed the confound audit, highlighting the need to systematically validate plausible LLM-generated hypotheses during autonomous discovery. A recurrent alkynyl-phosphonate principle was further examined using density functional theory, which reproduced the predicted energetic preference. These results demonstrate an autonomous discovery framework that not only searches molecular space and optimizes the scalar objective but also transforms its search trajectory into systematically testable design principles. The framework can also be extended to more complex ligands, including zwitterionic, multidentate, and polymerizable ligands, to explore a wider range of ligand-surface interactions and uncover new design principles for halide perovskite nanocrystals.

title: X-World: Transferring Video Priors to Cross-Embodiment Robot Control
abstract: Language-instructed manipulation requires robust closedloop policies, yet action-labeled robot trajectories are costly and limited in coverage. Human and robot videos provide complementary spatiotemporal priors for crossembodiment control. We propose X-World, which adapts pretrained video diffusion to variable views. A Q-Former compresses hidden states into tokens for a shared flowmatching expert that predicts action chunks. Datasetspecific projections map native states and actions. We adapt the backbone on large-scale robot and human videos, freeze it for action-only pretraining of the Q-Former and action expert, then post-train on the target platform. At inference, X-World responds at 20 Hz and overlaps updates with execution via asynchronous real-time chunking. X-World performs strongly on LIBERO and under zero-shot shifts on LIBERO-Plus. On hardware, it averages 81.7% success across six bimanual tasks on the side-mounted dual-arm UR5e, one of three real-robot configurations presented.

title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
abstract: General-purpose multimodal foundation models enable robots to adapt during deployment from observations and execution feedback, without task-specific demonstrations or training. However, the robot retains what it learns only in the model's working context. Once the task ends, it loses this execution knowledge, such as how to carry a bowl between two grippers. On the next attempt at the task, the robot may take just as long and repeat the same mistakes. To avoid this repetition, robots must retain execution knowledge across attempts. Yet replaying past actions is insufficient, because their effects depend on the current conditions. Procedures that determine actions from the current scene address this, but when they meet conditions that earlier attempts did not cover, revising them requires the measured effects of earlier actions. We therefore propose SEEK, an agentic framework that retains both, enabling robots to improve across attempts while keeping the underlying model fixed. To adapt retained knowledge to the current scene, SEEK adopts a Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy (SEPP) that encodes manipulation as executable procedures and determines each action from current observations. As the robot executes these procedures, SEEK records the measured effects of its actions, including those from failed attempts, in a Persistent Action-Effect Bank (PAEB). Where a retained procedure applies, it acts without a model request; where it meets a condition it does not cover, this evidence guides its revision. On RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks. On 34 of these tasks with GPT-6.2 Astra, SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts, against 49.6 for the same model acting directly, and uses 77.6% fewer model requests. https://zeyangguan.github.io/SEEK-Agentic-Robot-Manipulation/

title: False Positives and Innovation Incentives: Contracting for Noisy Experimentation
abstract: In many data-driven organizations, employees propose product changes that are launched only after passing noisy online experiments, and their compensation is often tied to successful launches. Because even low-value features may appear successful by chance, such launch-based incentives can encourage agents to conduct experiments that reduce total surplus. We study this problem in a principal-agent model in which an agent with private knowledge about feature quality chooses whether to conduct a costly experiment and is compensated through an affine contract consisting of a launch-contingent bonus and a long-run value-sharing component, subject to limited liability. We evaluate each contract by the largest fraction of the principal's full-information payoff that it guarantees uniformly across the agent's private knowledge. Our analysis reveals a fundamental tension between experimental noise and limited liability in incentive design. Launch bonuses create incentives for false-positive experimentation by rewarding features that succeed by chance, whereas limited liability can render pure value sharing insufficient to implement socially efficient experimentation. Therefore, the optimal contract balances launch-contingent rewards and long-run value sharing according to the default feature quality, the degree of distributional uncertainty, and the severity of the limited-liability constraint.

title: Event-WAM: Learning to Act with Event-Derived Futures
abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) leverage future visual modeling for robotic action learning, with recent studies exploring alternative or complementary objectives beyond conventional RGB prediction. We introduce Event-WAM, which incorporates event-derived visual changes as auxiliary future supervision alongside RGB. Event-WAM constructs temporally structured event representations from RGB demonstrations and encodes them using a frozen pretrained RGB video VAE, without training an event-specific VAE. Joint RGB--Event latent flow matching provides appearance- and change-oriented supervision without requiring event observations or explicit future generation at inference. Across simulated benchmarks, Event-WAM maintains comparable performance under standard conditions, while robustness gains under perturbations are benchmark-dependent, including improvements on LIBERO-Plus. Real-world evaluations further demonstrate improved manipulation success under both standard and unseen perturbation conditions. Further analyses show that policy improvements are not consistently accompanied by higher future prediction fidelity, suggesting the potential of change-oriented supervision for action learning.

title: MöbiuString: Structured String Art via Optimizing Generatrices on the Möbius Strip
abstract: String art is a worldwide handicraft that mimics an image with straight strings stretched between boundary pins. Existing image-driven methods primarily optimize individual strings for reconstruction fidelity, leaving the global organization of the strings weakly controlled.In this paper, we introduce the generatrix on the Möbius strip of unordered boundary-point pairs to formalize families of strings with finite generatrices, enabling explicit control over their arrangement. Based on this new formalization, we propose MöbiuString, a framework for generating structured, multi-color string art under a prescribed string budget. As an initialization, we place pins along boundaries of image-derived regions and select candidate string segments near each generatrix in the homeomorphic pin-index plane. During the iterative optimization, a 2DGS-based differentiable renderer jointly optimizes generatrix parameters and colors on multiple layers, while periodic discrete re-search revises string families to escape poor local configurations.To our knowledge, MöbiuString is the first automatic image-based method to generate string art with a structured string organization with freeform region boundaries. Evaluations with two datasets and a user study demonstrate the outperformance of MöbiuString over baselines.

title: DiCALM: Converting Autoregressive Convolution-Attention Language Models into Discrete Diffusion Language Models
abstract: Existing methods for adapting autoregressive (AR) language models to diffusion generation focus mainly on full-attention architectures. More efficient hybrid architectures remain underexplored. We introduce DiCALM, a recipe for converting the hybrid convolution-attention models of the LFM2 family (LFM2 and LFM2.5) from AR to masked-diffusion generation. DiCALM progressively extends LFM2's causal gated convolution so that it captures local context in both directions. It combines this extension with a masking warm-up and joint AR--diffusion training. In controlled experiments, DiCALM performs comparably to the corresponding fine-tuned LFM2.5-based AR models and delivers consistent speedups over them at both the 350M and 1.2B scales: over 1.4x on average and up to 1.79x.

title: UPP-Gauss: Ultrasound Propagation Physics-informed Gaussian Splatting for B-mode Novel-View Synthesis
abstract: Accurate novel-view synthesis of B-mode ultrasound images requires modeling acoustic propagation through tissue and the resulting appearance variations across probe poses. We propose Ultrasound Propagation Physics-informed Gaussian Splatting (UPP-Gauss), which integrates these acoustic interactions into an explicit Gaussian representation. UPP-Gauss constructs acoustic maps by sampling three 3D Gaussian fields using the probe pose and acoustic beam propagation direction, then combines these maps according to ultrasound propagation to synthesize B-mode images. Across three acoustically diverse datasets, UPP-Gauss achieves the best reconstruction quality with efficient rendering, improving PSNR over the best baseline on each dataset by 1.43 dB on average. These results demonstrate accurate and efficient B-mode novel-view synthesis through explicit Gaussian modeling of ultrasound propagation.

title: A degree-stability method for the $p$-spectral Turán-type problem for disjoint color-critical graphs
abstract: Let $F_1,\ldots,F_t$ be pairwise vertex-disjoint color-critical graphs with $χ(F_i)=r+1$ for each $i\in[t]$. For $r\ge 2$ and sufficiently large $n$, Simonovits [Discrete Math. 7 (1974) 349--376] proved that the graph $K_{t-1}\vee T_{n-t+1,r}$ uniquely maximizes the number of edges among $n$-vertex graphs containing no copy of $\cup_{i=1}^tF_i$. In 2024, Lei and Li [Electron. J. Combin. 31 (2024), P1.25] established the corresponding result for the adjacency spectral radius. We prove that, for every fixed $p>1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the same graph uniquely maximizes the $p$-spectral radius in this class. The proof reduces the problem to forbidding $t$ disjoint copies of a single color-critical graph and applies degree stability after deleting $t-1$ such copies.

title: iMFPO: Improving Mean Flow Policy Optimization with Drift-Aware Velocity Alignment for Embodied Control
abstract: Flow-based generative policies offer expressive action modeling for embodied control, yet achieving efficient one-step generation under reward-driven policy optimization remains challenging. In particular, evolving action distributions during online reinforcement learning may introduce inconsistencies between instantaneous-velocity learning and interval-averaged action generation. To address this challenge, we propose iMFPO, a one-step generative policy optimization framework with decoupled velocity learning and drift-aware velocity alignment. A shared interval-conditioned actor supports instantaneous-velocity supervision and interval-averaged action generation. JVP-corrected velocity regression is jointly optimized with reward-driven policy objectives, with action-level guidance from a frozen PPO teacher during training. At inference, iMFPO directly generates actions through interval-averaged velocity prediction, achieving one-step control without iterative flow integration. Across Go2, G1, H1, and Spot, zero-latent evaluation yields mean returns of 35.69, 34.44, 416.23, and 29.86. On Go2, action-generation latency drops from 15.57 ms to 0.41 ms relative to 64-step RFPO. Code: https://github.com/AIGeeksGroup/iMFPO. Website: https://aigeeksgroup.github.io/iMFPO.

title: Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao Reconstruction of Discrete space Population Dynamics
abstract: Reconstructing the continuous time dynamics of cell state evolution from sparse snapshot observations can be formulated as an unbalanced optimal transport problem. To study such dynamics at a coarse grained cell type level, unbalanced optimal transport must be extended to discrete state spaces. Inspired by discrete flow matching, we extended the dynamic Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) problem to discrete spaces, and derived a closed form for its solution. For particularly large state spaces or more general models, we proposed an unbalanced discrete flow matching as a numerical approximation method, which provides a Markovian reconstruction of the optimal WFR flow. Our discrete WFR framework also stays stable across different coarse grain resolution. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach, and applications to real biological data supported the plausibility of the reconstructed dynamics.

title: Monte Carlo-based secondary dose check platform for the world's first ultra-compact upright proton therapy system
abstract: Objective. This work aimed to develop and validate an independent Monte Carlo (MC) secondary dose check of the RayStation treatment planning system (TPS) for the Mevion S250-FIT, the world's first ultra-compact upright proton therapy system. Approach. The treatment nozzle, including the energy modulation system of boron carbide and polycarbonate plates and the adaptive aperture, was modeled in the TOPAS (TOol for PArticle Simulation) MC code, and the beam model was commissioned against integrated depth dose curves, in-air spot profiles, and dose per monitor unit measured at 12 energy settings. Based on this model, an in-house converter, RayStation2TOPAS, recalculates the TPS plans by reconstructing each pencil beam spot, the aperture for each energy layer, and the seated patient's rotation. In total, 15 water phantom plans and 25 clinical plans were recalculated and compared with the TPS by the point dose, with a tolerance of 5%, and by three-dimensional gamma analysis at 3%/2mm, with a pass rate of at least 90%. Main results. The simulated proton range agreed with the measurement within 0.25mm, the spot full width at half maximum within 6.8%, and the dose per monitor unit within 1.3%. The point dose differed from the TPS by -0.76% to +1.98% in the water phantom plans and by -3.03% to +3.99% in the clinical plans, with gamma pass rates of 96.39% to 99.93% and 90.08% to 99.98%, so every plan passed both tests. Significance. To our knowledge, this is the first independent MC secondary dose check for the S250-FIT, and it complements measurement-based patient-specific quality assurance of its plans.

title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
abstract: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or failed pickup with ground-truth object pose, contact, and surface points. WorldReforge turns this ground truth into two training signals without additional inference cost. Interaction Alignment focuses reconstruction on the small object and contact regions that a global loss underweights, and Surface Correspondence trains backbone features to follow the same physical surface points across frames. On Cosmos3 Nano, WorldReforge reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall and by 35.0% on unseen objects, and it lowers the error in predicting how two actions' outcomes diverge by 43.3%. Although trained only in simulation, it also improves reconstruction on DROID and on real failure videos. Controlled data studies show that failed contact and successful holding teach complementary physics: failed contact teaches how objects respond, and holding teaches how a grasped state persists. Our code, data, and models are available at aim-uofa.github.io/WorldReforge/.

title: Connecting AI Agents to Live Discrete Element Simulations via the Model Context Protocol
abstract: This paper describes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server through which a general-purpose AI agent operates a discrete element engine, commercial or open-source, while the simulation runs. The agent submits a long simulation to the engine and, while it computes, reads the running model, changes it, or stops it. The human modeler stays at the engine's console and graphical interface throughout, and the agent sees what the modeler does there. The tools are derived from what the agent needs to do at the engine and are held to four principles: correctness, coverage, orthogonality and simplicity. Two documentation tools let the agent search the engine's manual and browse it level by level. Five execution tools let the agent run code in the engine, submit long simulations in the background, check on them, read the running model, and stop them. A bridge inside the engine serves these tools in a commercial DEM engine, PFC, and an open-source one, YADE. In a case study, a general-purpose agent calibrated a drained triaxial model of dense Toyoura sand against laboratory data in both engines, while the modeler worked at the same engine; the agent noticed the modeler's actions at the console and acted on them. The same calibration on YADE was then given to seven language models, three sessions each and without human intervention. Twenty of the twenty-one sessions reached the targets, and nineteen of the parameter sets lie in one small region of the admissible ranges. The server and the bridge are released as two open-source packages, itasca-mcp, which also serves FLAC, 3DEC, MPoint and MassFlow, and yade-mcp.

title: Counting solutions to sparse systems of congruences
abstract: We obtain new bounds and asymptotic formulas for the number of solutions to sparse systems of $n$ diagonal congruences modulo an integer $q$ in $s$ variables. In a large range of parameters, our results improve and generalise those of A. A. Karatsuba (1976). In particular, our lower bound on $s$, which guarantees the solvability of such systems, depends only on $n$, rather than on specific degrees as in the work of A. A. Karatsuba (1976).

title: Almost Tight Hardness of Approximation for $0$-Extension
abstract: In the $0$-Extension problem, we are given an undirected graph $G=(V,E)$ with non-negative edge weights $w: E\rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$, a collection $T \subseteq V$ of $k$ terminals, and a metric $D$ over terminals $T$. The goal is to find a retraction $f:V\rightarrow T$ that maps every terminal to itself, while minimizing the sum over all edges of the product of the edge's weight and the distance in $D$ between the terminals to which its endpoints are assigned, i.e., \[ \sum_{\{u,v\}\in E} w_{\{u,v\}} \cdot D(f(u), f(v)). \] Fakcharoenphol, Harrelson, Rao, and Talwar achieve the best known approximation ratio of $O(\log k / \log \log k)$, while the known approximation hardness is $Ω(\sqrt{\log k})$ assuming the unique games conjecture. In this work, we establish an $Ω(\log^{1-\varepsilon}k)$ hardness of approximation for every constant $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ and arbitrarily large fixed $k$, almost matching the upper bound in the exponent of $\log k$. The main technical contribution is an $Ω(\log^{1-\varepsilon}k)$ integrality gap for the earthmover relaxation. Our construction is inspired by randomized extensions of expanders introduced by Schwartz and Tur for the metric relaxation. The result then follows from an existing theorem by Manokaran, Naor, Raghavendra, and Schwartz that translates the integrality gap for the earthmover relaxation to the approximation hardness for every fixed $k$.

title: Revisiting the Schottky-Mott Relation for Metal/ Transition Metal Dichalcogenide Interfaces: The Role of Interface Dipoles
abstract: High contact resistance, predominantly stemming from Fermi-level pinning (FLP), becomes a critical bottleneck in the contact engineering of transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) based two-dimensional field-effect transistors (2DFETs). Our study re-examines the inherent nature of FLP in 2D semiconductors, particularly focusing on regimes where the material thickness is commensurate with the interface thickness. Through the synergistic application of first-principles calculations and experimental validation via ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS) and scanning tunneling spectroscopy (STS), we rigorously establish the metal effective work function (eWF) as the definitive figure of merit for substantiating the Schottky-Mott relation. Our findings indicate that FLP is intrinsically governed by both long-range dipole interactions and extended short-range Lennard-Jones potentials. This framework, in conjunction with the linear Schottky-Mott relation, improves predictive capabilities in contact engineering.

title: Almost sure lower bound for the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of critical AMO
abstract: We show that there exists an absolute constant $d>0$ such that for almost all frequencies $α\in[0,1]\setminus\Q$, the Hausdorff dimension of the spectrum of the critical almost Mathieu operator $H_{1,α,θ}$ is bounded from below by $d$.

title: Near Optimal Pure Stepsize Adaptation Acceleration for Gradient Descent on Nonconvex Optimization
abstract: Existing accelerated first-order methods for nonconvex optimization typically rely on momentum or extrapolation, requiring auxiliary vectors beyond the current iterate and gradient. On the other hand, memory-free stepsize scheduling alone can accelerate certain convex problems, while no guarantee exists for nonconvex problems. This paper closes this gap by proposing Nonconvex Adaptively Clipped Chebyshev (NACC) gradient descent method, which achieves near optimal acceleration while keeping the vanilla gradient descent update. NACC combines an adaptive selection of reversed fractal Chebyshev stepsizes with an epoch-wise clipping mechanism to control the aggressiveness of stepsizes. For nonconvex problems with Lipschitz continuous gradients and Hessians, we establish a near-optimal $\widetilde O(ε^{-7/4})$ complexity. If the problem is convex in addition, then, without modification, NACC automatically achieves an $\widetilde O(ε^{-3/4})$ accelerated complexity. Importantly, NACC guarantees the standard quadratic sufficient descent at every iteration, even when the stepsizes are substantially larger than the conventional choice. These monotonicity properties further facilitate practical implementations that adaptively adjust the estimated gradient and Hessian Lipschitz constants, demonstrating significant advantages in numerical tests against the existing nonconvex acceleration benchmarks.

title: $99.99\%$ of cubic surfaces have a rational point
abstract: When cubic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ are ordered by height, we prove that almost every such surface satisfies the Hasse principle. This extends work of Browning, Le Boudec and Sawin and completes the proof of the conjecture of Poonen and Voloch for Fano hypersurfaces. We also obtain an upper bound for the least height of a rational point on almost all everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces and we give an upper bound for the number of cubic surfaces with a Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle. Finally, once combined with a calculation of Beneish and Keyes about the density of everywhere locally soluble cubic surfaces, this establishes the explicit proportion of cubic surfaces that have a rational point.

title: Transport Layer-Driven Optimization of Color and Efficiency in TADF OLEDs for Large-Area Applications
abstract: Balancing structural simplicity with high efficiency is crucial for practical applications of organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs), especially in large-area lighting devices. Optimizing the charge-transport layers in multilayer OLEDs controls the recombination zone within the emissive layer, thereby enhancing the device's performance. Herein, we experimentally and computationally investigate how the thicknesses of the electron and hole transport layers affect the performance of orange-red thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) OLEDs. Using a TADF emitter, 2-[4-(diphenylamino)phenyl]-10,10-dioxide-9H-thioxanthen-9-one (TXO-TPA), at 10 wt\% concentration in 4,4-Bis(N-carbazolyl)-1,1-biphenyl (CBP) host, we achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency ($η_{EQE}$) of 20.86\% and a peak luminance of 32,800 cd m$^{-2}$. Using a combination of drift-diffusion and optical simulations, we reveal how variations in hole- and electron-transport-layer thicknesses modulate the charge-carrier balance and shift the recombination zone within the emissive layer. This tuning not only optimizes exciton formation but also enables color tuning from green to red without altering the emissive material. Our findings highlight the critical role of transport layer engineering in achieving efficient, color-controlled OLEDs with simplified architectures. Furthermore, we successfully demonstrate a large-area OLED device (~20 cm$^{2}$), achieving an impressive $η_{EQE}$ of 17\%, underscoring the scalability and practicality of our approach for general lighting applications.

title: Towards 360$^\circ$ Embodied UAV Tracking Without Turning
abstract: Conventional embodied UAV tracking couples target observability with heading control because targets may leave the field of view of forward-facing cameras. We investigate a complementary paradigm that uses full-spherical perception to follow designated targets without active heading adjustment. To support this setting, we introduce 360UAV-ETrack, a simulation benchmark comprising 2,652 sequences, over 1.73 million synchronized observations, eight tracking tasks, and 150 held-out closed-loop scenarios. We propose 360UAV-TVLA, a panoramic vision--language--action (VLA) framework integrating persistent visual referring (PVR), compressed temporal memory (CTM), and geometry-aligned trajectory supervision (GTS) for instance identification, motion reasoning, and three-dimensional control. Experiments across two VLA backbones show consistent gains over standard fine-tuning, with normalized average tracking frames increasing from 22.56\% to 35.28\% for $π_0$ and from 25.68\% to 33.64\% for $π_{0.5}$. Our benchmark further reveals a substantial gap between offline imitation accuracy and closed-loop tracking reliability, establishing a challenging testbed for future research https://libingyu01.github.io/360UAV-ETrack_360UAV-TVLA/

title: BayesPath: Reliability-Aware Bayesian Reasoning for Whole-Slide Pathology Agents
abstract: Diagnosing whole-slide images (WSIs) requires hypothesis-driven reasoning: pathologists form a differential diagnosis, seek discriminative evidence, weigh its reliability, and stop once it suffices. However, existing training-free WSI agents lack an explicit framework for such reasoning. They typically use a large language model (LLM) to aggregate the region descriptions of a multimodal LLM (MLLM), without a belief over the candidates or regard for the descriptions' reliability. Consequently, a repeated model error counts as independent evidence for an incorrect diagnosis. We introduce BayesPath, a training-free WSI agent that casts the pathologist's Scan-Look-Weigh-Decide process as reliability-aware Bayesian reasoning. An explicit belief over the candidates is updated with each observation through a reliability-aware likelihood and guides where to look next and when to stop. This likelihood corrects for the models' answer bias, discounts correlated observations, and captures diagnostic confusions estimated without labels. The updates form an interpretable evidence trail of how each observation shapes the belief. On five MultiPathQA tasks spanning slide classification and slide VQA, BayesPath achieves the highest average accuracy among training-free agents, 58.6% against 34.1% for the next best, with large gains on slide classification. On identical observations, Bayesian updating outperforms LLM aggregation on average, even with a larger LLM. BayesPath's belief is also better calibrated than naive Bayes, so uncertain cases can be deferred to pathologists. Code is available at https://github.com/bryanwong17/BayesPath

title: Phonon-Aware Electron-to-Nuclear Spin Quantum Memory in NV Centers
abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are a promising solid-state platform for quantum memory: the electron spin can be optically initialized and read out, while nearby nuclear spins have long coherence times and can serve as storage qubits. In this work, we develop a phonon-aware open quantum system model for electron-to-nuclear spin state transfer in a single NV center. The model includes the NV electron spin, a coupled 13C nuclear spin, the hyperfine interaction, an effective microwave/radio-frequency-assisted SWAP interaction for writing and reading, a single effective phonon mode with longitudinal spin-phonon coupling, and Lindblad relaxation and dephasing channels. The dynamics are simulated with the Lindblad master equation in QuTiP, using the secular approximation and a hyperfine-resonant drive in the rotating frame. Without spin-phonon coupling and electron decoherence, the write-store-read protocol recovers the stored state with a fidelity above 0.9999. With the default decoherence rates, increasing the spin-phonon coupling from 0 to 0.06 MHz lowers the worst-case retrieval fidelity from 0.9994 to 0.9884, and the fidelity oscillates with the phonon-mode period because electron-phonon entanglement generated during the write step is partially undone during the read step. With a phenomenological temperature-dependent rate model, the fidelity decreases monotonically from 0.9997 at 1 K to 0.9938 at 300 K, while storage-time losses follow the assumed nuclear-spin decoherence rates. The storage-time plots, temperature sweep, and parameter maps identify operating regimes for NV-center quantum memory, and the accompanying open-source code provides a reproducible framework for studying phonon-limited quantum memory.

title: InstructTTS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Objective Instruction-Following TTS
abstract: Instruction-following text-to-speech (Instruct-TTS) renders a target transcript in the manner described by a free-form natural-language instruction, and a good rendition must succeed on three fronts at once: following the instruction, pronouncing the transcript correctly, and sounding natural. Reinforcement learning has become the standard way to post-train such generative models toward human preferences, and TTS systems increasingly adopt it. When the three objectives are optimized together under a single scalar reward, typically with group relative policy optimization (GRPO), training tends to be unstable: the objectives compete, and the shared update drifts toward whichever one is easiest to improve, producing a seesaw among them. We instead adapt on-policy distillation (OPD), which fuses several single-objective teachers by matching their velocity fields on the student's own rollouts. Realizing this for Instruct-TTS first calls for a sound reward on each axis, which we analyze carefully: a distilled Qwen-Omni proxy for the costly Gemini judge, dialect-free data for the WER reward, and DNSMOS in place of the language-biased UTMOS. We then train three single-objective teachers with GRPO and fuse them with OPD, routing each rollout to the instruction-following or WER teacher by its data domain and letting every rollout additionally follow the MOS teacher for quality. This lets instruction following and intelligibility improve together without a trade-off, but the quality target conflicts with instruction following, so following it additively reintroduces the seesaw. We therefore propose conflict-aware velocity fusion, which projects the quality target off the direction that opposes the primary objective before fusing, and show that it markedly reduces the instruction-following/quality trade-off. The fused model improves over scalar-reward GRPO on all three objectives at once.

title: Algebraic Diversity of Switching Functions
abstract: Algebraic Diversity generalizes averaging over many observations to averaging one observation over a group of transformations matched to its structure. This paper develops the framework on the Boolean cube $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ for the translations, the coordinate permutations, the hyperoctahedral group, and the general linear and affine groups. It determines the commutant of each action and gives closed forms for the group-averaged second-order statistic of one truth table, which collapses to the Walsh periodogram for the translations, to per-weight averages for the hyperoctahedral group, and to the weight up to complementation for the affine group. Bent functions are exactly those whose translation average is white, the Haar transform along an input order is the multiplexer tree of Shannon's expansion, and higher-order averages see only the weight below a first informative order, two for the translations and four for the affine group. A matched stabilizer stands in for repeated observations, since a vote over orbits of $s$ points divides by $s$ the number of noisy truth tables a target error requires. The same viewpoint gives the affine hull of a function as matched coordinates, an exact variance identity for XOR hashing, and matched hashes whose variance never exceeds that of a pairwise independent hash. Applications on public benchmarks include hash choice for approximate model counting, the decision of parity-structured formulas and the refutation of counting formulas modulo 3 and 4 from the spectra of clause blocks, separation of NPN classes by canonical spectra, tested on ISCAS-85 cut functions and all five-input classes, correction of noisy truth tables and protection of lookup tables by voting over symmetries, blind group matching, and an analog of the CLEAN algorithm that writes a truth table as the XOR of atoms in the fixed spaces of groups. All proofs are given in full.

title: CondUQ: Calibrated Conditional Uncertainty Quantification Using Distribution Matching
abstract: Many applications, especially reliability- and safety-critical ones, require accurate uncertainty quantification for the outputs of model- or learning-based measurement, estimation, and prediction systems. The errors of such systems often vary with factors such as input quality and operating conditions, and thus cannot be accurately described by a single Gaussian model. Although Gaussian mixture models and calibrated quantiles can approximate such error distributions, their unconditional forms do not capture how the error behavior depends on these factors. Hence, we propose condUQ, an approach that conditions error models on observable factors for enabling accurate and reliable uncertainty quantification. condUQ is built on top of an existing system without modifying it and applies even when the system is a black box. First, condUQ maps the observable factors to a latent quality index (QI) such that errors sharing the same QI follow a common, approximately Gaussian conditional distribution. The QI predictor is trained end-to-end with a distribution-matching objective, without requiring quality labels. Second, for each QI, a Gaussian error model is then fitted and calibrated on a large held-out dataset. condUQ is demonstrated on three examples: (a) GPS multipath errors conditioned on satellite elevation and signal strength, (b) relative attitude errors of a transformer-based visual relative pose regression model conditioned on its internal features of the image pairs, and (c) prediction errors of a world model conditioned on the input observations and actions. In all three examples, condUQ substantially reduces the discrepancy between the modeled and empirical error distributions compared with a single global model. Moreover, the learned QIs reveal how the underlying factors affect the error characteristics in a manner consistent with physical principles.

title: TAT-Det: A Dataset for Testicular Appendage Torsion Detection and Segmentation in Ultrasound Images
abstract: Background: Testicular appendage torsion (TAT) is the leading cause of acute scrotal pain in prepubertal children. Yet, its diagnosis remains challenging due to nonspecific clinical manifestations and the absence of standardized datasets for pediatric acute scrotal emergencies. Results: We present TAT-Det, an expert-annotated ultrasound dataset specifically designed for TAT. TAT-Det comprises 2,600 ultrasound images from 1,203 patients collected at the Children's Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine. Each TAT-positive image is accompanied by lesion-level bounding boxes for detection and pixel-level segmentation masks for fine-grained delineation. Annotations were produced through a multi-stage workflow involving independent annotation by board-certified pediatric sonographers, consensus review, and refinement. Baseline benchmarks for object detection and semantic segmentation using representative deep learning models are further provided, with YOLO11m achieving the best detection performance and RWKV-UNet the best segmentation performance. Conclusions: TAT-Det addresses the lack of publicly available resources for pediatric emergency ultrasound and establishes a foundation for developing and evaluating artificial intelligence methods for automated TAT analysis.

title: Multiwavelength Analysis of the Merging Cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8: A Three-way Merger in Disguise?
abstract: We identify the galaxy cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8 as a candidate bimodal merging cluster due to its optical properties listed in the redMaPPer cluster catalog. To confirm the cluster's merging state and reveal its dark matter halo and intracluster medium (ICM) morphologies, we conducted a multiwavelength follow-up campaign encompassing HST/ACS optical observations, XMM-Newton X-ray imaging, and Keck/Deimos multislit spectroscopy. The weak lensing mass reconstruction performed with the HST images shows two resolved peaks whose positions coincide with the two brightest cluster galaxies. The ICM morphology is consistent with a post-pericenter merger, with significant asymmetry in X-ray flux between subclusters. Our Keck/Deimos redshift measurements reveal a relative velocity $Δv_{\mathrm{LOS}} = 480$ km s$^{-1}$ between eastern and western subclusters. The eastern, more massive subcluster, however, exhibits a highly elongated shape, suggesting either a dark matter halo of considerable eccentricity or the presence of a third, unresolved halo, eliciting the question of whether RMJ1219 is truly binary or a three-way merger. To investigate these hypotheses, we fit the weak lensing shear data using four different combinations of spherical and elliptical NFW halo models and provide an estimate of the mass and concentration of each subhalo. Although the best fit is achieved with a three-halo model, the data are insufficient to determine whether the introduction of extra parameters is statistically justified.

title: Empirical De-Quantization and Norm-Controlled Spectral Audit of Quantum Cognition Machine Learning in an Emerging Equity Market
abstract: Quantum-inspired machine learning in econophysics describes states of financial markets through matrix Hamiltonians, using ground-state expectations to predict returns and spectral gaps to identify crises. Although early work reports encouraging advances, it remains unclear whether these stem from genuine noncommutative quantum geometry or from conventional classical regularization and scale effects. We test this in a controlled audit of matrix-form Quantum Cognition Machine Learning (QCML) and variational quantum circuits on the Moscow Exchange (2020-2025), combining daily equity data with causally lagged macro news under realistic trading costs, short-selling bans, and abrupt shifts in market regimes. By using capacity-matched operator swaps -- which progressively eliminate complex Berry phases and matrix noncommutativity down to a commuting classical Gibbs radial-basis limit under scale-invariant regularization -- as well as testing spectral indicators against radial-norm null hypotheses and untrained GUE random matrices, we isolate the contribution of each quantum element. In out-of-sample data, neither complex phases, noncommutativity, nor circuit entanglement improves the ranking of returns relative to classical controls. Once feature magnitudes are normalized, apparent crisis detection from raw spectral gaps drops below chance levels. These results show that on noisy equity panels, matrix-form QCML acts as an adaptive spectrally bounded classical smoothing kernel: it reliably integrates lagged news and curbs extreme crisis forecasts without passing economic multiple-testing thresholds, while our audit provides operator-swap and random-matrix controls for evaluating future quantum-inspired financial models.

title: What Does Skill Lift Actually Measure? A Source-Code-Level Audit and Noise-Aware Reanalysis of SkillsBench
abstract: Agent skills are directories of instructions, reference materials, and scripts loaded on demand by coding agents. According to SkillsBench, although human-curated skills can raise the passing rate by about 16.6 percentage points (pp) on average, they have actually reduced the results for some tasks. Later research has started to gate or eliminate skills according to the above per-task gains. We have audited the above benchmark at the source-code level and analysed 7,554 public trials to form 1,421 paired "(configuration, task) cells". Source-code audit identified two controlled-verified cases of grader dependence and one operational definition gap; the average lift on these three tasks was 74.6 pp, and the overall average lift for the full set was 18.7 pp. The audit also found that four tasks contained placeholder skill directories, and a certain execution harness additionally added 48 built-in skills in most runs. No task-level reduction achieved statistical significance in the pooled reanalysis with multiple-testing correction. As there were at most three runs per condition for each cell, the observed negative differences are very susceptible to run-sampling noise, and arithmetically, 58% of the cells could not have shown a decrease. Therefore, the raw numbers of negative cells cannot show that skills cause harm. A gating strategy based on the skill-free score seems to improve by 2-3 pp in the logs; however, even after shuffling condition labels to remove any skill effect, it still achieves an increase of 4-7 pp. On the held-out runs not used for fitting and decision-making, there was no statistically significant improvement. The audit ledger and analysis scripts have been published by us.

title: Energy cascade spectrum in wave turbulence of a two-dimensional quantum fluid
abstract: In the two-dimensional (2D) Gross-Pitaevskii model for a Bose gas, the naive dimensional non-equilibrium wave-turbulence power-law prediction for the direct energy cascade coincides with thermal equilibrium and therefore carries no energy flux. We resolve this degeneracy by deriving a logarithmically corrected spectrum that supports a positive, constant energy flux toward small scales.
