This work presents Surface-based Scene Stylization (Surf-Style), which reconstructs object surfaces in a 3D scene and uses these surfaces to achieve geometric consistency and localized stylization. Surf-Style defines a learnable appearance model over 3D space, which is modified to replicate the visual style of a reference image. Compared to state-of-the-art methods, our method achieves superior consistency and offers greater flexibility in controllable stylization, including the ability to target specific surface regions and combine different styles.

title: Near-Tight Robust Coresets for Clustering in Euclidean Spaces
abstract: This paper considers coresets for the robust $(k,z)$-clustering problem with $m$ outliers in Euclidean spaces. A robust coreset is a weighted subset of the data that, for every set of $k$ centers and every outlier budget $0\leq b\leq m$, approximates the clustering cost with $b$ outliers removed to within relative error $ε$. For every constant $z\geq 1$, we prove that the optimal worst-case size of such coresets over all ambient dimensions is \[ Θ(m) + \widetildeΘ_z(\min\{kε^{-(z+2)}, k^{2(z+1)/(z+2)}ε^{-2} + km^{z/(z+2)}ε^{-4/(z+2)}\}), \qquad 1\leq z \leq 2, \] \[ Θ(m) + \widetildeΘ_z(\min\{kε^{-(z+2)}, k^{2(z+1)/(z+2)}ε^{-2} + k \min\{m, \sqrt{m}ε^{-z/2}\} \}), \qquad z > 2. \]

title: SPARC: Geometry-Guided Attention Pruning for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation
abstract: We present SPARC, a geometry-guided attention pruning framework that turns the native self-attention of pretrained video diffusion transformers into a unified mechanism for camera control and persistent scene memory. Our key insight is that attention connectivity can simultaneously serve as geometric conditioning for camera control and spatial addressing for historical memory retrieval. Motivated by the asymmetric contextual requirements of reconstructing observed content and synthesizing novel regions, SPARC restricts observed tokens to geometrically corresponding historical tokens and local spatiotemporal context, while preserving dense attention for unobserved regions. Correspondence-aware attention biasing and order-invariant historical positioning further enable stable retrieval across long temporal gaps. Without introducing additional learnable control or memory modules, SPARC achieves precise camera adherence and faithful scene revisitation while substantially reducing attention computation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of aggressive attention pruning in improving camera adherence, revisit consistency, and visual fidelity, with an inference speedup of over 50x when combined with four-step distillation. Project page is available at https://zju3dv.github.io/SPARC.

title: How AI Is Reconfiguring Work in India: A Task-Based Framework for Understanding Augmentation, Displacement, New Roles and the Changing Structure of Jobs
abstract: Public debate on AI and Indian employment tends to compress a complicated phenomenon into a single binary: will AI take a given job, or not. This paper argues that the accurate picture is a taxonomy rather than a binary. AI rarely replaces a job wholesale; more often it automates a bundle of tasks within a job, and the size of that bundle varies with task structure, sector, regulatory setting, and, distinctively in India's case, the economics of AI access itself. We propose a four-level framework (task, job, occupation, labour-market outcome) and classify Indian job impact into two broad regimes: jobs where AI has automated most of the skill bundle and the human is reduced largely to validation, and jobs where the human remains the primary driver and AI functions as a productivity tool. Each regime splits further into policy-relevant sub-types. Drawing on Indian evidence from business process outsourcing, manufacturing, MSMEs, sanitation, financial services, law, and software engineering, we show that every job in our sample has had to be reimagined, through task-level augmentation, task reallocation, or a genuinely new role built around operating the machine, rather than simply eliminated or defended unchanged. We close with a distributional analysis of who bears the cost of this reimagining and a three-pronged policy recommendation: continue encouraging AI diffusion, invest in India-specific labour-market research, and pair adoption with structured worker-transition pathways.

title: A Path Integral Method with Far-Field Expansion for Open Quantum Dynamics
abstract: We establish a connection between the quasi-adiabatic propagator path integral (QuAPI) method and fast resummation of Dyson series (FRODS). Building on this connection, we introduce a path integral method with far-field expansion (PIFFE) for quantum systems coupled linearly to a thermal Gaussian bath. PIFFE combines QuAPI with a Taylor expansion of the far-field bath influence, keeping interactions within $r$ time steps in exponential form. The scheme has error $O(Δt^2)$ at fixed final time and is free of stochastic or tensor-compression errors. Spin-boson tests show that PIFFE gives results much closer to QuAPI than FRODS does, even for small $r$, while requiring substantially less storage than QuAPI. This allows much longer bath memory lengths and simulations of multilevel systems. Truncating the bath memory and limiting the total auxiliary degree further reduce storage and computational costs.

title: When to Respond, Where to Ground: Streaming 3D Affordance Grounding
abstract: Given a continuous RGB-D stream and a language request, streaming 3D affordance grounding requires an agent to decide when to respond and where to locate the requested functional part using only observations available so far. Existing 3D affordance grounding methods typically assume complete scene observations, while streaming vision-language models lack fine-grained 3D functional grounding. Our goal is to jointly determine response timing and functional-part localization during continuous scene observation. We propose StreamAff, an evidence-guided response strategy that makes both decisions from the grounding model's own visual evidence. The model scores the visual patches of the frames it reads: their combined support, weighed against a wait option, decides when to respond, and the highest-scoring patch selects the frame to ground in. A conditional look-back policy lets the model answer from an earlier observation at the moment of the request or wait for new evidence, and zoom-and-refine grounding segments the part named in the answer on the 3D points of the selected frame. We further introduce StreamFun3D, a benchmark derived from real-world 3D scenes that evaluates response timing and grounding across four evidence settings: Current, History, Future, and Unobserved, together with StreamIoU, a metric that credits a mask only when the response is timely and grounded in a valid source frame. We adapt offline 3D affordance grounding methods and build external-decider baselines that pair vision-language models with our mask decoder. StreamAff achieves 30.14% StreamIoU on 15-second streams, a 40.6% relative improvement over the strongest of these baselines.

title: Budget, Readout or Reasoning? Where Small Reasoning Models Lose Value in Auction Bidding
abstract: Ad platforms and marketplaces show bidders a bid landscape, the estimated chance of winning at each candidate bid, and increasingly let agents built on reasoning language models choose the bid. We give six open reasoning models of 4B to 14B parameters such landscapes, with win curves from eBay closing prices and from a simulated advertising market (AuctionNet), and score their bids on held-out auctions against an exact calculator. Because the agent is handed the estimates, the lost value can be split by cause. Two failures belong to the models. They pass over the best option even when the values written in their own trace already rank it first, and their wrong answers lean toward the highest bid on the menu. The lean is about the bid's size, not its place in the list, and it survives sampling. At 768 forced tokens on eBay, under pay-your-bid pricing, the wrong answers cost bidders 7-17% of the surplus the calculator's bids earn. Arithmetic errors are rare. Two further losses come from operator choices. A token cap cuts traces short: allowed to stop on their own within 4,096 tokens, five models recover 91-100% of the calculator's lead over a model that does no reasoning. Asking for the answer while the reasoning block is still open misreads it: closing the block first lifts the weakest model from 42% to 84% on eBay and from 24% to 81% on AuctionNet. Finally, an audit that flags bids disagreeing with the trace's own numbers, and overrides them with the calculator's bid, raises the share of the calculator's lead recovered at 768 forced tokens from 42-85% to 84-100% on eBay under nested cross-validation, and the same reader settings transfer from eBay to AuctionNet.

title: Toward a quantum resistance standard above liquid nitrogen temperature
abstract: Quantum Hall effect (QHE) -- the pioneering demonstration of one-dimensional topologically-protected edge channels -- manifest a transversal resistance quantized solely by two universal constants $e$ and $h$ (the elementary charge and the Planck constant, respectively), referred to as the von Klitzing constant $R_\mathrm{K}=h/e^{2}$. For decades, this has enabled a unique route for realizing quantum Hall resistance (QHR) standard in the Système international d'unitès (SI), yet high precision QHR under relaxed conditions, especially temperature higher than 30 K, has not been possible. Here, we show that interfacial charge-order coupling inbetween CrOCl and monolayer graphene offers enhanced Fermi velocity, creating a robust Landau cyclotron gap. Using a customized direct current comparator (DCC, mounted at room temperature), we obtain relative deviation of the Hall resistance from $R_\mathrm{K}/2$ of (15 $\pm$ 23)\,n$Ω$ $Ω$$^{-1}$ (23 parts per billion of relative uncertainty) at 50 K, with an external magnetic field of 12 T and a dc current of 10 $μ$A. At 100 K, the system exhibits QHR with 2 parts per million of relative uncertainty. Our results therefore suggest a platform toward a next-generation quantum resistance standard that may work at above liquid nitrogen temperature and free of conventional compressor refrigerators.

title: A new method of Ecological Inference based on the Cressie--Read power divergence
abstract: Ecological inference aims to estimate the bivariate association structure between a pair of variables from the row and column totals of a set of contingency tables. The paper introduces a new approach based on minimizing the Cressie--Read power divergence, applied to the estimation of vote transitions between two elections. It also outlines a Fisher scoring algorithm and derives the asymptotic distribution of the estimator.

title: Bayesian Calibration of Effective Material Parameters in Electric Machine Stators
abstract: Efficiency-driven faster switching by wide-bandgap semiconductor devices increases electromagnetic interference (EMI) in electric vehicles (EVs). Mitigating this EMI becomes more complex as system components grow. Therefore, electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) is assessed early via system-level simulation of the EV powertrain. A key EMC-critical quantity is the impedance of the electric drive machine, forming a major part of the EMI propagation path. Finite element (FE) simulations are typically used but are computationally expensive and limited by insufficient material property knowledge. We present a surrogate model based Bayesian calibration framework for 3D full-wave FE simulation of an externally excited synchronous motor (EESM) stator. Effective material parameters (EMPs) are calibrated to match broadband differential mode (DM) impedance measurements up to 30 MHz. A multi-output surrogate model replaces the demanding FE simulation, while an orthogonal surrogate model compliant discrepancy term assesses material modeling completeness. Using Hamiltonian Markov Chain Monte Carlo, we construct posterior distributions of the EMPs for three calibration scenarios with different parameter ranges. Two of three scenarios achieve good agreement with measurements. However, accurate calibration requires "datasheet-deviating" EMPs, while "datasheet-aligned" ones yield deficient results, indicating material models do not fully capture the underlying physics. The proposed methodology enables estimating unknown material properties from impedance measurements and evaluates the sufficiency of chosen material models. Although identified EMPs may differ from datasheet values, they reliably estimate frequency-dependent DM impedance. This work focuses on EMPs influencing the stator's DM impedance; complete machine calibration, including rotor and common-mode impedance, is the scope of future research.

title: Frustration in system with intercalated and bilayer smectic structure
abstract: The dimeric mesogens exhibit an unusual variety of mesophases - nematic and smectic, with distinctly different packing schemes. The relation between molecular and mesophase structure was studied for homologue series of non-symmetric bent dimers CBO6.Om, obtained by serial Pd- and Pt-catalyzed cross-coupling chemical reactions. The shorter homologues of the series form smectics with an intercalated structure, and longer homologues form bilayer smectics with broken up-down symmetry of molecular orientation within the layers, for intermediate homologues frustration leads to a nematic gap. The additional structure complexity arises from the tendency of bent dimers to form twisted structures, in which the azimuthal angle of tilted molecules forms both short- and long-pitch helices. Here we confirm, through resonant X-ray diffraction, that longer homologues form a helical four-layer structure of SmCTB-SH phase, along with a more complex one in which, in addition to the basic four-layer unit, an extra helix is superimposed, SmCTB-DH phase. This additional helix has a periodicity that is strongly temperature-dependent; upon cooling, it changes from 100 nm to 40 nm.

title: Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods for Multiobjective Optimization over Probability Measures via Hilbert-Space Lifting
abstract: Many sampling and inference tasks require a single distribution that balances several targets. We formulate this task as multiobjective optimization of Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences over probability measures, in the Pareto sense. The particle method MWGraD (Nguyen et al., 2025) uses explicit Wasserstein gradient steps, and its accelerated version A-MWGraD (Nguyen et al., 2026) lacks discrete-time guarantees. We propose the multiobjective Wasserstein proximal gradient (MWPG), which uses implicit Wasserstein gradient steps, and its accelerated version, multiobjective Wasserstein accelerated proximal gradient (MWAPG), with rigorous discrete-time guarantees. Our key idea is a Hilbert-space lifting: each measure is represented as the pushforward of a fixed base measure by a map in a Hilbert space. The problem then becomes a constrained multiobjective composite problem over transport maps, to which accelerated proximal gradient methods apply. For convex and smooth potentials, we show that MWAPG decreases a Pareto merit function at the rate $\mathcal{O}(1/k^2)$; for $m$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth potentials, the rate is $\mathcal{O}\big((1-\sqrt{m/L})^k\big)$. We also give closed-form Gaussian updates and particle implementations based on input-convex neural networks, which require no score estimation. Experiments on synthetic and real-world dataset show that MWAPG needs far fewer iterations than MWPG and matches or outperforms A-MWGraD in Bayesian multi-task learning.

title: Exact Error Analysis of Noise-Domain OTFS with Paired Covariance Signaling
abstract: Noise-domain orthogonal time frequency space (ND-OTFS) encodes bits through opposite correlations in Gaussian delay--Doppler pairs of equal average energy. This letter derives the exact conditional bit error probability (BEP) of maximum-likelihood detection using generalized covariance eigenvalues and characteristic-function inversion. For scalar channels, we obtain an incomplete-beta expression and its finite-sum Rayleigh average. Partial correlation yields an error floor for a fixed observation count. At unit correlation, the conditional BEP decays with an signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) exponent equal to the number of pair observations, and common Rayleigh fading yields diversity order one. Simulations validate the analysis and quantify pair-placement effects.

title: Hijacking 3D Generation: Targeted Adversarial Attacks against Image-to-3D Models via Prefix Trajectory Alignment
abstract: Online services that deploy Image-to-3D models enable users to generate high-quality 3D assets from a single image. However, the generated 3D geometry can violate content policies and cause broader security risks. To prevent such content, these services typically use policy-restricted inspectors to examine uploaded images before generation. Since the inspector examines only the visible content of the input, a visually benign image can still induce the generation of policy-restricted 3D geometry. However, turning this vulnerability into an effective attack is non-trivial in the black-box setting: global backpropagation through the long DiT generation trajectory is difficult to fit, while different image preprocessing pipelines across services can substantially reduce transferability. In this paper, we present PTA3D, a targeted adversarial attack against Image-to-3D models that addresses these challenges through Prefix Trajectory Alignment (PTA) and Preprocessing Aware Optimization (PAO). PTA progressively aligns the prefix DiT outputs of the adversarial trajectory with those of the target trajectory, where the core geometric structure is formed, allowing the final geometry to be controlled without optimizing through the complete generation trajectory. PAO exposes adversarial optimization to diverse image transformations rather than a single preprocessing pipeline, reducing sensitivity to the mismatch between surrogate and target services. We establish a prefix-to-output bound and a preprocessing-aware transfer bound to theoretically characterize the effectiveness of the two designs. Experiments on three open-source Image-to-3D models and three online services show that PTA3D achieves 41.5%-88.5% ASR on online services and 90.8%-94.6% ASR in white box settings, substantially outperforming existing attacks.

title: Quantum Geometric Origin of Néel-Order-Driven Magneto-Optical Response in MnTe
abstract: Magneto-optical (MO) responses provide a direct probe of magnetic order, yet resolving compensated antiferromagnetic order remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate in altermagnetic MnTe that the symmetry of the Néel order is imprinted on the MO response through distinct quantum-geometric contributions. Combining first-principles calculations with a Landau symmetry framework, we demonstrate that the quantum metric gives rise to a twofold optical anisotropy, with its diagonal and symmetric off-diagonal components forming an $E_{2g}$ doublet associated with the quadratic Néel-order invariants, providing a characteristic MO Voigt signature of the Néel-vector orientation. In contrast, the Berry curvature generates a complementary threefold Hall response governed by the cubic $A_{2g}$ Néel-order invariant. Although the Hall conductivity and the out-of-plane weak-ferromagnetic moment share the same symmetry and angular dependence, constraining the latter to zero leaves the optical Hall response essentially unchanged demonstrating that the Hall response originates directly from the compensated Néel order rather than the net magnetization. Our results establish quantum geometry as a direct link between Néel order and MO response, revealing distinct twofold and threefold optical signatures of Néel order in altermagnetic MnTe.

title: Pseudospin-mediated broadband hypersonic phonon transport beyond localized Berry curvature
abstract: Phononic nanostructures offer compact and highly confined control of elastic waves for signal transport, filtering, and quantum transduction. More recently, topological phononic structures have been explored as a route to robust waveguiding around defects and sharp bends, offering a promising basis for scalable and reliable phononic circuitry. However, how robust transport can persist as conventional localized Berry-curvature signatures diminish with increasing structural perturbation remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate bend-resilient hypersonic phonon transport beyond the conventional valley Hall framework. Using an engineered propeller phononic crystal operating at 1.9 GHz, we continuously increase the geometric perturbation to gradually weaken the valley topology while enhancing modal pseudospin character. Strikingly, as the Berry curvature progressively delocalizes from valleys, the complete elastic bandgap broadens to a normalized width of 34% and the interface modes become more strongly confined. Two-port electromechanical measurements on a thin-film lithium niobate-on-SOI platform experimentally confirm broadband interface-mode transport with no measurable bend-induced loss, despite the absence of well-localized valley-topology signatures. Our findings establish modal pseudospin engineering as a powerful design principle for robust acoustic guiding beyond conventional topological constraints, paving the way for broadband hypersonic phononic circuitry for classical and quantum information processing.

title: Projector Subspace Optimization for Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) achieve strong performance through instruction tuning, yet adapting them to sequential tasks requires Multimodal Continual Instruction Tuning (MCIT). Existing replay-free methods expand prompts or routed LoRA experts across multi-layer decoders, incurring heavy parameter and routing overhead while shifting internal feature distributions. Instead, we identify the final linear layer of the vision-language projector as a high-capacity, coordinate-stationary bridge, where sequential updates easily induce interface drift by displacing historical visual tokens. While low-rank subspace adaptation offers a compact remedy, selecting directions solely from historical statistics or task gradients sacrifices plasticity or stability, and unconstrained multi-step updates still accumulate large drift. To resolve both issues, we propose Projector Refinement through Optimized Update Directions (PROUD), a continual subspace optimization framework for the terminal projector layer. At task onset, PROUD combines retained input statistics with initial gradients to analytically extract a metric-orthonormal subspace maximizing first-order task gain under a drift budget. During training, it regularizes updates within this fixed subspace via an exact Frobenius penalty before losslessly merging them with zero inference or routing overhead. Experiments on UCIT and CoIN across MLLM backbones show that PROUD outperforms recent replay-free baselines in continual accuracy while curbing forgetting with a fraction of trainable parameters.

title: WorldBridge: Bridging Scattered Views for Coherent 3D World Generation
abstract: Generating coherent and explorable 3D worlds from scattered images with little or no visual overlap is a fundamental and long-standing challenge in computer vision, which existing geometry-aware methods fail to address. Meanwhile, existing image- and video-based methods may generate unseen regions but produce inconsistent geometry across views. To bridge this gap, we present WorldBridge, a framework for coherent and controllable 3D world generation under scattered images with little or no visual overlap. WorldBridge encodes scattered references into a global scene context to guide geometry and appearance generation across views. Our temporal and spatial reference attention mechanism further enhances the fidelity of temporal references along the target trajectory and supports flexible spatial references outside it. A plug-and-play latent-reference consistency strategy improves reference fidelity through reprojection-guided test-time optimization. We also introduce the WorldBridge benchmark suite to evaluate 3D world generation from scattered, low-overlap references, which is rarely explored by current benchmarks. Both qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate that our method enables controllable and coherent 3D world generation, surpassing the existing state-of-the-art solutions. Our project page is available at https://davidyan2001.github.io/WorldBridge/.

title: Smooth approximation of one-sided minimizing CMC hypersurfaces with isolated singularities
abstract: We consider a CMC hypersurface with an isolated singularity, given by the boundary of a set of finite perimeter, that minimizes the prescribed mean curvature functional on one side. If a varifold tangent at the singularity is a non--flat regular cone of multiplicity--1 that minimizes perimeter on the side occupied by the blow--up, then we show that, in a small neighborhood of the singular point, there exists a sequence of smooth CMC hypersurfaces, with the same prescribed mean curvature, that converges to the initial hypersurface. We also establish the full CMC variational equation and regularity for minimizers of a class of singular obstacle problems.

title: Gaussian Process Stochastic Frontiers with Two-Way Fixed Effects
abstract: Parametric frontier restrictions and unobserved time heterogeneity can distort efficiency measurement in panel data. This paper develops a Bayesian stochastic frontier model with a Gaussian process prior and unrestricted individual and time effects that may be correlated with inputs. Conditional on inefficiency, orthogonal projection eliminates both sets of fixed effects, yielding a restricted likelihood that retains observation-specific inefficiency. Monte Carlo experiments show competitive performance under correct parametric specification and improved performance when benchmark models impose an incorrect frontier functional form or omit time effects. An application to Spanish dairy farms observed from 1999 to 2010 yields similar average technical efficiency across specifications, but a lower posterior mean of average returns to scale, with greater uncertainty, under the Gaussian process frontier. Models with year effects also yield more stable estimated efficiency profiles than the benchmark with a quadratic trend and time-input interactions. These findings show that conclusions about scale economies and efficiency dynamics depend on both frontier flexibility and the treatment of time heterogeneity.

title: Defect Correlators from Supergravity: Finding the Missing Contact Terms
abstract: We resolve a puzzle in the computation of holographic correlators using supergravity when defects are present. Previous direct supergravity calculations of defect two-point functions were found to differ from bootstrap results by a set of contact contributions. We show that the discrepancy arises from two effects: nonlinear Kaluza-Klein field redefinitions in the bulk, which induce additional quadratic couplings when applied consistently to localized sources, and off-shell terms in mixed bulk--defect vertices, which can collapse internal defect propagators. We demonstrate how these two mechanisms resolve the puzzle in two concrete examples in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, where we consider two-point correlators in the presence of a $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS Wilson line and on $\mathbb{RP}^4$.

title: MulCLIP: A Multi-level Alignment Framework for Enhancing Fine-grained Long-context CLIP
abstract: Vision-language models such as CLIP excel at image-text alignment but struggle with long, detailed descriptions due to training on short captions. Recent methods address this limitation using region proposals to align visual regions with sentences, but at substantial deployment cost. We present MulCLIP, an end-to-end multi-level alignment framework that directly exploits natural long-text structure without region proposals. Instead of simply stacking objectives, MulCLIP aligns different textual granularities through compatible training signals: global contrastive alignment for long captions and short summaries, Word-Patch Reconstruction over locally calibrated features for within-sample word-patch semantics, and Subcaption-Aggregated Patch alignment for context-rich subcaption grounding. Experiments on benchmarks spanning varying caption lengths show consistent gains, and ablations confirm that the proposed objectives are complementary and jointly improve the overall framework. Code will be released at https://github.com/truongchau2602/MulCLIP.

title: TaCo: Rethinking Correlation for Visual Tracking on Edge Devices
abstract: Lightweight trackers have replaced cross-correlation with attention, and on low-power edge hardware they pay for it, since memory-bound softmax, normalization and reshaping operators of attention cost far more time than their arithmetic suggests. Benchmarking efficient trackers on an edge Neural Processing Unit (NPU) and an Arm CPU under one numerically validated protocol, we find that correlation trackers are the fast ones, but they lag in accuracy unless they adopt a ViT backbone, which brings attention back. We revisit what correlation lacks. Template--search interaction serves two roles: conditioning the search features on the target and matching them against it spatially. Attention does both, whereas correlation only matches, and does so on features extracted without knowledge of the target. We present TaCo (Target-aligned Correlation), which supplies the missing conditioning without attention by letting the template enter the per-frame network only as operands computed once per video. A descriptor of the target scales and shifts the search features channel by channel inside the backbone, and kernels aligned with the target box, each with a weight predicted from the template, correlate with them in one matrix product. With the backbone fixed, our correlation remains essential while incurring negligible NPU overhead, offering a better speed-accuracy trade-off than the attention-based interactions we tested. TaCo-T achieves 62.3% LaSOT AUC at 184 FPS on the Rockchip RV1126B NPU and 96 FPS on a Raspberry Pi 5 CPU, 3.0x and 3.5x the NPU speed of HiT-Tiny and AsymTrack-T at higher accuracy. TaCo-B reaches 65.6% at 50 FPS on the NPU, more than twice the speed of HiT-Base, AsymTrack-B and LightFC-vit, again at higher accuracy. Code and models are available at https://github.com/TsingWei/TaCo-Tracker.

title: Exact Integration of ReLU-type Neural Networks for Solving PDEs
abstract: Developing robust training methodologies for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with neural networks is crucial for reliable scientific computing. Piecewise-linear activations such as the Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) are a convenient choice in this setting as their structure resembles classical piecewise-linear approximations. However, when the loss functional incorporates the spatial gradient of the network, as in the Deep Ritz method, numerical integration becomes problematic. Specifically, relying on standard integration techniques (e.g., Monte Carlo sampling) during training yields incorrect gradients, even as the number of integration points approaches infinity, leading to optimization failure. To overcome this limitation, we present an integration framework for single-hidden-layer ReLU networks that computes correct gradients when using Deep Ritz for PDEs or PINNs for first-order problems. Our approach employs the Sutherland-Hodgman algorithm to partition the physical domain into subdomains according to breaking hyperplanes underlying the ReLU network. By finding these hyperplanes exactly, our method can correctly integrate the gradients, ensuring the optimizer receives correct information. In this work, we further assemble the energy in matrix--vector form that allows all neuron interactions to be computed efficiently with vectorized operations, introduce an alternative approach termed Conforming Monte Carlo that is a stochastic version of the proposed method, and propose two stochastic training strategies to reduce complexity. Numerical results on two-dimensional domains demonstrate that our framework recovers optimal PDE solutions that standard stochastic sampling and other existing quadrature methods fail to capture.

title: On canonical projections of the bipartite graph $D(k,q)$
abstract: The bipartite graphs $D(k,q)$, constructed by Lazebnik et al. in 1995, are $q$-regular, edge-transitive, and of large girth. In this paper, we primarily instigate the canonical projections of $D(k,q)$. First, as a generalization of $D(k,q)$, we define a bipartite graph $Γ(Ω,q)$, where $Ω$, referred to as a rooted binary tree, is a finite subset of binary sequences closed under the deletion of any suffix. We then derive several significant properties regarding the symmetry, connectivity and girth of $Γ(Ω,q)$. For arbitrary nonnegative integers $m$ and $n$, we fully characterize the connected components of $Γ(Ω_{m,n},q)$, which is isomorphic to a canonical projection of $D(k,q)$ with $k\geq 2m+2$. Our results demonstrate that the connected components of $\{Γ(Ω_{m,n},q)\}_{2\leq |m-n|\leq 3}$ form a novel family of graphs with large girth in the sense of Biggs.

title: Mathematical modeling of regime-dependent thermal response in multilayer wall assemblies with equal total steady thermal resistance
abstract: Steady thermal resistance is a fundamental characteristic of building-envelope assemblies; however, equal steady resistance does not uniquely determine their transient thermal behavior. This study aims to numerically separate the effects of layer order, temperature-dependent thermophysical properties, and redistribution of thermal resistance between bulk and interfacial components in stationarily equivalent multilayer wall assemblies subjected to periodic and finite-pulse thermal loading. A one-dimensional transient heat-conduction model with Robin boundary conditions, finite interfacial thermal resistance, and source-supported temperature-dependent material properties was employed. All compared configurations were constrained to the same total steady thermal resistance at the reference temperature, $R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 3.65315$ m$^2$ K/W. The numerical implementation passed the adopted verification procedure with restrictions. The combined grid/time uncertainty was 0.325 %, below the prescribed 0.5 % acceptance criterion. For the tested pair differing only in layer order, the relative effect was -0.905 % for the periodic decrement factor and +0.566 % for the finite-pulse peak transmission ratio, with effect-to-uncertainty ratios of 79.2 and 88.9, respectively; the opposite signs therefore refer to two distinct regime-specific metrics. The temperature-dependent configuration produced a numerically resolved periodic effect of -2.005 %, whereas the corresponding pulse effect of -0.282 % remained below the adopted numerical-resolution threshold. For a compensated 5-10 % redistribution of bulk thermal resistance to interfacial contacts, the additional dynamic effect was likewise unresolved. The results demonstrate the value of controlled factor separation combined with explicit numerical-uncertainty assessment when evaluating transient thermal behavior.

title: Feature Engineered Reinforcement Learning for S-pair Selection in Buchberger's Algorithm
abstract: Selecting the order in which to process S-pairs is a crucial decision in Buchberger's algorithm for computing Groebner bases: this choice can change the cost by orders of magnitude. Recent work has shown that reinforcement learning agents viewing exponent vectors of the polynomials outperform classical heuristics on binomial ideals. We extend this line of work to general polynomial ideals by using statistical features. We introduce a 17-dimensional feature vector to describe a polynomial and use PPO to train policies on five distributions of random ideals. We find that using S-polynomial features significantly outperforms S-pair features on all five distributions. The new policies also outperform the retrained RL baseline on all five distributions, reducing algorithmic work by 41--53\% relative to the degree heuristic on four distributions where learning helps. The additional cost of the feature engineering means that wall-clock cost remains similar to the baseline, but our new approach benefits from easier transfer to unseen distributions.

title: Concavity of cardinality-constrained interval stabbing and interval cover problems
abstract: We consider the cardinality-constrained interval stabbing problem, in which the goal is to maximize the total weight of intervals hit by at least one of at most $k$ selected points. Although this problem does not admit a simple greedy solution, we show that its optimal value is a concave function of $k$. We establish this result using a linear programming formulation whose relaxation always admits an optimal solution with integer values. This allows us to prove concavity for the original problem. We further extend the result to the related interval cover problem. These concavity properties provide a basis for applying Lagrangian optimization using algorithms for the corresponding unconstrained problems.

title: Disciplined Anthropomorphism: How to Extend Cognitive Language to Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Researchers increasingly describe AI in cognitive terms such as "understanding" and "believing", while critics denounce this as wishful anthropomorphism. Both sides align in taking a subsumptive approach, however: they ask whether AI systems fall under concepts minted for human beings, reporting verdicts as discoveries about those systems when they are largely determined by conceptual frames. Yet the problem AI poses is precisely the problem of how to conceptually frame these systems, and the explosive rise of anthropomorphism is best seen as a response to this problem that needs disciplining rather than discouragement. A disciplined anthropomorphism, I argue, should disentangle the inferential connections bundled up in our cognitive concepts and ask which connections to preserve, sever, or forge for AI. The disciplining then comes, on the one hand, from the human conceptual needs that give point to the drawing of these connections and motivate the concepts' extension in the first place; and, on the other hand, from empirical and especially mechanistic evidence that supports and constrains these connections. By reverse-engineering a concept's point in relation to a particular need before re-engineering it to better serve that point in our dealings with AI, anthropomorphizing extensions can be point-based, transposing the work those concepts do for us while revising the inferential workings through which they do it. Transposing human-tailored conceptions of understanding and belief on the pivot of the underlying conceptual needs gives us just the definitional freedom required to accommodate how AI systems differ from us, yielding conceptions that are not just thinned-out versions of existing ones, but potentially richer and better fitted to the peculiarities of AI.

title: From Diagnosing Alignment to Joint Supervision in Multimodal Draft Training
abstract: Multimodal drafts learn from multimodal (MM) and text-only (TXT) supervision, yet their effects on alignment and how to combine them remain unclear. We diagnose draft-target alignment through paired predictions with and without visual input, decomposing distributional error into text-conditioned and visual-response components. Drafts with similar text-conditioned alignment can still differ markedly in visual-response risk and acceptance. Controlled continuation training shows that high-risk groups outperform random and low-risk groups, and visual-response risk guides MM training more effectively than aggregate risk. Building on these diagnostics, we propose MNRS-Joint, which configures joint supervision from a given draft's component-risk distributions, using modality-specific mean risks to determine the MM:TXT mixture. Across three warm-ups, its distinct mixtures fall in high-performing regions of the ratio sweeps. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, MNRS-Joint improves mean accepted length from 3.35 to 3.53 and mean speedup from $2.04\times$ to $2.16\times$ over composition-matched random training under greedy tree decoding. The gains also hold under stochastic chain decoding.

title: Improving Tail-Augmented Speculative Drafting with Hidden State Mixing and Gradient Detach
abstract: Multi-token prediction (MTP) modules and EAGLE-style drafters support efficient speculative decoding by reusing target-model hidden states. Their autoregressive use, however, introduces a training-inference mismatch: training supplies sequences of hidden states from the backbone or a single MTP step, whereas inference attends to a target-model prefix followed by a growing tail of recurrently generated MTP states. EAGLE-3's training-time test (TTT) explicitly simulates this behavior during training, at the cost of additional memory and specialized attention masks. We introduce two training-only methods for improving autoregressive drafting. Hidden State Mixing (HSM) samples among backbone and MTP hidden states aligned to the same prediction target, exposing the drafter to mixtures of states from different MTP steps without explicitly simulating inference. Hidden State Gradient Detach (HSGD) is a regularization method that stochastically blocks gradients through hidden state and embedding pathways while preserving the forward computation. Neither method adds inference cost. In joint pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning, HSGD yields the highest acceptance rates at early draft positions, while HSM performs best later in the draft. These acceptance rate trends favor HSM for long-draft-length serving and HSGD for short-draft-length serving. Furthermore, across four Nemotron models and DeepSeek-V4-Pro, HSM-based MTP boosting with a frozen backbone improves mean acceptance length by up to 52.2% over the co-trained MTP. For EAGLE-3 drafters, HSM offers competitive acceptance with TTT, with 48% lower peak reserved training memory in a four-step Qwen3-8B comparison. HSM implementations are publicly available in Megatron-LM and NVIDIA Model Optimizer.

title: Exploring the Design Factors of Pixel-space Diffusion
abstract: In this paper, we introduce EiT by exploring the key design factors of pixel-space diffusion from three perspectives: model architecture, representation, and frequency domain. Inspired by Denoising Autoencoders (DAE) which perform denoising through a bottleneck, we construct a U-shaped pixel diffusion transformer that performs explicit compression along the channel dimension. In terms of representation, we find that both pixel and latent diffusion transformers exhibit a three-stage representation dynamics across layers and timesteps: denoising/local feature expansion, basis lift-up, and posterior projection. Moreover, earlier denoising and a longer basis lift-up stage are associated with better generation, which EiT naturally achieves through its channel bottleneck and increased network depth. From the frequency perspective, we establish the equivalence between pixel-space and frequency-space diffusion when keeping the network operating in pixel space. On ImageNet $256\times256$ and $512\times512$, EiT consistently outperforms JiT (Just image Transformers) in generation quality. Specifically, our EiT achieves better FID than JiT: 1.61 vs. 1.85 at $256\times256$, and 1.73 vs. 1.99 at $512\times512$. Remarkably, EiT can be seamlessly applied to video pixel diffusion by simply extending the patch size to temporal dimension and outperforms video latent diffusion in FVD evaluated on Kinetics-600 (resolution 256), under comparable total network parameters. Code is available at https://github.com/forever208/EiT

title: Silent on Code? A Computing Lens on Generative AI Guidance at Canadian Polytechnics and Research Universities
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools now write, explain, and debug code, which changes how computing students learn and how their work is assessed. Instructors, however, act within institutional guidance written largely with essays in mind. We report a document analysis of the public, institution-level GenAI guidance of the 13 members of Polytechnics Canada and the 15 members of the U15 Group of Canadian Research Universities, retrieved in October 2026. Using a 27-item codebook spanning governance, integrity and assessment, data and legal issues, values, AI literacy, and a computing lens, we find that both sectors leave course-level decisions to instructors, although polytechnics more often prohibit use unless the instructor permits it (8 of 13 vs. 4 of 14), and converge on disclosure, links to academic integrity policy, and, in most institutions, the expectation that programs adapt rules to their discipline. Polytechnics frame GenAI as workforce preparation substantively far more often (7 of 13 vs. 0 of 14), whereas universities more often address assessment redesign. Twelve of 27 institutions with retrievable guidance mention code, but almost always as one output type among many; none names an AI coding assistant or provides substantive code-specific guidance on attribution, assessment, or licensing. Institution-level guidance is thus not silent on code but leaves programming-specific questions largely to programs and instructors. We propose five elements of discipline-level guidance for computing and release our codebook and coded dataset.

title: Random walk on an induced component of the uniform spanning forest
abstract: Let $T$ be the component of the origin in the uniform spanning forest of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, and consider the induced graph $H$ obtained by retaining every lattice edge with both endpoints in $T$. Lyons, Peres and Sun (2020) showed that $H$ is recurrent if $d \ge 8$ and asked for which $d \in \{5,6,7\}$ this holds. We prove that simple random walk on $H$ is transient for $d=5$ and recurrent for every $d\ge6$. We also show that the quenched return probabilities to the origin satisfy $p^H_{2n}(o,o)=n^{-α_d+o(1)}$ a.s., where $α_5=4/3$ and $α_6=1$, while $α_7=4/5$ and $α_d=2/3$ for all $d\ge8$.

title: FoMNet: Adaptive Kernels Meet Contextual Matching for Cross-Modal Homography Estimation
abstract: Cross-modal homography estimation requires reliable correspondences despite appearance differences between sensing modalities. Multi-scale refinement progressively reduces the search range, but its accuracy remains limited by the ability of matching features to distinguish nearby candidates. The vision foundation model (VFM) provides complementary representations, yet integrating these features through fixed interpolation leaves their spatial aggregation independent of image content and the correspondence objective. We propose the Foundation Model-Enhanced Matching Network (FoMNet), which combines learned spatial adaptation of VFM features with contextual correspondence estimation. Patch Feature Upsampling (PFU) progressively predicts location-specific kernels to aggregate neighboring features on upsampled grids, preparing VFM representations for fusion with CNN features at different matching scales. Contextual Correlation Refinement (CCR) then jointly processes source descriptors and local correlations with spatial context to refine candidate scores before each homography update. To reduce upsampling overhead, we develop FoMNet-D, which replaces PFU with bicubic interpolation and uses multi-scale feature-relation distillation to recover accuracy. Experiments on five cross-modal datasets show that FoMNet achieves the lowest mean average corner error (MACE) among the evaluated methods, reducing MACE by 10.6%-72.7% relative to MCNet. FoMNet-D retains competitive accuracy while reducing inference latency by 34.0% relative to FoMNet.

title: Higher derivatives and ghosts through three centuries
abstract: We outline the history of the research of dynamic systems including higher derivatives in the Lagrangian, The story starts in 1744 when Euler published a book where the Euler--Lagrange differential equations for a HD system were first written. The next important landmarks were the papers of Ostrogradsky (1850) and of Pais and Uhlenbeck (1950). Many articles written in the second half of the last century were influenced by a misconception that was widespread at the time --- it was believed that higher derivatives necessarily bring about a violation of unitarity. We understand today that this is not the case and there are many systems with benign ghosts where HD are present but unitarity is not violated. In this review, we present and discuss several examples of such (quantum) mechanical systems and 2D field theories. Then we will briefly discuss higher-derivative gravity theories in 4 dimensions. In that case, the question whether the ghosts there are benign or not has a special status due to the absence of a nonperturbative Hamiltonian and does not have a definite answer yet. However, if one restricts oneself to classical theory, one can argue that the ghosts {\it are} benign (benign classical ghostly system is a system that needs an infinite time to reach a singularity, and it seems to the case both in ordinary and in HD gravity: the cosmic censorship conjecture implies that the singularities are always surrounded by horizons, and it takes an infinite time on the clocks of a distant observer to reach a horizon). Finally, I discuss supersymmetric HD theories: conformal supergravity, where the ghosts are also probably benign, and then an interesting supersymmetric HD gauge theory in 6 dimensions. It involves a dimensionless coupling constant, is renormalizable and rather beautiful. Unfortunately, it is not unitary --- ghosts are not benign there.

title: Whose Side Are You On? A Framework and Benchmark for Assessing LLM Political Stances through Politicians Social Media Posts
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly participate in political discussions, making it important to understand which positions they support or oppose. We propose a framework for assessing LLMs' political stances through simulated social media interactions. The framework uses politicians' posts and multiple prompting methods to identify consistently expressed stances. Using this framework, we construct WorldPOLL, comprising 4,600 political posts from X/Twitter collected from approximately 200 politicians representing ruling and opposition blocs across 23 countries. Our quantitative analysis shows how support and opposition vary across models, countries, and political directions, while our qualitative analysis identifies the political views and policies models support or oppose. Together, these analyses reveal shared positions across models and differences across national contexts. We also examine whether models express consistent stances across prompting methods, investigate the reasons for disagreement, and assess the effects of model size and instruction tuning in stance inconsistency. WorldPOLL offers a practical way to measure LLM political tendencies, identify the views behind them, and assess their consistency in real-world political discussions.

title: Will AI Replace Juniors? How Task Complexity Reduces Automation Risk
abstract: How does task complexity shape firms' willingness to substitute entry-level labour with artificial intelligence (AI) tools? We study this question using a pre-registered survey experiment with managers from 1,435 German firms in the information economy and manufacturing industry. Managers are randomly assigned to consider a long lasting need for additional capacity involving either well-structured and standardised tasks, or more complex tasks that require professional judgement, contextual knowledge and independent problem-solving. Relative to standardised tasks, complex tasks reduce willingness to use AI rather than hire an entry-level employee by 0.54 points on a five-point scale and increase the importance attached to human oversight by 0.15 points. Further, pre-treatment responses indicate that managers expect the availability of AI applications to reduce hiring of both entry-level employees and experienced workers, but significantly more strongly for entry-level workers.

title: When Position Favors the Wrong Part: Evaluating Left-Right Discrimination in Semantic Correspondence
abstract: Overall part-discrimination accuracy can conceal failures when image position favors the wrong bilateral part. We examine whether dense descriptors distinguish the correct part under this conflict and whether their discrimination scores help select matching coordinates. We evaluate position agreement and conflict within the same target images and annotated part pairs, using a bounding-box-side score to define the conditions. We compare the original descriptors with their even and odd components under horizontal reflection, examine feature upsampling with the backbone and adapters fixed, and test candidate-selection rules based on odd scores. On SPair-71k, odd discrimination accuracy falls from 86.66% under agreement to 19.63% under conflict for frozen DINOv2, compared with 95.27% to 86.16% for MARCO. With MARCO's input geometry fixed, odd accuracy in box-side conflict was 34.12% on the native grid and 88.84% after learned upsampling and pooling back to that grid. Odd-score rules improve on the original hard-peak matchers overall for DINOv2 and DINOv3 and on conflict queries for MARCO. With MARCO's soft decoder fixed, reranking the cosine peaks changes mean per-pair PCK by +0.47 pp. For supervised GeoAware-SC, using the odd score to select the localization window center yields only 15 net additional correct matches, with 330 corrections and 315 introduced errors. Evaluating discrimination under position conflict reveals failures hidden by aggregate accuracy. Reporting corrections and introduced errors separately also shows whether a discriminative score produces useful matching decisions.

title: AlignPre: Skill-Aligned Post-Training for Latent-Free Generative Precipitation Nowcasting
abstract: Precipitation nowcasting requires accurate short-term predictions under rapidly evolving spatiotemporal dynamics. Generative diffusion models can produce detailed and competitive radar forecasts by modeling conditional distributions. However, most existing approaches rely on separately trained components, such as deterministic branches or latent compression modules. More fundamentally, distribution matching alone fails to explicitly optimize operational forecast skill. We propose AlignPre, a streamlined pixel-space nowcasting framework that bridges this gap via skill-aligned post-training (SAPT). AlignPre employs an end-to-end flow-matching forecaster with a hierarchical spatiotemporal architecture for distribution matching and direct radar-field synthesis, without latent compression. During post-training, SAPT exploits the analytic structure of forecast verification scores to construct a differentiable objective. By backpropagating gradients of this objective from radar fields to the generator, SAPT turns forecast verification into direct training feedback. Across three real-world benchmarks spanning different forecast horizons, AlignPre consistently surpasses state-of-the-art deterministic and generative baselines in forecast skill, demonstrating that aligning generative modeling with domain-specific verification provides an effective paradigm for meteorological forecasting.

title: Proceedings of "Accelerating ALICE background simulations: A WGAN Approach to slow-neutron induced TPC loopers" CHEP 2026, 26/05/2026
authors: Andreas Morsch for the ALICE Collaboration
abstract: The simulation of background processes in high-energy physics can be computationally expensive and time-consuming. To provide the most realistic data description at the ALICE experiment using Monte Carlo simulations, we investigated alternative solutions to generate the products of electromagnetic interactions initiated by slow neutrons in the Time Projection Chamber (TPC). Specifically, electrons and positrons from these processes can spiral repeatedly within the magnetic field in the detector (so-called "loopers") and tracking them via full transport frameworks, such as GEANT4, requires extensive computing resources. A fast simulation framework based on a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN) was developed to speed up the simulation process. Our solution is designed to bypass the significant computational cost associated with transporting neutrons to low energies by directly generating the kinematic properties (e.g., momentum, production vertex) of the resulting electron-positron pairs (from neutron capture) and electrons from Compton scattering. The generative model successfully reproduces the complex multidimensional distributions of the background tracks with high fidelity, maintaining agreement with the full GEANT4 simulation. By replacing the full transport of these specific background components with the WGAN inference, a tenfold speedup is achieved, making the simulation of loopers a negligible component of the total processing time. Moreover, the fast simulation framework is modular, allowing for the future inclusion of other background sources, such as nuclear spallation products.

title: From Limit Theorems to Mixing Limit Theorems
abstract: Following the work of Gouëzel, we give an alternative proof, under weaker assumptions, of a result of Arana-Herrera and Forni, which provides a general method for upgrading limit theorems for cocycles over dynamical systems to mixing limit theorems.

title: Do Machine Learning Ensembles Beat Published Quotas? Target Parameterization, Censored Baselines, and Conformal Intervals Under Admissions Reform
abstract: Public admission capacity caps published prior to matriculation are widely used by ministries and institutional analysts as default intake projections in centralized postsecondary clearinghouses. Using an audited 2022 to 2026 Vietnamese undergraduate panel (26,895 program-year records across 309 universities) linked to strictly lagged t-1 occupational vacancy signals, this paper evaluates machine learning, multilevel, and censored econometric estimators against published quotas across 5,385 continuing 2024 programs (five-fold university-grouped cross-validation) and 3,348 matched (2,179 grain-consistent) 2025 programs strictly out of time. Because 62.8% of 2024 programs enroll their exact published quota, unanchored log-growth ensembles degrade accuracy, while the worst 5% generate half of total quota error via unfilled "phantom capacity." Controlled target ablations, including a single-factor test under widened non-binding clipping, show that parameterizing the log fill ratio ln(D_it / S_it) instead of log growth reduces 2024 MAE by 21.5% (14.86 to 11.67), aligns ML with Tobit, Cragg, REML HLM, and capped L1 baselines, and lifts combined tuition and institutional-tier TreeSHAP attribution from 2.5% to 45.8%. Hurdle stacking attains the lowest full-census 2024 MAE (H-Hard 11.29; H-Soft 11.32 vs. 12.35, p = 0.022, clearing 10% not 5% FDR; fold-overlap p = 0.134), whereas continuous QA-Stack outperforms H-Soft on mixed-reporting campuses, Tobit (median) ties H-Soft across both 90% MCS sets, and interior-only Cragg-ML lowers RMSE to 28.1. Under Vietnam's 2025 unified-clearing reform, exact filling falls to 10.4%, H-Soft and capped L1 tie quotas (p = 0.979), and 90% cluster-weighted conformal coverage drops from 89.3% to 74.6%. Across 257 reporting campuses, reconciled 2026 national totals (627,114 to 629,256) lie squarely within 604,533 to 662,044.

title: What Makes a Gavagai? Learning Visual Concepts from One Positive and Few Negatives
abstract: Humans can recognize novel concepts from only a few observations by identifying defining visual attributes and eliminating alternative interpretations. However, a single observation is consistent with multiple possible concepts, and accurate visual perception alone is insufficient to determine the intended interpretation. Negative evidence can reduce this ambiguity by eliminating competing hypotheses. Inspired by Quine's gavagai problem, we introduce the Gavagai Benchmark to evaluate whether vision-language models can identify the attributes defining a novel concept from positive and negative examples. The benchmark consists of synthetic images depicting novel combinations of visual attributes and real images of newly described species. Using these datasets, we examine how models use negative examples to identify novel concepts and analyze the respective roles of visual perception and reasoning. Several models struggle even when correct attributes are provided, while others show large gaps when ground-truth attributes are replaced with model predictions. These diagnostic comparisons highlight challenges in both attribute perception and inference from limited evidence.

title: SysBio-SR: Benchmarking Symbolic Regression for Trajectory Fidelity and Mechanism Recovery in Systems Biology
abstract: Symbolic regression seeks to discover interpretable governing equations for dynamical systems from data. In systems biology, however, accurately reproducing system trajectories does not necessarily imply recovery of the underlying reaction mechanisms. Existing benchmarks evaluate numerical accuracy, expression complexity, or equation-level similarity, but not agreement between recovered reactions and reference mechanisms in biological systems. We introduce SysBio-SR, a benchmark of 198 literature-based biological ODE systems with reaction annotations spanning mass action, Michaelis--Menten, Hill, and complex kinetics. Trajectory fidelity is evaluated across all systems under in-distribution reconstruction and out-of-distribution (OOD) extrapolation, while mechanism recovery is assessed on the subset of 161 systems. We evaluate trajectory fidelity across 11 symbolic-discovery methods and assess mechanism recovery for three reaction-based methods. Joint analysis across systems highlights how severely trajectory-based evaluation overestimates true mechanism recovery. Motivated by these findings, we develop KineSelect, a framework that searches candidate reaction topologies under biologically grounded kinetic laws to select optimal mechanisms that balance trajectory fidelity with structural parsimony. Compared with the strongest baseline, KineSelect improves aggregate OOD extrapolation \(R^2\) by 19.2\% and overall reaction F1 score by 14.3\%.

title: Tropical and maximum colorful matchings in vertex-colored graphs
abstract: A subgraph of a vertex-colored graph istropical if it contains every color. We study matchings by the number of colors they cover. A matching is maximum colorful if no matching covers more colors. When a tropical matching exists, the maximum colorful matchings are exactly the tropical matchings. We give polynomial-time algorithms for two problems: a maximum matching that covers the most colors, and a tropical matching with the fewest edges. Both algorithms rest on a counterpart of Berge's theorem: a matching is optimal if and only if it admits no tropical augmentation, or no tropical reduction. These are chains of alternating paths linked by relays, and each one is found by a single augmenting-path search in an auxiliary graph. The same tools give a maximum colorful matching with the fewest edges, and show that all maximum matchings that are maximum colorful are connected by flips. Finally, the sets of colors that a matching can cover form a matroid. The greedy algorithm then computes a matching of maximum color weight. This paper extends the conference version and the PhD thesis of one of the authors.

title: Detectable by Design: Learning a Continuous 3D Saliency Field from 2D Detector Responses
abstract: The 3D points kept in a map decide whether a camera can be localized against it, and this choice matters more as the map becomes sparser. Existing 3D keypoint detectors usually define saliency by semantics, repeatability, reconstruction or descriptor matchability. None of these definitions asks whether a point will actually be detected in an image, and as a result most of the points they select are not detected again in images. In this paper, we define 3D saliency as image detectability: the response of a 2D interest-point detector at a surface point, aggregated over all views in which the point is visible. We propose DetField, a continuous field over 3D space that takes a point cloud as input and predicts detectability at any location around it. The supervision is the response of a 2D detector, back-projected from images onto the point cloud. Multi-scale curvature invariants are passed to the decoder at every query point, bypassing the voxel pooling of the encoder. In a localization benchmark that isolates the choice of 3D points, DetField outperforms Harris-3D and five learned 3D keypoint methods on objects and on real indoor scenes. On unseen rooms, it improves localization success by 7.4 points over Harris-3D, the strongest baseline. On objects, it also leads under a 2D detector not used in training. On sparse maps, it stays ahead of Harris-3D on both objects and real scenes.

title: A family of forcings with hyperfinite equivalence of generics
abstract: We identify a class of forcings that includes several classical forcings and prove that for all forcings $\mathbb{P}$ in this class the associated equivalence of generics relation $\equiv^{\mathbb{P}}_M$, as defined by Smythe, is a hyperfinite CBER.

title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
abstract: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.

title: Halo spin-axis correlations in IllustrisTNG: Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping, baryonic effects, and redshift-space distortions
abstract: We investigate correlations of halo and stellar spin axes in the TNG300 volume of the IllustrisTNG simulations and compare them with a model based on linear tidal torque theory (LTTT). Dark matter (DM) halo spin axes at $z = 0$ exhibit positive correlations as a function of Lagrangian pair separation. The LTTT-based model describes their separation dependence well, with weak variation in the fitted amplitude across mass thresholds. A Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping based on the conditional distributions of initial separations at fixed present-day separation, measured directly from the simulations, allows the model to reproduce the overall trends in both real and redshift space without additional fitting. The hydrodynamic and DM-only runs generally show similar DM halo spin-axis correlations, although the DM-only run exhibits a steeper rise at small real-space separations. In the hydrodynamic run, stellar spin-axis correlations are consistent with the same Lagrangian form as their DM halo counterparts, but with approximately 60% of the DM correlation amplitudes. Positive stellar correlations persist in both real and redshift space, and the mapped model captures their separation dependence. Initial spin-axis correlations of protohalos are substantially stronger than their present-day counterparts at the same Lagrangian separations, consistent with subsequent nonlinear spin evolution weakening these correlations. These results suggest that present-day halo and stellar spin-axis correlations retain signatures of the initial tidal field and that their general behavior can be understood through LTTT-based modeling combined with pair-separation mapping.

title: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration
abstract: Executing monolithic neural weights, frontier foundation models, or entire multi-agent workflows uniformly on every input incurs substantial computational, latency, and monetary overhead. Conditional computation mitigates this cost by deciding dynamically which internal experts, model endpoints, or specialized agents to invoke per request. Yet token-level gating in sparse neural architectures, query-level model cascades, and task-level multi-agent coordination have largely progressed in disconnected research silos, obscuring recurring system failures and transferable fixes. In this systematic review, we synthesize 2,289 studies published between 2017 and September 2026 (selected from 13,884 unique records) across 20 methodological families under a unified two-step inspect-then-allocate framework. Discrete hard selection accounts for 70%, 83%, and 91% of token-, query-, and task-scale literature respectively, and computational overhead appears as a top operational bottleneck across every layer. Engineering safeguards remain sharply asymmetric: intra-layer gating prioritizes load balancing while rarely incorporating uncertainty estimation, whereas model selection and agent orchestration rely on confidence thresholds and budget rules while confronting miscalibration and cascading errors. At the same time, publication volume is accelerating fastest in agentic task delegation, where routing mechanisms are least often isolated experimentally and methodological bias risk is highest.

title: A Robust Optimization Framework for Energy System Capacity Expansion under Line Outage Uncertainty
abstract: Capacity expansion models are widely used in climate and energy policy analysis to find optimal investments in generation, storage, and transmission. As the share of renewable generation grows, these models rely more on transmission lines to balance supply and demand across regions. Transmission lines, however, can fail due to aging, extreme weather, or accidents. Models that represent outages as time-dependent events come mainly from electrical engineering and are applied to small-scale systems, as they quickly become computationally intractable for inter-regional capacity expansion. We develop a capacity expansion model in which the risk of line failures shapes the investments in all parts of the system. We formulate it as a two-stage, scenario-based robust optimization problem that samples time-varying outage scenarios from a Markov model and hedges the investments against the most severe ones. To solve the model, we propose a memory-augmented Benders decomposition algorithm combined with Monte Carlo simulation that can handle thousands of scenarios. The selected plan is then evaluated with an out-of-sample simulation to bound the Value-at-Risk (VaR) of its system cost. In a 25-node case study of Germany and its neighboring countries, the gap between the lower bound and the simulated VaR bound is below 1%. We compare the robust plans with a deterministic plan, which assumes all lines are always available, and with a reserve-margin heuristic, which requires local firm capacity to be above peak demand. Like the heuristic, the robust plans nearly eliminate loss of load in 1000 simulated outage scenarios. Their mean system cost is within 0.2% of the deterministic plan and about 4.5% below the heuristic. Instead of adding more generation capacity, the robust approach mainly changes the type and location of capacity, for example, by spreading storage across the network.

title: Schwinger-Dyson recursion, Gröbner elimination and graph combinatorics
abstract: Schwinger-Dyson equations are a cornerstone of quantum field theory (QFT). Derived using integration by parts, they capture relations between correlators of different orders, forming an open, infinite-dimensional system. In zero-dimensional QFTs with polynomial actions, which is just a physical interpretation for multivariate Gaussian integrals with polynomial insertions, conventional Gröbner elimination can be used to express all higher-order correlators (moments) in terms of a fixed basis set. One consequence is a closed finite-dimensional system of differential equations for the coupling dependence of these `master' correlators. An important application of zero-dimensional QFTs is in counting discrete geometric structures (as in simplicial approaches to quantum gravity). For the problem of counting labelled regular graphs, applying this Schwinger-Dyson closure results in a computational breakthrough relative to the existing state-of-the-art: for 9- and 10-regular graphs on $n$ vertices, a finite-depth, finite-width recursive formulation is obtained, making it possible to compute the total graph counts in $O(n)$ arithmetic operations.

title: A Simple Yet Effective Agent for Open-World Aerial Object Search
abstract: Open-world aerial object search methods often rely on persistent spatial maps, learned world models, or task-specific policy training. To examine how far a minimal, training-free design can go, we introduce SimpleUAV, an agent built around a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM). SimpleUAV separates current-view target assessment from history-conditioned action selection, combining fresh candidate evidence with lightweight search context. Local geometry converts visual selections into bounded straight-line movements, depth-based checks halt blocked segments, and measured execution feedback guides subsequent decisions. This closed loop sustains search without persistent spatial maps or task-specific training. SimpleUAV achieves 41.61% Success Rate (SR) on UAV-ON and 11.98% on AerialDojo-200K, compared with 23.80% and 3.20% for the strongest prior baselines, respectively. With limited benchmark-specific adaptation, the same core agent transfers to aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) on TravelUAV, improving Full SR by at least 19.66% across all three splits under L1 assistance. These results establish a strong baseline for evaluating when additional architectural complexity benefits aerial search.

title: Tunable quantum metric driven nonlinear valley Hall effect in the PT-symmetric sliding antiferroelectric MoS$_2$
abstract: The quantum metric, the real part of a quantum geometric tensor, plays an important role in fundamental transport and optical responses of quantum materials. While net quantum metric effects are typically realized by breaking both time-reversal (T) and inversion (P) symmetries, valley-contrast mechanisms enable the probing of quantum geometry in centrosymmetric, nonmagnetic systems, revealing physical signatures beyond Berry curvature. Here, we design a four-layer MoS$_2$ platform that combines sliding antiferroelectric order with strain-induced $C_{3z}$ breaking to realize a quantum metric driven nonlinear valley Hall effect (NVHE) under preserved P and T symmetries. Reversible interlayer sliding (ABBA $\leftrightarrow$ BAAB) provides nonvolatile electrical control of the valley response. First-principles calculations reveal an outer-layer-dominated NVHE with tunable sign and magnitude. This symmetry-preserving, sliding-tunable strategy activates hidden quantum geometric phenomena in realistic two-dimensional materials and opens a clean pathway for tunable valleytronics and quantum information devices.

title: CoTacWAM: Joint Modeling of Vision and Touch for Robotic Manipulation
abstract: We present CoTacWAM, a world-action model that learns shared contact semantics between wrist vision and touch, achieving the best observed performance in our nominal manipulation and missing-input evaluations. The two modalities observe the same local interaction through different signals: wrist images reveal nearby geometry, while touch records physical contact. Our approach connects their common contact meaning while preserving the evidence unique to each modality, giving the policy a joint description of interaction across available input combinations. This representation supports predictive action learning alongside head-view scene context and conditions corrections after an independent detector confirms a failed attempt. Experiments across four real-world tasks demonstrate improved manipulation performance over the evaluated baselines, robustness to missing local observations, and further gains from autonomous retries.

title: Quantum Metric Connects Bond Delocalization to Phonon Softening
abstract: Delocalized bonding electrons have long been associated with soft bonds and low phonon frequencies. However, a quantitative connection between electron delocalization and phonon softening remains elusive. We identify such a connection through the momentum-space quantum metric, which measures the intrinsic delocalization of the occupied electronic states. We show that a quantum geometric contribution to phonon softening is proportional to the integrated quantum metric. First-principles calculations of more than a hundred compounds demonstrate that greater quantum metric generally accompanies softer phonons. Localized Wannier orbitals reveal the bonding environments associated with this delocalization. In ferroelectric GeTe, LiBeSb, and BaTiO$_3$, polar distortion localizes the bonding orbitals, reduces quantum metric, and stabilizes the soft mode of the nonpolar structure. In PbSe, pressure-induced band inversion is accompanied by an enhanced quantum metric and phonon softening without change in crystal symmetry and bonding. These results establish a common quantum geometric interpretation of bond delocalization and phonon softening across distinct bonding environments.

title: Reconstruction of Poisson Random Measures in the Variational Framework with Applications to Jump-Driven SPDEs
abstract: We establish a reconstruction principle for Poisson random measures arising in compactness arguments for jump-driven stochastic partial differential equations. A basic difficulty in such arguments is that, after a Skorokhod-type representation, almost sure convergence of the solution processes does not by itself identify the limiting stochastic integral, since integration with respect to a compensated Poisson random measure is not a pathwise continuous functional of the solution and the noise. We address this problem in the variational framework of a Gelfand triple $V\hookrightarrow H\equiv H^\ast\hookrightarrow V^\ast$ for equations with locally monotone drift. Starting from a tight sequence of approximating solutions in $D([0,T];H)\cap L^α(0,T;V),$ we construct, on the represented probability space, a time-homogeneous Poisson random measure with the original Lévy intensity and compensator, compatible with the limiting filtration, such that the limiting process solves the corresponding SPDE. The main ingredient is a noise bridge. Together with a shifted dyadic approximation of the solution, the increments of the solution path over dyadic time cells approximate the compensated noise increments; since the time integral of the drift is continuous in $H$, no regularisation of the drift is needed. The jumps are then recovered by a measurable registration procedure, while injectivity of the jump coefficient permits reconstruction of the corresponding marks through a Borel inverse obtained from the Lusin--Suslin theorem.
