The reconstruction is performed simultaneously at all truncation levels; consistency of the resulting finite jump measures and a monotone patching argument yield a Poisson random measure with the full Lévy measure. Under the injectivity assumption, no enlargement of the represented probability space is required.

title: From Data Room to Report: End-to-End AI Support for M&A Legal Due Diligence
abstract: Legal due diligence in mergers and acquisitions requires lawyers to organize heterogeneous virtual data room documents, extract transaction-relevant information and consolidate reviewed findings into a due diligence report. We present LEXI (Legal Extraction and Intelligence), a work-in-progress system that demonstrates how large language models can support this process from document ingestion to report preparation. LEXI classifies documents under a configurable due diligence taxonomy, assigns relevant target entities, extracts predefined information with supporting passages and page-level provenance and prepares report content from reviewed findings. Structured outputs connect these stages and allow model-generated results to be passed through the workflow in a controlled form. Lawyers review and correct classifications and extractions and retain responsibility for legal assessments, recommendations, risk ratings and final report wording. Initial evaluations of the classification and extraction components provide preliminary evidence that the approach is feasible. LEXI illustrates how AI can be integrated across the legal due diligence workflow while preserving lawyer control over substantive legal judgment.

title: Unstable Action Boundaries in Lethal Drone Agents
abstract: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents raise safety risks that are not captured by text-only refusal behavior, especially when tools can trigger high-impact actions. This concern is salient in military settings, where autonomous weapons raise the possibility of delegating force decisions to software agents. In this work, we study whether a drone agent's action boundary is stable under changes to the target descriptor. We evaluate recent and popular LLMs in a simulated perception-action pipeline over real-world drone imagery, where models can localize requested targets and invoke a simulated lethal tool. We find two concerning failure modes. First, some LLM agents invoke the lethal tool for ordinary generic descriptors such as \emph{people}, requiring no jailbreak at all. Second, an agent that initially appears conservative under protected descriptors can become unsafe under a simple semantic target shift.

title: MUSE: Multi-Task Uncertainty-Aware Self-Supervised Encoder for mmWave ISAC
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) allows a wireless system to use the same waveform for communication and environment sensing. At mmWave frequency bands, ISAC enables diverse human sensing tasks, such as localization, gesture recognition, and pose estimation, with high precision. However, each task requires training a dedicated model, typically from scratch on a task-specific dataset, with no mechanism to flag unreliable predictions. This hurts the scalability, transferability, and reliability of mmWave ISAC models. In this work, we propose MUSE (Multi-task Uncertainty-aware Self-supervised Encoder), a unified framework for mmWave human sensing. MUSE leverages a self-supervised transformer model with per-dataset tokenization and is trained via masked autoencoding across five datasets. During fine-tuning, MUSE uses evidential classification heads that enable uncertainty quantification. MUSE replaces N separate encoders with a single shared transformer encoder, an N-times backbone parameter reduction, while achieving a 9.7 percentage points improvement in classification performance compared to the task-specific model, showing that learning jointly across tasks improves per-task generalization. Across four classification tasks, MUSE produces reliable uncertainty estimates that enable selective prediction, improving accuracy by abstaining on the least confident 20% of predictions. We further improve the reliability of the model's confidence estimates using temperature scaling and conformal prediction. Finally, MUSE's uncertainty signal remains reliable even under cross-user deployment, assigning higher uncertainty to wrong predictions than to correct ones 78% of the time, and recovering 9.2 percentage points of accuracy through selective prediction, with no additional retraining on the unseen user.

title: Scaled Coordinate Descent for Convex Quadratic Programs
abstract: We study a modification of coordinate descent for unconstrained symmetric positive definite quadratic programs that combines a coordinate correction with an exact scaling of the current iterate. For a selected coordinate, the method minimizes the objective function over the two-dimensional subspace spanned by the current iterate and the corresponding standard basis vector. Closed-form expressions are obtained for the two update parameters and for the resulting objective decrease. The scaling produces a state-dependent effective curvature that is no larger than the diagonal curvature used by standard coordinate descent, so the exact scaled update makes at least as much progress for the same selected coordinate. We discuss initialization, numerical stability, randomized coordinate selection, experimental comparisons with ordinary two-coordinate descent, and a block coordinate extension. In the spirit of previous theoretical results, we give a probabilistic linear convergence result. Finally, we provide experimental results to show the effectiveness of the proposed method on synthetic data.

title: WAtcher: Watching Ahead for Safe Robotic Manipulation with Efficient World-Action Models
abstract: World-action models (WAMs) couple future imagination with action generation, but they execute every action chunk while ignoring the potential risk. To fill this gap, we present WAtcher, a safety-aware world-action framework in which the policy imagines the outcome of the candidate chunk before execution. For fast future preview, WAtcher builds on a compact WAM whose video expert imagines the visual outcome in only two denoising steps. In addition, we propose Safe-Guard, a lightweight module kept outside the WAM that scores each candidate chunk from its imagined outcome and triggers a bounded retreat when the risk is high. Safe-Guard is detachable and can be applied to other WAMs. To train Safe-Guard, we build an autonomous pipeline to collect hazard data from RoboTwin, LIBERO, and a real robot. Specifically, the pipeline perturbs expert demonstrations and labels each candidate chunk from the physical events recorded when it is executed, such as contacts and losses of support. Using the ~25,000 labeled windows from this pipeline, Safe-Guard reaches 92.1% balanced accuracy on a blind set, and cuts hazardous closed-loop trials on training tasks from 27.0% to 10.8% without lowering task success. On a held-out 300-question benchmark, it scores 94.2%, against 72.5% and 63.3% for zero-shot GPT-6-Astra and Claude Opus 5.5. WAtcher also reaches 90.4% and 82.4% average success on RoboTwin 2.0 and ManiSkill3, on par with or above leading WAMs, and 74.0% on five real-world tasks with Safe-Guard on, against 59.5% for $π_{0.5}$. Project page: https://zyshan0929.github.io/WAtcher

title: Characterization and empirical correction of a spatially coherent spectral artifact in Gemini/GMOS-N IFU observations
abstract: We report a recurring spectral artifact identified in observations obtained with the integral field unit (IFU) of the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrograph on the Gemini North telescope (GMOS-N). The artifact appears as a vertically aligned structure in reconstructed images of the IFU field of view, associated with a specific group of fibers and exhibiting a broad spectral feature around 8000~\AAng. Similar features were repeatedly identified in observations of different astronomical targets obtained between 2020 and 2022 using the R150 grating in the two-slit IFU mode. Taking advantage of the reproducibility of the artifact in the fiber and wavelength domains, we develop an empirical correction method in which the artifact is modeled as the product of a common spectral profile and a fiber-dependent amplitude distribution, with an overall normalization determined independently for each exposure. The artifact template is constructed from observations in which the affected fibers are largely separated from the astronomical source and subsequently applied to independent observations in which the artifact overlaps the source. The correction substantially suppresses the artificial spatial structure in the reconstructed images. Although the physical origin of the artifact remains unidentified, we present its observational characteristics and correction procedure to facilitate the identification and treatment of similar features by other GMOS-IFU users.

title: Out of Sight, Not Out of Clues: Can Video LLMs Guess from Partial Evidence?
abstract: In real-world applications like egocentric recording, visual accessibility, and surveillance review, visual evidence for Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) is often only partially captured. A reliable model should match its response to the evidence: answering when sufficient, guessing from visible clues when partial, and abstaining when absent. Yet existing benchmarks enforce a binary answerable-or-unanswerable split, leaving partial evidence unmeasured and obscuring whether failures arise from missing evidence or misjudging sufficiency. We introduce ClueProbe, a diagnostic benchmark to (1) separate perceiving evidence from judging sufficiency, and (2) validate our diagnosis via targeted fine-tuning. ClueProbe comprises 1,721 human-annotated questions across 598 natural videos, labeled Answerable, Guessable, or Unanswerable, alongside controlled perturbations altering wording or visual input. Evaluating 10 open-source and proprietary Video LLMs reveals that failures stem from judgment rather than perception: models perceive the evidence yet lack graded sufficiency awareness, answering or refusing outright while rarely guessing from partial clues. Targeted fine-tuning shows that this reflects missing supervision rather than insufficient capacity: supervising the guess level lifts appropriate guessing from 1.6% to 40.4% without extra false refusals, whereas conventional refusal tuning rejects 92% of guessable questions. Data and code will be released at https://github.com/suat-llm/ClueProbe.

title: An oxygen-rich supernova remnant in NGC 253 with narrow [N II] emission lines
abstract: Context. Supernova remnants (SNRs) are the final evolutionary stage of supernovae. In rare cases, the remnant persists as an optically luminous remnant decades after the explosion. We report the discovery of an unusual oxygen-rich (O-rich) SNR that was serendipitously discovered in the MUSE mosaic of the nearby (D $\sim$ 3.5 Mpc) galaxy NGC 253 released by arXiv:2506.14921. Aims. We search for SNRs in MUSE integral field spectroscopy data of NGC 253. Methods. We search for unresolved point sources with broad and strong [O III]$λ$$λ$4959,5007, [O I]$λ$$λ$6300,6364 or [O II]$λ$$λ$7320,7331 emission lines. We also search for possible counterparts at other wavelengths in archival data. Results. We find a single O-rich SNR in NGC 253 with [O III]$λ$$λ$4959,5007. For this object, we report a coincident X-ray source detected by Chandra and a non-detection at mid-infrared wavelengths by JWST. Additionally, we identify [N II]$λ$$λ$6548,6583 emission lines and no detectable hydrogen or [SII]$λ$$λ$6716,6731 emission. The [N II] emission lines are broader (230 km/s) than the surrounding interstellar medium lines but still narrow in comparison to the [O III] emission (>1500 km/s) from the SNR. No detections of [O I]$λ$$λ$6300,6364 and [O II]$λ$$λ$7320,7331 were made. Conclusions. The discovery of a single O-rich SNR after a systematic search of NGC 253 highlights their scarcity in nearby galaxies. The structure of [O III] emission indicates complex structure in the O-rich ejecta. The relative narrowness of [N II] emission lines compared to the [O III] lines and the non-detection of hydrogen show that the remnant is surrounded by an N-rich circumstellar medium. The ejecta is currently interacting with this material of the preceding supernova explosion.

title: FoundSurface: Feedforward Ray-Based 3D Scene Surface Reconstruction from Unposed Images
abstract: Accurate 3D surface reconstruction from unposed images remains a fundamental challenge in computer vision. Recent feed-forward pointmap methods eliminate the need for camera poses but inherently produce discrete, sparse representations. In this paper, we present a generalizable pipeline that directly recovers continuous, high-fidelity 3D surfaces from unposed images by seamlessly integrating pointmap- and ray-based representations. Our approach first extracts explicit geometric priors using a pre-trained pointmap model. A query-view-centric selection module then identifies geometrically relevant reference views via a robust surfel voting mechanism. Next, a cross-attention regressor bridges target query rays with reference features to estimate a continuous coarse surface. Lastly, a raylet-based module aggregates local 3D features to carve out high-frequency details and analytical normals. Trained as a single foundation model on 9 diverse datasets, our method demonstrates exceptional zero-shot generalization on 6 unseen datasets, clearly surpassing state-of-the-art baselines in geometric accuracy and detail preservation.

title: Reconstructing massive quivers on a defect circle
abstract: We study the kink and particle spectra for the massive $ϕ_{2,1}$-deformations of minimal models $\mathcal M_{k+1,k+2}$ via truncated conformal space approach (TCSA) on a defect circle. The massive $ϕ_{2,1}$-deformation preserves a set of non-invertible symmetries, furnishing a fusion category $\mathcal C_k\simeq {\rm SO}(3)_k$. These non-invertible symmetries are spontaneously broken, and thus label the vacua and organize the kinks and particles into their multiplets in terms of quiver diagrams. We employ a finite-volume truncated Hamiltonian approach on defect Hilbert spaces, $\mathcal H_{X_i}$ for $X_i\in\mathcal C_k$, to study these quivers in the IR theories. The symmetry defect can then close an individual kink on a circle. We first establish the relation between states of definite fractional momentum on the defect circle and physical kink and particle states labelled by their vacuum pairs. Using form factors of local fields, we independently measure the squared amplitudes between the states of the two bases in defect TCSA. Combining these measurements with defect TCSA spectra, we reconstruct the quiver diagrams for $k=3,4,5$ without assuming them in advance. In particular, for $k=4$ we reconstruct the distinct quivers of the ordered and disordered phases. For $k=5$, we identify the quivers of both the light and heavy multiplets.

title: WorldPhy: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Physical Plausibility of World Models in Robotics
abstract: World models are increasingly used in robotics to improve the performance of embodied models. Compared with general-purpose video generation, robotics places more stringent requirements on world models. Generated videos must satisfy fine-grained physical constraints on robot motion and object interactions. However, existing world model benchmarks can overlook robotics specific physical details and struggle to assess them accurately. To address this problem, we introduce WorldPhy, a world model benchmark for accurate, fine-grained evaluation of physical plausibility in robotics. Our benchmark contains 300 tasks, each consisting of an initial-frame image and a task instruction, covering diverse robotics scenes, task categories, viewpoints, and robot configurations. We further collect over 12K high-quality human annotations, and use them to train WorldPhyReward to accurately provide scores and reasons across six fine-grained physical dimensions and an instruction-following dimension. Comparisons with general VLMs and existing reward models show that WorldPhyReward better aligns with human ratings. We system- atically evaluate 13 frontier open and closed-source world models. The results reveal that current world models struggle to consistently maintain fine-grained physical plausibility across different robotics scenarios. Our code is available at https://github.com/chuziyuan139/ WorldPhy.

title: Is Sara Omar the true author of Dødevaskeren (The Dead Washer)? Authorship attribution in Danish literature
abstract: The bestseller Dødevaskeren (The Dead Washer) was published in 2017 under the name Sara Omar. A Danish colleague has suggested that the novel may have been written by another author, possibly Mads Peder Nordbo. To investigate this authorship question, four authorship attribution methods were applied, namely Delta, intertextual distance, Nearest Shrunken Centroids (NSC), and naïve Bayes. Using various parameter settings, these approaches consistently identify Nordbo's writing style in the doubtful novel, although the results do not provide conclusive evidence that he authored the novel in its entirety. In a second step, the novel was divided into non-overlapping segments of 5,000 tokens. Once again, Nordbo's style was identified in the majority of the segments. However, a small number of passages do not clearly support this conclusion and instead suggest the possible involvement of another, as yet unidentified, author, possibly Sara Omar herself.

title: Agent-as-a-Verifier: From Scores to Evidence for General Verification
abstract: Verification is increasingly critical across various inference and learning paradigms, such as test-time scaling, recursive intelligence and automated research, where feedback can improve efficiency and optimization. Common score-based verifiers, or discriminative reward models, predict a scalar reward for an output. While useful for filtering, rewarding, and ranking, such scores provide no explicit, auditable evidentiary basis for the judgment. In parallel, although existing generative process reward models offer text feedback, most designs do not fully exploit agentic capabilities, such as tool use and iterative reasoning, which are essential for fact-checking and fine-grained claim verification. In this paper, we address these limitations by introducing Agent-as-a-Verifier, an agentic, certificate-producing verification system that places role-separated LLM agents inside a formal-methods-inspired claim-obligation-certificate protocol. Given a generation candidate, Agent-as-a-Verifier produces a certificate by extracting a verdict-blind dependency graph of claims, independently compiling the task's acceptance contract, and deriving checkable obligations. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, Agent-as-a-Verifier achieves higher accuracy than the state-of-the-art approach. Across different downstream applications, the augmented agent also outperforms the plain agent on FrontierMath and CyberGym. More importantly, Agent-as-a-Verifier is able to identify reward-hacking solutions that deceive the benchmark evaluator, highlighting its broader potential for iterative and recursive agent optimization. Code is available at https://github.com/sunyxedu/General-Verifier

title: Somatic Alignment: Scaffolding Non-Visible Inner Body Sensations in and beyond Vocal Pedagogy
abstract: Inner bodily sensations inform expressive musical performance but can be difficult to interpret and communicate. Through two separate workshops with five singing learners and four senior voice teachers, we investigate breath control in vocal pedagogy. Participants reported difficulty interpreting bodily sensations (Opacity of Inner Sensations) and translating awareness into intended adjustments (Disconnected Regulation of Inner Sensations), alongside strategies involving touch, demonstration, and imagery. Building on these accounts, we propose the Somatic Alignment Model (SAM), connecting an Intrapersonal Self-Sensing Loop with an Intercorporeal Co-Sensing Loop. SAM examines how external guidance relates to learners' bodily calibration and how interpretive and regulatory authority is negotiated. We articulate three generative design dimensions, Modality, Agency, and Temporality, and illustrate their possible applications in interactive learning systems and first-person soma design inquiries. SAM offers a conceptual lens for supporting bodily awareness and regulation through interaction design.

title: A Calibration-Referenced Protocol for Measuring Decision Stability under Reference Bank Compression
abstract: Reference banks used for industrial image inspection can be compressed to fit a deployment budget, but the resulting anomaly decisions depend on both the compressed scores and the operating threshold. We present a four-step protocol that compares compression methods at matched deployment sizes, establishes a reference distribution from 200 recalibrations, evaluates disagreement against two calibration benchmarks, and measures changes by distance from the full-bank threshold. With WideResNet-50, budget-matched product quantization (PQ) at the 10% budget has the lowest decision disagreement among five matched methods, including int8 scalar quantization, on VisA and MVTec AD at both operating levels. Int8 scalar quantization gives lower disagreement than PQ at the other four budgets. On MVTec AD at the lower operating level, PQ meets the calibration median in 34/39 cells and the upper quantile in 39/39 cells. Category-equally weighted image-level AUROC loss at this budget ranges from 0.0003 to 0.0037 across the evaluated configurations. On VisA at the 1% budget and a 1% operating level, disagreement reaches 28.12% (95% CI 23.25--33.58%) among near-threshold anomalies and 1.30% (0.79--2.14%) across the normal holdout. The 10% budget-matched PQ setting retains the lowest disagreement among four compared methods with ResNet-18, with clean reference banks, and when thresholds are estimated from normal-directory probes. The protocol connects deployment size to a calibration-referenced decision measure and identifies the evaluation populations most informative for inspection.

title: Real-Time Cryo-CMOS Photon-Number Readout from a Single SNSPD
abstract: Measurements leveraging the intrinsic photon-number resolution of Superconducting Nanostrip Single-Photon Detectors (SNSPDs) have recently gained traction due to the simplicity of the detector design. Intrinsic photon-number measurement schemes using SNSPDs encode the photon-number information in picosecond signal timing; these systems thus require high bandwidth readout and sensitive electrical measurement equipment. We show a cryogenic electronic circuit operating close to the SNSPD in the cryostat, which can isolate single-photon detection events directly from the SNSPD signal. This reduces the latency of the photon-number readout to (13.9 $\pm$ 0.3) ns, which enables feedforward operations based on intrinsic photon-number measurements with low latency.

title: SOC-Net: Second-Order-Cone-Constrained Neural Networks
abstract: In many applications, neural networks must learn input-output maps that respect prior knowledge such as physical laws, safety requirements, and operating limits. These requirements constrain which outputs are admissible for a given input and often admit second-order cone (SOC) representations, including norm bounds and robust linear inequalities. Examples in control include friction cones, thrust bounds, and input-robust control barrier function (CBF) conditions. However, existing approaches to enforcing general input-dependent SOC constraints require a conic solver, an iterative scheme whose feasibility depends on convergence, or an interior feasible point for each input. We propose SOC-Net, a neural network architecture that enforces input-dependent SOC constraints by construction for every input, even outside the training distribution. SOC-Net projects an affine lifting of the backbone output onto the reachable slice of a fixed product of Lorentz cones and maps the correction back to the output space. For separable constraints, this projection splits into one projection per cone, and each is available in closed form or reduces to a single scalar equation, regardless of the cone dimension. We prove that SOC-Net retains the expressive power of the backbone network under regularity conditions and accommodates end-to-end training by standard backpropagation with an explicit Jacobian. Experiments on contact force allocation with friction constraints and 3-D obstacle avoidance with an input-robust CBF demonstrate that SOC-Net satisfies the constraints at every evaluated input, with lower evaluation latency than the tested solver-based and iterative baselines.

title: How resampling method can help us: Improving the Delta model
abstract: Delta has been successfully employed as an authorship attribution method in various contexts, although its effectiveness is not always perfect. Since it is based on the most frequent words, its results can be readily interpreted and explained in plain English. In this study, we propose improving its performance by applying a resampling method to the selected stylistic features. The results show that this approach increases the accuracy of the model while preserving the interpretability of its outcomes. However, the main drawback of the proposed technique is the additional computational time required to obtain more accurate results.

title: On the Hardness of Optimal CNOT Circuits
abstract: This note revisits the computational problem of optimal CNOT synthesis: given an invertible binary matrix $A\in \mathsf{GL}(d,2)$ over the field of two elements and a budget $K$, decide if $A$ can be implemented with $\leq K$ CNOT gates. The $\mathsf{NP}$-completeness of this problem was recently published independently by Acuaviva, Acuaviva, and Acuaviva (arXiv:2608.03825) and by Li and Guan (arXiv:2609.04160). This note gives a new proof, with three features. First, $\mathsf{NP}$-completeness holds even over linear oracles, i.e., matrices of the form $(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})\mapsto(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}+F\mathbf{x})$, which are the standard reversible embedding of a linear function $F$. These are involutions, and seemingly simpler than the families of the two previous works, which both have order four. Second, hardness persists when SWAP gates are free and qubits may be permuted (and this holds under any connected topology). Third, the exposition is arguably simpler to follow. Along the way, it gives a proof of the XOR-circuit lower bound of Boyar, Matthews, and Peralta [J. Cryptology 26 (2013)] that is, perhaps, simpler than existing ones.

title: An Image Detectability Field as a Viewpoint Utility for 2D-3D Localization in Sparse Maps
abstract: In 2D-3D localization, a camera estimates its pose by matching an image to a 3D map. A camera held in a hand or mounted on a robot can often choose its viewpoint before it takes the image. In this work, we ask whether an image detectability field is a useful viewpoint utility when the planner reads only the geometry of the map. The field can be queried at any 3D point near a surface. From the local geometry around the point, it predicts how likely a 2D image detector is to fire at the projection of the point. We use the trained field as it is, without fine-tuning it for view selection. A fixed SuperPoint and EPnP-RANSAC localizer then estimates the pose from the chosen view. We answer in two settings, each with a test registered before the runs. On synthetic ShapeNet objects with sparse point maps, summing the field over the visible landmarks beats counting them by +2.0 points of localization success rate (object-clustered 95% interval [+0.7, +3.2]). It also beats summing Harris-3D ranks by +2.2 [+0.8, +3.5]. On real indoor scenes from SceneFun3D, our adaptation of the learned view scorer LWL falls below counting on the test rooms. We therefore add the field to a learned per-landmark planner. On the test rooms with sparse maps whose landmarks the field also selects, the planner with the field beats the same planner without it by +1.8 points. It beats the planner with Harris-3D or curvature in its place by +1.0 and +0.8 points. All three room-clustered intervals lie above zero. In both settings, the field helps in sparse maps and is on par with Harris-3D in dense maps.

title: Benefit of Structured Representations: When Equivariance Helps in Image Classification
abstract: Equivariant neural networks promise improved representation learning through structural guarantees. However, mainstream vision encoders rarely incorporate equivariance for most geometric symmetries. Images are a particularly interesting modality with many such symmetries and extensive datasets from which to learn this structure. In this work, we investigate when vision encoders benefit from geometric inductive biases. We study the discrete rotation group of quarter-turns (C4) which acts losslessly without interpolation or boundary artifacts. Combined with image classification as a controlled invariant objective, this allows for a principled empirical investigation into the role of structural guarantees. We introduce ConvNeXt-C4 as a rotation equivariant ConvNeXt with dimension-equivalent yet orientation-structured representations. Training from scratch, our experiments show, that the C4 variant outperforms its base model across all tasks while operating with 6x fewer parameters and 1.6x fewer FLOPs. Its performance advantage increases log-linearly with decreasing training set size, with pre-training providing a similar improvement across both model variants. Analyzing the classifier head reveals that orientation information from the representations' structure is actively used, improving performance by 4.90% across all datasets. Our results highlight the sample-efficiency benefits of equivariance and the value of retained orientation information, motivating further investigation beyond image classification. Code is available at https://github.com/hlzl/equivariant-convnext.

title: Spe3DUp: Faithful Trajectory Distillation for Fast Image-to-3D Generation
abstract: Recent 3D generative models can produce high-quality meshes with complex structures and fine geometric details, with broad applications in games, film, and digital design. However, high-quality generation typically relies on long multi-step sampling processes that repeatedly evaluate large networks, leading to long inference times. At the same time, reference-driven tasks such as game-asset reconstruction and product digitization demand close correspondence to the input image: generated geometry must faithfully reconstruct the specific reference object. Acceleration must therefore reduce sampling computation while preserving the model's ability to reconstruct that object. To enable fast and faithful 3D generation, we introduce Spe3DUp, a coarse-to-fine framework based on Faithful Trajectory Distillation (FTD). FTD directly supervises few-step students with the teacher's input-conditioned denoising trajectories to preserve its generation behavior. We apply FTD separately to coarse geometry generation and geometric refinement, compressing both sampling processes while maintaining correspondence to the reference input. We further accelerate the complete mesh-generation pipeline with efficient geometry decoding and parallel remeshing. Experiments show that Spe3DUp maintains geometric quality and input correspondence close to those of the teacher, accelerates the coarse and refinement DiTs by 10.0x and 19.9x, respectively, and achieves a 7.7x end-to-end speedup over the original teacher pipeline.

title: Reproducer Synthesis for AI-Reported Bugs in the Linux Kernel
abstract: Agentic review systems are increasingly flagging suspected bugs in Linux kernel patches as textual reports. A maintainer who receives such reports needs further inspection to determine whether the report is true. The inspection requires understanding whether the bug can be triggered and, if necessary, manually constructing one. As a consequence, despite the excessive textual explanation, many reports go unanswered. In this paper, we argue that a runnable proof-of-concept (PoC) is the key information in such AI-generated kernel review reports. It is, however, challenging to automatically synthesize a valid and runnable PoC. We present ReproCue, a framework that generates PoCs for AI-generated Linux kernel reviews. ReproCue replays the historical kernel bugs and learns one reproduction finite-state-machine (FSM) per subsystem from successful runs. An FSM records the steps a reproduction goes through, together with the requirements observed at each step. Given a new review, ReproCue follows the FSM of that subsystem, adjusting the PoC and the environment as execution shows what is missing. In 100 recent AI-generated reviews, ReproCue writes PoCs for 49 of them, compared with 10 for the current agentic reproducer and 9 for the state-of-the-art directed fuzzing. Excitingly, with our generated PoCs, Linux kernel maintainers confirmed 69.4% of them, much higher than 9.3% from Sashiko where only textual explanations are included, making AI reviews more actionable in practice.

title: Non-Linear Motion from Two Frames: Cubic Hermite Trajectories for Video Frame Interpolation
abstract: Two-frame video frame interpolation commonly resamples endpoint optical flow by the query time, which selects a constant-velocity straight-line path even though the same endpoint displacement is compatible with many intermediate trajectories. We present HermiteVFI, which replaces independent query-time motion prediction with one explicit continuous trajectory per pixel. The measured endpoint displacement fixes the two trajectory positions, while two latent endpoint derivatives learned from the frame pair control the interior path. A cubic Hermite curve is the minimum-degree polynomial that can independently satisfy these two position and two derivative boundary quantities. Its residual form contains linear motion exactly, structurally preserves the measured displacement endpoints for any network output, and has coefficients that are predicted once per frame pair and evaluated in closed form at arbitrary t. We further show that one interior query time gives a rank-deficient constraint on the two free trajectory coefficients, whereas any two distinct interior times are full rank at the representation level, motivating multi-time supervision. Appearance-derived directional cues help infer the latent derivatives that endpoint displacement alone cannot identify. On X4K1000FPS, SNU-FILM, and Vimeo90K-Septuplet, the largest gains occur for difficult non-uniform motion and high interpolation ratios. The amortization applies to trajectory-coefficient prediction; downstream reversal, refinement, and synthesis remain query dependent.

title: Radio Emission From Low-redshift Little Red Dots
abstract: High-redshift Little Red Dots (LRDs) are radio faint in existing survey and deep-field samples. Nearby LRD analogues allow the radio emission and spectra of individual sources to be measured, which is not possible at $z\sim6$. Our sample comprises 44 low-redshift LRDs ($0.101 \leq z \leq 0.882$) . Eight objects are radio-detected: five at 144\,MHz with LoTSS, six at 3\,GHz with VLASS at $\geq3σ$, and J1047 through its published VLA data. The rest-frame 144\,MHz luminosities of the LoTSS detections span $1.8\times10^{30}$ to $3.6\times10^{31}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$. The LoTSS--VLASS spectral indices range from $-0.27\pm0.04$ (J2048) to $-0.78\pm0.11$ (J1200). J1051 lacks 144\,MHz coverage and has $α_{0.9 \rm GHz}^{\rm 3 GHz} \simeq-0.93$. J1047 has a clear deficit at 144 MHz relative to its optically thin GHz spectrum, consistent with a turnover whose position and physical mechanism are not uniquely constrained by the archival data. The higher detection fraction among the Green Pea sample largely reflects their lower redshift: in this subsample LoTSS reaches luminosities roughly an order of magnitude fainter than in the more distant DESI gold sample. If their escaping spectra and radio luminosities are held fixed and extrapolated as power laws, the five LoTSS detections would have observed-frame 144 MHz flux densities of $\sim0.7$--$32\,μ\mathrm{Jy}$. Low-redshift LRDs span more than an order of magnitude in radio luminosity among the detections, and more than two orders of magnitude when the J1047 upper limit is included. They also show several distinct spectral shapes, so the optically defined LRD class encompasses diverse radio properties. Current detection statistics are strongly shaped by redshift and survey sensitivity. The source-by-source luminosity limits provide a reference for interpreting future LRD samples.

title: Nontrivial criticality and weakly first-order transitions in the frustrated spin-1 chain with single-ion anisotropy
abstract: Frustrated spin chains host exotic phases beyond the Landau paradigm, yet weak first-order transitions and unconventional criticalities remain elusive. Combining large-scale density-matrix renormalization group with bosonization methods, we map the phase diagram of a spin-1 chain with next-nearest-neighbor (NNN) coupling and single-ion anisotropy (SIA). We pinpoint two topological phase transitions: a weakly first-order transition between the Haldane and NNN-Haldane phases with a tiny gap and a continuous transition from the Haldane phase to the large-$D$ phase located via level spectroscopy with Richardson extrapolation. For negative SIA, a spontaneous dimerized phase emerges between the Néel and NNN-Néel phases. Its transition into the Néel phase is a deconfined quantum critical point falling into the eight-vertex universality class, with central charge $c = 1$ and critical exponents varying continuously along the phase boundary. For positive SIA, we identify two vector-spin-chirality orders---an ordinary chiral phase and a narrow Haldane-chiral phase---with a weakly first-order transition between them, evidenced by a soft jump in the string order parameter. Our results reveal that frustration and anisotropy generate emergent orders and non-Landau criticalities, providing a platform for deconfined and topological phase transitions.

title: Minimum Effective-Susceptibility Bounds for Arbitrary Polarization Transformations in Metasurfaces
abstract: Metasurfaces are increasingly employed for sophisticated polarization transformations, including general unitary and nonunitary Jones operations. Despite substantial advances in analytical synthesis methods, inverse design of these transformations remains challenging. Here, we show that the particular mathematical structure of Jones polarization transformations makes optimal effective-susceptibility synthesis analytically tractable within the generalized sheet transition condition (GSTC) framework. For reciprocal, lossless dipolar metasurfaces, we establish exact feasibility and global minimum attainment, and derive sharp effective-susceptibility bounds for representative unitary and nonunitary transformations. We identify when magnetoelectric coupling lowers the minimum susceptibility, when it offers no resource advantage, and how the required material response depends on the prescribed polarization transformation. Applications to polarization rotations, tunable compensators, and polarization-state separation, including unambiguous discrimination, demonstrate sharp physical limits and material-resource trade-offs. These results provide geometry-independent theoretical benchmarks that can guide numerical inverse design and the selection of metasurface architectures.

title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
abstract: Agent harnesses today manage context on the model's behalf: when the window fills, the harness triggers a compaction that summarizes the history. We study the alternative, \emph{model-driven} context management, in which the model itself decides when and what to compact through a context API. We gave models control over their own context in \nooa, NVIDIA's open source agent harness, and compared the two strategies on document research and machine learning engineering across context budgets from 8K to 512K tokens. Models that use the context API effectively reach higher accuracy, often with fewer input tokens, especially at tight budgets: \textbf{GPT 6.1 nearly triples its score at a 32K budget} on OfficeQA Pro v2 (21\%~$\rightarrow$~56\%), and \textbf{Kimi gains with up to 41\% fewer input tokens}. Models differ widely, however, in how often they use the API, how aggressively they compact, and when they start compacting, and prompt changes shift that timing. Finally, we show that \textbf{inference engines can make model-driven edits cheaper}: by reusing the KV cache of the unchanged suffix after an edit, \textbf{we cut prefill compute by up to 15\% per request with no measurable change in accuracy}. Together, these results point to a new co-design frontier: models trained to manage their own context, served by inference engines that support KV cache editing.

title: Ground Your Steps: Optimizing Sampling Schedules in Flow Matching Robot Policies
abstract: Flow matching robot policies generate action chunks by integrating a learned velocity field at inference. However, under a fixed budget of neural function evaluations (NFEs), the integration result depends on the sampling schedule. This motivates optimizing the schedule to bring the generated action distribution closer to the demonstrations and improve task success. We propose Ground Your Steps (GYS), a training-free method that optimizes the sampling schedule by matching the generated and demonstrated chunk distributions at each observation. GYS applies truncated fractional differencing along each arm joint's action sequence and compares two types of pairwise differences between action chunks at each observation: differences of a generated chunk against a demonstration, and differences of two independent generated chunks against each other. After fractional differencing, these two pairwise-difference distributions coincide exactly when the distributions of generated and demonstrated action chunks match. GYS minimizes the energy distance between these distributions to obtain an improved schedule for each task and NFE budget. Compared with the uniform grid, GYS brings the generated chunk distribution closer to the demonstrated distribution and raises the success rate through the sampling schedule alone. On RoboTwin 2.0 benchmarks, GYS improves success rates at nearly every budget, with gains of 2.8 percentage points for both $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7. The gains also transfer to three real-world manipulation tasks, reaching up to 3.3 percentage points. Code is available at https://github.com/D-Robotics-AI-Lab/GroundYourSteps.

title: Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU): the fraction of radio-detected quasi-stellar objects at high redshift
abstract: The aim of this paper is to use the Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) to assess the fraction of high-z quasi-stellar objects (QSOs) that are radio-emitting at ~0.2 mJy/beam level and to establish if the radio emission is mainly produced by relativistic jets. A sample of 808 type1 QSOs in the redshift range 4<z<9 and covering the sky area currently observed by EMU was compiled from the literature and the SDSS spectroscopic database and cross-matched with EMU source catalogue. In total, 124 high-z QSOs are detected by EMU, corresponding to 15% of the sample. The large majority (70%) of the QSOs radio detected by EMU are reported in the radio for the first time. We use this sample to establish the detection rate at different optical magnitudes. We show that the fraction of radio-loud (R>10) high-z QSOs is about 8% while the fraction of radio detections is a strong function of the optical magnitude and reaches values of ~35% when only the optically brightest (mag~18) QSOs are considered. Since all the radio detected QSOs, including those classified as radio-quiet (R<10), exhibit radio powers ranging from 5x10^24 to 5x10^27 W Hz^-1 at 5 GHz, we argue that they could all host a relativistic jet and that orientation could be one of the main causes of the different values of radio-loudness observed in the sample. To support this hypothesis, we show that the number of high-z QSOs detected by EMU is fully consistent with the predictions based on the beaming model, using as reference the high-z blazars discovered at higher radio flux densities. The results presented here suggest that relativistic jets could have been very common in the early Universe representing up to ~35% of the luminous (L_1450A>10^46 erg s^-1) QSO population. Future observations with SKAO will be instrumental to unambiguously confirm the jetted nature of the QSOs currently detected by EMU.

title: Counting complex elliptic curves with self-quotients via class numbers
abstract: Let \(n>1\) be an integer. We consider complex elliptic curves \(E\) admitting a finite subgroup \(C\subset E(\mathbb C)\) of order \(n\) such that \(E/C\) is isomorphic to \(E\). % with the additional requirement that the invariant factors of (C) are unequal. We establish class-number counting formulas for the cyclic, noncyclic, and general cases. More precisely, we associate to every negative quadratic-order discriminant \(D\) the norm form \[ Q_D(x,y)=x^2+\varepsilon_Dxy+q_Dy^2, \] where \[ \varepsilon_D\in\{0,1\},\qquad q_D=\frac{\varepsilon_D^2-D}{4}. \] The invariant factors of the kernel of the corresponding endomorphism are determined by \(\gcd(x,y)\). This leads to finite sets of admissible discriminants describing the cyclic, noncyclic, and general cases with unequal invariant factors. Our main result expresses the numbers of isomorphism classes in the three cases as sums of the proper ideal class numbers \(h(D)\) over explicitly defined finite sets of admissible discriminants. This provides an arithmetic class-number counting formulation of the CM classification developed in earlier work by \cite{CanepaGaba2014,CanepaGaba2019,CanepaGabaOlteanu2022} and its subsequent algorithmic extensions. We also characterize the equal-invariant-factor case: it occurs precisely when $n=m^2$, and in that case every complex elliptic curve satisfies the required condition, with the unique subgroup being $E[m]$. We derive an explicit bound for the admissible discriminants, implement the counting procedure in Magma, and give numerical examples. The proof relies on the Smith normal form of the multiplication matrix associated with a quadratic integer. The results provide an arithmetic class-number counting formulation of the CM classification developed in earlier work.

title: The type-D accelerating Taub-NUT spacetime: construction, geometry and physical properties
abstract: We investigate the geometry and physical properties of the vacuum type-D accelerating Taub--NUT spacetime in the sector with vanishing Kerr rotation. We recover its normalized metric from the Plebański--Demiański family and a dressed finite binary, tracking the horizon Killing directions through the large-companion limit. The black-hole and acceleration horizons have distinct projective Killing generators, and their intrinsic horizon geometry yields a relation between polar Gaussian curvatures and cone angles that differs from that of the type-I accelerating Taub--NUT solution without requiring a matching of acceleration parameters. We establish separability of the type-D null Hamilton--Jacobi equation and construct an unwrapped radial conformal atlas with four simple-horizon extensions and five angular conformal diagrams. We also examine axial identifications and chronology-violating regions. The resulting geometrical and dynamical distinctions clarify how the two accelerating NUT families differ despite sharing their nonaccelerating and zero-NUT limits; the radial atlas is not claimed to be a unique maximal four-dimensional extension.

title: Lost in the Grid: Where Multimodal LLMs Fail Between Seeing and Planning
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel at static visual understanding and are increasingly applied to spatial planning, where a model interprets a visual layout and outputs an action sequence to reach a goal. Grid games are a common testbed for this ability because their rules are explicit and a solver can verify every move. Yet existing benchmarks mostly report end-to-end success rates, which hide whether a failure stems from visual perception, rule application, or multi-step planning. We introduce GridProbe, a diagnostic benchmark that 1) locates the failing stage between visual perception and planning and 2) verifies the diagnosis by targeted fine-tuning. On Sokoban, GridProbe pairs end-to-end solving with four probes (recognition, localization, single-step prediction, and state tracking) and gives every board both as an image and as an equivalent text grid. Evaluating seven MLLMs on Sokoban and a maze game reveals distinct bottlenecks behind similar success rates: proprietary models are limited by multi-step planning, whereas open-source models are limited by rule application or by visual grid indexing, i.e., counting rows and columns. Planning failures also hide perception failures: when planning is easier, the visual cost of the same model grows from 7.6 to 37.7 points. The diagnosis identifies what to train: fine-tuning only the vision module of the perception-limited model on board reading raises its interactive Sokoban success 3.5-fold (5.8% to 20.4%) and transfers zero-shot to the unseen maze game (single-turn success 13.8% to 67.1%), whereas the same data does not help a rule-limited model and training on solver solutions brings no gain. We will release the benchmark and code at https://github.com/suat-llm/GridProbe.

title: HSTTA: Hierarchical Selective Test-Time Adaptation for Label-Free Cross-Subject EEG-to-Image Retrieval
abstract: Cross-subject EEG-to-image retrieval suffers from substantial performance degradation on new subjects due to subject shift. Test-time adaptation (TTA) can mitigate this shift by adapting pretrained models with unlabeled target-subject EEG. However, most existing TTA methods struggle to match supervision granularity to each query's prediction confidence, leaving many queries without reliable pseudo-labels. To address this, we propose a novel framework named Hierarchical Selective Test-Time Adaptation (HSTTA). HSTTA builds a hierarchy over gallery image embeddings, uses hierarchical selective prediction to assign each EEG query a supervision granularity matching its current prediction confidence, and constructs adaptation objectives accordingly. We further propose Cross-Session Consistency Calibration (CSCC), an unsupervised method that calibrates the global confidence threshold to target a predefined accuracy level for hierarchical predictions. Moreover, we introduce Reciprocal Hierarchical Backoff (RHB), which moves queries lacking reverse-matching support to coarser nodes to mitigate error reinforcement. Experiments on two public benchmarks and ablation studies validate the effectiveness of HSTTA and its key components. On THINGS-EEG2, HSTTA outperforms the strongest EEG-specific TTA baseline by 17.9 (13.4) and 8.9 (3.7) percentage points in Top-1/Top-5 accuracy, respectively, under cosine (CSLS) ranking. Further analyses show that HSTTA yields more accurate pseudo-labels during adaptation, supporting more reliable model updates.

title: When High Capacity Becomes Undeployable: Pore-Filling Constraints for Multi-Objective Optimization of Direct Air Capture Sorbents
abstract: Amine-impregnated sorbents with the highest nominal CO2 capacity are frequently the least deployable, as amine beyond the pore-volume limit blocks active sites. Yet multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) for direct air capture (DAC) treats formulation search as unconstrained. We encode the pore-filling boundary as an explicit outcome constraint, c(x) = tanh(1 - phi_hat) - tau, and use it as a diagnostic instrument on a hand-curated, DOI-traceable benchmark of 618 solid-amine formulations from 43 publications. Unconstrained MOBO attains higher nominal capacity (3.639 +/- 0.815 vs. 2.964 +/- 0.728 mmol/g, p = 1.0e-11), but across 100 seeds 63.2% of its Pareto-optimal candidates violate the pore-filling boundary versus 39.3% under the constraint: it is rewarded for proposing candidates outside the pore-confined design regime. The constraint steers the front to lower loadings (55.8 vs. 65.2 wt%) and larger pores. The boundary is corroborated once apparatus effects are harmonized hierarchically: 77.8% of kinetic variance is between-laboratory, and pore filling carries a significant kinetic penalty (p = 0.002). Standard hypervolume over-credits feasibility-agnostic methods by 13.9-16.1% (vs. 11.1% constrained), and three surrogate-based analyses---the constrained front, a regeneration-energy third objective, and harmonized kinetics---consistently point to a conservative deployable window at pore filling phi_hat ~ 0.4-0.5 (45-55 wt% loading). The benchmark and associated analysis outputs accompany this submission.

title: OceanFix: Reference-Guided Diffusion for Sparse-View Underwater 3D Reconstruction
abstract: Recent advances in Gaussian splatting have enabled efficient underwater reconstruction, but sparse observations, light attenuation, and backscatter still leave scene regions underconstrained and cause novel-view artifacts. We present OceanFix, a reference-guided framework for sparse-view underwater 3D reconstruction that combines diffusion-based view repair with Gaussian scene refinement. Our repair model follows a two-stage training strategy that separates underwater appearance adaptation from geometric refinement. The first stage learns underwater appearance from reference observations and estimated medium features. The second uses camera poses and reference depth to align reference features, with relative-depth supervision guiding structural repair without requiring target-view depth at inference. We further propose medium-aware distillation that transfers repaired views into the 3D scene according to geometric repair demand and channel-specific optical observability. Through iterative rendering, repair, and distillation, OceanFix refines underconstrained regions while retaining supervision from the observed views. Experiments on underwater datasets demonstrate that OceanFix improves rendering quality in sparse-view 3D reconstruction, reducing visible artifacts and recovering finer scene details.

title: Foundation interatomic potentials capture structural disorder in metallic glasses
abstract: Foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials transfer well across chemical and structural space, yet their reliability for highly disordered metallic states is less established. Metallic glasses are a demanding benchmark: they have traditionally been modeled with Embedded Atom Method (EAM) potentials fitted to specific compositions, while ab initio molecular dynamics remains too expensive at the required sizes and timescales. Using the prototypical Cu-Zr-Al glass, we show that foundation potentials capture structural disorder, reproducing the structure, quenching dynamics, and elastic, mechanical and thermal properties of the amorphous state at near first-principles accuracy. We benchmark MACE foundation models against a classical EAM potential along molecular dynamics quenches, validating against density functional theory and experiment, first at Cu46Zr46Al8 and then across the good glass-forming region of the ternary. We further test two specialization routes: fine-tuning on glass structures generated with Lennard-Jones surrogate models, and on automatically generated small periodic cells (ASSYST). Models pre-trained on databases that include non-equilibrium liquid and amorphous configurations, such as OMAT, are accurate and transferable across composition out of the box, clearly outperforming the composition-specific EAM potential. Fine-tuning on target glass structures brings only modest gains, while specialization on small crystalline cells degrades the description of disorder. The readiness of foundation potentials for disordered metals is therefore set mainly by the diversity of their pre-training data rather than by system-specific fine-tuning, shifting the modeling effort from bespoke dataset generation to pre-training coverage and careful validation of the resulting dynamics.

title: Minkowski Problems for Mixed Centro-Section Integrals
abstract: Recent studies in affine convex geometry have introduced two new families of geometric measures: affine dual curvature measures and centro-section measures. Motivated by these developments, we introduce mixed centro-section integrals and establish their variational formulas. Under the subspace concentration condition, we prove the existence of solutions to the corresponding Minkowski-type problems. We further introduce mixed bi-dual $m$-intersection bodies of index $q$ and establish the corresponding sharp affine isoperimetric inequalities. The resulting mixed centro-section measures include centro-section measures and affine dual curvature measures as special cases.

title: Strategic and Robust Task Allocation for Combat Objectives in Adversarial Multi-Agent Environments
abstract: Task allocation in contested-objective team games requires coordinated decisions under uncertainty, spatial constraints, and changing tactical conditions. In such settings, multiple agents must anticipate both teammate behavior and opponent actions. We study a hybrid predict-then-optimize approach for assigning controllable agents to objectives in real time. A masked multi-head model predicts tactical signals for each agent, including survival chance, local superiority, combat interaction, travel time, and objective contribution. These signals are combined with rule-based terms in a score matrix, and a minimum-cost flow solver computes coordinated global assignments constrained by capacity, occupancy, stability, and defensive strategies. Learning is limited to tactical scoring, while explicit rules and solver structure preserve controllability and interpretability. We evaluate the system using predictive metrics, offline assignment diagnostics, online A/B evaluation, and latency measurements. The system is an R\&D research prototype built on a commercial game and is not deployed in the shipped game. The results indicate that learned tactical estimates can support stable, feasible, and inspectable objective allocation under strict real-time constraints.

title: Interacting with Alexa: A Longitudinal Case Study of Voice Assistant Use in Down Syndrome
abstract: As life expectancy for individuals with Down syndrome (DS) continues to increase, supporting cog- nitive engagement, everyday autonomy, and participation throughout adulthood has become an important research priority. Conversational voice assistants have emerged as promising assistive tech- nologies for these purposes, yet evidence regarding their long-term use in naturalistic settings remains limited. This paper presents a longitudinal case study of the everyday use of Amazon Alexa by an adult with Down syndrome over nine months in a real domestic environment. The study combines analyses of interaction logs, audio recordings, and qualitative observations to investigate usage pat- terns, interaction performance, communicative adaptation, and the integration of the voice assistant into everyday life. Results show that Alexa became progressively embedded in daily routines, sup- porting entertainment, information access, and autonomy-related activities. Longitudinal analyses reveal stable interaction patterns, reduced retry behavior, and the emergence of effective communi- cation strategies, while qualitative observations highlight increasing communicative engagement and the value of proactive reminders. The study also identifies important limitations of current commer- cial voice assistants, including reduced robustness to non-normative speech, limited conversational continuity, and poor contextual reasoning. Beyond providing rare ecologically valid evidence of long- term voice assistant use, the findings highlight design considerations that are relevant to the ongoing evolution of LLM-based conversational systems.

title: Bringing Singles to $GW$: A Coupled-Cluster Perspective on Orbital Relaxation
abstract: The one-shot $G_0W_0$ approximation suffers from a pronounced dependence on the underlying mean-field starting point. Here, we explore an alternative to conventional self-consistent $GW$ schemes by introducing single excitations within the recently established connection between $GW$ and extended coupled-cluster (ECC) theory. Starting from the equivalence between $G_0W_0$ and ionization-potential/electron-affinity equation-of-motion direct-ring extended coupled-cluster doubles (IP/EA-EOM-drECCD), we extend the formalism to include right-hand single-excitation and left-hand single-deexcitation cluster amplitudes coupled to the direct-ring doubles amplitudes. The resulting approximation, denoted singles-$G_0W_0$ (s$G_0W_0$), incorporates orbital-relaxation effects without explicitly introducing self-consistency in the Green's function. We assess the performance of s$G_0W_0$ for molecular valence and core ionization potentials using Hartree-Fock and Kohn-Sham starting points. For both types of ionizations, the inclusion of singles largely suppresses the starting-point dependence observed in conventional $G_0W_0$, yielding quasiparticle energies close to those obtained from the Hartree-Fock reference, irrespective of the initial mean-field description. Although this does not necessarily translate into improved absolute accuracy, it demonstrates that singles provide an effective route to reducing the starting-point dependence of $GW$-like approximations without resorting to self-consistency.

title: CoordRoute: Coordinated Multi-Model Routing for Maximum Compute-Budget Utility
abstract: Model routing sends each request to one of several large language models (LLMs) of different sizes. In practice, requests share a fixed compute budget: a spending cap on rented model APIs or the capacity of a private GPU cluster. Most existing routers do not account for the total budget: each decides a request on its own, so per-request optima are not optimal overall. We advocate coordinated routing, which allocates the budget across requests to maximize its utility, their total satisfaction, along a predict-plan-rectify route: predict what each model would give and cost, plan the choice against later requests, and rectify it during generation. Each step faces a challenge: a request's gain from each model is uncertain before generation, later arrivals are unknown when a request must start, and observing answers during generation consumes the budget itself. CoordRoute addresses them with relative demand prediction, which compares candidate models through past requests that lead to the same routing choices; a lookahead solver, which charges each choice for what its compute could earn for later requests; and budget-aware runtime correction, which drops or upgrades in-flight requests at the same price, inspecting answers only when it pays off. On Azure Conversation and BurstGPT traces, CoordRoute improves total satisfaction by 18.72% over the strongest existing router.

title: Modality-Shift Contrastive Decoding for Temporally Grounded Audio-Visual Understanding
abstract: Audio-visual large language models (AV-LLMs) are designed to represent the temporal structure of audio and video, yet it remains unclear how effectively they use this temporal information to relate sounds to visual events. To examine this, we probe an AV-LLM on an audio-visual synchronization task by shifting the audio so that the queried sound overlaps a different visual event. We observe that the model still favors the originally aligned event over the newly aligned one, indicating limited sensitivity to changes in audio-visual temporal alignment. To address this, we propose Modality-Shift Contrastive Decoding (MSCD), a training-free decoding method that emphasizes audio-visual temporal alignment in model predictions. MSCD contrasts logits under preserved and disrupted temporal alignment to favor predictions supported by aligned audio and video. We disrupt this alignment by temporally shifting either the audio or the video, while keeping the other modality fixed. Extensive evaluations with two AV-LLMs across three benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of MSCD for temporally grounded audio-visual understanding. In particular, MSCD improves accuracy over the base models on Daily-Omni by 2.2 and 2.8 percentage points for OmniVinci and video-SALMONN 2+, respectively, suggesting that emphasizing temporal alignment can also benefit broader audio-visual understanding.

title: Admoab-DETR: Resolution-Tiered Fusion for Infrared-Visible Object Detection with Missing Modalities
abstract: Infrared and visible images offer complementary cues for all-weather object detection, yet real-world sensor dropouts can leave one stream unavailable and degrade paired-input detectors. Meanwhile, existing modality-adaptive methods apply heavy cross-modal attention uniformly across scales, incurring prohibitive token overhead on high-resolution maps. We propose Admoab-DETR, a unified real-time detector supporting infrared-only, visible-only, and paired inputs with a single set of weights. Specifically, \emph{Resolution-Tiered Fusion} (RTF) allocates fusion capacity by spatial token density and feature granularity: a lightweight Spatial Modality Gate governs fine local fusion at the highest-resolution scale with zero-cost single-view pass-through, while channel-compressed deformable Admoab necks capture cross-modal correspondence at coarser semantic scales. Furthermore, \emph{Mode-Matched Feature Distillation} (MMFD) aligns multi-scale encoder features with an availability-synchronized full-fusion teacher, avoiding ill-posed cross-modal hallucination while cutting parameters by 18.1\% and paired latency by 39.6\% at zero inference overhead. We also construct Admoab, a strictly registered 20,000-pair infrared--visible benchmark across diverse scenes. Experiments show Admoab-DETR achieves state-of-the-art accuracy--efficiency trade-offs across missing-modality and paired benchmarks. Our code will be available at https://github.com/liwenchao0615/Admoab-DETR.

title: The modulus of smoothness and \(\ell_p\)-generation
abstract: Fabian, Godefroy, Hájek and Zizler [\emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{200} (2003), 301--323, Theorem~2] proved that at density \(\aleph_1\), generation by a space whose modulus of smoothness has power type \(p\), \(1<p\le 2\), is equivalent to \(\ell_p(Γ)\)-generation. We extend this equivalence to arbitrary density, with \(|Γ|=\dens X\), answering \mbox{Problem~291} of Guirao, Montesinos and Zizler [\emph{Open Problems in the Geometry and Analysis of Banach Spaces}, Springer, Cham (2016), p.~127]. The proof combines an upper \(\ell_p\)-estimate on successive projection differences with transfinite induction on density. We characterize generation by superreflexive spaces and by their \(\ell_2\)-sums, and obtain \(\ell_{\min\{r,2\}}\)-generation for closed subspaces of \(L^r(μ)\), \(1<r<\infty\), including Hilbert generation for \(r\ge 2\).

title: Entropic continuity of Lyapunov exponents in arbitrary dimension
abstract: We prove that the sum of the positive Lyapunov exponents is entropically continuous for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism, provided the entropy exceeds its second-largest exterior growth rate. We also establish stable strong positive recurrence and show that the topological entropy is continuous, and the number of ergodic measures of maximal entropy is upper semicontinuous. This extends the result of Buzzi, Crovisier, and Sarig to arbitrary dimensions. We give examples in both the measure-theoretic and topological senses, showing that this entropy gap condition is sharp. We also present applications related to the Newhouse phenomenon and standard maps.

title: Cell-Type-Specific Expression Is Hard to Predict from Bulk, but It Is Still Useful
abstract: Single-cell-informed deconvolution provides cell-type-resolved features for clinical bulk RNA cohorts. Most existing methods predict the proportions $π_k$ of the $K$ constituent cell types (CTs). Fewer predict cell-type-specific expression (CTSE) $μ_{kg}$ of gene $g$ in CT $k$, which can capture cell states that proportions miss, but recent benchmarks find it much harder. We explain this gap with closed-form accuracy bounds. For CTSE, we derive an $R^2$ ceiling for per-gene linear estimators. For proportions, the best linear estimator, which pools evidence across genes, has a closed-form $R^2$, and a computable lower bound on it predicts which CTs are learnable. We study targeted deconvolution of 106 biologically curated (CT, gene) pairs, found post hoc to have higher learnability scores. On overall survival in non-small cell lung cancer, estimation difficulty does not predict prognostic value across these targets. Yet a sparse survival model on deconvolved features, mostly CTSE, predicts survival as well as a sparse model on the bulk genes themselves, while attributing its signal to specific cell types. Some deconvolved CTSE features reveal prognostic signal not seen in the corresponding bulk gene.

title: A general upper bound on broadcast function ${B(n)}$ using Kn{ö}del graph
abstract: Broadcasting in a graph is the process of transmitting a message from one vertex, the originator, to all other vertices. We consider the classical model in which an informed vertex informs one of its uninformed neighbours during each time unit. A broadcast graph on ${n}$ vertices is a graph in which broadcasting can finish in ${\lceil \log_{2} n \rceil}$ time units from any originator. A minimum broadcast graph on ${n}$ vertices is a broadcast graph that has the least possible number of edges, ${B(n)}$, over all broadcast graphs on ${n}$ vertices. This paper presents a new general upper bound on ${B(n)}$ for all odd ${n}$ except when ${n=2^{k}-1}$ for an integer $k$. In order to achieve this bound, a vertex deletion method is applied to Knödel graphs on ${n+1}$ vertices. To prove our result, we characterize all informed vertices in a Knödel graph after every time unit by applying the standard and reverse dimensional broadcast scheme with any cyclic shifts from an arbitrary originator. Furthermore, we completely resolve the open problem about the existence of minimum average time broadcast graphs.

title: Coefficient-Range Mitigation on an 8-Bit Coherent Ising Machine
abstract: Mapping optimization problems to the restricted coefficient range of an 8-bit CIM can distort their encoded energy landscapes. We investigate whether three coefficient-range mitigation techniques previously studied for quantum annealing---interaction extension, bounded-coefficient encoding, and augmented Lagrangian penalties---improve end-to-end optimization outcomes. Experiments on weighted Max-Cut, multidimensional knapsack, and quadratic assignment show that the benefits are selective. At a fixed number of CIM calls, intermediate interaction extension yields higher mean best Max-Cut objectives, whereas aggressive extension degrades performance. Bounded-coefficient encoding improves the mean best feasible profit on one knapsack instance but not the other. Augmented Lagrangian perturbations increase feasibility when unshifted constraint penalties are too weak, but do not outperform the best unshifted penalty setting. Overall, coefficient-range mitigation is most effective when its strength is tuned to the problem and encoding, with aggressive mitigation potentially offsetting its benefits.

title: Multi-view fnirs identifies neurophysiological subtypes in post-stroke aphasia
abstract: Post-stroke aphasia is clinically heterogeneous, and conventional classifications may not capture differences in brain functional organisation. We tested whether resting-state and task-based functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) could identify neurophysiological subgroups alongside clinical assessment.Seventy-nine patients underwent unsupervised clustering using three fNIRS feature views: resting-state activity and connectivity, language-task activation, and rest-to-task connectivity reconfiguration. Similarity network fusion and spectral clustering integrated the views. Clinical and behavioural measures were excluded from clustering.Three clusters (n = 32, 17 and 30) were identified. This solution had the largest eigengap and was the only candidate significant after permutation testing and Holm correction (adjusted P = 0.001). It was stable under subsampling (mean adjusted Rand index, 0.773), but agreement fell to 0.217 when the resting-state view was removed. Clusters differed in most regional intrinsic-activity measures and all resting-state connectivity summaries, with few differences in task activation or connectivity reconfiguration. Their profiles showed higher right anterior prefrontal activity, distributed fronto-sensorimotor and parietal alterations, and reduced interhemispheric connectivity, respectively.Cluster membership was not significantly associated with conventional aphasia subtype (Cramér's V = 0.287), and baseline clinical language scores and task performance did not differ between clusters.These findings identify three neurophysiological subgroups distinguished mainly by intrinsic activity and resting-state functional connectivity, not clearly aligned with conventional aphasia classifications or baseline clinical measures. Multi-view fNIRS analysis may complement clinical characterisation, requiring independent and longitudinal validation.

title: Beyond-quantum correlations for single system in pseudo-quantum model
abstract: Within the standard prepare-measure framework, it has been demonstrated that certain compositions of two elementary quantum systems can produce beyond-quantum correlations and can even lead to perfect discrimination of two non-orthogonal quantum states. In this Letter, we introduce the pseudo-quantum model (PQM) for a single system that incorporates the \emph{pseudo-states (effects)} (they satisfy all the properties of quantum states and effects except having negative eigenvalues), and yields valid probability. We consider a prepare-measure communication game known as random access code (RAC) and demonstrate that the success probability achievable within PQM exceeds the corresponding optimal quantum success probability, thereby giving rise to beyond-quantum correlations even for a single system. We then show that such correlations are unphysical as they violate the information causality (IC) principle. Moreover, we demonstrate that two non-orthogonal states can be perfectly distinguishable in PQM for a single system. Therefore, we demonstrate that for a single indivisible system (devoid of any composition), the negativity of \emph{pseudo-states (effects)} can lead to the emergence of beyond-quantum correlations.

title: Rank-size analysis of optimal portfolio weights with a reverse-engineering application
abstract: This paper investigates the shape of optimal portfolio weights using rank-size analysis. We consider four portfolio selection models: Global Minimum-Variance (GMV), minimum-CVaR, Risk Parity (RP), and the Most Diversified Portfolio (MDP). For each model, we fit seven rank-size specifications to the sorted portfolio weights generated over rolling windows. To compare the fitted specifications, we combine standard goodness-of-fit measures with Cumulative Second-order $\varepsilon$-Stochastic Dominance, an $\varepsilon$-parameterized generalization of Second-order Stochastic Dominance that quantifies the extent to which the exact dominance conditions are satisfied or violated. Empirically applied to major equity indices, this approach provides a systematic criterion for identifying the optimal functional form across diverse market compositions. Furthermore, we address the inverse problem of identifying the generating model from the observed weight structure. We use the calibrated rank-size parameters as inputs to a Random Forest classifier, evaluated by a blocked cross-validation that accounts for the overlap between estimation windows. The parameters separate minimum-risk from risk-diversification strategies and identify the RP and MDP portfolios, whereas the GMV and minimum-CVaR portfolios are difficult to distinguish. These results indicate that rank-size parameters provide a compact and informative description of portfolio allocation geometries.

title: Black hole accretion flows as dark matter bolometers
abstract: Astrophysical systems provide powerful probes of dark matter interactions, complementing direct-detection searches. We propose using accretion flows of the supermassive black hole as a bolometer for light DM. The kinetic energy of sub-MeV dark matter in the black hole gravitational potential can remain below the thermal energy of the plasma electrons. The colder dark matter population can therefore absorb energy through elastic scattering, cooling the electrons and modifying their emission spectrum. We integrate dark matter cooling into the advection-dominated accretion flow around M87$^{*}$ and solve the full set of thermodynamic equations to obtain the resulting temperature profile and radio-to-millimeter emission. By comparing the predicted spectrum with observations accompanying the Event Horizon Telescope campaign, we use, for the first time, the thermal energy balance of the hot accretion flow to constrain DM-electron scattering, obtaining stringent limits on keV-to-MeV DM for both heavy and light mediators.

title: Two-type thinning with alternative leader rate for random partition structures
abstract: A dust-free random partition structure with infinitely many parts is a random sequence $(\mathsf{X}_1,\mathsf{X}_2,\dots)$ with $\mathsf{X}_1>\mathsf{X}_2>\dots>0$ such that $\mathsf{X}_1+\mathsf{X}_2+\dots=1$, almost surely. The Poisson-Dirichlet $\mathrm{PD}(m,0)$ distributions for $0<m<1$ are defined such that $\mathsf{X}_n = ξ_n^{-1/m}/\sum_{ν=1}^{\infty} ξ_ν^{-1/m}$, where $0<ξ_1<ξ_2<\dots$ is a homogeneous Poisson point process. It is a model for thinning invariant random partition structures, where every one of the infinitely many parts $\mathsf{X}_1,\mathsf{X}_2,\dots$ are thinned IID at rate 1. We consider a 2-type thinning where the instantaneous leader is deleted with an alternative rate $1+r\geq 0$. Then we seek time stationary random partition structures. When $r =R\in \{0,1,\dots\}$ a solution is obtained by taking $\mathrm{PD}(m,0)$ and performing ``balayage,'' where balayage means simply excavating the first $R$ points. We find the solutions for all $r \in (-1,\infty)$, which we call $\mathrm{PD}^{(r)}(m,0)$. We motivate with an application, and we present graphical representations.

title: Equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
abstract: We construct explicit symmetric-function realizations of the torus-equivariant $K$-homology of affine Grassmannians of types B and D.
