Below the threshold, when the leading power correction is kept as a gauge-sector operator, the auxiliary field is no longer the field strength: $F=f(A)+(gα_sT_F/15πM^2)(D_αJ_β-D_βJ_α)$, with $J$ the light-quark colour current. We verify this identity against the full theory and show that it separates the long-distance gluon exchange, carried by $F$, from the short-distance heavy-quark effect, carried by a four-quark contact term.

title: Can Visual World Models See Force?
abstract: World models and vision-language-action policy models are increasingly proposed as foundations for robot manipulation. They predict how scenes evolve and which actions to take, yet successful manipulation depends not solely on following observable trajectories but also on the hidden variable of interaction force. Neurophysiology has shown that humans possess a visual prior for this hidden variable, motivating us to ask the question: Do the representations of visual foundation models also capture the forces involved in an interaction? We define force awareness as the ability of representations to (1) indicate when contact force is applied, (2) track how it changes during an interaction, and (3) reflect how large it is. We probe frozen image, video, world- and policy model representations with a lightweight readout trained on synchronized video and force measurements from two manipulation datasets. Our experiments show that most models capture when contact occurs but not how much force is being applied. Surprisingly, robot post-training does not improve this either, highlighting an important gap in current models capabilities.

title: Reading the Room with AI: FOMC Deliberation and Growth-at-Risk
abstract: Macro-at-Risk models forecast the growth distribution from public data; policy is set by a committee arguing over their meaning. From FOMC Minutes, public three weeks after each meeting, we add several dimensions of deliberation to a growth quantile model on FRED-MD's 123 series. Only disagreement present in the discussion but absent from the vote lowers out-of-sample loss by 4-6 percent, chiefly in the center, beyond professional, staff and Committee forecasts. Much of deliberation's informational value lies in the recorded discussion itself, and in the disagreement it reveals, rather than in the risk assessments the Committee chooses to state.

title: The singular Paneitz equation on four-manifolds: refined blow-up analysis and degree jumps
abstract: We compute the Leray--Schauder degree of the singular Paneitz equation on a closed four-manifold with conical orders strictly between minus one and zero. We assume that the kernel of the Paneitz operator consists of the constants. In each positive nonresonant chamber the degree is a partial sum of an explicit generating series determined by the Euler characteristic and the conical orders. We match the heights of exact blow-up solutions and expand the gradient near the corrected projected bubbles. A localized dilation identity gives its common-scale component on the zero set of the relative-scale equations. For generic data a fixed-mass homotopy then gives the signed degree of each concentrating configuration. Assign ordinary points weight one and conical points weight one plus their order. If the largest concentrating weight exceeds one half, a finite second moment gives the coefficient. At one half the expansion acquires a logarithm, and below one half the coefficient is a global finite part. On the round four-sphere with two antipodal points of equal weight below one half, perturbing the prescribed curvature away from both points selects the side of bubbling.

title: Counting Classical Fullerenes I: Exact Enumeration and Generic Achiral Symmetry
abstract: We give an exact arithmetic formula for the number of classical fullerenes on $2m$ vertices. The oriented count is known; the new contribution counts achiral fullerenes, those admitting an orientation-reversing symmetry. We transport these symmetries to a lattice, classify eleven types, and express their contribution as seven weighted orbit counts. The complete formula is printed here, together with an exact algorithm producing all counts through index $M$ in quasilinear bit time with fast integer multiplication. We also prove that the proportion of achiral fullerenes with a unique orientation-reversing symmetry tends to one as the size increases. That symmetry is either a reflection or a fixed-point-free involution, with cumulative proportions $527/529$ and $2/529$. Among all fullerenes on $2m$ vertices, the achiral proportion has order $m^{-5}$; the same order holds cumulatively. The exceptional achiral classes with nontrivial orientation-preserving symmetry number $O(m^2)$.

title: A Head-Level Investigative Study of Self-Supervised Backbones for Synthetic Speech Detection
abstract: Self-supervised learning (SSL) speech backbones are the standard frontend for synthetic-speech detection, and layer-wise probing has established which layers carry the most signal. But analysis stops there: which of a layer's twelve attention heads compute the spoof decision is unknown. We present the first head-level study of two frozen backbones, WavLM-base and Wav2Vec2-base, on ASVspoof 5. Per-head ablation shows that only a few heads carry the decision while others actively oppose it; removing those heads lowers equal error rate (EER) with no retraining, by 13% relative in WavLM and 22% in Wav2Vec2. We also find a probe-free signature: spoofed speech draws more focused attention than genuine speech, and this gap alone separates the two almost as well as the full representation, peaking at each backbone's most discriminative layer. Finally, attack identity is decodable from every head, yet heads differ in what they do, not in what they know.

title: Mitigating Hallucinations in Medical Question Answering on ESC Cardiology Guidelines: Evaluation and Retrieval Optimization
abstract: Background: Large language models produce hallucinations in medical question answering (QA). Verify-and-revise pipelines that check atomic claims against retrieved guideline evidence are a standard mitigation, but evaluations almost universally treat the verifier's output as ground truth, an assumption rarely tested. Objective: To measure, claim by claim against human judgement, how such a pipeline fails in a guideline-grounded clinical setting. Methods: We built a dataset of 160 questions (100 patient vignettes from 89 de-identified cases, 60 fact-based) over four recent ESC cardiology guidelines, all approved by a practising internist, and a retrieval corpus of 627 hand-verified guideline records at two chunk granularities. A five-stage pipeline was run under four retrieval configurations and three independent runs (1920 arm-runs); all 606 first-pass refuted claims were manually audited, an independent judge re-judged 906 decisions, and the expert blindly reviewed 100 accepted claims. Results: Only 44.7-50.6% of flagged claims were true hallucinations. Correction loops converged in 85.2-95.1% of cases, yet 35% of genuine final errors were introduced by correction. Single-run true-hallucination recall was 35.6-41.2%, the three-run union 71-80%; verifier agreement was moderate (kappa = 0.505). The blind probe estimated the accepted-claim miss rate at 3.2% (95% CI 0.7-6.7%). Final genuine-error rate: 1.7% of answers. Conclusion: Claim-level verification reduces hallucinated content by an order of magnitude, but verifier reliability, not generation, is the limiting factor and must be measured, not assumed.

title: Calibration of Neuromusculoskeletal Models Using Differentiable Physics: Recommendations for Improving Model Accuracy
abstract: Differentiable physics has shown potential to usher in a new paradigm in human neuromusculoskeletal (NMS) model calibration. Early results from pioneering works have demonstrated that auto-differentiable NMS models can greatly reduce NMS model calibration time while achieving comparable accuracy compared to traditional calibration methods. The efficient gradient-based optimizers have enabled calibration of increasingly sophisticated human models with a large number of parameters, which seek to narrow the gap between simulation and reality. Several modules have been evaluated separately in different studies, but have never been directly compared within the same study. In this work, these modules are compared on the same differentiable upper limb model with a 3-DoF shoulder, a 2-DoF elbow, and 11 superficial and 5 deep muscles in the calibration to find an optimal pipeline for improving model accuracy. The considered modules include muscle synergy, learnable bone parameters, optimizable geometry of wrap objects, and constraint torque of the differentiable arm model. To evaluate the effect and interplay between the modules on calibration accuracy, one or more modules were used in each of 16 calibration configurations, which were compared in terms of the error between two joint torques calculated by the forward and inverse dynamics with the calibrated model on 9 distinctive testing movements across 4 subjects. Results showed that torque loss was reduced by 23.6% on average using muscle synergy extrapolation to estimate deep muscle activities, and by 10.9% on average through bone dynamic parameter optimization, which are both recommended to be incorporated in the calibration.

title: Native higher-order optimization with entropy quantum computing
abstract: Higher-order interactions are common in applied optimization: parity checks, radar-code sidelobes, portfolio skewness and kurtosis, and marketing-channel synergies all yield cubic or quartic objectives. Quantum annealers and most Ising machines accept only quadratic objectives, and gate-based quantum processors build every higher-order term from two-qubit gates. Entropy quantum computing, realized in the hybrid photonic-electronic Dirac-3S system, accepts polynomials of degree up to five with all-to-all coupling over binary, integer or simplex-constrained continuous variables. No user-supplied quadratization or circuit compilation is needed. We formulate four industrial use cases as six cubic and quartic instances, run them on Dirac-3S with 30 samples each, and score every sample against a certified optimum or a classical best-known value. We also estimate their cost on quantum annealers, superconducting grids and trapped-ion registers under standard mappings. For the two densest instances, a portfolio with about 80,000 terms and a budget allocation with 360,000 terms, the quadratized problems need embeddings far beyond current annealers, over $10^5$ physical qubits for the portfolio alone, and one phase-separation layer costs over $10^6$ two-qubit gates before optimization. Dirac-3S ran all six natively and returned feasible, distinct solutions. All samples of the binary instances are single-flip local minima. The best portfolio sample lies within 0.32% of the best-known value and the best budget sample 15% above it, but no sample reached its reference. Classical solvers reach the references within minutes at these sizes, and random starts followed by a local polish reach comparable or better values, so the advantage established here is one of expressibility and mapping cost, not of solution quality. Whether it extends to time to solution at larger sizes remains open.

title: One Representation to Rule Them All -- Open-Vocabulary Change Detection from Text or Visual Examples
abstract: Open-vocabulary change detection (OVCD) aims to localise user-specified changes without retraining for predefined categories. Existing approaches typically rely on textual descriptions and combine separate models for region proposal, semantic recognition, and temporal comparison. This limits how target concepts can be expressed and makes detection dependent on several intermediate predictions. We introduce OVTSID3, a training-free framework that unifies region grouping, concept identification, and temporal comparison in the representation space of DINOv3. OVTSID3 supports two complementary modes of concept specification: zero-shot textual queries or one-shot visual prompting through a masked reference pair. OVTSID3 outperforms all prior training-free OVCD methods on two building and two natural-disaster benchmarks, raising the average F1 by 8.9 points. OVTSID3 also supports semantic change detection and achieves state-of-the-art on SECOND. These results demonstrate the flexibility of a unified representation for text- or example-guided change detection without task-specific model training.

title: $E_d$-Enhancements of $L_\infty$-Algebras Associated to Secondary Polytopes
abstract: We study $E_d$-enhancements of the geometric $L_\infty$-algebras associated to secondary polytopes of finite configurations in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\geq2$. We construct an action of the semialgebraic chains of the Fulton--MacPherson operad on the shifted algebra $B_A=\mathfrak g_A[1-d]$ when $|A|\leq3d$. The action recovers the prescribed higher Lie operations on fundamental chains. The construction is obtained from a general extension theorem for weighted shifted $L_\infty$-algebras, using reflection to control relative cohomology obstructions. For $|A|\leq3d-1$, the resulting reflection-compatible integration actions are homotopic relative to their shifted Lie structure. We also give an abstract enhancement without a cardinality bound, direct formulas for circuits, and explicit operations for convex pentagons and hexagons.

title: Evaluating Aviation Safety Knowledge Extraction with SmolLM2: From Zero-Shot to Retrieval-Grounded Prompting
abstract: Aviation accident narratives contain safety knowledge that is difficult to capture using structured occurrence fields alone. This study evaluates prompting-based knowledge extraction across four dimensions: concept accuracy, verbatim evidence grounding, structural compliance, and directed relation extraction. SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct was evaluated under zero-shot, one-shot, fixed few-shot, and retrieval-grounded prompting using 300 National Transportation Safety Board narratives from 2000-2020, containing 3,763 reference concepts and 467 directed relations. Evaluation combined structural checks, verbatim evidence matching, expert-reviewed semantic matching, and paired bootstrap confidence intervals. No prompting strategy performed best across all dimensions. Retrieval-grounded prompting achieved the highest concept micro-F1 of 32.27%, although its advantage over fixed few-shot prompting was uncertain (95% CI: -0.92 to 2.40 percentage points). One-shot prompting achieved the highest relation F1 of 6.95%, identifying directed relation extraction as the principal SmolLM2 bottleneck. Compared with fixed few-shot prompting, retrieval improved verbatim grounding (59.45% vs. 54.02%) but reduced complete structural compliance (33.3% vs. 42.7%). Verbatim matching establishes source presence rather than evidential relevance. An exploratory comparison using 35 benchmark narratives showed that Qwen3-8B achieved higher concept micro-F1 across all prompting conditions and higher relation F1 under demonstration-based prompting, reaching 51.37% and 34.62%, respectively, under one-shot prompting. The small subset limits generalization. These findings support evaluating semantic correctness, source traceability, structural reliability, and directed relation accuracy separately.

title: Experimental characterisation of compilation-dependent Grover--Rudolph probability distribution loading on a three-qubit NMR processor
abstract: Exact state-preparation circuits are normally judged by how closely the measured output distribution reproduces the target. Using the ancilla-free Grover-Rudolph construction compiled into {Ry, X, CNOT}, we ask instead how much the accuracy of a probability-distribution loading depends on which of several logically equivalent compilations is executed. Two Gray-code realisations of the level-2 uniformly controlled rotation, A and B, differ only in the order of their CNOT controls: same unitary, same angles. On a three-qubit liquid-state NMR processor they do not perform identically. Across 700 runs over seven targets the A/B contrast is significant for 3 of them under Holm, with no fixed sign. Two further campaigns isolate the effect within one unit. Removing the circuit's identity-equivalent gates, which changes the executed schedule but not the unitary, affects the two realisations differently: a ladder x intervention interaction of +0.0625 (95% CI [+0.0306, +0.0944], paired p = 4.8e-4), reversing the sign of the A/B advantage. Across five acquisitions of this one logical circuit the contrast runs from +0.0395 to -0.0229. Not every compilation choice matters: commanding the two level-1 inverse rotations as 720 deg - theta rather than -theta, with the gate list unchanged, moves the mean fidelity by -0.0006 ([-0.0157, +0.0146]) on one target in one session. We offer the order and timing of the executed pulses as the hypothesis these observations favour, without identifying a mechanism. The metric does not certify coherences, and the measured correlators are inconsistent with any global depolarising description: on the uniform target, at a classical fidelity of 0.962, a two-body correlation of +0.217 appears where the target has none. Run-level data and code are deposited for every campaign run on our own unit; the pulse-level campaign is reported from summary tables.

title: Counting Classical Fullerenes VII: Arithmetic Unranking of Fullerene Isomers
abstract: Given a vertex number $2m$ and a rank, we construct the corresponding ordinary fullerene as a planar adjacency list. Choosing the rank uniformly therefore samples ordinary isomorphism classes exactly from the vertex number alone. We select an integral period by counting lattice points on a quadratic level in polytopes with fixed facet directions. For a fixed positive semidefinite integral form on a box of radius $H$, with a linear term of coefficients $O(H)$, the algorithm computes all level counts simultaneously in $O(H^2\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit operations when $H=O(\sqrt m)$ and the facet offsets have $O(\log(2m))$ bits. A signed decomposition into orthogonal simplices gives this bound. For fullerenes we use deterministic $O(m^2\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit work to construct an index of $O(m\log(2m))$ bits. With this index a rank costs $O(m\operatorname{polylog}(2m))$ bit work, uniformly in the rank. Two families of recuts let energy descent escape self-contacts in the slit polygon. The decoder then writes the graph from its selected period in $O(m)$ arithmetic word operations.

title: Most of the Way There: Turning a Strong Video Prior into an Action-Conditioned World Model
abstract: Modern video generators excel at producing visually plausible futures guided by text and image prompts. Yet their emphasis on semantic plausibility does not guarantee fidelity to the physical consequences of specific actions. Action-conditioned world models (ACWMs), in contrast, aim to simulate how the world responds to robot actions, enabling scalable policy evaluation and improvement without costly real-world rollouts. The challenge is not merely to generate a plausible future, but to predict what follows from a specific physical action. As video priors grow stronger, we ask how little adaptation is truly needed to bridge this gap. We introduce Dianjing, a minimal recipe that preserves and unlocks the capabilities of strong video priors through unified physical action conditioning, training concentrated at the high noise levels where motion and layout, and thus the consequences of actions, are decided, and native history conditioning. Built upon MiniMax H3, a 33B video foundation model, Dianjing freezes the pretrained backbone and trains only 0.34% of its parameters using approximately 65 hours of robot video across two embodiments, without additional robot-specific pretraining or camera calibration. Controlled ablations show that where training is allocated across noise levels matters more than how actions enter the network. On WorldOracle, which evaluates predictions against paired real-world executions, Dianjing achieves the best scores on four of the five evaluation tracks and ranks second on AgiBot-Long. Our findings suggest that strong video priors already bring us most of the way to world modeling; lightweight physical action grounding can unlock their potential for real-world prediction.

title: Grounding User Preferences in Shared Multimodal Concepts for Recommendation
abstract: Multimodal recommendation has substantially advanced item understanding by incorporating rich visual and textual content. Yet user preferences are still commonly encoded as implicit signals tied to individual items, leaving recurring semantic factors without persistent identities that can be shared across items. We introduce MKGE, a multimodal knowledge graph framework that represents these factors as canonical, addressable concepts. MKGE induces a domain-adaptive concept vocabulary from item images and titles, grounds each user's interaction history in supported concepts, and jointly models direct user-item evidence and concept-mediated preference signals. By turning recurring semantics into shared coordinates, MKGE enables evidence from different items to accumulate around the same preference factors. Extensive experiments on three public benchmarks demonstrate that MKGE consistently outperforms collaborative, knowledge-graph, multimodal, and recent LLM/MLLM-based recommenders across all six reported metrics. Controlled studies further demonstrate the importance of canonical concept identities and personalized user-concept correspondence, with especially pronounced gains over removing or rewiring the user graph for low-activity users. These results establish canonical multimodal concepts as effective units for preference modeling and transfer. Code, constructed knowledge graphs, and prompts are available at https://github.com/Garden1a-X/MKGE.

title: Graph Parameterization for Invariant Manifolds Attached to Quasi-Periodic Tori
abstract: We develop a high-order Fourier-Taylor graph-parameterization method for computing local invariant manifolds attached to reducible quasi-periodic invariant tori of discrete dynamical systems, with particular emphasis on Poincaré maps. Assuming that the invariant torus and its Floquet reduction are known, we represent the manifold as a graph over a selected spectral subspace and compute its coefficients recursively through jet transport and cohomological equations on the torus. The formulation accommodates stable, unstable, and center spectral selections. For center manifolds, it simultaneously determines the nonlinear reduced dynamics, providing a low-dimensional representation from which nearby invariant objects can be lifted to the original phase space. For real systems with complex-conjugate Floquet multipliers, we derive an equivalent real formulation based on Hermitian symmetry and Krawtchouk transformations. This allows real-valued jet transport while retaining the advantages of complex spectral coordinates in the cohomological solver. The implementation also incorporates inverse dynamics for stable directions, multiple shooting, coordinate scaling, and a posteriori validation tests. Numerical experiments with a quasi-periodically forced pendulum, an oscillating solar sail in the Earth-Moon system, and a simplified solar system model illustrate the construction and its computational properties. In the solar-sail benchmark, the real formulation reduces computation time by approximately a factor of 2.2 compared with the complex implementation.

title: Lighting up LZ with Loopy Transitions in a leptophilic Dark Sector
abstract: We study the direct detection phenomenology and cosmology of a multicomponent dark sector with a leptophilic t-channel portal. The coupling to right-handed Standard Model leptons is mediated by a charged vector-like fermion, allowing both a scalar and a vector dark candidate to connect to the SM through the same mediator. Motivated by the high-energy nuclear-recoil event recently reported by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment, we consider a nearly degenerate dark sector with mass splittings of order a few hundred keV and investigate the resulting inelastic transitions. Concretely, we focus on endothermic scattering of the dark states, which can shift the recoil spectrum towards the high-energy region preferred by LZ while suppressing low-energy events. We scrutinize the effective operators generating the dark-matter-photon coupling, which provides the essential interaction for nuclear recoils. Interestingly, the inelastic transition arises at dimension five whereas elastic scattering on nuclei is induced only at dimension six. This naturally explains the prominence of endothermic scattering compared to its elastic counterpart. We determine the parameter space compatible with the observed dark matter abundance and scrutinize the event rate and signal shape for scattering on xenon. Our results demonstrate that the observation of a single $E_R=248\pm 46$ keV nuclear recoil event in LZ can be accommodated by thermally produced dark matter in a leptophilic dark sector.

title: Inverted Pendulum in the Sky: Floquet Stabilization of Cosmological Axions
abstract: Many cosmological scenarios require a scalar field to sit near the top of its potential, which usually requires a fine-tuned initial condition. We ask whether the hilltop of an axion potential can be dynamically stabilized by a rapidly oscillating coupling, as for the inverted pendulum of Kapitza, and to what extent this can reduce the fine-tuning. Using Floquet theory, we determine the stability window of the hilltop and analyze several realizations: an oscillating coupling, a spinning or oscillating second field, and a gyroscopic analogue, an inverted spinning top realized by a sigma model on a squashed three-sphere. In an expanding Universe the stabilized phase lasts for a number of $e$-folds logarithmic in the hierarchy of scales, independently of the cosmological background. Classifying the stabilizers by how their effective frequency redshifts, we show that in these realizations the hilltop cannot both attract the field and leave it frozen by the Hubble friction during radiation or matter domination, and that during inflation the attraction is limited by the Hubble friction and the energy budget. Thus the simple realizations studied here do not generically remove the hilltop fine-tuning. They can instead delay the onset of the oscillation and enhance the relic abundance as $n_ϕ/n_{ϕ,{\rm std}}\propto(\tilde m/H_c)^{3/2}$ in radiation domination. We discuss the implications for axion dark matter, inflation, quintessence and curvatons.

title: vSFT: Learning to Verbally Tune Agents at Test Time
abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly improved via agentic reinforcement learning, which can be on-policy but suffers from expensive rollouts and sparse rewards, limiting its application at test time. In this paper, we present a verbally Supervised Fine-Tuning (vSFT) framework that enables the conjunction of dense feedback in natural language and weight updates at test time. Specifically, our vSFT forms a closed loop between an agent and a supervisor via a hypernetwork, in which the supervisor generates verbal supervision from the agent's failed trajectories, and the hypernetwork converts that supervision into low-rank weight updates to tune the agent. We validate that this test-time in-parameter evolving process outperforms both its in-context counterparts and prevalent reinforcement learning methods. In particular, our vSFT using Qwen3-4B outperforms GRPO and Reflexion by 8.7% and 13.9% in success rate on ALFWorld, and by 4.8% and 18.2% on WebShop, respectively. We believe that learning how to adapt a model, rather than an adapted model, offers a promising path towards more capable agents that improve themselves.

title: Full-waveform inversion with adaptive anisotropic Gaussian primitives
abstract: Reparameterizing the velocity model has emerged as an effective way to regularize full-waveform inversion (FWI) and reduce its sensitivity to the starting model. Existing parameterizations, however, either fix the position and shape of every basis function in advance, as in grids and splines, or control the spatial structure of their updates only indirectly through the shared weights of a neural network. We propose Gauss-FWI, which represents the velocity perturbation as a sum of anisotropic Gaussian primitives with learnable amplitudes, centres, scales, and orientations. The basis itself thus adapts to the subsurface. Primitives move onto interfaces, stretch along layers, and rotate with the dip, so model updates follow the geological structure without a hand-designed regularizer. A gradient-energy criterion adds finer zero-amplitude primitives where the data call for more detail, increasing resolution progressively without perturbing the current model. All parameters receive analytic gradients through the adjoint-state method on a fixed simulation grid, so the representation fits into existing FWI workflows and combines directly with frequency continuation. Each primitive keeps an explicit position, extent, and orientation, and the representation Jacobian links the waveform gradient to the resulting model update, which makes the behaviour of the inversion interpretable. In two-dimensional acoustic examples, Gauss-FWI uses about fifty times fewer parameters than implicit FWI and recovers the Marmousi, Overthrust, and BP salt models more accurately than grid, multiscale, B-spline, and implicit parameterizations. It remains accurate under missing low frequencies, noise, and discretization mismatch, and it recovers the main structure from starting models where the other methods fail, such as a linear model without the BP salt body.

title: The Weak Negotiation Function
abstract: Subgame-perfect equilibria (SPEs) constitute a refinement of Nash equilibria, where the players are not allowed to resort to non-credible threats to discourage deviations. In graph games equipped with a broad class of objectives, SPEs are captured by a tool called the negotiation function. After giving a quick overview of what has already been achieved using this tool, we define a variant of it: the weak negotiation function. We show that weak SPEs, a standard relaxation of SPEs, can be captured by the weak negotiation function exactly like SPEs are captured by the negotiation function. This characterisation yields a new computational result: deciding whether a given game contains a weak SPE where each player's payoff lies in a given interval is an NP-complete problem if the game has mean-payoff objectives. We also provide a new proof that the same problem in Büchi games is in P. The proofs reuse many arguments from their SPE counterpart, demonstrating the robustness of the tool. We also use the weak negotiation function to present a new proof, significantly shorter than the known one, of the existence of weak SPEs in mean-payoff games. We argue that those new techniques should be reusable in other settings, in particular to prove an open conjecture about the existence of randomised $ε$-SPEs in mean-payoff games.

title: Prandtl Batchelor flow in a Periodic Channel with Counter Moving Walls
abstract: We study the vanishing viscosity limit of steady two dimensional incompressible Navier Stokes flows in a horizontally periodic channel with counter moving walls. The prescribed wall velocities are small periodic perturbations of constant velocities with opposite signs. The Batchelor Wood relations select an affine Euler shear with constant vorticity and a unique interior zero. We establish the existence of steady Navier Stokes solutions that are uniformly approximated by the selected Euler shear together with two Prandtl boundary layers. Moreover, the vorticity converges locally uniformly to the selected constant vorticity. The principal analytical difficulty is the loss of global coercivity caused by the interior zero of the Euler shear. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness rigidity argument that combines signed near wall positivity estimates, interior vorticity estimates, adjoint tests eliminating the affine limiting modes, and a streamline circulation equation ruling out concentration near the walls. These ingredients yield an estimate for the linearized inverse, which, together with a high order Euler Prandtl approximation, enables us to solve the nonlinear error equations. Our result provides a rigorous realization of the Prandtl Batchelor selection principle in a periodic channel with counter moving walls.

title: Black hole entropy from angular holonomies of Sine-Gordon soliton lattices in AdS$_3$
abstract: We construct boundary conditions for AdS$_3$ gravity that realize Sine-Gordon dynamics. For a periodic soliton lattice at fixed winding, we relate the angular holonomy to the exact acoustic dispersion by continuing the Bloch momentum through the zero-frequency band edge associated with rigid translation of the lattice. For suitable embedding angles, the stable vacuum has a regular BTZ geometry. When only one chiral sector carries winding, we construct a family whose asymptotic region extends to a BTZ black hole. As the spectral parameter of the winding sector tends to the corresponding band edge, the black hole approaches extremality. The leading correction to the extremal entropy is linear in the Hawking temperature defined with respect to laboratory time, with a coefficient inversely proportional to the sound velocity of the lattice. The same inverse-velocity dependence appears in the low-temperature entropy of one-dimensional quantum fluids.

title: Travelling-Wave-Based Protection of DC Hubs in Bipolar HVDC Grids
abstract: This paper presents a stationary wavelet transform (SWT)-based method for DC fault detection and classification in a three-terminal bipolar modular multilevel converter (MMC)-based HVDC system with a dedicated metallic return (DMR). The system incorporates DC switching stations (DCSSs) with interconnected DC circuit breakers (DCCBs). The method uses line-mode voltage wavelet detail energy for fault detection and wavelet detail energy derived from pole voltages and DMR current for fault classification, distinguishing pole-to-pole, pole-to-ground, and pole-to-DMR faults. Its performance is evaluated using a real-time hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) platform integrating an real-time digital simulator (RTDS) with embedded processing hardware. Busbar and cable faults with varying fault types, resistances, and locations are investigated. The results demonstrate the feasibility of real-time implementation and characterize the effects of fault location and travelling-wave propagation on transient energy and protection response time. The effectiveness of pole-voltage and DMR-current detail energy features in distinguishing fault types is also evaluated.

title: PreserveReward: Reliable Consistency Reward Modeling for Image Editing via Dual-Teacher On-Policy Self-Distillation
abstract: Instruction-guided image editing has a wide range of applications, yet existing models may inadvertently alter content that should remain unchanged. Reliable consistency evaluation is therefore essential for assessing content preservation and providing reward signals for Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, existing reward models may overlook subtle visual changes or fail to distinguish necessary modifications from unintended alterations, limiting the reliability of consistency assessment. To address this challenge, we propose PreserveReward, a consistency reward model for image editing that integrates visual On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) to enhance fine-grained visual perception and consistency assessment. PreserveReward learns from reference preservation scores through a regression-based scoring loss and employs two complementary teacher views for self-distillation. The local teacher uses matched crops to identify subtle visual changes, while the joint teacher combines local details with global context to determine whether these changes align with the editing intent. To improve the reliability of distillation supervision, we calibrate teacher score distributions via minimum-KL projection under reference-score error constraints and adaptively select teacher process supervision based on gradient alignment with the scoring objective, mitigating scoring bias and optimization conflicts. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that PreserveReward achieves strong alignment with human preference on non-edited content preservation and generalizes well across diverse editing scenarios.

title: Optimal \texorpdfstring{$(1,1)$}{(1,1)}-Criss-Cross Deletion-Correcting Codes with Linear-Time Encoder and Decoder
abstract: We consider a $q$-ary $n\times n$ array subject to a $(1,1)$-criss-cross deletion, which removes one row and one column. We first derive a sphere-packing type lower bound on the redundancy of codes correcting such deletions. For every $q\geq 2$ and $n\geq 27$, the redundancy is greater than $2n+2\log_q n-2$. For fixed $q$, it is at least $2n-1+2\log_q n-o_q(1)$ as $n\to\infty$. We then present two code constructions. The first construction achieves redundancy $2n-1+2\log_q n+o_q(1)$ by selecting a largest syndrome class. It matches the lower bound up to a vanishing term and admits $O_q(n^2)$-time decoding. The second construction has redundancy $2n+2\log_q n+O_q(1)$ and admits $O_q(n^2)$-time algorithms for both encoding and decoding. For fixed $q$, these running times are linear in the number of array entries.

title: Quantum dynamics of a charged particle on rotating curved surfaces and space curves in electromagnetic fields
abstract: We develop a gauge-consistent framework for a charged particle confined to a rotating curved manifold in an electromagnetic field, starting from the covariant Klein--Gordon equation. The non-relativistic reduction casts the rotational effects as effective gauge potentials while preserving the $U(1)$ symmetry, so that rotation and the external field enter alike, the geometry entering separately as the da Costa potential. The obstruction to dimensional reduction is gauge--geometry entanglement: transverse magnetic fields on a two-dimensional (2D) surface and structural torsion on a one-dimensional (1D) curve couple the tangential dynamics to the transverse degrees of freedom. We remove this entanglement by three mechanisms---a generalized transverse Poincaré gauge, the rotation-minimizing Bishop frame, and the parity of the transverse ground state, the last of which annihilates the residual first-order magnetic coupling for a single inversion-symmetric well. On a torus, an axial field generates a joint Sagnac--Aharonov--Bohm residual of tunable sign without spoiling the poloidal--azimuthal separability, whereas an in-plane field couples only through the out-of-plane extent of the structure: it breaks the axial symmetry there but leaves a planar curve unaffected to first order. The same torus shows the axial field tuning the curvature-induced localization, and a corrugated quantum ring converts periodic geometric and flux modulations into an artificial superlattice whose in-plane-field immunity follows from planarity and parity, not from the smallness of the field. Non-inertial quantum dynamics on surfaces and curves of arbitrary shape is thus reduced, within the thin-layer regime, to two ingredients: an effective gauge potential and a geometric potential.

title: HoloBrain-0.5 Technical Report
abstract: We present HoloBrain-0.5, a family of vision-language-action (VLA) models for manipulation across robot embodiments. The policies plan in a shared action space using robot state, kinematic structure, and calibrated camera observations. We standardize joint axes, coordinate frames, and tool-center points in robot descriptions (URDFs) and encode their kinematic graphs in a shared 3D representation. HoloBrain-0.5-Continuous generates action chunks by diffusion, while HoloBrain-0.5-Discrete uses residual finite scalar quantization (FSQ) and delayed autoregression. We pretrain both policies on over 10,000 hours of real-robot, simulation, and human-manipulation data spanning 15 embodiment categories. Across six closed-loop simulation settings, the discrete policy converges faster and reaches a higher mean success rate than the continuous policy (56.77% vs. 49.71%). On seven real-robot tasks, it achieves a mean progress score of 87.76% without task-specific post-training. After post-training, the continuous policy outperforms $π_{0.5}$ on the seven-task benchmark (94.52% vs. 86.25%) and an 11-task dual-arm benchmark (79.07% vs. 69.41%). The discrete-initialized continuous policy transfers five tasks zero-shot from Piper to Piper-X, scoring 63.28% on average. With target-robot demonstrations, the continuous policy scores 89.2% on Franka Panda and 92.94% on a mobile dual-arm platform. Although pretraining includes no Unitree G1 data, post-training with limited G1 demonstrations yields a mean progress score of 70.24% across three humanoid tasks, compared with 11.00% for $π_{0.5}$.

title: Investigating the Neupert Effect with HEL1OS/Aditya-L1
abstract: We investigate the Neupert effect in solar flares using broadband hard X-ray observations from the HEL1OS instrument onboard Aditya-L1. By separating thermal and non-thermal components from HEL1OS spectrograms, we analyse a sample of 312 flares observed between November 2023 and May 2026. We find that the soft X-ray flux is strongly correlated with the time-integrated hard X-ray emission, with a median correlation coefficient of 0.984, indicating that Neupert-like behaviour is nearly ubiquitous in flares with detectable non-thermal emission. Extending beyond statistical correlation, we develop an empirical forward model in which the thermal lightcurve is reconstructed from the non-thermal emission by resolving the hard X-ray lightcurve into individual energy-release episodes and convolving their fitted profiles with finite thermal-response functions. This approach successfully reproduces the observed thermal evolution, including flares that exhibit quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs). Our results demonstrate that the broadband HEL1OS observations sample both thermal-dominated and non-thermal-dominated flare emission within a single instrument, providing an observation-driven link between the temporal structure of non-thermal HXR emission and the thermal X-ray response. This provides a different framework for interpreting flare energetics and temporal evolution using broadband hard X-ray measurements.

title: Decision-Aligned Value Learning for Selective Adoption of EEG Fusion in Human-Robot Collaboration
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) captures neural activity associated with human perception and decision-making. It provides human-robot collaboration (HRC) systems with measurable evidence for event recognition, situation assessment, and action preparation. External sensing cannot easily provide such evidence. However, the quality and complementarity of this evidence vary across samples, and existing EEG fusion methods do not explicitly determine when EEG improves a prediction. We therefore framed selective EEG use as a sample-wise incremental-value estimation problem and proposed Value Estimation and Constraint-Aware Triage for Adoption (VECTA). VECTA separates the generation of an EEG-informed Fusion prediction from the decision about whether it should replace the existing Base prediction. The framework uses system gain to quantify the loss reduction from Base to Fusion and matching gain to assess whether benefits arise from sample-matched EEG. A signed-value learner estimates system gain from decision-time evidence and prioritizes high-value Fusion outputs under budget constraints. Cross-subject evaluations on three HRC datasets showed that matched Fusion outperformed shuffled controls. Estimated gains tracked realized gains, with Spearman correlations of 0.347-0.612 and positive-gain areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) of 0.708-0.842. Under budget constraints, VECTA reduced Brier loss and harmful Fusion adoption and achieved the highest mean normalized AUBC across three datasets among the selective-decision methods evaluated. Validation on three external multi-modal datasets showed that VECTA could be applied directly as a post-hoc decision layer to task-specific predictors without retraining. These results show that selective Fusion adoption can translate the uneven utility of EEG into system-level gains.

title: Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit
abstract: Solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) constitutes a core task in many engineering and scientific disciplines. Physics-informed neural networks and the deep Galerkin method effectively leverage machine learning models to approximate solutions of known PDEs by minimizing residuals corresponding to the PDE operator alongside external constraints. Although second-order optimizers are becoming increasingly popular for training neural networks (NNs) to solve PDEs and empirically outperform their first-order counterparts in both speed and accuracy, the convergence theory for training such models is essentially confined to first-order methods. In this paper, we close this gap and develop a convergence analysis for the regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton methods. As the number of hidden units tends to infinity, the training dynamics converge in probability, with explicit rates, to the solution of a deterministic limit equation involving a Newton neural tangent kernel operator associated with the PDE. Although the limiting kernel operator admits no spectral gap, we prove that, in the overparameterized limit, the PDE residual vanishes as training proceeds, and, under mild assumptions, the NN converges to the PDE solution. We further show that, provided a sufficiently small regularization parameter, the projection of the residual onto any fixed number of leading eigenfunctions decays exponentially fast, demonstrating that this hyperparameter acts as a spectral filter: it lifts the convergence rates of high-frequency components toward those of low-frequency ones, thereby mitigating the spectral bias inherent in gradient descent. Mathematical challenges arise from the implicit parameter update involving a linear system whose dimension increases with the NN width and, for Newton's method, a potentially indefinite Hessian, as well as from the PDE operator entering the kernel.

title: DynaRC: Dynamics-Robust 4-D Radar Relocalization with Rate-Adaptive Sequence Matching
abstract: Four-dimensional millimeter-wave radar measures radial velocity within a single scan and remains resilient under adverse weather and visibility. Yet sparse directional returns, moving objects and occlusion make place matching ambiguous. We propose DynaRC, a dynamics-robust framework encompassing single-frame retrieval and sequence relocalization. Doppler evidence separates static returns and masks motion-affected cells in a polar descriptor; median ring keys retrieve candidates. Its sequence variant, Seq_DynaRC, couples endpoint-anchored rate alignment and candidate-index voting with ordered verification to associate the latest scan under unequal map/query advancement, without odometry or cloud accumulation. Across four indoor and outdoor map--query pairs, Seq_DynaRC achieves the highest conditional localization success within 2m among tested methods. On a campus-road revisit under changing traffic, success reaches 91.8%, exceeding descriptor-matched SeqSLAM by 55.0 percentage points when each method retains all its published outputs; output availability is reported separately. Code and indoor/outdoor dynamic 4D radar data are available.

title: Solitons as conversion events in quadratic crystals
abstract: In a $χ^{(2)}$ crystal with temporal walk-off and negligible dispersion, signal, idler and pump pulses obey the integrable three-wave interaction. For a pump of intermediate group velocity we describe each soliton as a conversion event: the fusion of a signal--idler pair into a pump pulse, or the decay of a pump pulse, at a definite depth in the crystal. The asymptotic $\mathrm{sech}$ pulses, usually treated with three separate $2\times2$ scattering problems, are the legs of the event, a single pole of the $3\times3$ problem. For one event we give the conversion curve in closed form and the minimum crystal length; for several events, the rule by which they displace each other. A pump pulse is unstable, and its growing mode is the tail of a decay event: a seed carrying a fraction $\varepsilon$ of the photons along this mode makes the pulse decay after $Γ^{-1}\ln(c_+/\varepsilon)$, with $Γ$ the conversion rate and $c_+$ of order one. Unmatched signal and idler pulses form the resonance of Kaup, Reiman and Bers; we show that it is a fusion followed by a decay, each within a conversion length, and give its pump photon number in closed form. Since the delay between the input pulses sets the depth of the vertex, these quantities can be read on the output face of a single crystal; we give the scales for periodically poled KTiOPO$_4$.

title: Exact Lyapunov spectrum and localization length of the multichannel disordered Schrödinger equation
abstract: We consider the multichannel Schrödinger equation, describing the evolution of $N$ transverse modes in a finite width wire, in the presence of a Gaussian white noise potential in the unitary symmetry class. For arbitrary energy $E$ and disorder strength $T$, we compute exactly the set of Lyapunov exponents $\{ γ_n(E,T) \}_{1 \leq n \leq N}$ which define the decay rates of the wave functions. In the large energy regime, we recover that the Lyapunov exponents are equally spaced, as predicted by the so-called DMPK approach. However we show that this property breaks down at arbitrary energy, giving rise to a richer Lyapunov spectrum. We also uncover a direct relation between the localization length, given by the inverse of the smallest Lyapunov exponent, and the density of states. Our derivation relies on the analysis of matrix stochastic differential equation for a modified Riccati matrix.

title: Existence of odd-frequency free boundary points in the Signorini problem
abstract: Up to a lower-dimensional set, the free boundary of the Signorini problem consists of points with frequency that is half-integer, even (at zero density points), or odd (at full density points). Surprisingly, despite extensive work on the structure and regularity of each of these sets, the existence of odd-frequency free boundary points has remained open. In this paper, we construct a solution with a free boundary point of frequency 3.

title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation
abstract: Recent video generators produce realistic videos, yet controlling how scenes unfold remains challenging. Structural proxies, such as animated 3D blockouts, guide generation by specifying scene layout, motion, camera behavior, and event order. However, these coarse inputs leave details unspecified and may contain artifacts that should not be reproduced. Successful proxy-guided generation must therefore Preserve intended structure, Complete missing content and correct proxy artifacts, and Bind text, image, and audio conditions to the right entities and events. We introduce ProxyGenBench to study these interacting requirements, with 312 evaluation cases from 60 scenes across three scene tasks and controlled variations in proxy fidelity, text detail, and multimodal inputs. We evaluate five video generators using verified, case-specific checklists. Experiments show that proxies improve spatiotemporal control, but greater proxy detail can coincide with poorer completion, while strong structural adherence does not ensure correct binding.

title: Very fast 2D inversions of Stokes profiles using neural emulators
abstract: We aim to carry out fast, spatio-temporally regularized inversions of full fields of view, optionally including the PSF of the telescope, for both photospheric and chromospheric spectral lines. We replace the forward model by fast, precise, and differentiable neural emulators trained on synthetic Stokes profiles. Neural surrogate models are used to emulate the Stokes profiles of the Fe I doublet at 6302 A, the Ca II line at 8542 A as well as the Si I line and He I multiplet at 10830 A. These emulators are then used in a fast inversion code that includes spatial regularization terms and can compensate for the aberrations of the telescope. The emulators are unbiased, with errors that are, in most cases, comparable to or below the noise of current observations in the polarization profiles. Inversions of large fields-of-view can be carried out in minutes in a off-the-shelf GPU, opening up the possibility of real-time analysis of large-scale solar observations. We provide a few illustrative examples. Emulators open up the option of inverting lines with very complex and time consuming forward models.

title: Uphill Diffusion in Yukawa Plasmas
abstract: In a fluid mixture of many species an individual species can diffuse toward higher concentration without any external driving force because its flux is coupled to the gradients of other components. Such `uphill diffusion' is well known in the chemical and metallurgy literature but to our knowledge has not been studied for strongly coupled plasmas in neutron star and white dwarf interiors. We have previously developed a semi-analytic diffusion model that accurately predicts diffusion coefficients of individual species in a mixture in equilibrium. Uphill diffusion allows us to test this model out of equilibrium, and also test a generalized Darken relation for predicting diffusivities. We derive an analytic theory and compare to three-component molecular dynamics simulations and find very good agreement. This provides a novel out-of-equilibrium test of the generalization of our diffusion model to arbitrary multi-component mixtures.

title: Functional Factor Graphs and the Functional Sum-Product Algorithm
abstract: We propose a generalization of factor graphs and the sum-product algorithm (SPA), widely used in the estimation of data, channel state information and sensing parameters, to unknowns that are functions, such as waveforms, time-varying channels and continuous-aperture array currents, which must otherwise be sampled first. In order to mitigate the challenge that functions have no probability density functions (PDFs), the proposed scheme measures densities relative to the prior of each function, not to the flat reference implicit in every PDF. Messages then become likelihood ratios, and the factor-node rule an average over the priors, still exact on trees. For Gaussian models, the proposed functional SPA (FSPA) is Gaussian belief propagation (GaBP) with kernels in place of matrices and a grid-independent convergence condition, whereas scalar GaBP on grid samples provably slows down under refinement, as information hops from sample to sample. Simulations in a multi-user detection setting confirms the latter, and shows that sampling first can also fail for smooth priors.

title: SceneDesigner++: A Unified 9-DoF Pose Control Framework for T2I and T2V Generation
abstract: Precise 9-DoF pose control is essential for visual content generation, enabling users to specify object location, size, and orientation in 3D space. However, existing methods typically focus on either text-to-image (T2I) or text-to-video (T2V) generation, with limitations in pose controllability and temporal coherence. We present SceneDesigner++, a unified framework for 9-DoF pose control across both T2I and T2V generation. We construct ObjectPose9D++, a dataset containing high-quality images and videos with accurate pose annotations. Trained on ObjectPose9D++, SceneDesigner++ combines absolute and relative pose encoding strategies to decouple frame-wise spatial grounding from inter-frame motion modeling. Specifically, absolute pose encoding leverages CNOCS map sequences to provide explicit, frame-wise 9-DoF pose guidance. Meanwhile, our relative pose encoding, termed VPRoPE, incorporates relative pose information into rotary position embeddings to explicitly model inter-frame pose transitions, thereby promoting temporally coherent object motion. A learnable orthogonal transformation is further introduced for each attention head, allowing different heads to capture complementary geometric relationships while preserving input feature norms to promote training stability. We further adopt a two-stage training strategy to learn the absolute and relative pose encoding mechanisms separately. Benefiting from this lightweight and decoupled design, SceneDesigner++ also supports integration with an independently trained camera-control module, enabling separate or joint control over object and camera motion. Finally, we introduce T2IVPoseEval, a benchmark for evaluating diverse object poses and motion patterns in both T2I and T2V tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SceneDesigner++ consistently outperforms same-backbone baselines in pose fidelity and motion quality.

title: Same Seed, Different Top Prediction: Cross-Platform Reproducibility of AlphaFold 3 Inference on TPUs, GPUs, and CPUs
abstract: AlphaFold 3 returns the highest-ranked of several sampled structures and computes each prediction on one device. Computing centers may schedule them on different GPU types or CPU nodes. Floating-point results can differ between devices, so the same input and seed may return another structure. Neither AlphaFold 3's documentation nor its outputs warn of this. We measure how often the device changes the returned structure, and tell users what to report and how to make devices agree. We used identical inputs, weights, seeds, and settings on two Google tensor processing unit (TPU) generations (v5e, v6e), three NVIDIA GPUs (L4, A100, H100), and an Intel Xeon CPU. On 60 protein-ligand complexes, with five seeds each, switching TPU generations changed the top-ranked sample in 18.0% of 300 predictions. Recompiling never changed it on either TPU, but did so in 7.3% on the L4 GPU. Yet the structures barely moved. The top-ranked pose switched between correct and incorrect in 3.3% to 3.7% of predictions, against about 10% for a new seed. These switches nearly always came from one validity check, with the ligand within 2 angstroms. Follow-ups found the effect again on 72 new targets and between the TPUs and the CPU. Between the A100 and H100 it exceeded recompilation, although AlphaFold 3's developers verified its numerical accuracy on both. An exploratory analysis links the changes to near-tied candidates. We recommend reporting the device and every near-tied sample. A float32 trunk with full-precision matrix products made all five accelerators agree on nearly every prediction.

title: Least Restrictive Halfplane Control Barrier Functions for an Autonomous Hydrofoil Boat with Moving Obstacles
abstract: Finding valid Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) is difficult for non-linear systems subject to actuation constraints and moving in complex environments. One way to enable analytically derived CBFs is to represent obstacles as supporting halfplanes, allowing the agent to move safely on one side. In this paper, we propose such a CBF for an agent with Dubins car dynamics. A potential drawback of halfplane CBFs is that they can be highly conservative, overestimating the obstacles and thereby restricting the agent's motion. To address this problem, we make the CBF halfplanes less restrictive as follows. First, the orientation of the supporting halfplane for a single obstacle is optimised to find a safe control input as close as possible to the desired one. Second, we use multiple halfplanes to better approximate complex geometries, and derive rules for handling halfplane intersections. Comparative simulations show that our method reduces conservatism compared to existing CBF techniques, enabling tighter obstacle clearance and faster goal arrival, with delays reduced by more than 33%. Finally, experiments on an autonomous hydrofoil boat demonstrate successful real-world implementation.

title: Ultralight Dark Matter Spectrum with Gravitational Focusing and Doppler Motion
abstract: Ultralight dark matter can produce signals in experiments through its couplings with the Standard Model particles. The resulting signal spectrum is determined by the phase-space distribution of dark matter, which encodes information about its production mechanism and the history of the local universe. However, the local environmental effects can modify the observed spectrum and should be included in signal modeling to avoid biased parameter estimates. In this work, we investigate how the gravitational focusing by Sun and the Doppler effect due to the detector's motion modify the signal spectrum and affect inferring the underlying dark matter parameters. We analytically estimate the signal significance and perform Bayesian analysis on simulated data to demonstrate their impact.

title: Evidence-Aligned Benchmarking and Learning for Medical Video Language Models
abstract: A medical video language model should answer from the visual evidence its question asks about. We find three places where this breaks down and address each with an approach we call MedEvidU. First, benchmarks reward answers that ignore the video: on one dataset, the position of a clip within its recording predicts the surgical step in 37% of questions, and a constant answer beats every trained model on a standard safety-assessment metric. We build MedVidBench-v2, 34 tasks from 18 surgical and clinical video datasets, in which prompts and metrics are audited with answers given without video, and which tests unseen hospitals and windows cut blindly from whole recordings. Second, common video encoders merge consecutive frames into shared tokens, so a question about one frame is answered from a blend of two. Query-slot inputs give each queried frame its own tokens at almost no extra cost. Third, a fine-tuned model has memorized its training questions, which leaves little to learn from. Label-matched question resampling (LQR) adds unseen questions about the same recordings while keeping the answer distribution fixed, in a final supervised epoch and in reinforcement learning. Together, these raise the grounding IoU of a 4B model from 30.4 to 44.4, above a supervised 27B model, and instrument grounding at an unseen hospital from 33.9 to 72.5. On blindly cut windows, event-presence accuracy improves by 5.5 points and localization F1 by 8.1 points. Project page: https://gaozhongpai.github.io/MedEvidU/

title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
abstract: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. Through first-person observations, agents can identify objects and activities relevant to user requests and ground digital tasks in the surrounding context. We call this interaction paradigm Ego Use. However, first-person observations are limited by the wearer's viewpoint and may provide incomplete or ambiguous evidence of ongoing activities. As new observations arrive, agents may need to revise their understanding of the physical context and user intent, and reassess whether prior digital actions remain valid. Whether current agents can reliably handle these changes remains insufficiently evaluated. We introduce EgoUseBench, a benchmark for evaluating Ego Use across three interaction settings with different levels of first-person context. Computer-Use relies on explicit instructions, Offline Ego Use provides prerecorded first-person context before execution, and Online Ego Use provides continuous observations as user intent evolves. Based on over 74 hours of real-world first-person recordings, we construct 693 tasks across the three interaction settings. To capture task evolution, we track first-person observations, user requirements, and website state separately. We further group tasks by how information changes during execution, resulting in three types: Graft (revised user requirements), Refresh (new first-person observations), and Clarify (agent-initiated information seeking). We evaluate advanced models and find that average success rates in Online Ego Use are 26.3% lower than in Computer-Use. This result reveals the difficulty of keeping task execution aligned with evolving first-person context and user intent.

title: Attacking Hard-Label Large Vision-Language Models with Model-Sensitive Adversarial Patch Designs
abstract: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in handling multi-modal downstream tasks, gaining increasing popularity. However, recent studies show that LVLMs are susceptible to both intentional and inadvertent attacks. Existing attackers ideally optimize adversarial perturbations with backpropagated gradients from LVLMs, thus limiting their scalability in practical scenarios as real-world LVLM applications will not provide any LVLM's gradient or details. Motivated by this research gap and counter-practical phenomenon, we propose a novel hard-label attack method for LVLMs, named HardPatch, to generate visual adversarial patches by solely querying the model. Our method provides deeper insights into how to investigate the vulnerability of LVLMs in local visual regions and generate corresponding adversarial substitution under the practical yet challenging hard-label setting. Specifically, we first split each image into uniform patches and mask each of them to individually assess their sensitivity to the LVLM model. Then, according to the descending order of sensitive scores, we iteratively select the most vulnerable patch to initialize noise and estimate gradients with further additive random noises for optimization. In this manner, multiple patches are perturbed until the altered image satisfies the adversarial condition. Extensive LVLM models and datasets are evaluated to demonstrate the adversarial nature of HardPatch. Our empirical observations suggest that with appropriate patch substitution and optimization, HardPatch can craft effective adversarial images to attack hard-label LVLMs.

title: Exponential Analysis for Trace-Distance Errors in Quantum Information Theory
abstract: We study the trace-distance error in classical-quantum soft covering, privacy amplification against quantum side information, convex splitting, and decoupling by a Haar-random unitary followed by partial trace. In the independent and identically distributed setting, we determine exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for soft covering with independent codewords, uniform convex splitting, and Haar partial-trace decoupling. For privacy amplification, we determine the exact reliability function for independent random binning and the exact strong converse exponent for every two-universal hash ensemble. The reliability and strong converse formulas involve sandwiched and Petz-Rényi information, respectively. The proofs connect trace-distance errors to quantum hypothesis testing, using Rosenthal inequalities for sums of random matrices in the reliability analysis and conditional second-moment bounds for the strong converses.

title: Infinite Hyper-Order of Entire Solutions of a First-Order Differential Equation
abstract: Let $φ$ be a transcendental entire function of finite order. We prove that every entire solution of $$g'=e^φg+1$$ has infinite hyper-order. Then we prove the Brück's conjecture.

title: Fuel as Identity: Authenticating Inter-Satellite Laser Links after Total Key Compromise
abstract: Optical inter-satellite links form the backbone of entire constellations in low Earth orbit, yet their security rests on keys alone. When an attacker obtains every key of a satellite, no secret is left to authenticate it again. Existing fixes fail, since ground rekeying encrypts new keys under the leaked ones, and post-compromise protocols assume an authenticated start. As a remedy, the satellite's orbit can take over as the trust anchor. The attacker then needs an impostor satellite that blocks and retransmits the beam, a chord beneath the curved orbit. Hence, the blocking point lies off free fall and costs the impostor continuous thrust. We formalize this position-gated adversary and prove, for satellites on a shared circular orbit, a tight lower bound on the propellant cost in delta-v of a point-mass craft that keeps blocking, however it moves. We present OrbitLock, a history-chained protocol that combines this position gate with ML-KEM. Each link authenticates on its own, and we sketch how combining links forces an impostor onto every link. Once the chain outlasts an impostor's propellant, every key back to the first is authenticated retroactively. A satellite thus needs no crosslink key before launch, so none can leak in the supply chain. The same mechanism heals the link after total key compromise, even without compromise awareness. A passive attacker is shut out at the next round, whereas an active one splits the chains and is exposed once its propellant runs out. The chain can then heal after an operator reset. As a result, every Starlink satellite has a partner on whose link a CubeSat-class impostor runs out of propellant in about two days. This holds against one rigid craft per link running the best attack we know, if each terminal enforces a 1 km exclusion zone, while the protocol only uses under 0.02% of the link.

title: Signatures of multiorbital density waves in the electronic Raman response of bilayer nickelates
authors: Luis G. G. V. Dias da Silva
abstract: Recent Raman scattering experiments on bilayer nickelates have revealed pronounced spectral features in the spin-density-wave state, whose microscopic origin remains controversial, with interpretations ranging from two-magnon excitations to electronic transitions across SDW-induced gaps. Here, we demonstrate that the multiorbital electronic structure of low-pressure bilayer nickelates naturally generates distinct orbital-selective Raman signatures in different symmetry channels. Using a two-orbital bilayer model incorporating the $d_{3z^2-r^2}$ and $d_{x^2-y^2}$ orbitals in the orthorhombic structure, we analyze the electronic Raman response of the multiorbital spin-spinless double stripe SDW state and show that the $B_{2g}$ response exhibits a peak at the energy scale $(M_{z^2}+M_{x^2})/2$, associated with SDW gap openings in weakly hybridized bands. In contrast, the dominant peak in the $B_{1g}$ channel emerges at the multiorbital energy scale $(M_{z^2}^2+M_{x^2}^2)^{1/2}$, reflecting the strongly hybridized character of the relevant electronic states. These distinct energy scales provide a unified interpretation of several Raman signatures observed in La$_3$Ni$_2$O$_7$ and offer a means of disentangling the orbital contributions to the SDW order parameters. Our results highlight that in contrast to the superconducting state, Raman peak positions in the SDW state cannot generally be identified with a single SDW gap and establish symmetry-resolved electronic Raman scattering as a sensitive probe of multiorbital density-wave order.

title: DiversePlace: Diversity-Seeking Curriculum Reinforcement Learning for Macro Placement
abstract: Macro placement is a critical early-stage decision in physical design because macro locations strongly constrain subsequent implementation stages. The task is difficult because these high-impact discrete decisions must be made before downstream quality can be measured accurately, forcing training to rely on fast but imperfect training-time oracles such as half-perimeter wirelength (HPWL). Existing RL-based placers therefore mostly optimize single HPWL-driven solutions, and their long sequential horizons often require heavy search assistance or offline expert data while leaving little room to preserve multiple competitive layouts. We address this gap by making quality-controlled diversity an explicit objective for macro placement. Instead of relying on a single proxy-optimal solution, we maintain a compact archive of HPWL-competitive yet meaningfully different placements for downstream selection. We realize this idea in DiversePlace, a curriculum proximal policy optimization (PPO) framework that combines a quality-gated diversity reward with an expanding placement horizon, enabling from-scratch RL optimization while keeping exploration inside competitive HPWL regions. On the ISPD2005 benchmarks, DiversePlace consistently improves top-5, top-10, and top-20 archive diversity and achieves lower or virtually identical HPWL on all eight designs with better efficiency. Code: https://github.com/William030422/NIPS2026-DiversePlace.

title: High-performance metapopulation models for epidemic emergencies: Scalability and performance of implicit and explicit mobility representations on CPUs and GPUs
abstract: Epidemics form a subclass of natural disasters impacting countries or entire continents, where suitable reactions might differ substantially across spatio-temporal dimensions. Spatially resolved models based on ordinary differential equations (ODEs) are an efficient modeling approach for large and distributed populations. Commonly referred to as metapopulation models, they allow a realistic representation of spatial heterogeneities and mobility. Yet, their application in epidemic settings under high time pressure requires efficient, parallelized implementations leveraging modern supercomputers. The different ways to represent mobility in metapopulation models affect both epidemic trajectories and computational costs. In contrast to implicit mobility modeling, where populations are coupled through transition and transmission intensities, explicit Lagrangian mobility tracks traveling subpopulations according to their home and current location. In this paper, we compare metapopulation models with implicit and explicit mobility. A four-patch experiment shows that the trajectories of both formulations remain close, but differences increase with the mobility cycle length. We present CPU- and GPU-based parallelizations and analyze fully connected networks with up to 16,384 patches on 128 CPU cores and NVIDIA A100 and H100 GPUs. Roofline analyses show near-maximum performance for the most time-consuming GPU subroutines and identify data reuse and the cost of mobility events as the main performance drivers. Our results show that mobility assumptions, event frequency, numerical solvers, and available hardware need to be considered together when developing metapopulation models for epidemic emergencies. In a synthesized setting with a disease outbreak in central Europe, we show how a worldwide pandemic with 12,865 patches and four billion state variables can be simulated in 24 seconds using GPUs.

title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
abstract: A quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. Here we show that, for Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues $λ_X,λ_Y,λ_Z$, the advantage is governed by $λ_X^2+λ_Y^2+λ_Z^2$. We prove that no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage when this sum is at most one, reduce the general case to the additivity of a Rényi-2 coherent information, and find coded memories that retain a growing advantage within 1% of this threshold. On a superconducting processor, nine simultaneously operated Bell pairs show an advantage that grows or shrinks exponentially with system size, reversing where a parameter-free model predicts. A three-qubit repetition code turns a shrinking advantage into a growing one with all processor and readout errors included, and under dephasing its memory performs better than Bell sampling in any memory frame on a perfect processor.

title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
abstract: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. The results distinguish conditional state identifiability from operational temperature inference.

title: TACC: Target-Aware Carrier Compression for Dense-Context Novel View Synthesis
abstract: Recent feed-forward approaches mark a paradigm shift in novel view synthesis by eliminating the reliance on per-scene optimization, directly inferring 3D representations from input views. However, their reliance on global scene-token context incurs substantial memory and latency overhead, constraining their ability to handle increasingly dense source-view contexts. Compressing source representations offers an intuitive way to limit this token budget. Prior general-purpose compression methods are not tailored for novel view synthesis, as their fixed, target-agnostic nature fails to adapt evidence allocation to individual target views. To overcome this, we introduce TACC, a target-aware compression module tailored for feed-forward latent NVS. Specifically, TACC organizes each source view into a progressive carrier hierarchy. Driven by source-target geometric relevance, it adaptively retrieves tokens to dynamically allocate exact computational quotas. This selective retrieval directly yields a compact, target-conditioned representation. Extensive experiments on the RE10K demonstrate that under dense input settings, TACC achieves $9.23\times$ and $64\times$ higher Effective FPS than Full Context on LagerNVS and LVSM, respectively. Effective FPS excludes one-time source encoding and Carrier construction.

title: Exact sequences of regular LF-spaces
abstract: We show that the category of regular LF-spaces has all kernels but, unlike the category of regular LB-spaces, does not have all cokernels. Its topological exact structure, maximal exact structure and maximal deflation-exact structure form a strictly increasing chain of proper subclasses of the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs.
