Although the unconstrained dark energy parameters reduce the cosmic shear-only $S_8$ constraints to smaller values, our joint multi-probe analysis agrees with the baseline HSC-Y3 $Λ$CDM structure growth amplitude. We obtain $S_8 = 0.774^{+0.027}_{-0.034}$ for $w$CDM and $S_8 = 0.772^{+0.031}_{-0.030}$ for $w_0w_a$CDM. Our results demonstrate that the weak lensing amplitude is robust to extended dark energy parameterizations, and that the dynamical dark energy signal is currently driven primarily by the geometric distance ladders, a critical consistency test for next-generation Stage-IV cosmological surveys.

title: A formula to construct all elements of finite order in Riordan matrix groups
abstract: We characterize the elements of finite order in the Riordan group over the complex field by providing explicit conditions on their entries. Our main result generalizes a previous characterization of involutions to arbitrary finite orders and gives a constructive procedure to determine all Riordan matrices of a prescribed finite order from a suitable choice of parameters. The proof relies on an inductive analysis of the principal submatrices. We further derive consequences for the Lagrange subgroup and the group of formal power series under composition, obtaining a characterization of finite-order series and a constructive description of the solutions to associated functional equations.

title: Source Detection in Complex Networks: Observability, Identifiability, and Inference Frameworks
abstract: Tracing diffusion to its origin is a central inverse problem in complex networks, with applications ranging from epidemic investigation and information spreading to cyber incidents and disruptions in interconnected systems. Although source-detection methods have advanced along diverse methodological lines, their capabilities cannot be assessed independently of the evidence on which they operate. Network structure and diffusion dynamics determine which propagation histories are possible, while the observation mechanism determines which traces of those histories are retained. This review develops an information-centric and identifiability-aware perspective that connects these elements to source inference. We organize existing research around three overlapping observation settings: complete state snapshots, incomplete or noisy observations, and sensor-based observation and design. Within this organization, we examine structural, probabilistic, message-passing, simulation-based, and learning-based methods, comparing their required inputs, underlying assumptions, inference mechanisms, and computational demands. System-theoretic observability, statistical identifiability, and information-theoretic constraints provide complementary ways to examine what the available observations can reveal, while separating limitations of the evidence from those of estimation. Drawing on applications across epidemiological, information, biological, neural, and socioeconomic systems, we identify challenges in uncertainty assessment, model robustness, transfer across networks, and the acquisition of informative observations. This synthesis clarifies the conditions under which diffusion sources can be identified and how inference methods should be selected according to the available observations.

title: Minimising sample size across analysis strategies in preclinical research: Reduced power or negligible benefit
abstract: Preclinical animal studies often allow multiple valid statistical analysis strategies, which can result in different sample sizes required to achieve a target power. Because reducing animal use is an ethical, financial, and practical priority, researchers have a clear incentive to choose the strategy requiring the fewest animals. This may, however, favour an overly optimistic estimate of the sample size required, particularly when prior information is uncertain or biased. This study investigates how minimising sample size across analysis strategies affects statistical power and animal use. We conceptualise this practice as sample size hacking, describe its underlying mechanism, and evaluate its consequences using a simulation study based on a real preclinical cancer study. We varied effect sizes, the level of uncertainty in prior information, and the degree of follow-up bias to assess the resulting sample size reductions and achieved statistical power. Sample size minimisation across analysis strategies substantially reduced the achieved statistical power in several scenarios, particularly for moderate effect sizes and greater uncertainty in prior information. For larger effect sizes or in the presence of follow-up bias, the impact on power was less pronounced, but the resulting reduction in sample size was also smaller. Selecting an analysis strategy solely because it yields the smallest calculated sample size may in fact compromise statistical power, while offering only limited animal savings in other settings. These findings underscore the importance of justifying and pre-specifying the analysis strategy before sample size planning to limit potentially problematic analytical flexibility, reduce the risk of underpowered studies, and promote transparency in preclinical research.

title: Connectedness Principle in the Complex Analytic Setting
abstract: We show that if $(X,B)$ is a normal compact Kähler pair and $f:X\to Z$ is a proper morphism with connected fibers to a normal compact Kähler variety $Z$ such that $(-K_X+B)$ is nef over $Z$, then $\mathrm{Nklt}(X,B)\cap f^{-1}(z)$ has at most two connected components for every $z\in Z$. More generally, we prove the result for generalized pairs whose nef part is allowed to be transcendental. Moreover, we record that the same result holds for projective morphism between analytic varieties (possibly non-compact).

title: Nav4Manip: From Navigation to Dexterous Mobile Manipulation through Co-Evolution
abstract: Dexterous mobile manipulation is essential for robots to perform useful tasks in complex, unstructured environments. However, existing systems face two challenges. First, navigation remains too coarse for downstream manipulation, which often requires a precise base position and approach orientation rather than merely reaching a meter-scale goal region. Second, navigation and manipulation are commonly trained in isolation, lacking a feedback loop that enables the two capabilities to co-evolve. These limitations prevent current systems from reliably executing long-horizon dexterous mobile-manipulation tasks in real-world environments. To address them, we introduce Nav4Manip, a bidirectionally coupled co-evolution system for long-horizon dexterous mobile manipulation. It comprises two complementary architectures: Nav4Manip-N learns long-horizon navigation and refines its policy through manipulation feedback, while Nav4Manip-M trains a world-action model (WAM) for downstream dexterous manipulation. We train Nav4Manip-N in three stages: multi-task co-tuning learns navigation behavior and manipulation-aware affordance prediction; rejection sampling fine-tuning (RFT) rejects low-quality policy-generated paths and fine-tunes the model on retained trajectories; and reinforcement learning from AI feedback (RLAIF) uses counterfactual preferences to further improve navigation decisions. To support this framework, we establish the Nav-N-Manip benchmark and construct Nav4Manip-Pairs from benchmark rollouts, providing large-scale paired navigation--manipulation trajectories and affordance supervision. Extensive experiments on public vision-language navigation (VLN) benchmarks and Nav-N-Manip demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, while real-world evaluations show that Nav4Manip completes diverse dexterous mobile-manipulation tasks. Project website: https://nav4manip.github.io/.

title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
abstract: Reinforcement learning has achieved remarkable success in sequential decision-making, but learning effective policies often requires substantial interaction experience. Model-based reinforcement learning alleviates this dependence by leveraging world models, which are typically used to support planning or policy optimization. In this paper, we investigate an alternative paradigm in which autonomous LLM-based coding agents directly synthesize control policies by reasoning over readable world models. By examining environment source code, these agents translate environmental knowledge into executable decision rules and iteratively refine their policies using online feedback or offline data, without task-specific RL training. Experiments across diverse decision-making benchmarks show that synthesized policies match or outperform conventional RL methods while requiring substantially less experience. Further analyses reveal interpretable decision rules and how they evolve through feedback-driven refinement. Comparisons with policies generated without source code access and experiments under challenging conditions further demonstrate the benefits of readable world models. These findings suggest that direct policy synthesis can reduce reliance on trial and error, challenging the necessity of task-specific RL training.

title: Counting Beyond Frames: Codec Motion Tells Frozen Diffusion VLMs How Many
abstract: Counting how many times something happens is among the simplest questions about a video and among the hardest for video-language models, autoregressive and diffusion alike. The difficulty lies between the frames: a model samples only a few of them, while each repetition unfolds as movement in between. Video codecs already record this movement densely as block displacements, and codec-based video models use it to shape their visual input. We are the first to show that this motion provides direct evidence for the count: a candidate count is a testable motion hypothesis, and unwinding the cycles it implies measures how strongly the observed directions support it. We present CoDiCount, a unified training-free framework that turns this test into a count potential and applies it while a frozen diffusion vision-language model (dVLM) denoises its answer. At every denoising step, structured count messages map each option letter, or each grammar-valid edit of an open integer, to the count it expresses and reweight the model's own probabilities within that set. Consistent gains over the official decoders on MotionBench, TOMATO, and SVCBench demonstrate the broad generalization of CoDiCount across diffusion models, datasets, and diverse counting tasks. With CoDiCount, a 7B dVLM outperforms GPT-5.1 and Gemini-2.5-Pro on MotionBench, surpasses GPT-4o and much larger open models on TOMATO, and matches GPT-5.4 on SVCBench.

title: FeaXDrive2: Body-Scene Spatial Grounding for Feasibility-Aware Generative Driving
abstract: Generative driving planners may produce trajectories that appear feasible at their reference points but violate environmental constraints over the full vehicle body. We propose FeaXDrive2, an end-to-end generative planning framework that enhances vehicle-embodied spatial feasibility (VESF) through body-scene spatial grounding. The proposed method constructs spatial queries from actual vehicle-body corners and dynamically updates visual sampling locations using evolving trajectory estimates across Flow steps. Retrieved local visual features condition subsequent Action Flow-DiT velocity predictions, allowing trajectory generation to guide spatial information retrieval. Rollout-Consistent Safety Fine-Tuning (RC-F) combines high-risk trajectory supervision with reference behavior preservation, followed by planning-supervised VLM-Action Alignment. Vehicle-geometry counterfactual analysis reveals safety differences under identical trajectories but varying vehicle geometry. On NAVSIM, FeaXDrive2 reduces at-fault collisions by 36.5% relative to the base planner and improves PDMS from 87.0 to 88.8. Under NAVSIM v2 evaluation, EPDMS increases from 86.5 to 88.3. Ablation and body-clearance analyses further demonstrate the safety benefits of body-scene spatial grounding.

title: Uniqueness Sequences in the Bargmann-Fock Space
abstract: We show that a locally finite sequence with prescribed multiplicities is a uniqueness sequence in the Bargmann-Fock space if and only if a variational supremum involving Jensen potentials and Gaussian relative entropy is infinite. The proof combines exact subharmonic duality with holomorphic realization at the original Gaussian weight. Restricting the supremum to radial tests yields a necessary and sufficient integral criterion for locally finite unions of pairwise disjoint regular rotation orbits satisfying a bounded-overlap condition. For a planar lattice containing the origin and having fundamental area $π$, changing only the arguments of its nonzero points yields a uniqueness sequence provided that the resulting points are pairwise distinct. In particular, independently and uniformly rotating the nonzero points of the critical square lattice yields an almost surely complete system of coherent states. Finally, we reduce the general criterion to countably many polynomial tests and give finite approximations to each test score with explicit error bounds.

title: Entire function related to shift and difference operator
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the uniqueness problems of entire functions involving difference operators. First, we examine the case where $f-a$, $Δ_c^n f-b$, and $Δ_c^{n+2}f-b$ share $0$ CM (counting multiplicities), where $a$ and $b$ are two entire small functions of $f$ such that $Δ_c^m a \equiv 0$ ($1 \le m \le n$), and $b$ is $c$-periodic. As a consequence, we establish two main results, one of which resolves a conjecture posed by Farissi et al. \cite{FLBA1}. Second, we obtain a uniqueness theorem for an entire function $f(z)$ when $f(z)$, $f(z+c)$, and $Δ_c f(z)$ share a single value, thereby improving and generalizing the corresponding result of Farissi et al. \cite{FLA1} by removing the growth restriction on the order of $f$. Third, we establish uniqueness results for $f(z)$ when $f(z)$ and $Δ_c^k f(z)$ share a value, which improve and generalize the findings of Chen et al. \cite{CCL2} and Huang and Zhang \cite{HZ1}. Finally, we provide several examples to demonstrate that our results are best possible in certain senses.

title: Cyclic polynomials in mixed-weighted Dirichlet-type spaces
abstract: For $\boldsymbolα=(α_1,α_2,α_3)\in\mathbb R^3$, we investigate cyclic polynomials in the mixed-weighted Dirichlet-type space $\mathscr{D}_{\boldsymbolα}$ of holomorphic functions $f(z_1,z_2)=\sum_{m,n\geq0}a_{m,n}z_1^mz_2^n$ on the unit bidisk satisfying $$ \sum_{m,n\geq0}|a_{m,n}|^2 (m+1)^{α_1}(n+1)^{α_2} (m+n+1)^{α_3}<\infty. $$ We give a complete characterization of cyclic polynomials in terms of their zero sets and the parameters $α_1,α_2,α_3$. Our results extend previously known characterizations for anisotropic and total-degree Dirichlet-type spaces on the unit bidisk.

title: Multi-Party Authorization of Maintenance Prescriptions on a Permissioned Blockchain
abstract: In industrial prescriptive maintenance, an equipment supplier's model may recommend an intervention that a plant schedules, a contractor executes, and a quality or safety function approves. A shared ledger records who submitted the prescription, yet cannot check whether the agreed model and decision rule produced it. We require permissioned-blockchain endorsers to verify a succinct proof of that calculation before releasing a work order. On a four-organization Hyperledger Fabric testbed using a public engine benchmark, this stopped all nine contested or mis-operated prescriptions, whereas hash checks accepted four that either raised simulated maintenance cost or reintroduced late failures.

title: The Random Intercept Cross-Lagged Panel Model as a Statistical Model: Identification, Estimation, and Model Comparison
abstract: The random intercept cross-lagged panel model (RI-CLPM) distinguishes stable differences between people from lagged associations within individuals. We use a matrix representation to study its statistical properties for p variables measured across T waves. We derive a necessary and sufficient rank condition for global identification when transition matrices and innovation covariances vary by wave. Under time-invariant transitions, the condition specifies when three waves suffice. For complete Gaussian trajectories, matrix differentiation yields the profile likelihood score for each covariance and transition block. We also derive the population parameters of the conventional cross-lagged panel model (CLPM) when an RI-CLPM with fixed parameters generates the data. Our formulas quantify how CLPM slopes for observed variables differ from RI-CLPM slopes for within-person deviations at each transition. When the RI-CLPM transition matrix is time-invariant, the comparison also covers CLPM slopes pooled across waves. The formulas recover earlier bivariate results and show when cross-lagged slopes can appear, cancel, reverse sign, or change their ordering across models.

title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
abstract: We prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order $k \geq 3$: every spectral point is connected by a path to every "one leg versus the rest" flattening rank. In particular, the asymptotic spectrum evaluated at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. This was previously known only on specific families of tensors (Strassen, FOCS 1986, Crelle 1987-1991; Wigderson and Zuiddam, Bull. AMS 2026) or for specific families of spectral points (Christandl, Vrana and Zuiddam, STOC 2018; Sakabe, Doğan and Walter, FOCS 2026; Alman, Li and Pratt, FOCS 2026). To obtain our path-connectedness theorem we develop a general method for "interpolating" between spectral points, which applies to Strassen semirings that are appropriately decomposable (in the sense of an information-theoretic "method of types" on the semiring) and whose spectral points satisfy a cover property (inspired by slice rank). This covers tensors and asymptotic rank (with "types" given by decomposition into symmetric group irreps), as well as other objects and asymptotic problems, like graphs and Shannon capacity, where it matches the interpolation of Vrana (2019). Using our interpolation methods we furthermore obtain new results and simpler proofs of previous results regarding the asymptotic spectrum of rectangular matrix multiplication, polynomial multiplication and non-crossing (laminar) quantum functionals.

title: Transverse Shifts Driven by Geometric Orbital Torque in Altermagnets
abstract: Anomalous transverse shifts in interface reflection are conventionally attributed to spin-orbit coupling or its pseudospin analogue. Here, we uncover a distinct geometric mechanism driven solely by an orbital torque arising from Fermi-surface anisotropy. During total reflection, an incident wave packet penetrates the anisotropic transmitted medium as an evanescent wave. There, the broken rotational symmetry about the interface normal exerts an orbital torque, and the accumulated angular impulse---the product of the torque and the dwell time---leads to a transverse spatial shift. Applying this mechanism to altermagnets without spin-orbit coupling, we show that the orbital torque is odd in spin. As a consequence, the two spin channels are deflected to opposite sides of the incident plane, giving an intrinsic spatial spin separation in altermagnets. The shift also inherits the angular symmetry of the altermagnetic spin splitting and is strongly enhanced near the onset of total reflection. Our work thus uncovers a new mechanism for transverse shifts, predicts a novel spin separation effect in altermagnets, and offers a direct probe of the altermagnetic order.

title: A Garnett--Jones estimate for matrix weights
abstract: For an \(N\times N\) matrix \(A_p\) weight \(W\) on an averaging basis, set \(M_p=\max\{1,p-1\}\), \(1\leq p<\infty\). At rate \(1/M_p\), the operator-norm exponential moment of \(\log W\) centered on each basis set is bounded by \(2[W]_{\mathbf A_p}^{1/M_p}\). With scalar Garnett--Jones constant \(G\), the BMO distance from \(\log W\) to bounded Hermitian functions is at most \((2N^2-N)GM_p\), uniformly in the characteristic. Power weights on intervals show the sharp order in \(p\). Conversely, a uniform distance bound for scalar \(A_2\) logarithms gives the scalar property with the same constant. Under a uniform small-BMO condition this is equivalent to scalar \(A_2\) decomposition. The estimates apply to cubes and axis-parallel rectangles on \(\R^d\) and \(\T^d\). For rectangles with \(d>1\), the scalar quadratic estimate bounds the distance by \(\sqrt{2N^2-N}\,C_d M_p\), where \(C_d\) depends only on \(d\). The rectangular BMO distance is comparable to the critical exponential scale.

title: Learning to Be Truncated: Preparing LLM Checkpoints for SVD Compression
abstract: Compression based on singular value decomposition (SVD) often requires subsequent fine-tuning or weight correction to mitigate performance degradation. Budget-specific optimization must be repeated for different compression ratios. We introduce LLift, which prepares a pretrained model for SVD compression across ratios without further fine-tuning. LLift fine-tunes a low-rank approximation at a single ratio using the original model as a teacher. We merge the learned updates into the original weights while preserving the complementary components excluded from the training forward pass. We apply SVD to the prepared model's target matrices and reuse the decompositions at different truncation ranks. On LLaMA-7B, we demonstrate accuracy gains across three compression ratios using a single prepared model. The gains extend across model families, model sizes, and SVD compression operators. We analyze gradients and an early training update to provide local evidence that updates learned at one ratio can benefit compression at other ratios. These results show that LLift can improve compression across deployment budgets without fine-tuning each compressed model separately.

title: Magic Moments: An Operational Approach of Certifying Nonstabilizerness from Few Copies
abstract: Magic is the key resource enabling universal fault-tolerant quantum computation beyond classically simulable stabilizer circuits. Certifying it, however, usually requires either full state tomography or an optimization over the set of stabilizer states, both of which rapidly become prohibitive as the system grows. Here, we introduce a moment-based criterion that certifies magic from a few moments of the discrete Wigner function, without fully reconstructing the distribution itself. For pure states of any number of qudits the criterion is necessary and sufficient, while for mixed states we construct a hierarchy of higher moments conditions that reaches the exact negativity threshold. We also derive lower bounds on sum negativity and mana from low-order moments, and use them to bound the negativity factor in quasiprobability simulation. Each moment can be evaluated as the expectation value of a two-outcome observable on a few copies of the state, measurable with a constant-depth Clifford circuit and a number of rounds independent of qudit number, providing efficient, experimentally accessible tools for certifying and quantifying nonstabilizer resources.

title: An Embedded Ergonomic Posture Monitoring and AI-Assisted Home Learning System on a Raspberry Pi 3B Edge Platform
abstract: During independent home study sessions, students frequently sustain improper sitting postures, accumulate excessive sedentary hours, and experience productivity loss from off-task digital distractions. Furthermore, learners often lack real-time pedagogical scaffolding for demanding self-study curricula. To mitigate these ergonomic and instructional challenges, this paper presents an affordable, privacy-preserving cyber-physical embedded system for domestic study spaces. Engineered on a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B (1 GB RAM) paired with a UVC optical camera and a USB condenser microphone, the system executes on-device computer vision utilizing MediaPipe Pose and OpenCV to monitor upper-body alignment, sagittal head inclination, and coronal shoulder asymmetry in real time without persisting raw video streams. A deterministic finite state machine (FSM) quantifies active study durations, enforces health-compliant rest periods, and detects illicit smartphone usage. Simultaneously, an integrated multimodal AI tutoring agent parses voice and text queries via an encrypted API gateway, synthesizing Socratic conceptual hints rather than direct solutions. A lightweight parental web dashboard delivers encrypted session analytics and scheduling configurations. Empirical benchmarks on the physical prototype confirm an end-to-end inference latency of 244-250 ms at a 352x288 resolution (4.0-4.1 FPS), a trunk-angle estimation error of 4.39 degrees MAE over 5,760 synthetic ground-truth poses, a resident set size of 320 MB, a peak SoC temperature of 58.0 degrees Celsius under sustained load, and a 1.58 s total latency for the offline TTS feedback path, proving high practicality for resource-constrained edge deployment.

title: Autonomous Ergodic Robotic Palpation for Elastic Mapping of Curved Soft Tissues
abstract: Autonomous robotic palpation offers repeatable, quantitative estimates of tissue properties for stiff inclusion localization. However, existing methods often rely on prior mesh models or planar surface assumptions that do not generalize to complex human anatomy. We propose an ergodic palpation framework that operates directly on curved soft surfaces using point cloud data. Central to our approach is the Laplace--Beltrami operator, which grounds both online estimation and exploration in the surface intrinsic geometry. We estimate local viscoelastic parameters using an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) and fuse them into a surface-aware Gaussian Process (GP). This probabilistic model drives a diffusion-based ergodic motion planner, generating a continuous exploration trajectory that feeds the new informative samples back to the GP in a closed loop. Throughout this process, a hybrid force-impedance controller regulates interaction forces to maintain contact. We evaluate the approach against existing methods in simulation and validate it in physical experiments on tissue-mimicking silicone phantoms with varying geometries and viscoelastic properties, demonstrating geometry-consistent mapping and stiff inclusion localization under contact-rich conditions.

title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
abstract: Scaling robot learning requires demonstrations that combine realistic visual observations with reliable action supervision. Simulation-based synthesis faces a substantial visual gap relative to real environments, while video-only generation struggles to maintain physically consistent interactions and provide aligned action labels. We present DemoFoundry, an automated framework that couples coding agents with generative rendering to synthesize photorealistic and physically grounded robot demonstrations. Coding agents both construct aligned real--proxy video pairs from existing robot episodes to train a video renderer and write executable interaction programs to generate new demonstrations. Given a scene reference and task instruction, an agent reconstructs task-relevant geometry and writes a control program without requiring target-task human demonstrations. Program execution in a physics simulator produces proxy videos with aligned robot states and actions. The video renderer translates these proxy videos into scene-consistent, photorealistic observations, reducing the need for detailed appearance modeling in each scene. Automated task-execution checks select successful trajectories for rendering and policy learning. Experiments show improved visual quality and action--video consistency. Policies trained on the generated demonstrations outperform raw-simulation training and approach the performance of training on an equal number of real demonstrations.

title: Signals from the early Universe: primordial features from the full-shape analysis of BOSS galaxies and eBOSS quasars in combination with Planck
abstract: We search for primordial oscillatory features using cosmic microwave background (CMB) and large-scale structure (LSS) data, combining \textit{Planck} Public Release 4 (PR4) with galaxy clustering from the Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (BOSS) and quasars from the extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (eBOSS). For the LSS data we perform a full-shape analysis of the power spectrum multipoles with the one-loop effective field theory of large-scale structure, applying infrared resummation separately to each oscillatory component. We consider four templates: linearly and logarithmically oscillating features in Fourier space, with constant, localised, or power-law-decaying amplitudes, and fit them to the CMB and LSS data separately and jointly. We find no statistically significant evidence for primordial features in either dataset, individually or in combination. The best-fitting LSS features improve the fit by $Δχ^2\simeq-6$ to $-10$, which corresponds to global significances of at most $1.6\,σ$ once the look-elsewhere effect is accounted for. In the CMB alone, the most significant feature is reduced to $\sim2.6\,σ$. Over the full frequency range, the LSS bounds on the feature amplitudes are weaker than those from \textit{Planck} by factors of $1.4$--$3$. Combining \textit{Planck} with \textit{BOSS+eBOSS} leaves the CMB constraints essentially unchanged, because the LSS data do not favour the frequencies preferred by the CMB.

title: Supporting Without Taking Over: AI Support in Gratitude Writing
abstract: Gratitude writing can support well-being, but independent practice may lack guidance. Generative AI could help while shaping reflection, agency, and ownership. We investigated how gratitude-writing format and AI-assistance mode influence well-being and writing experiences. In a 2x2 between-subjects study (N=401), participants completed a gratitude reflection or a gratitude letter using two AI-assistance modes: scaffolding, which provided reflective questions after inactivity, or co-writing, which offered inline text suggestions. Participants' well-being improved after using our AI-assisted gratitude-writing system, consistent with the activity's intended benefits. However, participants' experiences revealed a trade-off between the AI-support types: co-writing received higher usability ratings, yet its immediacy could disrupt writing, and greater suggestion acceptance was associated with weaker perceived agency. Scaffolding supported stronger perceived human ownership but was sometimes overlooked. These findings extend human-AI writing research beyond productivity and text quality by showing how AI involvement shapes psychological outcomes and the experience of self-guided, emotionally meaningful writing.

title: A Large Envelope Can Explain Super-Puffs
abstract: Super-puffs are a class of exoplanets with extremely low bulk densities, having masses of a few to tens of Earth masses but radii comparable to that of Jupiter. Observations suggest that these inflated radii can persist for Gyr timescales, even for planets receiving relatively low stellar irradiation. The physical mechanisms responsible for maintaining such large radii, however, remain poorly understood. Here, we model the thermal evolution of super-puffs with substantial H/He envelopes using a one-dimensional planetary structure and cooling model. We follow the coupled cooling and contraction of the planetary interior and H/He envelope while self-consistently calculating the planet's hydrostatic and radiative--convective structure. We find that planets with H/He envelope mass fractions of approximately $40-60\%$ can retain Jupiter-like radii over Gyr timescales, provided that they begin with sufficiently hot interiors. Massive H/He envelopes substantially delay planetary contraction through two effects: (1) strong thermal blanketing, which slows the cooling of the underlying rocky core, and (2) Kelvin--Helmholtz luminosity generated by the cooling and contraction of the envelope itself, which helps maintain its high entropy and inflated radius. Our results suggest that super-puffs may represent a distinct class of planets that accreted large quantities of nebular gas during formation without undergoing runaway gas accretion.

title: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
abstract: Robots should adapt to unfamiliar environments and acquire new skills through interaction, then execute those skills efficiently with practice. Vision-language-action policies provide efficient control, but often need additional human demonstrations to handle unfamiliar settings; reasoning agents can discover solutions using broad prior knowledge and robot-control APIs, but repeated deliberation and repair are costly. Inspired by human learning through reasoning and practice, we propose RoboEvo$^2$, a framework for recursive harness-policy co-evolution. In Policy-to-Harness (P2H) evolution, policy failures guide a coding agent to search complementary Code, Code+ICL, and Code+Policy routes, consolidating verified solutions into reusable skills, routing strategies, and experience memory. In Harness-to-Policy (H2P) evolution, verified trajectories provide supervised training, while Counterfactual Preference Distillation (CPD) teaches the policy to favor successful corrections over failures from the same starting state. The improved policy provides stronger motor skills for subsequent search, while its remaining failures redirect harness evolution, closing the reciprocal loop. Through recursive co-evolution without additional human demonstrations, RoboEvo$^2$ improves standalone success from 11.0% to 84.1% and hybrid success from 30.4% to 90.5% on LIBERO-PRO, with similar gains and reduced agentic costs on RoboTwin C2R. Further experiments demonstrate autonomous task acquisition, cross-embodiment harness transfer, and 95.0% hybrid success on the Unitree G1-D. Our models and code will be publicly released.

title: Electrostatic effects on settling cloud droplets: from pair collisions to size distribution evolution
abstract: We investigate how droplet charge and a uniform vertical electric field influence collisions between cloud droplets settling in still air and how these collisions shape the droplet size distribution. We compute collision efficiencies by analyzing the relative trajectories of pairs of spherical, conducting droplets, accounting for droplet inertia, exact hydrodynamic, electrostatic, and van der Waals forces. The hydrodynamic interactions are based on exact two-body solutions for Stokes flow with interfacial mobility and internal circulation. In the absence of an applied electric field, collisions between like-charged droplets are suppressed, whereas collisions between oppositely-charged droplets are enhanced. A vertical electric field promotes collisions between uncharged droplets through induced polarization and, when sufficiently strong, can overcome the repulsion between like-charged droplets. When the larger droplet has a radius of $10$ or $20μ$m raising the electric field strength from $5\times10^{4}$ to $3\times10^{5}\,\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$ can enhance the collision efficiency of uncharged droplet pairs by an order of magnitude. Depending on droplet size and field strength, for oppositely charged pairs, an applied electric field can either enhance or suppress collisions relative to the zero-field case. Using collision kernels computed from droplet pair trajectories, we solve the stochastic collection equation with a flux method on a two-dimensional grid that resolves droplet mass and charge. For an initial mean droplet radius of $10μ$m , by $40$ min in every electrified case the large-droplet mode of the mass spectrum reaches a larger radius than in the hydrodynamic reference case. This suggests that electrostatic interactions can hasten warm rain initiation by accelerating droplet growth through collision and coalescence.

title: First Order Real Resonant Digital Filters and A Novel Orthogonal State Generator
abstract: We describe FOREST, a real, first order digital resonant filter and orthogonal state generator. We show that in spite of the imaginary nature of the roots of the transfer function of a resonator, appropriate interpretation of this transfer function nonetheless leads to a practical first order filter with real coefficients. We use a discrete state space model of FOREST to predict the resonator properties, and implement the filter in digital signal processing slices on a digital signal processing platform. Applications are in real time digital signal processing, engineering fields such as mains electricity monitoring and motor control, any application requiring a phase locked loop, and physics applications utilising high-quality-factor resonators.

title: Provably Efficient Concave Utility Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation
abstract: Concave utility reinforcement learning (CURL) unifies a diverse range of problems, including standard reinforcement learning (RL), imitation learning, and maximum entropy exploration. Unlike standard RL, CURL generally requires estimating high-dimensional state-action occupancy measures. Consequently, existing methods for CURL either sidestep the exploration problem, are restricted to the tabular setting, or lack computationally efficient policy optimization. To address this, we study CURL in finite-horizon episodic bilinear MDPs, where the transition model admits a low-dimensional representation in known feature spaces. We use the bilinear structure to efficiently estimate occupancy measures via low-dimensional feature expectations, and propose a model-based optimistic concave utility policy optimization (OCUPO) framework. We first instantiate OCUPO in the on-policy setting, where each iteration uses independent trajectories to estimate the concave utility policy gradient, and prove an $\widetilde{O}(ε^{-4})$ sample complexity. To improve sample efficiency, we then instantiate OCUPO in the off-policy setting. We propose a novel backward feature regression subroutine that reuses trajectories collected by past policies to estimate the occupancy measure of the current policy. Under suitable technical assumptions on the policy class (satisfied, e.g., by log-linear policies with sufficiently expressive features), we prove that the resulting algorithm achieves an $\widetilde{O}(ε^{-2})$ sample complexity, up to a controllable projection error. We further extend our framework to linear MDPs and show that the resulting off-policy algorithm retains the same sample complexity. In these settings, the dependence on $ε$ matches that for standard RL with linear function approximation. Moreover, our algorithms do not rely on the integral oracle required by prior work.

title: Boundary Observability for a Class of Degenerate Kolmogorov-Type Equations in a Cylindrical Domain
abstract: This paper investigates the boundary observability for a class of multi-dimensional degenerate Kolmogorov-type kinetic equations in a cylindrical domain $Ω= \mathbb{T}_{x_1} \times (0,1)_{x_2}$. The model features a horizontal drift term $x_2^γ\partial_{x_1} φ$ coupled with a boundary-degenerate diffusion operator $\partial_{x_2}(x_2^α\partial_{x_2} φ)$ acting solely on the velocity variable, where $γ= 1$ and $α\in (0,1)$. By leveraging the structural advantages of the cylindrical domain, we establish an analytical framework based on the method of separation of variables. Crucial Carleman estimates tailored to the degenerate dual operator are derived to capture the subtle dissipation effects under the influence of the transport term. Consequently, by virtue of a uniform a priori estimate, we establish the quantitative boundary observability inequality for the state function.

title: Neural Rendering Compiler: Generative Video Models as Programmable Renderers
abstract: Generative video models are becoming powerful renderers, yet lack the predictable control interfaces of conventional systems such as HTML/CSS engines or Blender. Their capabilities emerge implicitly from training, making it difficult to determine what they can reliably execute. We present Neural Rendering Compiler (NeurCo), which automatically probes frozen video models to construct model-specific capability manuals describing which semantic requirements they can reliably satisfy. NeurCo represents user intent in a model-agnostic intermediate representation of objects, constraints, events, and cameras, then compiles it into model-specific execution strategies. Reliable requirements remain unchanged, while unreliable ones are selectively rewritten or compiled into alternative execution strategies. We introduce VComBench, a benchmark of 380 compositional, multi-requirement tasks spanning text-to-video, image-to-video, and reference-to-video generation. NeurCo improves requirement satisfaction from 46.8% to 52.3% on Wan and from 66.5% to 69.3% on Minimax H3, and achieves further gains when combined with prompt enhancers, including on Seedance 2.5. Our analysis reveals model-specific differences in control capabilities and trade-offs between controllability and photorealism, highlighting capability-guided compilation as a promising approach to programmable generative video rendering.

title: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models
abstract: Answering a knowledge-based visual question requires first recognizing the entity in the image and then recalling knowledge about it. Thinking vision-language models (VLMs) reason for thousands of tokens before answering, yet it remains underexplored how well such thinking VLMs perform each of these two steps. We therefore analyze thinking VLMs on this task and make two key observations. (1) Recognition is the bottleneck, since 76.3% of errors across four models on ViQuAE stem from misrecognizing the entity, and 84.9% of these failures are resolved once the entity name is provided in the question. (2) Recognition is driven by entity-recall clues rather than by general descriptions of the image. An entity-recall clue is a distinctive visual detail that helps the model recall the entity, such as keys, a traditional attribute of Saint Peter. Based on these findings, we propose ClueRL, a reinforcement learning approach that extends Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with an advantage localized to the entity-recall clue in the thinking trace. Rather than injecting new entity knowledge, ClueRL changes how VLMs think: it leads them to attend more closely to visual details and spot these clues, helping them use the knowledge they already have. Consequently, it outperforms both GRPO and a perception-reward baseline on three entity recognition benchmarks. Moreover, this clue-seeking behavior generalizes beyond entity recognition, the only task used for training. Since recognition is the bottleneck, the gains carry over to knowledge-based visual question answering. They even extend to general multimodal reasoning, raising Qwen3.5-4B by 4.4 and 4.0 points on the ScienceQA and MMMU subsets of MMStar, respectively.

title: Slow mixing of Gibbs sampling for the quantum Curie-Weiss model
abstract: Hamiltonian evolution can spread local operators across a dense quantum magnet. We show that this global support does not remove the bottleneck to thermalization in the quantum Curie-Weiss model: at fixed low temperature and weak transverse field, the Chen-Kastoryano-Gilyen Gibbs sampler [arXiv: 2311.09207] has an exponentially large mixing-time lower bound. A dynamical quantum bottleneck theory that generalizes the classical notion of conductance has been proposed alongside existing frameworks that rely on spatial locality. We also give a complementary interpretation of slow mixing using an effective Fokker-Planck equation.

title: Experimental Quantum Hardware Benchmarks of Flat Non-Clifford Hypergraph States, Antipodal Obstructions, and Nonlocal Games on IBM Heron r2
abstract: Real-hardware demonstrations of quantum contextuality have reached high precision on superconducting processors, exemplified by Google Quantum AI's Mermin-Peres magic square and stabilizer games on Willow (Science, 2026). Extending such benchmarks beyond the Clifford regime requires non-Clifford hypergraph states |ψ_f> = 2^{-n/2} \sum_x (-1)^{f(x)} |x> governed by discrete algebraic invariants. Building on our Lean 4-verified framework of Modular Walsh Rigidity and Antipodal Obstructions, we present an experimental study on two 156-qubit IBM Heron r2 processors (ibm_fez, ibm_kingston) across 3 to 50 qubits and 11 auditable jobs (2.13 RUs total). First, we verify antipodal obstructions and mod-17 Walsh rigidity for degree-3/4 states (n=6,8,10), observing 5.4x-11.6x X-basis flatness separation between bent states, obstructed controls, and a degree-4 mod-3 fooler (W = +-1 mod 3), plus n=7 nonlinearity extraction (54.83 vs. 56.00). Second, barrier-protected Loschmidt echoes confirm non-Clifford coherence up to genuinely entangled 16-qubit degree-4 states (1,488x above random on ibm_fez; 17,296x on ibm_kingston for 2x8q, a 2.87x cross-chip gain) and locate a Heavy-Hex depth-513 coherence cliff. Third, calibration-aware layout raises the raw Mermin-Peres win rate on ibm_fez to 96.85 +- 0.09% raw (+87.4 sigma above 88.89% classical; 1.45 pp below Willow's 98.30% raw), while a tensored SPAM diagnostic reaches 98.35%. Uniformly random even-weight GHZ parity games beat the classical bound up to n=30 (89.44% [+79.4 sigma] at 6q to 59.46 +- 0.54% [+17.4 sigma] at 30q). Finally, 3-qubit CCZ rotated Mermin-3 (83.95 +- 0.29%, +31.2 sigma) and Hardy/Guhne-Cabello (77.15 +- 0.33%, +6.5 sigma) games strictly violate the exhaustive 75.00% LHV ceiling, and degree-3/4 antipodal parity witnesses achieve up to +45.87 pp (n=12) and +35.79 pp joint advantage on connected 16-qubit degree-4 states.

title: BridgeHammer: DNN Backdoor Attack via CPU-iGPU Shared-memory Rowhammer
abstract: Heterogeneous systems-on-chips (SoCs) share physical memory between CPUs and integrated GPUs (iGPUs), creating a path for CPU-side memory corruption to compromise the integrity of deep learning models used for iGPU inference. Implanting a backdoor that causes targeted misclassifications on trigger-bearing inputs while retaining accuracy on normal inputs requires carefully selected weight changes. However, realizing these changes presents two challenges: where to induce faults, since vulnerable DRAM locations may not contain the targeted weights, and when to intervene, since memory placement and fault injection must align with different stages of the model deployment lifecycle that involve two distinct computation domains. We present BridgeHammer, a Rowhammer-based backdoor attack that addresses these challenges by coordinating targeted weight placement before zero-copy binding for the iGPU and fault injection before inference. The iGPU then uses the corrupted model for subsequent inferences. We evaluate BridgeHammer on a heterogeneous Intel CPU-iGPU platform using OpenVINO, targeting ResNet-20, VGG-16, and ResNet-50 at both INT8 and FP32 precision. Across all six configurations, BridgeHammer achieves an 88.9% attack success rate (ASR) and 86.3% clean accuracy on average, with reliable target-page placement and bit-flip reproduction. These results demonstrate a new integrity vulnerability on heterogeneous CPU-iGPU SoCs, motivating cross-domain memory integrity protections.

title: Numerical analysis of a conservative Crank-Nicolson scheme for quasilinear Gross-Pitaevskii equations
abstract: We propose and analyze a fully discrete Crank-Nicolson finite-difference scheme for one-dimensional quasilinear Hamiltonian Gross-Pitaevskii equations with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. We establish the existence and uniqueness of numerical solutions and an $H^1$-stability estimate. For sufficiently regular exact solutions, we obtain second-order convergence in both time and space in the discrete $H^1$-norm. The analysis covers the focusing and defocusing cubic nonlinearities and both signs of the quasilinear coefficient $κ$, under a uniform discrete ellipticity condition when $κ<0$. The main difficulty in the error analysis comes from the derivatives introduced by the quasilinear interaction. To overcome this problem, we introduce a discrete action combining the discrete energy and mass, and establish a coercivity inequality in the discrete $H^1$-norm that allows us to control the numerical error. Together with consistency estimates and a discrete Gronwall inequality, this yields second-order convergence. Numerical experiments with bright solitons corroborate the predicted convergence rates.

title: Technical Report MEG2text: Beyond Alignment in Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text
abstract: Non-invasive brain-to-text seeks to recover language from brain activity without surgery. A central challenge is turning learned brain-language representations into accurate word predictions. We present MEG2text, a decoding system that combines corrected training and evaluation, brain-text alignment, a class-balanced word readout, and target-word language-model fusion. On LibriBrain100's word-ranking task, MEG2text reaches 64.12% mean Top-10 balanced accuracy, improving on published MEG-XL by 16.92 percentage points across four corpora, with gains on each corpus. Controlled comparisons show that both implementation corrections and a learned readout contribute to this improvement. Candidate-level analysis reveals that some words receive informative scores yet consistently lose to competing candidates, while an identical-feature comparison shows that learning the classification rule improves decoding without changing the representation. These findings identify the decoding rule as a consequential part of non-invasive brain-to-text and show how system improvements can make better use of aligned neural features.

title: Evacuation Traffic Prediction for Dynamic Transportation Networks over Multiple Hurricanes: A Generalized Graph Learning Approach
abstract: High traffic demand during hurricane evacuations causes severe congestion on major highways, leading to delays and safety risks for evacuees. Predicting evacuation traffic in real-time can significantly enhance evacuation management efforts. However, evacuation traffic is highly dynamic and uncertain due to evolving hurricane characteristics and diverse population response. Each hurricane has unique characteristics and evacuation contexts, resulting in different spatial-temporal traffic patterns. Moreover, the structure of detector-based transportation networks varies across multiple hurricanes. Hence, a model trained on the data from one hurricane may not generalize well for others. This study proposes a generalized dynamic graph learning framework using traffic detectors and evacuation data from 12 historical hurricanes. Leveraging the dynamic nature of transportation network, we develop a Graph Convolutional Long Short-Term Memory (GCN-LSTM) model that predicts evacuation traffic up to 6 hours in advance. For an unseen hurricane (Milton, 2024), the model shows strong generalizability, achieving an RMSE of 280.6 and R2 of 0.96 for 1-hour prediction, and an RMSE of 459.8 and R2 of 0.89 for overall 6-hours prediction. We also introduce a modular training approach, where we evaluate performance improvements by sequentially incorporating data from multiple hurricanes. The proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models for overall 6-hour prediction horizons. Ablation experiments show an 8.4% improvement in RMSE for the proposed dynamic GCN-LSTM model compared to its static counterpart. Traffic management officials can use the developed model to understand future traffic conditions during hurricane evacuation in advance and take proactive measures to reduce delays during evacuation.

title: Who Fills the Gap? Role Similarity and Teammates' Minutes When NBA Players Are Ruled Out
abstract: When a core player is ruled out before an NBA game, do teammates whose statistical role resembles that of the removed set (every rotation player ruled out, about three per case) play more? Using injury reports stamped at least six hours before tip-off and rosters reconstructed after the season, we study 2,441 team-games from 2023-24 to 2025-26 in which a core player was ruled out for a medical reason. Among teammates in the same game, one within-case standard deviation more similarity in role profile (three-point attempts, assists and rebounds per minute) goes with about 0.63 more minutes, holding reference minutes and headroom fixed (p < 0.0001); this compares teammates within a game, not the minutes gained because of the absence. The pattern holds in two earlier seasons and in exploratory within-player and without-and-with comparisons. Whether similarity adds to listed position is not settled. The association is small and yielded no statistically detectable reduction in the error of the retrospective minute forecasts we tested. Role coverage, how much of the missing minutes and roles the remaining rotation could restore, showed no consistent incremental association with team role output or the final margin.

title: Non-archimedean generalisations of the Kuznetsov formulas
abstract: In this paper we develop non-archimedean analogues of the Petersson-Kuznetsov formulas. Specifically, choosing a particular test function on either the geometric or spectral side of the formula, one may express the other side in terms of integral transforms. Such transforms involve representation theoretic Bessel functions attached to irreducible unitary admissible representations of $\text{PGL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)$.

title: PoVi: Agentic Poetry-to-Video Generation with Knowledge Grounding and Figurative Understanding
abstract: Poetry-to-video generation requires more than translating text into visual scenes. Poetic language is highly compressed, often depends on historical and cultural knowledge, and frequently conveys meaning through metaphor, imagery, and other non-literal expressions. We introduce PoVi, a benchmark and agentic framework for grounded poetry-to-video generation, evaluating semantic grounding, discourse coherence, and audiovisual realization. PoVi reconstructs poem semantics into an evidence-bounded representation and progressively transforms them into narration, interpretation, character assets, and shot-level visual plans, followed by narration-aligned video generation. Across three planning backbones and four video generators, PoVi consistently improves over single-call generation, with the largest gains on implicit background knowledge and metaphorical relations. PoVi provides a testbed for studying knowledge-grounded, long-horizon multimodal generation beyond direct text-to-video synthesis.

title: First detection of s-cis-acroleine (sc-CH2CHCHO) in the interstellar medium
abstract: We report the first interstellar detection of the higher-energy $s$-cis conformer of acrolein (CH2CHCHO) toward TMC-1 using the Quijote line survey. Local thermodynamic equilibrium modeling, assuming a rotational temperature of 7.5 K, yields a column density of $(1.0\pm0.2)\times10^{11}$~cm$^{-2}$ when fitting the observed lines. The s-cis/s-trans abundance ratio is $0.45\pm0.11$, despite an energy separation of approximately 1025~K, indicating a strongly nonequilibrium conformational distribution. An exploratory gas--grain chemical model identifies C3H5 + O as the dominant acrolein formation route, pointing to this reaction as a first entry to consider when explaining the isomeric ratios. The observed ratio provides a new constraint on conformer-specific formation, destruction, and interconversion processes in cold interstellar clouds.

title: Is Chaotic Dynamics Enhancing Particle Swarm Optimization? An Anytime Performance Assessment
abstract: The search dynamics of particle swarm optimization (PSO) can be driven by random or chaotic values. We study if there are performance differences between random and chaos if distributional equivalence of the used sequences is observed. Therefore, we consider an anytime performance assessment which quantifies the fraction of runs reaching a given target value within a specified numerical budget. Furthermore, we connect quantifiers of the chaotic dynamics to performance metrics of the anytime analysis. The results show that once the underlying distributions are controlled, deterministic chaotic sequences yield no general or consistent advantage over random sequences. Performance differences arise most prominently from the underlying distribution, but also from search-space dimensions, benchmark targets, and numerical budgets. We also find potential budget-dependent advantages under specific parametrization of chaotic maps and distribution settings.

title: ShowNow: Fine-Grained Speculative Streaming for Responsive World Models
abstract: Interactive world models must generate video continuously while responding promptly to user actions. Real-time throughput alone leaves input latency unresolved: coarse generation blocks delay action updates, and generation after input adds work to the response path. We introduce ShowNow, a fine-grained speculative streaming framework that uses computation available during playback to prepare action-conditioned futures before input arrives. Single-latent commitment enables frequent decisions, while configurable preparation covers one to eight actions. We construct a matched multi-future dataset to train alternative continuations from a common state; shared-history tree execution and fused commitment make their preparation efficient. On a single H100, our 5B model sustains 480p generation at 16 fps with eight prepared futures. In ViZDoom, the complete ShowNow deployment reduces median input-to-display latency from 620 to 208 ms relative to the native-block SolarWM-FT deployment. Matched-policy experiments reduce restart empty ticks from 1.56% to 0.09% (94%) and improve on-time responses to action changes. These results establish complementary roles for fine-grained commitment and advance preparation, with measured trade-offs in visual fidelity and long-horizon consistency. ShowNow turns playback-time computation into responsive visual interaction. Project: https://github.com/showlab/ShowNow.

title: Automatic dual basis sets for self-consistent field calculations
abstract: Density functional theory (DFT) has long been the workhorse of electronic structure theory, and it is experiencing a new boom thanks to big data applications and machine learning. A DFT calculation requires the iterative solution of the self-consistent field (SCF) problem, whose cost is the product of (i) the number of SCF steps and (ii) the cost of a single step. The number of SCF steps depends strongly on the initial guess, regardless of the SCF algorithm, and quantitative DFT accuracy is known to require at least a polarized triple-$ζ$ basis set. However, a qualitatively correct solution may often be found already in a smaller \emph{dual basis} (DB), which can then bootstrap a calculation in the full basis set. Traditionally, the DB is chosen by hand for each application to enable robust convergence to the ground state. In this work, we pursue automatic generation of DBs for SCF calculations. Our generator constructs a pruned orbital basis from the target orbital basis for a predefined precision threshold and a given Fock matrix. As expected, the larger the basis set is, the smaller the fraction of kept basis functions. The DBs produced by our algorithm exhibit similar performance for a wide range of systems from the first 4 periods of the periodic table. Ultimately, we find that presently available initial guesses for the Fock matrix are not accurate enough to unlock the use of adaptive basis sets, and believe that the same limitation may hold for similar attempts for basis compactification.

title: Non-Existence of Eigenvalues and Interface States for the Schrödinger Operator with Longitudinal Interface Potentials
abstract: We consider the Schrödinger operator in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a flat interface separating two half-spaces in which the real potential varies only in the directions parallel to the interface. This problem generally possesses no shift invariance. Nevertheless, using the method of multipliers, we prove the absence of eigenvalues. In addition, in the case of periodic potentials on each side of the interface the same method shows the absence of interface states which are quasi-periodic in the directions parallel to the interface and localized in the transverse direction.

title: Distance from the Truth: Why Fragmented Merchant Underwriting Misses Risk, and What Source-Attributable Evidence Changes
abstract: Merchant underwriting becomes vulnerable when evidence is evaluated without enough visibility into its source, freshness, relationship to the applicant, or meaning for the proposed activity. Individually favorable checks do not necessarily establish that the same business is operating the merchant account, that its representative may bind it, or that its settlement instructions are authorized. We describe three failure modes of fragmented underwriting: distance from the source, the gap between a decision and the evidence needed to justify it; the correlation gap, in which material relationships among the person, legal entity, owners or controllers, representative, business activity, and settlement destination are not evaluated when each signal is considered alone; and point-in-time controls, in which a historical verification is treated as present eligibility. We map these failure modes to identity-proofing, customer-due-diligence, sanctions, third-party-risk, card-network, and Nacha requirements, and propose a merchant-underwriting application of the ChainIT Transaction Truth Architecture built on provenance, correlation, and persistence. The application keeps a logically unified evidence record that identifies what was checked, the subject and relationship involved, the relevant times, the applicable policy, the decision, and any exceptions, and it keeps evidence validation, applicant verification, organizational authority, and the institution's risk judgment separate. We also set out a proposed evidence and decision receipt, a defined 90-day shadow enrollment pilot with adjudicated outcome measures and deliberate control-failure tests, and a ten-question self-assessment. Proposed controls, illustrative scenarios, and pilot measures are identified as such and are not represented as observed production results.

title: Symplectic bumpless pipe dreams
abstract: Bumpless pipe dreams are combinatorial objects in bijection with alternating sign matrices. Double Grothendieck polynomials can be expressed as weighted sums over bumpless pipe dreams, a perspective that has led to many advances in the combinatorics of Schubert calculus and connections with integrable systems. We introduce symplectic bumpless pipe dreams and present an analogous formula for symplectic Grothendieck polynomials, which represent the equivariant K-theoretic classes of Sp(2n)-orbit closures in the flag variety. To prove this result, we construct an analogue of Lascoux's inflation on these objects, providing a combinatorial realization of the symplectic transition equations that appear in work of the first author, Marberg, and Pawlowski. We also show that certain marked symplectic bumpless pipe dreams correspond to set-valued reverse plane partitions. This allows us to give a tableau formula for a class of symplectic Grothendieck polynomials and to compute principal specializations of the corresponding symplectic Schubert polynomials, answering a question of Hamaker-Marberg-Pawlowski in the fixed-point-free case.

title: A Failure-Driven Data Flywheel for Post-Training Vision-Language-Action Models
abstract: Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models rarely satisfy all behavioral requirements of a new platform, and teams without a large deployed fleet lack the data to address the resulting failures. We propose a failure-driven data flywheel for post-training such models. It constructs target scenarios absent from the available data by inserting task-relevant entities into reconstructed real-world scenes, and evaluates the model against each behavioral requirement of the target task. Failure rates form a failure map across task conditions and difficulty levels, which is re-evaluated after each round and assigns larger data generation quotas to conditions where the model still fails. We instantiate the framework in autonomous driving for occluded-pedestrian emergence and yielding at stop-sign-controlled intersections, and evaluate it on two VLA models and one non-VLA planner in simulation and on a real vehicle. For occluded-pedestrian emergence, five rounds of post-training improve the critical-phase collision-free rate on the sealed test set from 0.261 to 0.579 for AutoVLA and from 0.390 to 0.765 for ReCogDrive, while the unnecessary braking rate in paired control scenarios never exceeds 0.013. On a full-scale vehicle without real-world training, post-trained ReCogDrive achieves 4 of 5 safe passages, versus 1 of 5 for the base model. Fine-grained evaluation reveals a pattern obscured by the collision-free rate alone: both VLA models learn anticipatory deceleration before reaching the occluding vehicle, while braking after pedestrian emergence remains limited. For stop-sign yielding, the stop-before-line rate rises from 0.100 to 0.897 for AutoVLA and from 0.000 to 0.667 for ReCogDrive. With sequential training from the pedestrian-capability models, it reaches 0.599 and 0.358, respectively, while the pedestrian collision-free rate decreases by at most 0.032.

title: Diagnosing internal leakage currents through magnetometry of lithium-ion cells
abstract: Internal leakage currents are difficult to detect and to localize through measurements at the terminals of lithium-ion cells. We measured the magnetic fields of pouch cells non-invasively with a magnetometer while a battery cycler set the current and recorded the voltage. A three-axis magnetoresistive sensor remains fixed inside a three-layer magnetic shield, and two linear stages move the cell in two dimensions relative to the sensor to acquire a map of the magnetic field above the cell. The field of an intact cell was linear in current from 10 to 420 mA, and its maps were symmetric between charge and discharge. To create internal leakage currents, two 600 mAh cells were damaged by mechanical indentation. Both cells developed a magnetic field at zero applied current that decayed over hours, while the cell voltage showed a loss of charge by self-discharge. This field breaks the symmetry between the charge and discharge maps, which allows leakage to be detected while the cell is being cycled. At rest, the setup detects leakage currents down to about 1--3 mA. The results highlight opportunities for battery diagnostics and safety, and may help in designing techniques for characterizing soft shorts.

title: Seeing the Right Context: Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Remote Sensing
abstract: Remote sensing scene understanding requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to interpret queried targets in relation to nearby objects and surrounding structures, which serve as spatial references or define the scope of an answer. However, standard answers and bounding boxes often leave these contextual relationships implicit. Thus, we construct GeoContext-5K to make them explicit in 5,394 training pairs for visual question answering (VQA), with spatial cues, visual facts, and supporting regions. GeOPD uses these annotations for on-policy distillation, guiding a frozen teacher with region marks on the full image and a visual fact while preserving surrounding spatial references. It prioritizes teacher corrections that agree with the shift in the student's next token distribution when evidence is restored. A complementary objective weights the contrast between the student's scores on the two views by how much masking lowers the teacher's log probability for the same sampled token. Experiments on five remote sensing VQA benchmarks show that GeOPD outperforms the evaluated open-source MLLMs and matched post-training baselines, improving over the 4B and 9B base models by 5.81 and 2.97 percentage points on average. The dataset and code will be publicly released at https://github.com/YeeCharm/GeOPD.

title: Direct generation of N00N states with layered semiconductors
abstract: Photonic N00N states enable phase sensing beyond the classical limit, but their generation conventionally relies on interferometric manipulation of photons using bulk optical components. Here we demonstrate the direct generation of a family of tunable two-photon polarization N00N states from a subwavelength-thick 3R-MoS2 flake. For propagation along the optic axis, the in-plane crystal symmetry allows all symmetry permitted spontaneous parametric down-conversion pathway to interfere coherently, while the large second-order nonlinearity provides sufficient brightness at submicrometer thickness without phase matching. The pump polarization sets the basis of the N00N state or equivalently a two-photon Holland-Burnett state without altering its structure or the generation efficiency. The biphotons are highly indistinguishable, reach high fidelity with the target state across a wide range of pump polarizations, and show two-photon interference fringes with visibilities above the threshold for the postselected phase supersensitivity. Our theoretical analysis further indicates that, in the ideal single-mode limit, the same interaction would yield higher-order Holland-Burnett states. By eliminating interferometric stages, our results establish a compact, pump-programmable source for quantum-enhanced polarization interferometry

title: Effect of class proportion shifts on classifier curvature
abstract: Changing the class mix can alter mean loss without changing the classifier. To distinguish this reweighting from changes in the model itself, we studied ten-class CIFAR-10 classification in separate branches for two target classes, measuring the trace of the loss Hessian with respect to the output-layer parameters on fixed images of each target class. Across ten new initialisations, after 60 updates to the output layer with frozen features, the trace changed by -0.152% on average in branches where the target class share rose from 10% to 19%, and by +0.071% in branches where it fell to 1%, relative to each branch's initial trace. These changes do not isolate the effect of class share from that of the assigned training images. We developed a forecast based on initial class gradients after examining the first experiment's results and then tested it prospectively without modification. For direct increases from 10% to 19%, rather than increases after a deficit, its mean absolute error was 0.022 percentage points on the initial-trace scale, compared with 0.152 for a zero-change forecast and 0.104 for equally weighted gradients. Using the assigned class proportions improved the forecast of how much the trace would change.

title: Maco-RL: Scaling Agent Capabilities with Mixed-Task Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Mixed-task reinforcement learning (MixRL) directly trains a unified policy across domains to continually expand agent capabilities without training separate specialists or requiring an extra distillation stage. Despite its appeal, scaling MixRL poses significant challenges in achieving stable and efficient mixed-task learning, effectively allocating rollout compute, and supporting continual domain expansion. To address these challenges, we propose Maco-RL, an approach that effectively scales MixRL. Specifically, Maco-RL employs a quota-based scheduler for asynchronous rollouts across multiple task domains, thereby stabilizing training by balancing gradient contributions and mitigating off-policy effects. Along an orthogonal axis, Maco-RL further introduces Tri-Buffer Sampling (TBS) to allocate compute among samples with varying levels of mastery, promoting sustained frontier exploration while preserving acquired capabilities. Experiments on five benchmarks show Maco-RL raises Qwen3.5-27B's overall score from 43.6 to 54.2 and then to 60.1 with continual expansion, reaching the frontier held by Qwen3.8-27B, which is further pushed outward by +5.7. Maco-RL also outperforms single-task RL with less compute for policy updates. These results support MixRL as a practical and compute-efficient post-training approach with substantial potential to strengthen general agent capabilities.

title: On the equivariant Heegner point main conjecture and refined conjectures of Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer type
abstract: In 1992, Darmon formulated refined conjectures of Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer type for Heegner points, and proved the ``order of vanishing'' part of his conjectures by a development of Kolyvagin's Euler system arguments. In this paper, for good ordinary primes split in the underlying imaginary quadratic field, we prove the $p$-part of the ``leading coefficient formula'' conjectured by Darmon, as well as its derived strengthening by Bertolini-Darmon. Our method, which also offers a novel perspective on earlier results, is based on the formulation and proof of new equivariant anticyclotomic main conjectures, including an equivariant extension of Perrin-Riou's Heegner point main conjecture.

title: Interfaces in Long Range CFT$_1$
abstract: We consider interfaces in the theory of a single free scalar in AdS$_2$ defined by adding relevant operators along portions of the boundary. We begin with Neumann/Dirichlet interfaces, computing the associated scaling dimension and $g$-factor ratio; we also explain how arbitrary interface correlators can be computed numerically efficiently. Then we move on to interfaces between generalized free field and long-range interacting theories such as long range Ising, determining many quantities in perturbation theory. Finally we setup a bootstrap problem for four-point interface correlator. We use this to find tight bounds on the $g$-factor ratio as a function of the interface scaling dimension.

title: Entanglement and HBAR entropy in a Lorentzian non-commutative black hole
abstract: We investigate how Lorentzian non-commutative smearing affects entanglement and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) outside a black hole. For a massless scalar field, tracing over the interior partner gives the exterior quantum channel, its logarithmic negativity, mutual information, and Bell entanglement fidelity. At fixed mass and Killing frequency, increasing the smearing lowers the surface gravity, increases the accessible correlations, and suppresses the leading atomic emission probability. The horizon displacement begins at order $\sqrtΘ$, while the thermal correction at infinity begins at order $Θ$. At fixed local frequency, the redshift introduces a term of order $\sqrtΘ$ at fixed areal radius. Holding the proper distance fixed, it cancels this term and recovers the common Rindler response close to the horizon. For a freely falling atom, emission and absorption obey detailed balance at the Hawking temperature in the leading horizon approximation. Random atomic injection drives the selected mode from the vacuum to a thermal state with an exact relaxation law and nonnegative entropy production. Near equilibrium, we obtain $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/4$ when the radiated energy is drawn from horizon heat, where $\dot A_p$ is the positive radiative area loss. When the radiation is assigned to ADM mass loss at fixed smearing length $\ell=4\sqrt{Θ/π}$, the result is $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/[4(1-\ell/r_+)]$. The mass dependence of the exterior source thus enters the entropy per unit area lost at order $\sqrtΘ$.

title: When the Proxy Is Wrong: Mismatch-Corrected Bandits for Adaptive Data Sampling
abstract: Data allocation methods often use a small proxy model to select training data for a larger target model. However, this proxy can rank data differently from the target, leading to suboptimal training performance. To address this problem, we model the mismatch between the proxy and target models and incorporate it into the allocation decision. To do so, the problem is cast as a multi-fidelity bandit, where each arm is a data intervention. The proxy reward is observed every round, whereas the target reward is revealed only on rare audits of the same update. These paired observations identify arm-wise mismatches without assuming a shared offset or preservation of rankings. Mismatch-corrected bandits correct the proxy with paired residuals, audit only uncertain decisions, and pace the audit budget over training. From a theoretical viewpoint, we prove a regret decomposition and lower bounds under stationarity. These bounds show that proxy-only allocation can incur linear regret and that a minimum number of paired audits is necessary. Under abrupt changes, using the audit budget early can also incur linear regret. A sliding-window policy that spreads audits over training achieves regret of order $\sqrt{Γ_T T\log T}$ where $Γ_T$ denotes the number of change points. Experimentally, we test the approach in a closed-loop proof of concept on CivilComments-WILDS, where BERT-Small guides the training of BERT-Large. Mismatch correction improves worst-group accuracy over a target-only policy with the same target-model budget. Spreading audits over training improves worst-group accuracy by 6.3 to 10.5 percentage points at the same audit count.

title: From Shared Patterns to Individual Evidence: Two-Stage Reasoning for Emerging Entities in Temporal Knowledge Graphs
abstract: Temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs) continually introduce emerging entities whose interaction histories evolve from zero-shot debuts into sparse, bursty few-shot trajectories. However, current paradigms are fragmented: pattern-transfer methods lack catalog-wide event memory, whereas online memory models suffer from endpoint-role asymmetry that degrades unseen-answer ranking. Furthermore, sparse early interactions exhibit both long-range dispersion and local redundancy under skewed distribution. To address these challenges, we propose INSPIRE (Integrating Shared Patterns and Individual Evidence for Reasoning), a two-stage forecasting framework over a known catalog. In Stage I, INSPIRE learns an availability-aware shared-pattern predictor that fuses event-updated memory across the full candidate catalog while applying coordinated query- and catalog-side masking. Subsequently, Stage II freezes this predictor and optimizes a lightweight individual-evidence adapter (EA) combining textual semantic priors with correlation-weighted long-range event statistics under support- and role-balanced co-answer supervision with prior-odds debiasing and soft residual alignment. In addition, we decompose evaluation by endpoint roles and track longitudinal emerging-answer cohorts via query-micro and answer-entity macro metrics.
